# Lapidary: Implementation Plan

This file is the design log, written for the coding agents that build the app. Users read `README.md`; developers read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Written 2026-09-08. This plan is meant to be executed by a Claude Code session phase by phase. Read `CLAUDE.md` first for repo rules.

## 0. What we are building

A Windows desktop app (Electron) for reviewing Claude-suggested copyedits to novel chapters written as Markdown in an Obsidian vault. The author sees their original text double-spaced, with each suggested change floating above the words it would replace. Each change can be accepted or dismissed at any time, in either direction. Dismissed changes stay visible but faded. Accepted changes swap places with the original, which becomes the faded ghost. Paragraph-level comments (continuity, plot, flow) appear in a side panel. Claude is called from inside the app using the author's own Claude subscription; since `codex.3` ChatGPT can answer instead, on the author's own ChatGPT plan through Sign in with ChatGPT (5.7, 5.8). The OpenAI API key that could answer from Phase 5c went in `codex.6` (section 5.0). The author can also write their own edits, which become suggestions like any other. Nothing is ever written into an existing manuscript file except through an explicit Save to chapter, which first copies the version it replaces into the app's data folder (6.5); nothing saves to the chapter by itself. The only other writes to the manuscript folder create a file that is not there yet, a new chapter or the guidelines file on first use, and cannot touch one that is. The one exception is a reviews folder the author keeps inside the manuscript folder (6.1): there the app saves over, moves and removes its own review files and the small records it keeps beside them (6.4) as it would anywhere else, and never a chapter (CLAUDE.md rule 1).

| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Shell                 | Electron 44 + electron-vite 5 + Vite 7 + React 19 + TypeScript (see Appendix C.1)                                                                                                              | The Node main process hosts the provider layer (the user's Claude Code run as a child process, the `openai` package), file I/O, and the watcher with no friction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Claude access         | The Claude Code each user installs and signs in to themselves, found on their computer (5.6 item 1) and run from the main process as `claude -p` over stream-json: every built-in tool removed, no settings files, the app's system prompt and its JSON schema for structured output (11.3 q, C.42). A Claude Code from Anthropic's installer keeps itself current (a WinGet or Homebrew copy is updated by hand), so new models need no release of the app. Signed in with a Claude plan, `claude -p` draws on the plan's usage limits (Help Center, 2026-10-07, Appendix A); with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment, which Claude Code always uses in `-p` mode when it is there, reviews are billed per token to the key's Console account. |

The old check said ready when signed out and spent two model requests on every launch (11.1). |

Review with AI's Guidelines row says when the style sheet is still empty (5.5, `setup.10b`). | The friend sets the app up alone, from the README and the app (11.0), and a reviewer without the style sheet "fixes" names, invented words and the spelling variant. |
| Primary Claude output | A change list: `{changes: [{paragraph, before, after, category, reason}], comments: [...]}`                                                                                 | The author's edits are a few words at a time. Short exact quotes anchor reliably, output is tiny, and every change carries a reason and category. Larger issues become comments by design.                                                                                                                                                |
| Secondary input       | Full-text diff (a corrected copy of the open chapter, pasted or loaded from a file)                                                                                          | Needed for "Submit manual review" (7.5) and for imports. Same hunk model, same UI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Folders               | User picks a manuscript folder and a reviews folder, anywhere on disk                                                                                                       | Inside or outside the vault does not matter. Reviews are `.json`, which Obsidian does not index.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Before a save that changes the file, the bytes it replaces are copied to `<userData>/backups`; no backup, no save (6.5). Main refuses any target but a chapter in the manuscript folder or opened from it (6.1, CLAUDE.md rule 1). | The author decides when the chapter changes, and a write in the background would race Obsidian's own autosave and a sync tool (11.0). The friend may not use git, so a copy outside the vault, never listed, indexed or synced, is what undoes a save. |

List populated from Claude Code's `initialize` reply, each entry labelled with its version and grouped by family (`shared/ai/claudeModels.ts`, round 5). Opus uses a Pro plan's limits fastest, so on a Pro plan the review dialog notes that Opus models, Default included, use the limits fastest, and the first welcome guide preselects Sonnet. |

There is no way anybody is paying for API tokens for this. I think the ChatGPT sign in alone is fine." The ChatGPT sign-in is then the one credential the app stores, encrypted, main-process only, and never shown (CLAUDE.md rule 2). |

## 3. Data model (`src/shared/types.ts`)

```ts
export type ChangeCategory =
  | 'spelling'
  | 'typo'
  | 'homophone'
  | 'grammar'
  | 'agreement'
  | 'tense'
  | 'punctuation'
  | 'word-choice'
  | 'redundancy'
  | 'awkward'
  | 'consistency'
  | 'formatting'
  | 'other';

export type CommentCategory =
  | 'consistency'
  | 'plot'
  | 'flow'
  | 'pacing'
  | 'clarity'
  | 'repetition'
  | 'pov'
  | 'style'
  | 'suggestion'
  | 'other';

export type HunkStatus = 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'dismissed';
export type AnchorQuality = 'exact' | 'fuzzy' | 'ambiguous' | 'stale';

export interface Hunk {
  id: string;
  start: number; // char offset in review.base.text (LF-normalized)
  end: number; // exclusive
  baseSide: 'original' | 'replacement'; // which text currently occupies [start,end) in base
  original: string; // may be '' for a pure insertion
  replacement: string; // may be '' for a pure deletion
  paragraph: number; // paragraph index at anchor time, for display and navigation
  category?: ChangeCategory;
  reason?: string;
  source: 'claude' | 'diff' | 'manual'; // 'manual' is an edit the author typed (7.4)
  status: HunkStatus;
  anchor: AnchorQuality; // 'stale' hunks are listed in the side panel, not inline
  edited?: boolean; // a model suggestion whose wording the author rewrote
  supersededBy?: string; // id of the manual hunk whose span swallowed this one
  keptOut?: KeptOutReason; // files.7: why the guard kept this model suggestion out of the text; only on a stale hunk at offset 0 (11.3 k)
}
// A SyntaxKind (src/shared/text/obsidian.ts), or 'paragraph-break', 'markup' or 'combined' (11.3 k, C.73)
export type KeptOutReason = SyntaxKind | 'paragraph-break' | 'markup' | 'combined';

export interface ReviewComment {
  id: string;
  paragraph: number | null; // null when Claude gave no usable anchor, or when its paragraph left the file
  wasParagraph?: number; // the paragraph it had when a change on disk took that paragraph away (ui.7, C.60)
  quote?: string; // short excerpt Claude referenced, if any
  category: CommentCategory;
  text: string; // may include a suggested rewrite
  status: 'open' | 'resolved';
}

export interface Review {
  version: 1;
  id: string; // <chapter-slug>--<ISO timestamp>
  sourcePath: string; // absolute path of the chapter; the review belongs to exactly this file (files.1, C.45)
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  decidedAt?: string; // files.1: last decision (suggestion, comment, save); picks the review a chapter opens with only while none is recorded as last on screen (apply.26, 6.4)
  base: { text: string; hash: string; eol: 'lf' | 'crlf'; bom: boolean; trailingNewline: boolean };
  generator: {
    // 'manual' was called 'paste' until Phase 5b; migrateReview renames it on load.
    // For a model-written review the kind is the provider id (Phase 5c). 'openai' is a review on the
    // OpenAI API key, a provider until codex.6; such a review still opens, named "OpenAI (API key)".
    kind: 'claude' | 'chatgpt' | 'openai' | 'manual' | 'file';
    provider?: 'claude' | 'chatgpt' | 'openai'; // Phase 5c; withGeneratorProvider fills 'claude' on load when missing
    model?: string; // model that actually answered (modelUsage key, or the Responses API's model)
    effort?: string;
    guidelinesHash?: string;
    costUsd?: number; // Claude: Claude Code's own estimate (`total_cost_usd`). An OpenAI key's review: this app's price table, only for known models. ChatGPT: none, the plan pays
    costEstimated?: boolean; // true when costUsd is the app's own arithmetic, as on an OpenAI key's review; the status bar says "estimate"
    usage?: unknown; // result.modelUsage or response.usage, stored verbatim
    durationMs?: number;
    sessionId?: string;
    fallbackNote?: string; // set when a safety classifier moved the request to a fallback model (5.1)
    paragraphBase?: 0 | 1; // Phase 5d: what the paragraph numbers in `raw` count from (5.2); absent on older reviews
  };
  raw?: unknown; // untouched structured_output from Claude, never edited
  hunks: Hunk[];
  comments: ReviewComment[];
}
```

Settings (`src/shared/types.ts`; every key normalised with its default in `src/shared/settings.ts`, 11.3 d):

```ts
export interface Settings {
  manuscriptFolder: string | null;
  reviewsFolder: string | null; // null: <userData>/reviews (6.4)
  guidelinesPath: string | null; // null: <manuscriptFolder>/GUIDELINES.md (10)
  provider: 'claude' | 'chatgpt'; // default 'claude'; the review dialog's Provider list (5.0, 5.5); 'openai' too until codex.6
  model: string; // the Claude model; default 'default', passed as no --model flag (section 1, setup.1)
  chatgptModel: string; // default '': the list's default, `defaultChatGptModel` (5.8); `openaiModel`, the key's, until codex.6
  effort: EffortLevel; // default 'high', shared by both providers
  zoom: number; // 1 is normal size (section 7 Zoom)
  theme: 'system' | 'light' | 'dark'; // default 'system' (11.3 d and e)
  onboardingDone: boolean; // the welcome guide was finished or skipped (section 7, setup.11)
  dismissedHints: string[]; // 'pro-model-preselected' (setup.1, C.67), 'save-to-chapter' (apply.12)
  checkForUpdates: boolean; // default true
  updateDownloadConsent: string | null; // the version the author agreed to download
  sideSplit: number | null; // the side panel's split; null is the usual one (ui.6)

```

`model` stays the Claude model under its old name so every settings.json on disk still reads correctly; `modelFor(settings, provider)` picks the right one, so neither provider can be sent the other's model. `effort` is shared. `onboardingDone`, when the key is missing, is true for settings that already name a manuscript folder, so an install from before 1.0 never sees the welcome guide unasked. The ChatGPT sign-in is not a setting and is never in settings.json (CLAUDE.md rule 2), nor was the OpenAI key before `codex.6` took it out; a settings.json from before then that names `openaiModel`, or `openai` as the provider, is read as 11.3 (d) gives.

Invariants:

- Hunks never overlap. Sorted by `start`. Anchoring rejects the later of two overlapping hunks and records it as `stale` with a note in `reason`.
- An edit the author types is a hunk like any other (`source: 'manual'`), so the composed output stays a pure function of base plus decisions and every edit is reversible and re-anchorable. A hunk carrying `supersededBy` stays `stale` through a rebase: its words often still exist inside the edit that replaced them, and re-anchoring it there would undo a decision the author already made.
- `base.text` is the file content normalized to LF with BOM removed. All offsets refer to it. EOL, BOM, and trailing-newline flags are restored on write.
- YAML frontmatter at the top of the file (`---` ... `---`) is never inside any hunk and is never sent to Claude as an editable paragraph.
- A model suggestion that would change Obsidian syntax is kept out of the text (`files.7`, 11.3 k): it is stale at offset 0 with `keptOut` saying why, is listed under Unanchored with that reason in words, and never reaches the page or the file. It stays out: neither the guard nor a rebase places it again.
- The composed output text is a pure function of `base` and `hunks`. See `compose.ts`.

## 4. Text algorithms (`src/shared`)

### 4.1 Paragraphs (`text/paragraphs.ts`)

Split `base.text` on runs of blank lines (`splitParagraphs`; the separator is `/\n(?:[ \t]*\n)+/`, a little wider than the `/\n[ \t]*\n+/` first planned, so several blank lines that hold spaces or tabs are one separator), keeping exact `start`/`end` offsets for each paragraph and preserving the separators. A paragraph index is stable for the life of a review. Frontmatter, a `---` line at the very start of the text up to the next `---` line (`frontmatterRange`), is returned separately with `isFrontmatter: true` and index -1, and excluded from numbering sent to Claude. No paragraph starts or ends with a line break (`files.22`, C.76): blank lines at either end of the body, which a separator of two line breaks or more does not take, belong to no paragraph, so the first body paragraph starts at `bodyStart` or later, also where the body starts on the line after the frontmatter's closing `---`. Spaces before a paragraph's first words stay, as indentation.

### 4.2 Compose (`diff/compose.ts`)

For each hunk in offset order, the desired side is `replacement` when `status === 'accepted'`, otherwise `original` (`desiredSide`). If `desiredSide !== baseSide` and the two sides differ (`changesBase`), the other text goes into the span; otherwise the base's own slice is copied, so drift between `base.text` and a hunk's recorded strings never rewrites untouched prose. Stale hunks take no part (`activeHunks`). Because hunks do not overlap, `composeText` is a single left-to-right pass that copies the base between hunks. `composeForFile` restores EOL/BOM/trailing newline last (4.6).

### 4.3 Change list to hunks (`diff/anchor.ts`)

Input: Claude's `changes[]` and the paragraph list.

1. Look for `before` as an exact substring of paragraph `p`, matches on word boundaries first (`cleanOccurrences`, C.4: "began" is not found inside "beganning"; when it occurs only inside words, those count). One match on word boundaries: `exact`. Several matches, or only matches inside words: choose the first and mark `ambiguous`.
2. No match: try paragraphs `p-1`, `p+1`, `p-2` and `p+2`, nearest first (Claude occasionally miscounts). Found once, on word boundaries: `exact` with corrected paragraph index; otherwise the first found, `ambiguous`.
3. Still nothing: fuzzy match (`fuzzyFind` in `diff/fuzzy.ts`) with diff-match-patch `match_main` against the whole text near the stated paragraph's start offset, `Match_Threshold` 0.3 and `Match_Distance` 2000, on the first 32 characters of `before` (diff-match-patch's `Match_MaxBits`), the end then moved by up to a quarter of its length (2 to 12 characters) to fit the whole of it. Accept only if the matched span's edit distance over the longer of the two lengths (`distanceRatio`) is at most 0.2 and it starts at or after `bodyStart`, past the frontmatter and the line break that closes it (`files.7`, C.72). Mark `fuzzy` and set `original` to the actual matched text.
4. Otherwise `stale`, its reason followed by "[Could not find this text in the chapter.]". The hunk keeps `before`/`after` for display in the side panel.
5. Normalize: if `before` and `after` share a common prefix and suffix, trim both so the hunk covers only the differing words (`trimCommonAffixes` in `diff/trim.ts`, which widens the cut back out to whole words: "colour" to "color" stays one word, not "ou" to "o"). This makes the floating suggestion short and precise.
6. Drop any hunk where trimmed `original === replacement`.
7. Screen (`AnchorOptions.screen`, which `createAiReview` sets to `screenModelHunks` in `diff/protect.ts`, `files.7`): each pending model suggestion that would change Obsidian syntax is kept out of the text (11.3 k), before overlaps are resolved, so one kept out never pushes another off the page as an overlap.
8. Resolve overlaps as in the invariants, with the touching rule in the same pass (`AnchorOptions.touching`, which `createAiReview` sets to `touchingRule` in `diff/protect.ts`): of the hunks that overlap nothing left on the page, a model suggestion that starts exactly where the one before it on the line ends is kept out as `combined` (11.3 k). It is off the page before the hunks after it are measured, so, as in step 7, it pushes none of them off as an overlap (the `files.7` review; run after the pass, it did).
9. A review loaded from disk goes through the screen and the touching rule again (`guardLoadedReview`, run by `upgradeLoadedReview`, with `guardTouching`, as a saved review's hunks on the page never overlap), so one saved before the guard is screened as it opens. Before them, any other hunk still on the page that the page does not draw is taken off it, its words and decision kept (`unanchorOutsideBody`, `files.22` and its review, C.76): one that starts before the first body paragraph or ends past the last, or, in a body with no paragraph, one that starts before `bodyStart`. A zero-width hunk at the very start of the first paragraph or the very end of the last is drawn and stays. The paragraph box and the full-text diff made such hunks before `files.22`, at the line break after the frontmatter's closing `---` and at a single blank line that starts or ends the text, and the page no longer draws them, while Save would still write them.

### 4.4 Full-text diff to hunks (`diff/wordDiff.ts`)

1. Split both texts into paragraphs. Align them with jsdiff `diffArrays` on paragraph strings (exact equality first; if a paragraph was edited it shows as remove+add).
2. For each removed/added paragraph pair in sequence (pair by position within the changed block; unpaired ones become whole-paragraph hunks), run `diffWordsWithSpace` and group consecutive changed tokens into one hunk: `original` = concatenated removed tokens, `replacement` = concatenated added tokens. Adjacent hunks separated only by whitespace are merged. An unpaired removed paragraph is deleted with the blank line after it where a paragraph follows the block, and otherwise with the one before it, as the paragraph box deletes a last paragraph, except the first paragraph of the body, which has none before it (the `files.22` review, C.76): blank lines that end the text belong to no paragraph, and a deletion there, or one left past the last paragraph by a save, is not drawn. An unpaired added paragraph goes after the last removed paragraph or the paragraph before the block, behind a blank line; at the top of the body, before the first body paragraph, followed by one; in a body with no paragraph, at the end of the text. None goes before `bodyStart`, in the frontmatter or at the line break that closes it (`files.22`, C.76).
3. Offsets are computed in the original text. `source: 'diff'`, no category or reason.

### 4.5 Rebase (`diff/rebase.ts`)

When the file changes on disk (or before a Save when the disk hash differs from what the app last knew):

1. New base = disk text, normalized.
2. For every hunk, the text expected in the new base is `baseSide === 'original' ? original : replacement`. Also try the other side: if the user already applied the change by hand in Obsidian, the replacement is what exists now. Every occurrence of a side's words in the body of the new text is a candidate, those on word boundaries first, as in 4.3 step 1 (`cleanOccurrences`), and the 12 nearest the old offset are scored (`NEAREST`); the fuzzy search of 4.3 step 3 runs, near the old offset, only when neither side has a candidate. (The plan first said to search a window of a few hundred characters round the old offset, then the whole text; the ranking below does what the window was for. `RebaseOptions.window`, 400, stayed declared and read by nothing until `files.23` removed it and its default, with a test that over 3,000 characters of new paragraphs above leave every hunk found where, and as surely as, one short paragraph does, which a 400-character window fails.) Update `start`, `end`, `baseSide`, `anchor`. A side that holds no text, the empty side of a deletion or an insertion, is a zero-width place found by the text that surrounded the hunk (48 characters either side together, then 24 and 12, then either side alone), never inside a word, and it competes with the other side's words (`apply.23`, C.52). Candidates rank by word boundaries, then by how much of the 40 characters either side still reads as before (where both texts begin or end, the edge counts as reading as before), then the side the base holds, then distance. The other side wins, and the decision follows it (C.5), only where the file plainly shows the change made or undone there: an empty place whose surroundings read as before in full on one side, or for at least 12 characters of whole words on both (a side with less old text than that says nothing), once copies of the hunk's own words within 40 characters of it have been weighed against it in whole words (`settleCopies`, the `apply.23` review): a copy that reads further takes the place's claim away; words whose surroundings read as before on both sides, or on one side when they did not stand beside a copy of themselves (the twin of a doubled word); or, for a hunk whose own side has words, the only such words in the file. None of these counts for a hunk already off the page (step 3). A decision Save would write stays only where its own side is plainly in place: words with one side of their surroundings as before, or the only such words when they did not stand beside a copy of themselves, and not tied with a place beside them; an empty place with one side as before in full and the other for at least 12 characters of whole words. Only words are placed by the fuzzy search: a deletion or an insertion with no place found exactly goes to Unanchored. Only the body of the new text is searched (`files.20`, C.74): no hunk of any source, the author's own edits and decided suggestions included, is placed before `bodyStart`, in the frontmatter or at the line break that closes it. Words in the frontmatter are no candidates and do not count towards the only such words in the file, a place may be found by text that starts in the frontmatter but may not lie there, no copy there is weighed against a place, and the fuzzy search reads the body alone. A review loaded from disk keeps none there either (4.3 step 9, `files.22`).
3. Hunks found nowhere become `stale` and drop out of the inline view, and so does a hunk whose other side seems to be in the file but not plainly, or whose unsaved decision would otherwise be written at a guessed place. A deletion or an insertion that is stale stays stale: only its surroundings could place it, and a stale hunk has none. Any other hunk that is stale comes back only on its own side's words, with its decision as it was: with no place in the old text, nothing shows that its other side, wherever it stands, is the change made or undone there, so its other side never wins (`plainlyOnDisk`, the `files.20` review, C.74). A suggestion the guard kept out of the text (`keptOut`, 11.3 k) is not looked for at all and stays as it was, since found again it would be back on the page, syntax change and all (`files.7`, which needed this so a change on disk could not undo the guard). Nor is one the author's own edit swallowed (`supersededBy` naming a hunk still in the review, C.23), which stays off the page, since its words often still stand inside the edit that replaced them. The rest of the guard runs as when a review is made (4.3 steps 7 and 8, `files.20`): each model suggestion still undecided is screened in its new place (`screenModelHunks`) before overlaps are resolved, and the touching rule runs within the overlap pass (`resolveOverlaps` with `touchingRule`), so a change on disk that puts one into syntax, or right where another ends, keeps it out of the text with the reason, and one kept out pushes no other off the page as an overlap. A review the rebase gives therefore loads as it is (`guardLoadedReview` changes nothing).
   `RebaseStats` counts what the cards say (`files.20`, C.74): `anchored`, the hunks on the page after the rebase; `newlyStale`, those it took off the page, which were on it before and are not kept out; `keptOut`, the suggestions it kept out of the text, those kept out before not counted again; `adopted`; `stale`, every hunk off the page after it; and `orphanedComments`, the comments step 4 unanchored. "Could not be found" and "lost" count `newlyStale`, a sentence says how many it kept out, and the opened and reloaded cards warn only when `newlyStale` is above 0 (6.2). `RebaseResult.changes` names the hunks behind `newlyStale`, `keptOut` and `adopted` by id, for the reload card, which reports a run of reloads (6.2, the `files.20` review).
4. Comments keep their paragraph index if the paragraph text still exists (match by first 40 characters, then by the quote), otherwise `paragraph: null`, with the index they had in `wasParagraph`, so the side panel can say where they were (`ui.7`, C.60). A comment already unanchored keeps that number, and nothing anchors it again.
   Property tests should confirm: compose(rebase(review, compose(review))) reproduces the same output, and status is preserved across a round trip.

### 4.6 EOL and BOM (`text/eol.ts`)

Detect `\r\n` presence, a leading UTF-8 BOM, and a trailing newline on read (`normalizeText`). Normalize to LF internally. Restore all three on write (`restoreText`) so git diffs and Obsidian see only the intended changes. A file counts as CRLF when it holds a single CRLF pair, and a lone CR is read as a line break too, so a file that mixes CRLF with LF or lone CRs is written back all CRLF by a save that changes it; only one final line break lives in `trailingNewline`, and any blank lines before it stay in the text.

## 5. AI integration (`src/main/providers/`, `src/shared/prompt`, `src/shared/ai`)

### 5.0 The provider layer (Phase 5c)

Every service that can answer "Review with AI" implements one interface in `src/main/providers/types.ts`:

```ts
interface ReviewProvider {
  id: 'claude' | 'chatgpt'; // and 'openai', an API key's, until codex.6
  label: string;
  runtime(): Promise<RuntimeStatus>; // can it run now, and under whose account
  models(): Promise<ModelInfo[]>; // in the order the dialog shows them
  review(request: ReviewRequest, hooks: { onProgress; onRateLimit?; signal }): Promise<ProviderResult>;
  test?(hooks: { onRateLimit?; signal }): Promise<{ model? }>; // Test the connection (setup.8); throws when it fails
}
// ProviderResult: { output: ReviewOutput (the shared zod schema), raw, model, usage, costUsd?, durationMs, ... }
```

- **IPC is provider-neutral.** `ai:runtime`, `ai:models`, `ai:review`, `ai:cancel` and `ai:test` each name the provider in the payload (`ai:test`, `setup.8`: one very small request, answered with `{ok, model?, durationMs, error?, rateLimit?}` rather than a thrown error, after at most 60 s; `testConnection` in `providers/connectionTest.ts` times it, aborts it at the limit or on quitting, and answers a provider without `test` with "has no connection test": Claude's is the one test, ChatGPT having none (`codex.3`) and the OpenAI API key's, one unstreamed Responses call that no button offered, having gone with it in `codex.6`); progress and rate-limit notices arrive as `ai:progress` and `ai:rate-limit`. The IPC layer (`src/main/ipc.ts`) owns request ids, Cancel (an `AbortSignal` per request) and the broadcasts; providers only call their hooks, so no provider imports IPC. The key's three channels, `secrets:openai-status`, `secrets:openai-set` and `secrets:openai-clear`, went in `codex.6`. Sign in with ChatGPT (`codex.2`, 5.7) has five, `chatgpt:status`, `chatgpt:sign-in`, `chatgpt:cancel-sign-in`, `chatgpt:sign-out` and `chatgpt:confirm-data-settings`, which answer with the status alone (`ChatGptStatus`), never a token or an id; and `shell:open-external` opens a web page by its name (`ExternalPage`, today only `chatgpt-data-controls`), never an address the page sends.
- **Everything downstream is shared.** Both providers get the same system prompt (5.4) and the same numbered chapter (5.2), and both replies go through the same zod schema (5.3), the same anchoring, the same guard on Obsidian syntax (4.3, 11.3 k, `files.7`), hunks and comments. A review records `generator.provider` and the model that answered; the status bar and the history badges show both.
- **Claude** (`providers/claude.ts`) is 5.1 and 5.6 unchanged, moved behind the interface. Since `cli.1` it runs the user's `claude` instead of the SDK (11.3 q, C.42).
- **The Responses request** (`providers/openai.ts`), the official `openai` package's Responses API, which the ChatGPT provider sends since `codex.3` and alone since `codex.6` (it was the OpenAI API key's provider from Phase 5c until then; what of it went with the key is under **The key**, below):
  - `instructions` = the system prompt, `input` = the numbered chapter (a list of one user message for ChatGPT, 5.8 item 1), `text.format` = `{type: 'json_schema', name: 'manuscript_review', strict: true, schema}`, `reasoning.effort` from the app's effort, `store: false`, `stream: true`, and the request's `AbortSignal`.
  - The schema is the draft-07 export rewritten by `toStrictJsonSchema` (`src/shared/ai/openaiReply.ts`) into the strict subset: every property required, `additionalProperties: false` everywhere, optional properties made nullable, and unsupported constraint keywords dropped. On the way back `stripOptionalNulls` removes exactly the nulls that transform introduced (a comment's `quote: null`), keeps legal ones (`paragraph: null`), and the shared zod schema validates the result. `raw` keeps what the model sent.
  - Streaming: `response.output_text.delta` accumulates the text and drives the progress label with an estimated token count (four characters per token) until `response.completed` supplies the real usage. A stream that ends without `response.completed`, or with `response.incomplete` or `response.failed`, is an error.
  - Models: the list is ChatGPT's, from its own endpoint (5.8 item 2). `NOT_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `/-(pro|codex|deep-research|chat)(-|$)|chat-latest/i`, names the models a default passes over (`hardening.10`, C.82), which `defaultChatGptModel` reads.
  - Effort: `OPENAI_EFFORT_FOR` maps low/medium/high/xhigh/max. The installed SDK's `ReasoningEffort` accepts all five, so the map is the identity (C.25); a model that refuses a level says so in the error (`chatgpt-failed`, "... The model or the effort level may not be available on it: choose another under Model or Effort in Review with AI.", 5.8 item 7), the dialog's note on it having gone in `codex.5` (C.116).
  - Errors are the provider's (ChatGPT's in 5.8 item 7); what the request words itself: a stream that closed early, a reply that fails to parse (a message naming the model that answered and what was wrong), and a response that ends `incomplete`, which says what stopped it (`incompleteFailure`, `files.10`): at `max_output_tokens` the model reached its output limit, named with the tokens the reply had used, which are the model's own limit since the app sets none, in `replyLimitMessage`'s words (C.77); at `content_filter` OpenAI's content filter stopped it; any other reason is named. Cancel maps to `cancelled` like Claude's.
  - Cost: token usage is always stored. A ChatGPT review has no cost, as the plan pays.
  - `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_OPENAI_BASE_URL` (formerly `STET_OPENAI_BASE_URL`), a development switch that packaged builds ignore (C.39), points the SDK at another base URL. Otherwise the client is always built with `https://api.openai.com/v1` and a null organization and project, so the SDK never takes them from `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_ORG_ID` or `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` (`clientOptions`). It exists so the path can be driven against `test/helpers/mockOpenAi.ts`, whose every scenario a window run reaches through the ChatGPT route since `codex.6` (Appendix C "What taking out the OpenAI API key settled"); nothing sets it in normal use.
- **ChatGPT** (`providers/chatgpt.ts`, `codex.3`) sends that request, its `input` a list, with the Sign in with ChatGPT access token as the bearer, which `src/main/chatgpt` renews: 5.8.
- **The key** went in `codex.6` (the author, 2026-10-24: "This is for hobbyists. There is no way anybody is paying for API tokens for this. I think the ChatGPT sign in alone is fine."; Appendix C "What taking out the OpenAI API key settled"). From Phase 5c to then, `src/main/secrets.ts` kept an OpenAI API key the author saved in Settings (a password field with Save key and Remove key, encrypted with `safeStorage`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` its fallback), and the `openai` provider sent the request above with it, listed its models with `models.list()` (the newest full gpt-5 its default, `hardening.10`), worded its errors (a refused key with Open Settings on the card, a rate limit or no credit, an unverified organisation with Verify Organization) and estimated its cost from `src/shared/ai/pricing.ts`. All of that went, with its channels, its rows in Settings and the review dialog, the welcome guide's Use OpenAI instead, its connection test and its label "experimental" (`hardening.11`). What stays of it: a secrets.json from before `codex.6` that still holds the key's part is read past, the key never used, and the part left out of the next write (`knownParts`, as any part this version does not know); a settings.json that names `provider: "openai"` reads as Claude, the default, and its `openaiModel` is dropped at the next save (`normalizeSettings` drops what it does not know); and a review saved on a key keeps `generator.kind` and `generator.provider` `openai` (`GeneratorProvider`), opens as before, and is named "OpenAI (API key)" in History, the review selector and the status bar, with its cost still marked "estimate".

### 5.1 The request

_Superseded by C.42 and 11.3 (q): there is no SDK. The app runs the user's `claude` with the flags in `claudeOptions.ts`, sends the system prompt and the schema in the `initialize` request, and `claudeCli.ts` reads the same messages listed below from its stream-json output; the usage-limit prefixes are copies in `src/shared/ai/claudeStatus.ts`. The SDK call is kept as the record of what those flags replace._

```ts
import { query } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';

const q = query({
  prompt: renderChapter(paragraphs), // see 5.2
  options: {
    systemPrompt: buildSystemPrompt(guidelinesMd), // static instructions + GUIDELINES.md
    model: settings.model, // alias such as 'opus'
    effort: settings.effort, // 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'
    outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: reviewOutputJsonSchema }, // draft-07
    maxTurns: 1, // raise if structured output needs more, see risks
    settingSources: [], // do not load the user's ~/.claude settings or CLAUDE.md
    persistSession: false,
    includePartialMessages: true, // progress from message_delta usage
    disallowedTools: ALL_BUILTIN_TOOLS, // see risks: verify the current tool names in sdk.d.ts
    cwd: app.getPath('userData'), // never the vault
    env: { ...process.env },
    abortController,
    stderr: (line) => log.debug(line)
  }
});
```

Message handling while iterating `q`:

- `stream_event` with `event.type === 'message_delta'`: read `usage.output_tokens` for a progress counter.
- `system` / `model_refusal_fallback`: note the fallback in the review's generator info.
- `system` / `model_refusal_no_fallback`: surface `api_refusal_explanation` to the user.
- `rate_limit_event`: read its `rate_limit_info` into `RateLimitInfo` (`readRateLimit` in `providers/claudeResult.ts`, `setup.9`): the status, the reset, which limit (`rateLimitType`, kept as `kind`), the share of it used (`utilization`, a fraction, which Claude Code 2.1.302 sends only with `allowed_warning`, while it warns) and whether extra usage is paying (`isUsingOverage`, kept as `usingOverage`, set on a `rejected` notice). The status bar words it with `describeRateLimit` (section 7), and the card for a review that stops at a usage limit names the limit from it (5.6 item 4, C.64).
- `assistant` with `error` set (`authentication_failed`, `rate_limit`, `billing_error`, ...): map to a user-facing message. `authentication_failed` opens the sign-in instructions.
- `result`: success requires `subtype === 'success'` and a present `structured_output`. Parse with zod. Any other outcome is an error shown with the SDK's message. Record `total_cost_usd`, `modelUsage`, `duration_ms`, `session_id`.
- The `for await` loop can throw after an error result. Wrap it.

Exported constants `USAGE_LIMIT_ERROR_PREFIXES`, `USAGE_WARNING_PREFIXES`, and `USAGE_TRANSITION_PREFIXES` from the SDK identify usage-limit text in results. Use them.

### 5.2 Chapter rendering (`prompt/chapter.ts`)

Send paragraphs numbered so the model can reference them. **Numbers start at 1** (Phase 5d), the same numbers the author sees in the rail beside each paragraph (7), so a comment that says "see paragraph 12" means the paragraph labelled 12:

```
<chapter file="Chapter 12" paragraphs="57">
[1] It was the third night of rain, and the river had began to climb the steps.

[2] "You should of told me," Mara said.
...
</chapter>
```

The app itself keeps 0-based indices everywhere (`Paragraph.index`, `Hunk.paragraph`, `ReviewComment.paragraph`). `paragraphNumber` and `paragraphIndexFromNumber` in `prompt/chapter.ts` are the only crossing between the two, and `fromPromptNumbering` converts a model's reply once, in the renderer, before `createAiReview` anchors it; a model that answers 0 anyway is clamped to the first paragraph. The system prompt tells the model the numbering and to cite paragraph numbers, never line numbers. Reviews record `generator.paragraphBase: 1`, which says what the numbers in `raw` count from; older model reviews, prompted from 0, have none. Their stored hunks and comments were always 0-based and display correctly; only the free text of an old comment ("see paragraph 37") still counts from 0.

Markdown is left exactly as written inside each paragraph; the paragraphs are joined by one blank line whatever separates them in the file. Frontmatter is omitted, and so is the line break after it where the body starts on the next line (`files.22`). `file` is the chapter's file name without its folder or extension (`chapterName`), as both providers pass it. The parser strips nothing on the way back because Claude returns quotes, not the chapter.

A paragraph lying wholly inside comments, code or maths is not shown to the model (`files.8`): `renderChapter` sends it as `[N] (author's note or code, hidden; skip it)` (`HIDDEN_PARAGRAPH`), so its text never leaves the app, and keeps its number, so the numbers after it still match the page and `paragraphs="..."` still counts it. `hiddenParagraphs` decides which, from the chapter's `syntaxSpans` read whole (`files.6`): a paragraph is hidden when every character of it but white space lies inside a `comment`, `code` or `math` span. So a `%%` note, an HTML comment, a fenced code block or a `$$` block alone in its paragraph is hidden, as is each paragraph of one that holds a blank line, and a paragraph of two notes; a paragraph with any prose beside them, such as `Rain %% Ellen %% fell.`, or with words after an unclosed opener, is sent as written (C.75). The system prompt quotes the hidden line and says to skip it (5.4).

### 5.3 Output schema (`prompt/schema.ts`)

```ts
export const ChangeSchema = z.object({
  paragraph: z.int().min(0), // each field also carries a .describe() line for the model
  before: z.string().min(1), // exact text copied from that paragraph; shortest span that is unique in the paragraph
  after: z.string(), // '' means delete
  category: z.enum(CHANGE_CATEGORIES),
  reason: z.string().max(240)
});
export const CommentSchema = z.object({
  paragraph: z.int().min(0).nullable(),
  quote: z.string().max(200).optional(),
  category: z.enum(COMMENT_CATEGORIES),
  text: z.string().max(1200)
});
export const ReviewOutputSchema = z.object({
  changes: z.array(ChangeSchema),
  comments: z.array(CommentSchema)
});
export const reviewOutputJsonSchema = z.toJSONSchema(ReviewOutputSchema, { target: 'draft-07' });
```

Keep it shallow. Claude Code is handed the draft-07 schema in its `initialize` request (11.3 q), as the SDK was before C.42, and retries on a mismatch; OpenAI gets the strict version (5.0). Either reply is checked again with `parseReviewOutput` (OpenAI's through `parseOpenAiText`).

### 5.4 System prompt (`prompt/system.ts`)

Static part written by us, then the contents of `GUIDELINES.md`. The static part states: you are a copyeditor for fiction; return only the structured output; `before` must be copied verbatim from the numbered paragraph, minimal but unique; never quote across paragraph boundaries; edits of more than about eight consecutive words are forbidden and must become comments; do not restate the chapter; if there is nothing to fix, return empty arrays. Since `files.8` it also states the Obsidian rule, whatever the guidelines file says, since a file made before `setup.10` has no such bullet: leave links, embeds, tags, block IDs, footnote and callout markers, comments, code, maths, web addresses and HTML exactly as written, each with an example of how it looks, a footnote and a callout by their markers alone, as 11.3 (k) protects them (`[^1]`, the `[^1]:` that starts a footnote's line, the `^[` and `]` of an inline footnote, a callout's `> [!note]` and the `>` before each of its lines); the words a reader sees are prose and may be corrected, and only those words changed: the alias after the `|` in `[[Page|alias]]`, the text of `[text](url)`, the words of a footnote or an inline footnote, and a callout's title and body; `%%` and HTML comments are the author's private notes, neither corrected nor commented on; words in angle brackets that are not an HTML tag, such as `<Where are you?>`, are prose, often dialogue; never add, remove or change one of the guard's markup characters, nor let one change alter words on both sides of one, as the app sets such a change aside, so change only words and ordinary punctuation and give each place its own change, while quoting those characters unchanged around the words changed is fine (11.3 k: the guard reads a change trimmed to the words it alters); and a paragraph shown as the hidden line (5.2) is to get no change and no comment (C.75). The guidelines file (see `resources/GUIDELINES.default.md`) carries the author-editable rules and style sheet. The same system prompt string for every chapter lets the providers' automatic prompt caching apply (`buildSystemPrompt`; the SDK's until C.42, Claude Code's since).

### 5.5 The review dialog

Each provider's item in the toolbar's Review menu (`codex.3`; With AI from `polish.7`, and before that a button of its own, "Review with AI") opens a modal, Review with AI, rather than firing a request, because a review costs real money and minutes and the settings that shape it were sitting in the toolbar all day for a decision made a few times a day. The dialog asks, in one place:

- **Provider**, a select backed by `Settings.provider`: "Claude" or "ChatGPT" (`codex.3`), the Review menu's item choosing it as the dialog opens (Claude's label was "Claude (subscription)" until `opensource.6`). A third, "OpenAI (API key, experimental)", with its grey note on what experimental meant (`hardening.11`, C.83), its **API key** row with Open Settings, its line on billing per token and the card with Open Settings for a missing key, went with that provider in `codex.6`. The Claude Setup screen only stands in front of the dialog when Claude is the provider. Choosing ChatGPT swaps in its model list and adds one row to Claude's, **Account** (`chatGptAccountLine`), with Open Setup only while there is no sign-in, as high as the other rows with the button or without (`modal__row--account`; it closes the dialog for the ChatGPT view, and leaving the view opens the dialog again, 5.6 item 5, `setup.19`), and, before the first ChatGPT review, the training warning with its box under it; Start review waits for a sign-in and the box (5.8). Nothing else of ChatGPT's own stands in the dialog since `codex.5` (the author, 2026-10-24: "make the ChatGPT one minimal like the Claude one", keeping "the warning about data privacy"): OpenAI's "Using ChatGPT plan" with Manage usage, the note under Effort on the reasoning effort sent and, in a development run, the runtime's "Using a development endpoint" line went then (C.116); "Using ChatGPT plan" with Manage usage stands on the ChatGPT view's status card instead (5.7 item 6, since the `codex.5` review).
- **Model** and **Effort**, persisted on change. The model select writes `model` or `chatgptModel` depending on the provider. A model list that could not be fetched is not kept as an empty one (`codex.3` review; until then one failure, offline or a server error, left "no models" for the rest of the run, with Start review disabled and nothing said): under the Model row an orange box (`role="alert"`) says whose list could not be listed, then main's words for why (`modelListFailedText` in `src/shared/ui/models.ts`, as "The models on your ChatGPT plan could not be listed. Could not reach OpenAI to list the models of your ChatGPT plan. ..."), with **Try again**, held while the list is asked for again, after which a focus left on it goes to the Model select. The dialog asks once more as an opening first shows that provider, and never on every draw (`retryModels` in `useAi`, which keeps main's words in `modelsError` until an answer comes). While no model is chosen and none is listed, the line beside Start says "The review cannot start until a model is listed." (`NO_MODEL_BLOCKER`); a model the author chose still starts. A ChatGPT list that came back empty says "Your ChatGPT sign-in lists no model Lapidary can review with." in the same box, with Try again (`CHATGPT_EMPTY_MODEL_LIST`).
- **Guidelines**, the effective path with **Open** and **Open folder** (`polish.3`, in place of `setup.10b`'s Open in Obsidian and Open; C.101). Open asks main to open the file in the system's app for its type (`guidelines:open`, which the page sends nothing; section 10), and Open folder to show it in its folder (`shell:reveal` with `guidelines`); each creates the file from the template first when it is missing. Under it, while the style sheet is still empty, an orange note: "Your style sheet is still empty: spelling variant, character names, invented words. Without it the reviewer may "fix" them." (`styleSheetNote` in `src/shared/ui/guidelines.ts`: `blank`, or a file the review has still to create from the template). The dialog reads `guidelines:status` as it opens, after Open or Open folder and whenever the window gets the focus back, so the note goes once the author fills the style sheet in and returns (`setup.10b`).
- **Chapter stats**: paragraphs and words, from `chapterStats` in `src/shared/text/stats.ts`, so the size of the job is visible before it is paid for. Under them, for a long chapter (`reviewSizeAdvice`, same file, `files.10`): from 12,000 words a grey note, "A long chapter. The review may take several minutes, and uses more of your plan's limits or your API credit than a short one."; from 40,000 an orange box (`role="note"`), "A very long chapter. The model may reach its output limit before it has written every suggestion; the review then fails, and what it used still counts. A lower effort leaves more room for the reply, and shorter files are safer." Both thresholds count, as the line does, the body's words, never the frontmatter, and are the same for either provider. A review that does run out of room says so in `replyLimitMessage`'s words (5.0, C.77).
- **The previous review**, if there is one: when it was made, how many suggestions it holds, how many are still pending (both counted from the page when it is the review on screen, as History counts it: `historyCounts`, 6.4, `apply.5`), and a sentence saying that a new review replaces the working set while the old one stays in History.
- **Start review** and **Cancel**. Escape cancels. Under them, the dialog's last line is the caution that goes with every review, `AI_OUTPUT_NOTICE` from `src/shared/branding.ts`: "Suggestions and comments come from an AI model and can be wrong or misleading. Check each one, and verify any factual claim, before you accept it." (`release.9`).
- **No stranded decisions** (`apply.20`). A new review replaces the working set, and the model reads the chapter file, so changes on the page that the file does not have yet (`unsavedDecisionCount`) would stay behind in the old review, out of sight in History, and the dot in the chapter list, which follows the review the chapter opens with, would go. With such changes the dialog says so ("2 changes are not saved to the chapter yet. The review reads the chapter file, so save them first to have them included.", `reviewStartNote`) and its buttons are Cancel, "Review without them" and the blue "Save 2 changes, then review" (`reviewStartLabels`, singular "Save 1 change, then review" and "Review without it"); with none they are Cancel and "Start review", as before. The blue button runs Save to chapter (6.3) and starts the review only on `saved` or `nothing-to-save`, so the review on screen then stands on the bytes just written and the review is made from the saved text; a save that is cancelled, blocked or fails starts nothing and leaves the dialog open, and a dialog closed while the save runs starts nothing (`saveThenReview` in `src/renderer/state/reviewStart.ts`). The save's cards sit in the corner of the manuscript pane, under the dialog's backdrop, where they can be neither read nor closed, so the dialog says why itself: the warning gives way to a red box (`role="alert"`) that reads "The review has not started, because the changes were not saved." and then the text of every card the save put up, in order (`notSavedLines` in `src/shared/ui/save.ts`, handed over by `onNotSaved`); after Cancel to applying paragraph boxes, which the author answered, it adds nothing. The box goes when the blue button is pressed again, and the cards stay behind for when the dialog has closed (`apply.20` review). "Review without them" asks first, "Review without saving?" with Cancel focused (`reviewWithoutPrompt`): the review will not see them and may suggest some again, and they stay in the review from <date> (History's date), which the chapter stops opening with once the new review comes back, so it is reopened from History to save them. Both buttons are disabled while a save runs and when Start would be. The review reads the provider, model and effort when it starts, after the save, not when the button was pressed.

While a review runs, the toolbar shows its progress label and Cancel before the Review menu, whose providers' items are disabled until it ends (`polish.7`, `codex.3`).

### 5.6 Claude's setup: the check, the Setup screen and the ways to it

How the app finds out whether Claude can review, says so, and tells the author what to do about it, without ever signing anyone in itself (`setup.2` to `setup.9`, `setup.11`; the tables are in 11.3 f, the shapes in section 3, and what Anthropic's pages say about each step in Appendix A, re-read for `setup.13`). The pure parts are `src/shared/ai/claudeStatus.ts`, `src/shared/ui/setup.ts` and `src/shared/ui/usage.ts`; the screen is `src/renderer/components/SetupScreen.tsx`.

1. **Binary.** The app runs the user's own Claude Code; nothing of Anthropic's ships (C.42). `src/main/providers/claudeBinary.ts` (`setup.3`) looks, in order, where Anthropic's installer puts it (`%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe` on Windows, `~/.local/bin/claude` elsewhere), in each `PATH` folder, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` on macOS or `/usr/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` on Linux. On Windows only `claude.exe` counts, never npm's `claude.cmd` shim, which cannot run without a shell, so a copy installed only with npm reads as not installed (the npm package now carries the same native binary, but inside its package folder, which is not on PATH: setup page, re-read 2026-10-19). Development and packaged builds look the same way. Troubleshoot-install says an older Claude Desktop can put a `Claude.exe` in the `WindowsApps` folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`) ahead of Claude Code on PATH (on this machine the folder comes before WinGet's `Links`, where a WinGet copy is found), and Windows matches `claude.exe` to `Claude.exe` (Appendix A, 2026-10-19). The lookup never takes such an alias, on two counts (`setup.17`). `claudeCandidates` leaves out every PATH folder that ends in `Microsoft\WindowsApps` (`isWindowsAppsDir`), on Windows only. And the entries in that folder are App Execution Aliases, reparse points that `fs.stat` refuses with EACCES, so `canRun` says no to them anyway (measured by the `setup.13` review on 2026-10-19 on this machine's `winget.exe`, `python.exe` and the current Claude Desktop's `claude-desktop.exe` aliases, under Node 24.21.0 and under Electron 44.3.0's own Node 24.20.0; this machine has no older Desktop's `Claude.exe` to try). Leaving the folder out costs nothing, since `canRun` already passed over everything in it, and it means that a Node or Electron whose `fs.stat` followed an alias still could not find Claude Desktop there and run it with `--version` (`fs.access` already succeeds on an alias, measured 2026-10-19). `test/main/claudeBinary.test.ts` pins both: the folder left out of the candidates however PATH spells it, and, on Windows, `canRun` false for every alias in this machine's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps` (every `.exe` there that is not a folder, 50 here, each only stat'ed, never run; Node lists them as symbolic links, but the test does not ask for that, so a Node that listed them as plain files would still test them rather than skip; skipped where the folder holds no `.exe`) and no candidate in that folder on this machine's own PATH. A terminal does run the alias when it comes first on PATH, so there `claude` may start Claude Desktop, and the full-path form is the way round it, as Troubleshooting says (item 5). The same module is the only one in `src` that imports `child_process`, and its `runClaudeCli` runs nothing but `--version` and `auth status --json`, without a shell or a window.
2. **The check.** On every launch, on Check again, and as the window comes back to the front (item 6), `src/main/providers/claudeRuntime.ts` asks three things side by side and sends no prompt, so it uses none of the plan: `--version`, `auth status --json` and the `initialize` exchange (`setup.4`, C.46; until then a one-word prompt was sent). The one request Setup ever sends is Test the connection (item 5), and only when it is pressed. `classifyClaude` reads the answers into `ready` (with the credential: a Claude plan, an API key, a cloud provider or the bearer token in `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, which outranks an API key and the sign-in but not a cloud provider (C.71), and a warning for the free plan), `missing-binary`, `not-signed-in`, or `error`: a check that failed or ran out of time, or a Claude Code older than `MIN_CLAUDE_CODE`. Nothing is cached across launches. A review that fails says why through `classifyClaudeFailure` (`setup.5`, C.47), and the last failure that bears on setup is kept beside the check (`nextLastFailure`).
3. **Views.** `setupView` reads the two into one of nine: checking (no answer yet), not installed, signed out, sign-in ended, could not check, out of date, usage limit, ready with an API key, and ready, in the order 11.3 (f) gives. The status bar names it (`runtimeLabel`), and so does the Setup screen's status card (`setupStatus`).
4. **The ways to Setup** (`setup.7`).
   - **The launch card.** Once the settings and the first check are in, and Claude is the provider and neither Setup nor the welcome guide is open, a view with something to do (not installed, signed out, sign-in ended, could not check, out of date) puts up a card under the key `claude-runtime` that says so in a line (`runtimeCard`), with Open Setup. While it is up, later checks keep its words current; a check that leaves nothing to do withdraws it by its key, and so does opening Setup, which says the same at length, and the welcome guide showing, whose first step does (section 7, Notification cards; `setup.11`). Closed with its X, it stays closed: only the first check of the run may put it up. With another provider there is no card, and switching to it, in the review dialog's Provider list or the Review menu, withdraws one that is up; switching back does not bring it back (OpenAI's API key was that provider until `codex.6`, ChatGPT since `codex.3`). One pure rule decides all of this after every check, `runtimeCardAction` (raise, update, withdraw or nothing; `setup.7` review).
   - **The status bar.** The provider's readiness on the right of the status bar is a button: Setup for Claude, its ChatGPT view for ChatGPT (`codex.3`), its tooltip "Open Setup" (`RUNTIME_BUTTON_TITLE`); it opened Settings for OpenAI's API key until `codex.6`, when `runtimeButtonTitle` said which.
   - **Settings.** The Claude account row has Setup, as before.
   - **The welcome guide.** Its first step, Connect Claude, has Set up Claude, which opens Setup over the guide; Setup's Done, Close or Escape goes back to it, the focus on Set up Claude (section 7, `setup.11`, `setup.19`, item 5).
   - **Claude**, in the toolbar's Review menu (`codex.3`; until then With AI with Claude as the provider, `polish.7`), opens Setup in place of the dialog only when Claude Code is missing or definitely signed out (`reviewGate`). A check that failed or ran out of time, a Claude Code too old for the app, or a sign-in or usage failure that the last review reported and the check no longer finds, opens the dialog with a warning in a line and Open Setup beside it (`reviewDialogWarning`), since the review may still go through and says why if it does not. That Open Setup closes the dialog for Setup, and leaving Setup opens the dialog again (item 5, `setup.19`). Before the first check has answered, the dialog opens, its model list loading. The dialog can still be open when a check finds Claude Code missing or signed out: the first check answering, its Provider list switched to Claude, its Check again or the window coming back to the front. The warning then says what that check found, "Claude Code is not installed, so this review cannot run yet.", "Claude Code is not signed in, so this review cannot run yet." or, after a review said the sign-in had ended, "Your Claude sign-in has ended, so this review cannot run until you sign in again.", never what the last review said (`setup.7` review). Start review stays enabled: a review that then fails opens Setup, as below, and a check that is out of date by then does no harm.
   - **A review that fails** because Claude Code is missing, too old, not signed in or its sign-in has ended checks again and opens Setup (`setup.5`), its card showing over it.
   - **A review that stops at a usage limit** opens nothing: its card gives Claude Code's own words, which name the limit and when it resets, then what to do (`usageLimitCard` in `src/shared/ui/usage.ts`, `setup.9`). The advice is only for one of the plan's limits (`isPlanLimit`, `setup.9` review): the last usage notice says a plan limit was reached, or Claude Code's words name one ("You've hit your session limit", "weekly limit", "Opus limit", "Sonnet limit" or "Fable limit", or "You've hit your limit" alone); not when the notice says extra usage was paying or was itself the limit reached, nor when Claude Code's words already say to switch model. Any other usage limit, such as a team's shared budget, a spend limit, usage credits with no plan limit reached, or a seat without usage, keeps Claude Code's words alone, which say which limit and what to do about it. When a plan limit and the extra usage behind it run out together, Claude Code's words give the plan's reset ("You're out of usage credits · resets 3pm") and the notice names the plan's limit, so the advice is given. The advice comes from the notice, which says which limit was reached, on the plan the check found: for a limit that holds one model, the weekly Opus, Sonnet or model limit, the models it leaves free, "Sonnet and Haiku do not count against the weekly Opus limit: choose one under Model in Review with AI to go on now, or wait until the limit resets.", and for the weekly model limit, which Claude Code names after its model ("Fable limit"), "Other models do not count against this weekly model limit: choose another under Model in Review with AI to go on now, or wait until the limit resets."; for any other, "Wait until the limit resets, then try again. Sonnet and Haiku use your limits more slowly than Opus models (including Default), so choosing one under Model in Review with AI makes them last longer." (`usageLimitAdvice`). On a Pro or Enterprise plan Claude Code counts the weekly Sonnet limit as the account's weekly limit and says "You've hit your weekly limit", so there the app names it and advises on it as the weekly limit (C.64). The notice is read from `useAi`'s `latestRateLimit`, kept as each notice arrives, since the page may not have drawn the one that came just before the failure (C.64). The status bar then says "Claude: usage limit reached" and, in its usage notice, which limit and when it resets (section 7). Setup's usage-limit view says what the card said: `useAi` records the failure with the card's decision, from the same message and notice (`failureSetupEvent`, `LastFailure.planLimit`), so for one of the plan's limits Setup gives the same advice under its text, and for any other it says the limit is not one of the plan's, with no advice; the review dialog's warning follows it.
5. **The screen.** It takes the place of the chapter list, the prose and the side panel; the toolbar and the status bar stay, the notification cards sit at the top of its column, before it in the flow, so that they never cover its Close or Check again and stay in view as it scrolls (section 7), and the dialogs, Settings among them, and the close question open over it as over the main view, the page inert under them. The screen scrolls across the window's whole width under the cards, its page a centred column 720 CSS px wide at most, so the wheel scrolls it over the margins too and its scrollbar is at the window's edge (`.setup` and `.setup__page`; `setup.7` review: the column alone scrolled, and the cards came after it, at its foot). The suggestion editor is not drawn while Setup is open, but its words are kept for when Setup closes (7.4). From the top:
   - "Set up Claude", with Close. Escape leaves as Close does (`setup.19`; until then it did nothing here, as in the dialogs that have no Cancel of their own), unless something over the screen takes it first: a dialog, which closes on it or, for New chapter and Submit manual review, ignores it, a question, Restart now's overlay, or a toolbar menu or the status bar's legend, which close on it (`setupTakesEscape` in `src/shared/ui/setup.ts`, `useSetupEscape` in `src/renderer/state/setupEscape.ts`, a window listener in the bubble phase, after the dialogs' and the question's in the capture phase).
   - **The status card**: the view in a few words, what the check found (the version, the account and plan when ready, the source of an API key or the `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in use and how to use the plan instead (C.71), the check's own words when it failed, the free-plan warning; in the usage-limit view, what to do about the limit, from the last usage notice, as the review's card says it: `usageLimitAdvice`, item 4, `setup.9`; for a usage limit that is not one of the plan's, which the card gives no advice for, "The last review stopped at a usage limit that is not one of your Claude plan's own limits, such as usage credits, a spend limit or a team's shared budget. Claude Code's message said which. Nothing here needs setting up." in place of the plan's text, with no advice: `LastFailure.planLimit`, `setup.9` review), with its state's colour at its edge, Check again (blue while there is something to do, "Checking…" while a check runs, and held rather than disabled while it does, so that pressed from the keyboard it keeps the focus: `heldButton`, below), Test the connection (below) and, with a chapter open where the dialog would open anyway (`canTryReviewAnyway`), Try the review anyway, which closes Setup and opens the dialog.
   - **Test the connection** (`setup.8`) sends one very small request through the same Claude Code, flags, environment and folder as a review (Haiku, one turn, the system prompt "Reply with the single word OK.", no schema; `runCliTest`), so it goes through wherever a review would and fails wherever one would. It sits in the status card after Check again wherever Claude Code has been found and the check has not said for certain that it is signed out (`canTestConnection`: a ready check, the ended sign-in that only a test or a review clears, and a check that failed, where the test can say more); not before the first check, for a missing Claude Code or a definite "signed out", where the steps say what to do. Under the buttons, across the card, a note on what the request costs, in the terms the card itself uses for what Claude Code signs in with (`connectionTestNote`, `setup.8` review): on a Claude plan the task's "Sends one very small request to Claude, which counts against your plan like any other."; with an API key "Sends one very small request to Claude, which is billed to your API key like any other.", since the card says a few lines higher that reviews are billed to the key "not to a Claude plan"; through a cloud provider "Sends one very small request to Claude, which is billed through your cloud provider like any other."; with the token "Sends one very small request to Claude, which is billed to the account behind your ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN like any other." (C.71); and where the check failed and so did not say, "Sends one very small request to Claude, which counts against your plan or API key like any other." Then one line: while the test runs "Testing: waiting for Claude to answer…", with the button held but keeping its label, so the buttons keep their width and the card's text does not reflow. Held, not disabled (`heldButton` in `src/renderer/state/heldButton.ts`, for Check again too): the button is `aria-disabled`, drawn as a disabled one, and has no click handler, so a click, Space or Enter does nothing until the work ends, but it keeps the keyboard focus, which Chromium takes from a focused button that becomes `disabled` and leaves on the page, so a keyboard or screen-reader user had to Tab in again from the top of the window (`setup.8` review); then how it went, "Claude answered the test at 18:35:37, in 1.7 s (claude-haiku-5-5)." in `--accept` or "The test at 18:35:37 did not go through: <the reason, as a review would give it>" in `--danger` (`connectionTestLine`), kept for the rest of the run and shown again when Setup opens again. The card is the live region, so the line is read out. A test that went through clears the last failure, as a review that went through does, and one that did not is remembered as a review's failure is (`testSetupEvent`, `nextLastFailure`'s `success` and `failure`); one that fails for a reason Setup can fix (missing, too old, not signed in, sign-in ended) checks again, as such a review does. Its rate-limit notice goes to the status bar, as a review's does. The test stops after 60 s, from the app's side (`testConnection`), with "Claude did not answer within 60 seconds, so the test was stopped. Try again in a minute."; quitting ends it as it ends a review. The signed-out and sign-in-ended views with a ready check say "test the connection or try the review: this clears once either goes through" (`SIGNED_IN_AGAIN`).
   - **The out-of-date note** of the review dialog (`setup.6`): a Claude Code older than `RECOMMENDED_CLAUDE_CODE` may not offer the newest models, with `claude update` and, on this machine's own tab, its full-path form. It shows here in every view but out of date, whose steps are the update, and not installed; the review dialog keeps it, from the same `UpdateNote`, below its model list.
   - **Steps** for the view (`setupSteps`), under a heading, on the system chosen in three tabs, Windows, macOS and Linux, the user agent's preselected: open a terminal (`openTerminalHint`), run one command, come back. Not installed: the one line that installs Claude Code and signs in through the path it installs to (`installAndLoginCommand`), since that is the first run for most people; through the full path, because Anthropic's installer does not add its folder to PATH itself, only says how in its output when the folder is missing (troubleshoot-install, re-read 2026-10-19, Appendix A), and a terminal opened before the install would not see it anyway. Signed out and sign-in ended: `claude auth login`. Out of date: `claude update`. Each command has a Copy, and the sign-in and update commands have their full-path form under them whenever the path is known, for a terminal that does not find `claude` (the terminal's PATH need not be the app's), on the tab of the system this machine runs only (`pathForTab`, the user agent's system): the path is this machine's, and on another system's tab it would be quoted in that system's syntax, such as a Windows path quoted for a Mac terminal, which runs nowhere (`setup.7` review). Not installed also lists other ways to install that put `claude.exe` or `claude` where the app looks: WinGet on Windows and Homebrew on macOS, which do not sign in, so `claude auth login` follows them. npm is not offered: on Windows its `claude.cmd` reads as not installed (item 1), and Troubleshooting says so.
   - **Copy** puts the command on the clipboard and says "Copied"; a copy the clipboard refuses says "Copy failed" and, under the command, "Could not copy. Select the command and copy it yourself." A click on a command selects all of it, and a long one wraps rather than scrolling.
   - **Troubleshooting** for the view and the tab (`setupTroubleshooting(view, runtime, os, host)`), each question opening on its answer: the terminal does not recognise `claude`; on the Windows tab, the terminal starts Claude Desktop instead of Claude Code; no browser window opened; signed in, yet the app says not signed in (its Claude Code runs without the user's Claude Code settings, so a sign-in kept there does not reach it, 11.3 c); which plans work, and the API key in their place; installed with npm (Windows); `claude update` refusing a copy a package manager installed; a check that keeps failing. The two terminal answers follow the steps (`setup.17`). Where the steps show a full-path form (signed out, sign-in ended and out of date, on this machine's tab once the path is known, `pathForTab`), they lead with it: "Use the full-path form of the command, shown under it: it names the Claude Code that <APP_NAME> found, so the terminal does not have to find claude by name.", then that a new terminal helps only once Claude Code's folder is on PATH, which Anthropic's installer does not arrange. Where the steps show none, the answers never point at one. On another system's tab they name the folder the installer uses there (`%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`, `~/.local/bin`) and the view's command run from it, such as `~/.local/bin/claude auth login` (`installerPathCommand`, from which the install line is built too), and say that a WinGet or Homebrew copy is found by name in a terminal opened after the install. In the not-installed view, whose install line signs in through the full path already, they say that line needs no PATH, and that a terminal opened before a WinGet or Homebrew install may not see where it put Claude Code, so open a new one for `claude auth login` (on Linux, which offers no other install, how to put `~/.local/bin` on PATH). The Claude Desktop answer says an older Desktop can put a `Claude.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`, which a terminal runs for `claude` when that folder comes first on PATH (item 1), then the way round it: the full-path form shown under the command, the installer's path on another system's tab, and, not installed, the install line, even after a WinGet install. `test/shared/setup.test.ts` walks every view, tab and host: an answer says "shown under it" exactly where the steps show a full-path form. Against Anthropic's pages as re-read on 2026-10-19 (Appendix A): the browser answer matches what `claude auth login` does, printing the link and reading a pasted code; the plans answer matches the setup page (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise or Console; not the free plan); WinGet and Homebrew copies do not update themselves, as the update answer assumes. Until `setup.17` the first answer told everyone to close the terminal and open a new one, which helps only once the installer's folder is on PATH, and then to use a full-path form that the not-installed view and another system's tab do not show (the `setup.7` review saw the second gap).
   - **Advanced**, folded: the Claude Code found and its version, the versions needed, what it signs in with, when it was last checked, and where the app looks (`advancedRows`).
   - **Copy diagnostics** (`hardening.5`): a line of its own above the privacy footer, "Copy diagnostics puts <APP_NAME>'s versions, its settings and what its last checks found on the clipboard, for a message or a GitHub issue when something goes wrong. It holds no chapter text, email address or key.", whose first two words are a link-styled button (`data-opens="diagnostics"`) that opens Diagnostics (section 7) and copies the report as soon as main has made it; the report runs no check (Appendix C "What Copy diagnostics holds"). Drawn whenever the page gives Setup the way to the dialog, which App always does.
   - **Done** (`setup.19`, the author, 2026-10-24: "there is no \"Ok\" button other than \"Close\" at the top"): the blue button at the foot, on the right as the welcome guide's Start is, after Copy diagnostics and before the privacy footer (`.setup__foot`, `SETUP_DONE`), leaving as Close and Escape do. Close stays at the top. Once a check finds Claude ready after the view had something for the author to do, as when the focus re-check (item 6) finds the sign-in made in a terminal, the focus goes to Done (`claudeSetupSucceeded`: a view `needsSetup` names, then ready or ready with an API key; not the first check, from checking, nor a usage limit that has reset). The page keeps still while Done is wholly in view, so the status card that says so stays where it was; when Done is below the fold, as under the long steps, in a short window or at a large zoom, the page comes up just far enough to show it, Done's foot the app's 24 px above the page's (`focusInView` in `src/renderer/state/scroll.ts`, with `scrollRectIntoView`'s `if-needed`, the setup.19 review), so the focus never lands where the author cannot see it. ChatGPT's Done after a sign-in does the same (5.7 item 6).
   - **Leaving** (`setup.19`, the author: "it does not bring you back to where you were before"). Done, Close and Escape go back to where Setup was opened from, on both views (`setupLeave`, applied by the store's `leaveSetup`; `openSetupScreen` notes the view and where from as Setup opens, in place of Review with AI and Settings). Asked for again while it is open, from anywhere but Review with AI, as the status bar's label, Settings' Setup over it and the Review menu can, in the same view or the other, Setup keeps where it was first opened from, and App keeps where the focus was then (`showSetup` notes it only while Setup is closed), so a press that changes nothing on screen, or only the view, never loses the way back (the setup.19 review: the label pressed on a Setup that the dialog's Open Setup had opened sent Done to the chapter, and the guide's Set up buttons lost theirs the same way). Open Setup in a Review with AI that the Review menu opened over Setup is the one way in that replaces it, since that dialog is where the author has just been. Open Setup in Review with AI, beside Claude's warning or on ChatGPT's account row (5.5): the dialog opens again as it was, its provider, model and effort being settings, with the focus on its Start (the blue button, which reads "Save N changes, then review" with changes not saved), as soon as Start can be pressed; with ChatGPT after a sign-in that is once the model list has come, the focus waiting on the dialog's box meanwhile, where any opening puts it, and staying wherever the author moves it (`focusStart`). Before the first ChatGPT review of an account Start waits for the data settings box (5.7 item 7), so the focus stays on the dialog's box, and ticking the box keeps it there. What the dialog held of its own, the red box of a save that did not reach the chapter and a training warning kept after its box was ticked, is not kept, as for any new opening. Only with a chapter still open and no review running, since the Review menu waits for a review too; and the Review menu opening the dialog over Setup forgets the dialog as the way in. The welcome guide's Set up Claude or Set up ChatGPT: the guide, under Setup all along, with the focus on that button, or on the step's button for the other view should the step show that one instead, as when the provider was changed in Settings over Setup (`welcomeLandingAction`, `landOn`).
