The rename puts the temp file, made at the save, in the chapter's place, and NTFS keeps the new file's own time: measured on 2026-10-19 on this machine's NTFS drive with Node 24.21.0, renaming a temp file made as `atomicWriteFile` makes it over a file 3 s and 20 s old gave the file the temp file's creation time both times. **Unverified:** Obsidian's created time and Dataview's `file.ctime` should then read as the time of the save, so that a vault sorted by created time moves a chapter after each save that changes it; this was not checked in Obsidian itself, as no agent run starts it (C.65), so since `opensource.11` the README says only what File Explorer shows and leaves Obsidian and Dataview out. Keeping the time (`files.15`, a two-step rename with recovery) is cut (Appendix D), and the README says that Save resets the file's creation date.
- **Changes made outside the app** (6.2, `files.5`, `files.21`). The watcher reloads the open chapter when its bytes are not ones the app loaded or wrote, rebases the review onto them (4.5) and says what moved in a card that each reload replaces and that counts the run of reloads, so Obsidian saving as the author types leaves one card. A chapter deleted, renamed or moved while open says so in a warning card, and opened again from the list it brings its reviews where they plainly are its own (below); a live rename is not followed (`files.18` cut). A folder another program holds at start-up is not watched until a list read works, and the list says so (`watchNotice`); once the watcher is ready, chapters changed meanwhile are reported (`catchUp`). The one race the app cannot prevent is the author typing in the same chapter in Obsidian while saving here: a write that comes just after Save's last check is seen only afterwards (6.3 step 4). **Unverified:** that Obsidian, saving what is typed a moment later, can write over a save was not seen in Obsidian, so since `opensource.11` the README says only that the app cannot stop another program writing the file a moment after its check and sees such a write only afterwards.
- **Reviews follow their chapter (11.3 g, `files.1`, C.45).** Reviews live outside the vault unless the author places the reviews folder inside it (`<userData>/reviews` by default), in a folder per chapter file name, and belong to the path in their `sourcePath`, so same-named chapters in two folders never share one. When nothing belongs to a chapter that opens, the reviews of a path whose file is gone are taken over if one of them is based on exactly the chapter's present bytes, as the app last read or saved them, and the text is at least 500 characters (a rename or move in Obsidian), or if the last two segments of the paths match (the vault moved, the file and its folder keeping their names), with an information card that names the old path. A chapter renamed or moved and also changed before the app opens it again, or one shorter than 500 characters, matches neither and opens with no review; its old reviews stay under the old name. Backups never follow a chapter (6.5).
- **Sync tools and git (`files.11`, C.78).** Conflict copies that Obsidian Sync, Dropbox and Syncthing name are listed with a "conflict copy" badge whose tooltip names the tool and the chapter copied; other tools' copies, OneDrive's and iCloud's among them, are listed as plain chapters. A chapter holding merge markers opens with a warning, and a save that finds the change on disk brought them stops before writing. Nothing is ever hidden, moved, merged or deleted.
- **What the app adds to the vault.** `GUIDELINES.md` once, from the template, never overwritten (`ensureGuidelinesFile`, section 10), or in its place the guidelines file Settings names, made the same way when it is missing, wherever it is; the chapters New chapter makes (`createChapter`, `wx`); the reviews, `.last-open.json` and the adoption journal only when the reviews folder is placed inside; and, while a save runs, its temp file beside the chapter, renamed over it or removed. Never backups, drafts, settings or logs, which stay in the app's data folder (11.3 p).
- **Not handled in 1.0.** Rendering Markdown or Obsidian syntax, Dataview or Templater, several chapters to a file (`files.14`), the creation time (`files.15`), a live rename of the open chapter (`files.18`), chapters reached through a symbolic link or junction (6.1). Not known: whether files a cloud sync tool keeps online only, OneDrive's Files On-Demand above all, are listed. They are reparse points, and libuv, under Node's `readdir`, may report every reparse point as a link, which the walk skips, so a vault in OneDrive with chapters freed up could show fewer chapters than it has, or none; not checked, as no agent run may use the author's OneDrive (`files.24`). Whether the links, callout, note, footnote and block ID of `samples/manuscript/Chapter 03 - Obsidian.md` still render in Obsidian after a Save is the author's check in sitting C (`files.9`).

## 7. UI specification (`src/renderer`)

Layout: left column file list, each chapter with the unsaved dot before its name while its file lacks some of its changes and a badge after it (a tick for a review with nothing pending, else the pending count), a sync tool's conflict copy with a "conflict copy" badge in `--badge-conflict-*` on a line under its name, so the name keeps the width any chapter's has, and the tick or count beside both (the `files.11` review), its tooltip naming the tool and the chapter copied (`files.11`, 6.1), and a header carrying a folder button and a "+" for a new chapter (the open chapter's dot and badge come from the review on screen, the others' from their current review as last written: `chapterListMarks`, `apply.5`); with no rows the list says why (`chapterListNotice` in `src/shared/ui/chapterList.ts`, `apply.25`): "No manuscript folder chosen yet." with Choose folder, "No .md or .txt files in that folder.", or, when the manuscript folder could not be read, main's words for it (6.1) in the text colour with Try again, which reads the folder again; while main is not watching the folder, as after a start the folder refused (6.2, `files.21`), "Lapidary is not watching the manuscript folder, so changes made outside Lapidary will not show until Try again succeeds." in the text colour (`watchNotice`), under main's words or the empty-folder line, or above the rows, with one Try again, 8 px above the rows when they show; center review pane with a comment gutter; right column with, at its very top, the review selector, then the focused suggestion in a box of fixed height (below, `ui.5`), the suggestions list, the comments under one heading (open, then unanchored, then resolved; One comments list, below, `ui.7`), stale/unanchored suggestions, and review history below (each review's provider or kind, its model, and its pending count when there is one; the row of the review on screen is highlighted and counts from the page, the others as last written: `historyCounts`, `apply.5`). The right column does not scroll as a whole: under the box, the suggestions list, its heading pinned and alone on its line (Show states sat beside it from `polish.12` until `polish.17`, and went under it in a narrow panel), takes what it needs up to about 55% of the height the box leaves and scrolls on its own, and everything below it scrolls as a second region, with a handle between the two that moves the line between them (The split, below; `ui.6`), so the box stays in view while j and k step through the list; when the focus moves, a row already in view stays where it is. In a window less than 540 CSS pixels high inside, which zoom changes and a chapter does not, the column scrolls as one instead, the box at its top and the list at its full length: the smallest window, 900 by 600, from 110% zoom, and the default 1440 by 940 from 175% (C.49). Show backups, which a footer under both regions held from `apply.11`, is in the toolbar's Actions menu since `polish.7` (6.5), so both regions, or the one scroller, reach the panel's foot. The category filter chips are in the toolbar's row, where the chapter's name was, before the buttons, after an eye that shows or hides them all (Toolbar order, below; `polish.10`, `polish.11`, C.98, C.107), so there is one bar at the top, and the chapter list, the prose and the side panel all start at its foot. A chip is its category's name and count, "punctuation 3", in the category's colour. The author's own edits (`source: 'manual'`, which the paragraph box makes) have a chip of their own, "You 3", last in the row whatever its count, in `--accent`, the colour of the YOU tag on their rows (`.cat-you`; since `polish.12` every row has its chip's tag, The suggestions list below); `other` counts only the rest, the model's `other` and a manual review's suggestions, which carry no category, so the two never share a suggestion (`chipKeyOf`, `chipCounts` in `src/shared/ui/chips.ts`). The review's comments have a chip too, "comments 2", after the categories and before You, counting the open comments, there while the review has any comment at all ("comments 0" once all are resolved), its words in `--ink-soft`, the colour of a margin card's head (`COMMENTS_CHIP`, `polish.13`, C.109). Its menu holds Hide or Show and Show only alone. Hiding it hides the margin's comment cards, whose column then gives its room back to the prose, and the side panel's comments under their heading, which keeps its count over "Hidden. The comments chip at the top shows them again." (`commentsNote`); the commented paragraphs' numbers lose the comment colour and the active comment's paragraph is no longer lit, so nothing on the page points at a comment that is not shown; and `n` does nothing (`nextComment`, `commentsHidden`). Show only on any other chip hides it, the eye and Actions' Hide all categories hide it with the rest, and Actions lists no Accept all or Dismiss all after it. A model's suggestion the author reworded (`edited`) stays under its category, as the change and its category are the model's. Hiding You hides the author's edits as hiding a category hides its suggestions: they leave the list, the margin and the position strip, and the line shows the text without them (`chipHidden` in each of them). A paragraph box that applies an edit shows the chip of what it applied, You for the edits it adds and a category for a suggestion it accepts because the author typed exactly that, and leaves every other chip as it was, so the author's words never vanish from the line as they land (`commitDraft`, the `polish.11` review). Each chip is a menu button (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`), named by its words, with no pressed state, which would make Chromium call it a toggle button; its tooltip, which is also its description, says whether it is shown: "Shown. Click for Hide, Show only, Accept all and Dismiss all." ("Hidden. Click for Show, ..."; You's starts "Your own edits."; `chipTitle`). A click anywhere on it, Enter, Space, the down or up arrow (as on the toolbar's menu buttons, so the arrows on a chip no longer move between suggestions), the keyboard's menu key or Shift+F10 (`contextMenuKey`), or a right-click opens its menu, named "punctuation suggestions" or "Your edits" ("Comments" for the comments' chip, which has the first two items alone): Hide, or Show on a hidden chip; Show only, which shows this chip and hides every other chip in the row (`showOnlyHidden`; a chip that comes later, as You does with a first edit, is shown); and under a line "Accept all 3" and "Dismiss all 3", the count the suggestions of the chip still pending, which each would move, greyed out at 0 with the note the question would give as its tooltip (`chipMenuLabels`, `bulkPlan`). The menu behaves as the toolbar's do (`useMenu`), opens on its first item (the up arrow on its last), gives the focus back to the chip, and goes when the row scrolls; a second click on the chip closes it. Actions lists Accept all and Dismiss all of the chip the focus was last on (Toolbar order, below). The eye is an icon button at the left of the row, an open eye while every chip in the row is shown and a closed one otherwise, named by what it does, "Hide all categories" or "Show all categories" (`eyeLabel`, `allChipsShown`), and Actions lists both. The chips are drawn at the size they had before `polish.10`, `polish.6`'s 13 px type with 2 by 8 px of padding and 6 px between them, and shrink only when they would not fit, in three steps, 12.5 px with 2 by 7, 12 px on a 16 px line with 1 by 6, both 5 px apart, down to `polish.10`'s compact size, 11.5 px on a 16 px line with 1 by 5 px, 4 px apart (`CHIP_STEPS`, `[data-chip-step]` in app.css). `chipsStep` picks the first, the largest, step at which they fit the row, from the row's width less its padding and each chip's width at every step, measured from a copy of the chips out of sight (`.chips__measure`, `aria-hidden`), so the choice never depends on the step drawn. The row is no taller than a toolbar button at any step, so the toolbar keeps its height, 42 CSS px at 100%. Only at the compact size do they overflow: in the default window at 100% with thirteen categories and You beside "Save 3 changes to chapter", or thirteen beside "Save 12 changes to chapter", where the eye's 34 px take them past the row (C.107); in the smallest window once there are more than six or seven categories; and zoomed in. They then scroll sideways and never wrap: by the wheel turned over it, up and down as well as sideways (`chipsWheelLeft` in `src/shared/ui/chips.ts`; Chromium did nothing with an up-and-down wheel there), by a translucent ‹ or › laid over each end that has chips out of sight, which pages the row by its width less 28 px at each end (`chipsEnds`, `chipsPageLeft`), and by Tab and Shift+Tab, which bring the whole of a chip they reach into view, 28 px from the row's edge, clear of the arrow there (`chipsRevealLeft`, `CHIPS_REVEAL_MARGIN`; Chromium brought in only a chip none of which showed, so one half cut off at the edge took the focus as it was). Only a focus the keyboard gave moves the row: a press on a chip half cut off leaves it where it is, so the release lands on the chip pressed (C.49). The row draws no scrollbar; while the chips overflow, a 2 px line under it, a thumb in `--ink-faint` on `--border`, shows where it stands (`chipsIndicator`). There are no chips behind the Setup screen and the welcome guide, which have no chapter text to filter. From `polish.10` to `polish.11` each chip was a toggle of its filter, drawn at the compact size alone, with its menu, Accept all and Dismiss all only, on a ▾ that showed under the pointer or the keyboard's focus, and You's edits were counted under other. From `polish.6` to `polish.10` the chips were a row of their own at the top of the centre column, with the browser's scrollbar under it while they overflowed (51 CSS px tall at 100% then, 36 when they fitted), and until `polish.6` a row across the whole window that wrapped, one to three rows at 100% in the smallest window (36, 65 and 94 CSS px) and six at 200% (184 px), and the chapter list and the side panel lost that height as well as the prose. Status bar: a "?" legend, pending/accepted/dismissed counts, the count not saved to the chapter ("3 not saved to chapter", in `--unsaved`, only when there is one), the time the review on screen was last written ("Decisions kept 14:02", 6.4; nothing for a chapter whose review has not been written), provider and model used ("ChatGPT · gpt-5.5", or "OpenAI (API key) · gpt-5-mini-..." for a review on the key `codex.6` took out), cost (with "estimate" when it is the app's own arithmetic, as on an OpenAI key's review), Claude's usage notice in `--warn` (`describeRateLimit` in `src/shared/ui/usage.ts`, `setup.9`, C.64: "5-hour limit 85% used, resets 15:45" from 80% of a limit, when Claude Code sends the share, which it does only while it warns itself (C.64), "Weekly Opus limit reached, resets Sat 09:00" once one is reached (the weekly Sonnet limit named as the weekly limit on Pro and Enterprise, as Claude Code names it), "Using extra usage (may be billed)" while extra usage pays, and nothing otherwise; a reset that is not today gives its day, "tomorrow 09:00", "Sat 09:00" or "29 Oct 09:00"; its tooltip says it in full with the time left, "85% of your Claude plan's 5-hour limit is used. It resets at 15:45, in 2 hours and 10 minutes." (`rateLimitTitle`); worded again every 30 s while it shows, so the time left keeps up and it goes once its limit resets; only while Claude is in use, the provider or Setup open), the active provider's readiness, a button that opens the Setup screen, Claude's view for Claude and ChatGPT's for ChatGPT (5.6, `setup.7`, `codex.3`; Settings for the OpenAI key until `codex.6`), and the zoom control. Its items never break in two; zoomed in, the bar wraps onto a second row instead. In a window narrow in CSS pixels, as zooming in makes it, the file list and the right column shrink and then fold to strips that open them as drawers (Narrow windows, below; `ui.3`).

**The window's title** (`polish.10`, C.98). The system's own title bar, with no frame of the app's, carries the open chapter's name: "Chapter 01 - The Flood — Lapidary", the file's name without its extension and the app's after an em dash; while the chapter file lacks some of the page's changes it leads with a dot, "• Chapter 01 - The Flood — Lapidary", so the taskbar shows it too. Pasted text is "Pasted text — Lapidary", with no dot, as it has no chapter file to save to, and with nothing open the title is "Lapidary" alone (`windowTitle` in `src/shared/ui/title.ts`). App sets it as `document.title`, which Electron gives the window, in every layout. The dot goes with Save to chapter's count, exactly when `saveButtonState` gives `dot`, and the chapter list keeps its orange dot before each such chapter. Until `polish.10` the toolbar began with the dot and the chapter's name, cut short with an ellipsis, and the window's title was "Lapidary" whatever was open.

**The Mode select** (`rr.2`, C.112). At the top right of the prose column, inside it and above the prose, on a strip of the page's own colour (`.modebar`, 33 CSS px tall at 100%), a select labelled "Mode" offers Main, Full edit and Preview, in that order (`MODES` in `src/shared/ui/modes.ts`, `ModeBar.tsx`), with the tooltip "Main reviews the suggestions. Full edit edits the whole chapter in one box. Preview shows the chapter as Royal Road will." (`MODE_TITLE`); the toolbar is as `polish.10` left it. It is there while a chapter is open, after the chapter list and its handle in the Tab order and before the find bar and the prose. Closed, it holds back the arrows, Home, End and the page keys, as the review selector does (`pickerHoldsKey`), so a key never switches the view at every press; a letter picks a mode by its first letter, and Alt+Down, F4 and Space open its list. A choice that lands in Main or Preview hands the focus back to the page, as the review selector's does, so in Main j, k, a and the arrows act at once (a focused select takes them as typing); Full edit's box takes the focus itself, and after Cancel in a question the focus stays on the select. The review keys (j, k, the arrows, a, u, d, e and n) are Main's (`reviewKeysActive`, `rr.2` review): Full edit and Preview show no suggestion, so in them none acts, and the arrows, Home, End and the page keys are the browser's, which scroll Preview's page once it has been clicked or reached with Tab. The mode is the window's and no setting keeps it: a chapter opens in Main, or in Full edit when the author left Full edit with something typed in it, which comes back as a paragraph box with typed text does (11.3 j); another review of the same chapter keeps Main or Preview (`viewMode` in the store, set back by `setReview` for another chapter) and does not open while Full edit is open (11.3 i), and Full edit is open exactly while its box is (`currentMode`, `WHOLE_DRAFT_KEY`), so Done, Cancel, a save that applies it and a change of chapter all leave Full edit with the box, into Main. The three modes draw in the one scroller (`.center`), and Main and Preview each keep their own place in the chapter (`useModePlaces` in `src/renderer/state/modePlaces.ts`, `modePlace`): back in either, the page is where the author left it, put back at once rather than animated, and held there while the page grows back to its height (`holdPlace`) until it gets there, the author scrolls or moves on, or 1.5 s pass; a mode not shown yet in the chapter starts at its top, and Full edit always does, as its box opens afresh with the caret at the top; another chapter forgets them all. Without it Main came back wherever Preview had been left. **Main** is the review page as it was. **Full edit** (7.4 item 4) is the whole chapter in one box the height of the column, in the prose's typeface at 17 px with a line height of 1.75 (`FullEdit.tsx`): the body as the page reads it, every decision applied (`fullEditText`), with no suggestion marks; above the box the frontmatter in Main's frontmatter block, not in the box and so not editable, as no paragraph box opens on it; under the box the paragraph box's hint ("Nothing changed yet. Esc closes.", "Ctrl+Enter applies, Esc cancels"), Cancel and Done. It takes the focus as it opens, with the caret at the top, and keeps the browser's own focus ring. Done, or Ctrl+Enter, applies it and goes back to Main with a card in the paragraph box's words ("Full edit: 4 changes added, already accepted; 2 suggestions your edit replaced moved to Unanchored.", `fullEditAppliedText`, `editSummary`); Cancel, or Escape, goes back to Main, first asking "Discard your changes in Full edit?" with Keep editing focused when something was typed (`discardFullEditPrompt`). While it is open every suggestion is frozen, as a paragraph box freezes its own: the rows fade, with the tooltip "Full edit is open", and their buttons are disabled; the review keys do nothing (above); the pencils say "Full edit is open. Finish it, or cancel it, to change this suggestion."; Actions' bulk items, Review with AI, Submit manual review and another review of the chapter from the review selector or History give "Finish or cancel Full edit first."; Ctrl+S from inside the box says "Full edit is still open. Press Done or Ctrl+Enter to apply it, then save."; Save to chapter from the toolbar asks "Apply Full edit first?" (and closes a Full edit with nothing typed, as it closes a paragraph box left as it opened), and when Full edit then cannot be applied it writes nothing and says "Nothing was saved. Resolve Full edit as the card above says, then save again.", where boxes have "Resolve the paragraphs above"; a paragraph box does not open ("Full edit is open, and holds every paragraph. Edit the words there, or finish Full edit first."). It does not open while a review of the chapter runs ("Wait for the review to finish, then open Full edit.") or a save is under way. **Preview** draws the HTML Export HTML gives (`toRoyalRoadHtml(composeReview(review))`, `rr.1`), so a pending suggestion counts as its original, read-only in the column (`PreviewPane.tsx`), read back through a list of the elements and attributes the converter writes into the page's own elements (`previewTree` in `src/shared/ui/preview.ts`), so nothing of the chapter's reaches the page as markup: a sheet in `--panel` with a `--border` frame, 760 CSS px wide at most, in the prose's serif at 17 px with a line height of 1.6, paragraphs 1.2em apart, the lines of a tight block (`rr-tight`, rr.1's `TIGHT_P`) with nothing between them, headings with 1.6em above and 0.6em below, a rule in `--border-strong`, a quote with a 4 px bar in `--border-strong` and its words in `--ink-soft`, lists and tables, a link in `--accent`, underlined, its address as its tooltip and no `href`, so nothing in the preview navigates, and a web image as its words in a dashed frame ("Image: the mill at dawn"), since the page fetches nothing from the web (its policy allows no image from the web anyway). Nothing of Royal Road's is fetched: the spacing is the author's own converter's preview, which he tuned to Royal Road's (C.112). The scroller is the one Main uses (`.center`), a Tab stop of its own as a scroller with nothing focusable in it. In a column 820 CSS px wide or more, the width from which Main shows its margin notes, Full edit's box and Preview's page keep Main's margin, 344 px, free on the right, where the notification cards stand, so a card does not cover their first lines; in a narrower column the cards stand over the text in every mode, as in Main (C.112). The find bar, the hover card, the margin notes, the position strip and the paragraph rail are Main's alone: leaving Main closes the find bar and the hover card, Ctrl+F does nothing in Full edit or Preview, and Edit text on a comment in Preview goes back to Main to open its paragraph. **Switching with something typed** asks, as leaving the chapter does (7.7; `chooseMode` in `src/renderer/state/modes.ts`, the questions in `src/shared/ui/modes.ts`): from a Full edit whose text changed, "Leave Full edit for Preview?" (or Main) with Cancel, Discard and Apply first, focused, which does what Done does; into Full edit over paragraph boxes whose text changed, "Apply the paragraph you are editing first?" with Cancel and Apply first, focused, since Full edit holds their paragraphs too (boxes left as they opened just close); from Main to Preview over such boxes, "Leave Main for Preview?" with Cancel, Keep for later, focused, which leaves them open in Main as they are while Preview shows the chapter without them, and Apply first. Leaving the chapter and closing the window count Full edit's box among the boxes whose text changed and say "What you typed in Full edit is kept as you left it and opens in Full edit again when you come back to this chapter." (`CloseGuardState.fullEdit`); it is kept on disk as a box is (11.3 j).

**The review selector** (`apply.26`). Above both regions, and above the one scroller too, so it never scrolls, a select lists the open chapter's reviews as History does, newest first by `createdAt`: History's date, the provider (or the kind, "manual" or "file", for a review no model wrote), the model, "N pending" when there are any, and, unlike History, "N not saved to chapter" when the review holds changes the chapter file does not have, in the status bar's words (`unsavedPhrase`), joined by " · " ("17/10/2026, 14:02:11 · Claude · claude-haiku-4-5 · 3 pending · 1 not saved to chapter"; `reviewChoiceLabel`), the review on screen selected and counted from the page as its History row is, the others as last written (`ReviewSummary.unsavedCount`). The unsaved count is there because the chapter list's dot, Save and the leave and close questions follow only the review on screen, and changing reviews asks nothing, so the selector is where changes left in another review show (6.4, `apply.26` review). Its accessible name is "Review shown", and its tooltip is the selected entry's label, which a narrow panel cuts off. When the review on screen is not the newest by `createdAt`, a warning mark stands before the select and its frame takes `--warn`; the mark's tooltip, spoken name and the select's description are "Not the newest review. The newest is from <date>." (`notNewestText`). Choosing another entry opens it as a History row does, with no question (7.7): the chapter opens with it from then on. A choice hands the focus back to the page (the select's `blur`), as a History row's click leaves it on a button, so j, k, a and the arrows act on the suggestions at once; a focused select takes them as typing (`isTypingTarget`). While its list is closed and no modifier is held, the select holds back the arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down (`pickerHoldsKey`), which on Windows change a closed select at once and so would open another review at every press, the arrows being review keys besides; Alt+Down, Alt+Up, F4 and Space still open the list, where the arrows only move the highlight until Enter or a click chooses. Type-ahead is left to the select: a digit typed into it, the start of a date, picks the next review whose date starts with it, once, and the focus then goes back to the page. The review on screen is listed even before History has it (a new review before its first write, or before History is read again), and History's entries of another chapter, still listed for a moment after a chapter opens, are left out. A chapter with no review shows a disabled select reading "No reviews yet". The pure part is `reviewPicker` in `src/shared/ui/history.ts`; the side panel draws it, and it fades and goes inert with the rest of the panel while a review of the chapter runs (7.6). The focused suggestion's box is directly under it (`ui.5`, below).

**The focused suggestion** (`ui.5`, `polish.8`). Directly under the review selector and above the list, the focused suggestion is a box of fixed height, 119 CSS px, that fits its heading line, which names the category (with the anchor when it is not exact) and ends in the pencil, Original and Suggested on a line each, and two lines of explanation. Until `polish.8` the category had a line of its own under the heading, 16 px and the 4 under it, in a box of 139 px (the author, 2026-10-22: "the focused section is a bit big in general"); the list, the handle and the region below share the 20 px it gave back. Each line in it has a line height of its own, so no font's metrics change the sum (`.side__focus` in app.css). A longer suggestion or explanation scrolls inside the box, below the heading line, which stays in view; each newly focused suggestion shows from its first line. Nothing below the box moves when the focus does: the list and the comments start at the same y whatever is focused. Until `ui.5` the details sat between the list and the comments, at the height of their text, so the comments region grew and shrank as the focus moved and often showed one or two comments (the author, with the `1c0877c` build on a 130-chapter manuscript). The heading line reads "Focused suggestion · punctuation": the heading in `--ink-faint`, the separator, the category in its own colour (`--cat`, as the list's dots show it), "your edit" for words the author wrote, in the colour of the category they came from, "change" for a suggestion with none, and the anchor after it in `--warn` when it is not exact ("Focused suggestion · word-choice ambiguous"); all of it uppercase at 11 px, as the panel's headings are. It ends in the pencil the list rows use, an icon button named "Edit suggestion" with the tooltip "Edit suggestion (e)", which opens the suggestion editor as `e` does; Tab goes from the selector to it and then to the list. Where the line is too narrow for all of it, the heading's words give way, to an ellipsis and then to nothing, and the category never shrinks, unless it is wider than the whole line by itself, when it ends in an ellipsis at the line's end (`.side__focus-title` and `.side__focus-cat`; C.102). The heading's accessible name is the whole line, "FOCUSED SUGGESTION · PUNCTUATION" as Chromium gives it, with the case `text-transform` sets, whatever is cut on screen. When the box has more text than it shows, its scrolling part is a Tab stop of its own between the pencil and the list, as Chromium makes every scroller with nothing focusable in it, so a keyboard user can reach the rest; there the arrows scroll it, as do Space, Shift+Space, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End, and `j` and `k` still step through the list (`arrowsScrollBox` in `src/shared/ui/scroll.ts`, asked by keyboard.ts before the review keys). The arrows were review keys there at first and moved the focus to the next suggestion, which also sent the box back to its top, so only Space scrolled it (`ui.5` review). A click in the box does not focus it, and a box that shows its whole text is no Tab stop, so the arrows step through the list from everywhere else as before. With nothing focused the heading line reads "Focused suggestion" alone, there is no pencil, and the box keeps its height and says "Press j or click a row to focus a suggestion. Shift+J goes to the next pending one.", two lines in the default window and three in the narrower panels measured, 211 to 240 px wide, which the body's 80 px hold without scrolling. Until `polish.8` the category kept its own line because on the heading line it would cut the heading or itself short in a narrow panel; the author asked for the one line, and the heading's words are what give way. The pencil is enabled while the suggestion's paragraph is open for editing, as the Edit button was, and a card says why nothing opens (7.4). In the short window's one scroller the box is the first thing, at the same height, and scrolls away with the list: pinned above it, it would leave the default window at 200% 63 of the scroller's 202 px, and a box that grew with its text would move the list under the pointer at a click; so there a long explanation's scrollbar is the one scroller inside another the panel has, beside the panel's own. The price is height: the list and the region below share what the box leaves, so in the smallest window at 100% the list's cap falls from 191 to 115 px (about three and a half rows) and the comments region has 94 px in view at all times, where the details used to take most of its 157 (as measured for `ui.5`, with the chips above the panel and the footer under it); `ui.6`'s split lets the author move the line between the two (below). The author judges, now that `polish.6` and `polish.7` have given the panel the chips' row and the footer, whether it is roomy enough; if not, the next step would be a box with one line of explanation, recorded by `polish.8` and not built.

**The split** (`ui.6`). Between the list and the region below, where a line divided them, a handle 7 CSS px tall with a grip at its middle moves that line up or down, so that once the suggestions are dealt with the comments can take most of the panel (the author, 2026-10-17). It is a control of its own: a focusable `role="separator"` named "Split between suggestions and comments", its value the list's share of the height in per cent ("Suggestions 23% of the height"), its tooltip "Drag to give the suggestions or the comments more room. Double-click it, or press Enter, for the usual split.", with the row-resize pointer, which keeps its shape over whatever a drag crosses (`.splitting` on the root while it lasts), and a focus ring in `--accent` drawn inside its band, where neither region covers it. The grip is in `--ink-faint`, which has 3:1 on the panel in both themes, and darkens under the pointer. A drag follows the pointer with the pointer captured; a press on the handle does not take the focus, as a click in the focused suggestion's box does not, so the arrows go on stepping through the list after a drag. Tab reaches it after the list's last row, wherever it can move (below), and there the up and down arrows move it 24 CSS px, Home and End to the limits, and Enter puts back the usual split, as a double-click does; j and k still step (`splitTakesKey` in `src/shared/ui/split.ts`, asked by keyboard.ts before the review keys). Where the panel has room for it, each region keeps three rows in view whatever the split (`SPLIT_MIN_ROWS`): the list its heading and three of its rows, the region below three list rows' height of what it scrolls, which is the Comments heading and the top of the first comment; in the default window at 100% the list then has 103 to 571 of the 664 CSS px the two share since `polish.8` (103 to 475 of 568 as measured for `ui.6`, with the chips' row above the panel, the footer under it and the box 20 px taller), and the handle moves by that height less 196 px, the two least heights (103 and 86) and the handle's 7. A shorter panel has no room for both (C.59, from the `ui.6` review). There the list has its heading and three rows or 55% of the height, whichever is less (`splitMin`), and the region below the rest, so a split set never leaves the region below less than the usual split leaves it under a full list: as measured for `polish.6`, a 1000 by 985 window at 175% (562 by 540 CSS px inside, the side panel in its drawer, the toolbar and the status bar on two rows each) had 195 CSS px under the box, where the usual split gives the list 107 and the region below 81 px of what it scrolls, and a split set 103 and 85, whatever the share. Since `polish.7` put that toolbar on one row and took the footer away, and `polish.8` the category's line, the window has 287 px under the box, room for both, and the handle moves 91 px there; the rule stands for a panel whose bars take more rows still. Until `polish.6` took the chips out of the panel's column, the smallest window, 900 by 600, at 100%, with the chips and the status bar on two rows each, had 180 px under the box, which gave the list 99 and the region below 54, about two and a half rows, whatever the split, and a 1000 by 900 window at 150%, in the drawer, with the chips on three rows, 136 px, which gave 75 and 34; they had 245 and 229 px after it, and have 305 and 321 since `polish.7` took the footer away and `polish.8` the category's line. Where the handle could move less than one arrow step, under 220 px at 100%, it is no control (`splitMovable`): it has `aria-disabled`, leaves the Tab order, and is drawn as the plain line, with no grip and the usual pointer, its tooltip "The panel is too short to move this line. Make the window taller, or zoom out, to give it room."; a press, a drag, a double-click and its keys do nothing, and should it have the focus when the window shrinks, the arrows step through the list again. Since `polish.8` the smallest window at 100% has 324 px under the box, or 305 with the status bar on two rows, so the handle moves 128 or 109 px there, whatever the chips; after `polish.6` it had 264 or 245 and moved 68 or 49 px, and the footer that `polish.7` took away gave 40 px of the difference and the category's line 20. The 1000 by 985 window at 175% above was one where the handle was still no control until `polish.7`. Until `polish.6` it was no control in the smallest window at 100% for any chapter whose chips took two rows or whose status bar took two, and with both on one row, 228 px, it moved 32 px. A move that would go against the pointer or the key does nothing, so a list of one or two rows under the usual split, shorter than its least, stays where it is on a move up and grows to three rows on a move down (`splitMove`). The split is kept in settings (`sideSplit`, 11.3 d) as the list's share of the height the list, the handle and the region below share, which is the panel under the focused suggestion's box (and above the footer, until `polish.7` took it away), so the line keeps its place as the window, the zoom or the status bar change that height; null is the usual split, where the list takes what it needs up to 55% (C.59). A split set keeps the list at its share however many rows it holds. app.css draws a share as `clamp(least, share * 100%, 100% - room below)`, with both limits measured by the page (`splitRoom`; `useSplit` in `src/renderer/state/splitHandle.ts`), so a resize needs no script. The page takes a new split at once and writes it through `settings:set`, one write after another, a run of key presses ending in one write of the last, and a close waits for the write with the others (`state/split.ts`). In the short window's one scroller there is no handle and the split is ignored (C.49); in a drawer (Narrow windows, below) it applies as in place wherever the window is tall enough for two regions.

**Zoom** (round 5). The whole window zooms, prose and controls together, from 80% to 200% in fixed steps (`shared/ui/zoom.ts`): the status bar's minus and plus, a click on the percentage to reset, Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus / Ctrl+0, and Ctrl+wheel. `src/main/zoom.ts` is the one place that decides it: it applies the level to the window, keeps it in settings (`zoom`), puts it back after every load, and tells the page (`view:zoom-changed`) so the label follows. The keys are caught in `before-input-event`, so they work wherever the focus is, and Ctrl+wheel arrives as Electron's `zoom-changed` event. The side columns give way to the prose when the window is narrow in CSS pixels, which is what zooming in does (Narrow windows, below).

**Narrow windows** (`ui.3`). The chapter list and the side panel give way so that the centre column keeps at least 480 CSS px (`PROSE_MIN`) while the window allows it. `columnLayout` in `src/shared/ui/columns.ts` works the layout out from the page's own width, which zoom changes and nothing on the page does, so it cannot feed back on itself. It takes the first of four steps that leaves the centre column its 480 px: (1) both columns at the widths they had before `ui.3`, the chapter list 18% of the window between 170 and 230 px and the side panel 24% between 240 and 320 px, or at the widths the author set with their handles (Column widths, below, `polish.5`); (2) both shrink toward their floors, 150 and 200 px, each in proportion to what it can give, so neither reaches its floor first; (3) the chapter list folds to a strip 32 px wide at the window's left edge, and the side panel takes its usual width, or the width set, or less down to its floor; (4) the side panel folds too, to a strip at the right edge, and the centre column takes the rest. When even that is under 480 px (`body--narrow`), the review pane's side padding narrows from 40 to 16 px (`NARROW_PANE_PADDING`); the margin column never shows there. Column widths are whole pixels, rounded down. In the smallest window, 900 by 600, at 100% both columns shrink a little (168 and 236 px, centre 480); at 110% the chapter list folds (centre 532); from 125% both do, which leaves the centre column 643, 525, 441 and 378 px at 125%, 150%, 175% and 200%, and the prose's text 487, 371, 337 and 275 px. In 1100 by 700 the list folds at 150% and both from 175%. In the default 1440 by 940 nothing changes up to 150%; the list folds from 175%, and the side panel never folds (200 px at 200%). A folded column is one button the height of the column (`ColumnStrip`): a chevron at the top pointing the way its drawer goes, the column's name, "Chapters" or "Suggestions", written down it and cut off where a short window leaves no room, the tooltip "Show the chapter list" or "Show suggestions, comments and history" ("Hide" while open), and `aria-expanded` (`stripText`). That is how the author gets the column back: a click, Enter or Space opens it as a drawer beside its strip, over the edge of the prose (and, from `polish.6` to `polish.10`, of the chips' row above it), at the column's usual width, or the width set (`polish.5`), less what the window cannot spare (its strip, the other column as drawn, a strip or in place, and 48 px of the centre column stay uncovered, `DRAWER_MARGIN`), with a shadow; one drawer at a time, and Tab goes from the strip into its drawer. The drawer closes from its strip; with Escape, first when the focus is in the drawer or on its strip, which then takes the focus, and otherwise after the suggestion editor and the find bar, never behind a dialog, and never with something else on the same press: an Escape something else has already taken (`defaultPrevented`), such as one in the find bar's box, which closes the bar before keyboard.ts sees it, leaves the drawer open, and so does one pressed while a toolbar menu (Review or Actions) or the status bar's legend is open, which close on it themselves (`popupTakesEscape`; an Escape pressed in a menu's list never leaves it, `polish.7`; `ui.3` review, where one press in the find box closed the bar and the drawer); with a press anywhere in the prose's scroller, which also does what it would have done; and, for the chapter list, once a chapter is chosen in it or made with its +. Choosing a review in the side panel's drawer leaves it open. Widening the window or zooming out until the column has room puts it back in place, and a drawer left open is forgotten then (`shownDrawer`). With no chapter open the side panel's strip has no button, as the panel is empty. Each column's wrapper (`.column`, `display: contents` while the column is in place) stays in the tree whatever the layout, so the list and the panel keep their state as the window changes; a closed drawer is hidden and `inert`. The drawer is above the page (z-index 10) and under the first-use hint (11), the notification cards (12), the lock card, the menus, the dialogs and the hover card, so neither a hint nor a card is ever lost behind it; while open it covers the edge of the prose and the find bar's end there. Its background is the page's (`--bg`), which is what lies under the column in place, so the side panel, faded while a review of the chapter runs (7.6), shows no prose through it (`ui.3` review). The page measures `.body` with a ResizeObserver and renders the new layout before the frame is painted (`flushSync`), so a zoom step never shows a frame of the old layout, and the first layout comes from the window's width (`useColumns` in `src/renderer/state/columns.ts`); the widths reach app.css as custom properties on `.body` (C.58).

**Column widths** (`polish.5`). The chapter list and the side panel each have a handle on their inner edge, between the list and the prose and between the prose and the panel, which makes the column wider or narrower (the author, 2026-10-22). Each is a control of its own, built as the split is: a focusable `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named "Width of the chapter list" or "Width of the side panel", its value the column's share of the window's width in per cent ("Chapter list 16% of the window's width"), its tooltip "Drag to make the chapter list wider or narrower. Double-click it, or press Enter, for the usual width." ("the side panel" for the other), with the col-resize pointer, which keeps its shape over whatever a drag crosses (`.column-resizing` on the root while it lasts). It is a band 7 CSS px wide laid over the column's own border, which is its line, and over the 6 px beside it on the side that has no scrollbar at that edge: the prose's left edge for the list, the side panel's left edge for the panel, so a press on either column's scrollbar is never taken for a drag. From `polish.6` to `polish.10` the chips' row at the top of the prose scrolled sideways under its own scrollbar, which would have started at that edge, under the list's band, so the row had a left border 6 px wide in its own colour, and the line under it was the wrapper's below (C.104); the chips are in the toolbar's row since `polish.10`, above the columns and their bands, and the row draws no scrollbar. It takes no width of its own, so the widths of Narrow windows above are unchanged. A grip 3 by 28 px in `--ink-faint`, which has 3:1 on the page and the panels in both themes, sits on the line halfway down, and the line and the grip darken under the pointer, as on the split; the band paints nothing else, and the focus ring is the browser's own (C.104). It is above the columns (z-index 1) and under the drawers and everything that floats over them. A drag follows the pointer with the pointer captured, and a press on the handle does not take the focus, so the arrows go on stepping through the suggestions after it. Tab reaches the list's handle after the list's last chapter, and the panel's after the prose and before the panel; there the left and right arrows move the edge 24 CSS px the way they point, Home gives the column its least width and End its most, and Enter puts back the usual width, as a double-click does; the up and down arrows, j and k still step through the suggestions (`columnKeyAction` in `src/shared/ui/columnHandle.ts`). A column is never narrower than its floor, 150 px for the list and 200 for the panel, and never so wide that the prose has less than `PROSE_MIN` beside the other column as drawn (`columnRoom`): in the default window at 100% the list goes from 150 to 624 px beside the panel's usual 320, and the panel from 200 to 714 beside the list's usual 230. A width set is kept in settings (`columnWidths`, 11.3 d) as the column's share of the window's width, to six places, so the column keeps its share as the window or the zoom changes; null is the usual width. `columnLayout` draws the widths set in place of the usual ones, to the nearest pixel (`keptWidth`), before anything gives way; where they leave the prose less than 480 px, both columns shrink toward their floors and then fold as Narrow windows says, at the same window widths as with the usual widths, whatever was set. A folded column has no handle, and its drawer opens at the width set. Where a column could move less than an arrow step, as the list in the smallest window at 100% (168 px beside its floor of 150), its handle is the border it lies on (`columnMovable`): it has `aria-disabled`, leaves the Tab order, has no grip and the usual pointer, its tooltip "The window is too narrow to move this line. Make the window wider, or zoom out, to give it room.", and a press, a drag, a double-click and its keys do nothing. The page takes a new width at once and writes it through `settings:set`, one write after another, a run of key presses ending in one write of the last, with the writer the split's uses (`createSettingWrites` in `state/settingWrites.ts`, `state/columnWidths.ts`), and a close waits for the write with the others (`state/pageIo.ts`); during a drag the page lays the columns out with the width the drag has reached, the other column's as set, and writes it when the button comes up (`useColumnHandle` in `state/columnHandles.ts`; what a drag draws and what a key writes are decided in `columnHandle.ts`, by `columnDragShare`, `columnLiveShares` and `columnKeyWrite`). With no chapter open the side panel's handle is still there, and sets the width a chapter opens in.

**Primary buttons**, the "blue buttons" of this plan, are filled in the icon's turquoise since `theme.12` (11.3 e), as is the active tab on the Setup screen. They darken on hover and press (`--accent-hover`, `--accent-active`) rather than taking the generic near-white hover, which had left their text unreadable. Save to chapter is one only while changes are waiting to be written, or a save of them is under way (`polish.9`, C.103): with nothing to save it is an ordinary button, so its turquoise says something is waiting. Disabled, either kind is faded the same way (`opacity: 0.45`).

**Toolbar order**, left to right: the eye that shows or hides every category and the category chips (Layout, above; `polish.11`), where the unsaved dot and the chapter title were until `polish.10` moved both into the window's title (The window's title, above); while a review runs, its progress label and Cancel; "Review", a menu holding an item for each provider, Claude and ChatGPT (and OpenAI (API key, experimental) until `codex.6`), each opening Review with AI (5.5) with that provider chosen (`codex.3`; one With AI until then), and, under a line, Manual, which opens Submit manual review (7.5); "Actions", a menu holding Accept all, Dismiss all and Reset, then, under a line, Accept all and Dismiss all of the category whose chip the focus was last on, as "Accept all punctuation" and "Dismiss all punctuation", or "Accept all your edits" and "Dismiss all your edits" for You, while the focus has not left the toolbar since (`useChipFocus`, `polish.10`, C.98), and nothing after the comments' chip, which has neither (`suggestionChip`, `polish.13`), then, under a line, the eye's two, Show all categories and Hide all categories, each greyed out when it would change nothing, while the chips are drawn, the comments' chip counted among them since `polish.13` (`polish.11`, C.107), then, under a line, Copy result, Export HTML (`rr.1`) and Show backups (6.5); "Save to chapter" with its count ("Save 12 changes to chapter", 6.4), a primary button only while it has changes to write or is writing them (`polish.9`); "Settings". Four controls since `polish.7` (C.99), where there were six: Review with AI and Submit manual review were buttons of their own, Bulk's menu held only the three bulk actions, Copy result sat between Save to chapter and Settings, and Show backups was in a footer under the side panel. The items name the providers as the dialog's Provider list does, in `PROVIDERS`' order, each with a tooltip saying what it reviews with (`REVIEW_WITH_TITLES`): With AI, which named none, gave way to them with ChatGPT (`codex.3`, 5.8 item 8). Review is disabled with no chapter file open and while a review of the open chapter runs; the providers' items are disabled while any review runs, since one runs at a time, with the tooltip "Wait until the review that is running ends, or cancel it", so on another chapter only Manual can be used. Actions is disabled with no review open; its bulk items, a chip's two included, while the chapter is read-only or a paragraph box is open (tooltip "Finish or cancel the paragraphs you are editing first"), and Copy result, Export HTML and Show backups never. Each menu behaves as a menu (`ToolbarMenu`, the keys in `src/shared/ui/menu.ts`): a click, Enter or Space opens it with the focus on its first item that can be used, and the down or up arrow on its button opens it on the first or the last; in the list the arrows step through the items that can be used, round from the last to the first and back, Home and End go to the first and the last, and a letter goes to the next item that starts with it; Escape closes it with the focus back on its button, Tab and Shift+Tab close it and go on from the button, and a click outside it, or the focus going elsewhere in the page, closes it. The items are `role="menuitem"` with `tabIndex={-1}`, so only the arrows reach them. A key the list takes stops there, so j, k, a, d, the arrows and Escape never reach the chapter, the find bar or a drawer behind it; Ctrl+S still saves. An item puts the focus on its menu's button before it runs, so the dialog or the question it opens hands the focus back there (ui.4); Review carries `data-opens="review"` for both review dialogs (`REVIEW_BUTTON_SELECTOR`). The row has to fit a 1100 px window on one row at 125%, which is why model and effort moved into the review dialog (5.5) and the buttons into the two menus. The chips take the room the buttons leave (there is no spacer) and are what gives way first: they shrink by steps, then their row scrolls, down to about 8em for the eye and the chips together (`.chips-bar`, `flex: 1 1 8em`, unchanged by `polish.11`, so the buttons wrap where they did), as the chapter title did until `polish.10`, ending in an ellipsis. Past that, zoomed in, the row wraps as the status bar does: the last buttons move to a second row on the right, and no button label ever breaks onto a second line (`apply.4`). Since `polish.7` the row is one line in the default window up to 200% and in the smallest window up to 150%; at 200% there Settings moves to a second row (C.99). With thirteen categories' chips in it since `polish.10` the same holds, and the smallest window is one row at 175% too ("Save to chapter"; measured again with the eye, You and the larger steps for `polish.11`, C.107); at 1100 by 720 and 125% with "Save 12 changes to chapter" the row is one line, the chips' bar 419 CSS px wide (C.98). While a review runs, its progress label (at least 15em, about 250 CSS px at "Writing suggestions (2345 tokens) (1m 12s)") and Cancel come before Review, and at 1100 px and 125% the row still fits on one line, the title cut short beside "Save 5 changes to chapter" (measured for `polish.7`; the chips' bar has the title's rule since `polish.10`). The label itself is free to wrap: the row wraps first, so it keeps one line, and if it is ever given less room than its words they break inside its own box rather than spilling over the name; with `white-space: nowrap` it had been drawn leftwards over the dot and the name, and cut off at the window's edge.

**First-use hint** (`apply.12`). The first time the page holds a change the chapter file does not have, a note hangs under the toolbar, over the top of the side panel, its arrow on Save to chapter: "Your decisions are kept in this review, not in your chapter yet. Press Save to chapter (Ctrl+S) to write them into Chapter 01 - The Flood.md. The version it replaces is backed up first.", with the chapter's own file name and extension, and a Got it button (`saveHintText` in `src/shared/ui/saveHint.ts`, drawn by `SaveHint.tsx`). Got it, or any Save to chapter that reaches the file, puts it away for good, whether or not it was showing: the toolbar's button, Ctrl+S, the leave and close prompts' Save, "Save N changes, then review" and "then build" (App's `onSaved`, which also runs for a save that found the file already reading like the page). Its id, `save-to-chapter`, goes into `dismissedHints` (11.3 d) through `settings:set` (`dismissHint` in `src/renderer/state/hints.ts`), one write after another, each from the settings as they then stand; the hint leaves the screen at once, before the write, and a close waits for that write with the review and paragraph writes, so Save and close puts it away too. A write that fails keeps it away for the session, and the next start shows it again. Until it is put away, it shows whenever the review on screen has a change not saved to the chapter (`saveHintVisible`), and nothing else dismisses it: turning the change back, opening another chapter and a restart only hide it until a change is unsaved again. It waits while a review of the chapter runs or a save is under way, since Save to chapter cannot be pressed then, and with the side panel folded it gives way to the prose (below). So the button it points at is always the turquoise one, enabled, since `polish.9` made Save to chapter a primary button only while a change is waiting or a save is under way, and the hint waits during a save (`test/shared/saveHint.test.ts` holds the two together); its width, and so the arrow's place, does not change with the class. It also waits while the Setup screen or the welcome guide is up, and shows again when they close: neither has a side panel, and hung over them across the toolbar's width it covered the guide's Skip and Setup's Close in the smallest window (884 by 561 CSS px inside) until Got it (`saveHintVisible`'s `singleScreen`, `setup.11` review). It sits inside the toolbar, `top: calc(100% + 9px)`, so it hangs below the toolbar's last row and never covers one of its buttons, whichever row Save has wrapped onto. It keeps to the side panel's column, 300 px wide or the column less 8 px at each side, lined up 8 px in from the column's right edge, and moves left within the column to bring its arrow over Save (`saveHintPlacement`, the column measured from `.body .side`), measured again whenever the toolbar, the button, the side panel or the centre column changes size; so it never meets the notification cards, the find bar or the chapter's text, which are all in the column beside it, nor the chips, in the toolbar's row above it since `polish.10`. With the side panel folded to a strip (Narrow windows, above), its column is where its drawer opens, beside the strip, whether the drawer is open or not: the hint stays clear of both strips and hangs over the top right of the prose instead, and there it gives way to the prose (`ui.3` review). It waits while a paragraph is open for editing (7.4), whose text and Done it would cover, and once it has shown, the author's next press anywhere but on the hint, review key (j, k, the arrows, a, u, d, e, n) or drawer opened sets it aside for the rest of the session while the panel stays folded. The press or key still does what it does, nothing is written, and with the panel drawn in place again the hint shows over it as before. The press, key or drawer that makes the first change comes before the hint shows, so it never sets it aside (`saveHintVisible`'s `sideFolded`, `editingParagraph` and `setAside`; `saveHintGivesWay` in `src/renderer/state/hints.ts`, called by a capture-phase `pointerdown` listener that `SaveHint.tsx` adds while it hangs over the prose, by keyboard.ts after a review key, and by a strip opening its drawer). A full-width row under the toolbar that pushed the prose down instead would have covered nothing, but in a 900 by 600 window with five chip categories it is 91 to 111 CSS px tall, where the prose has 287, 166, 112 and 68 px at 125%, 150%, 175% and 200%, so from 175% it would have left no prose at all. What it may cover: the top of the side panel (the review selector, its warning mark included, and most or all of the focused suggestion's box, since `polish.6` starts the panel at the toolbar's foot: since `polish.8` shortened the box, the hint ends at 179 CSS px in the default window at 100%, 26 px above the box's foot at 205, and at 217 in the smallest window, where the narrower panel makes it taller, 12 px below it, over the box and the top 2 px of the list heading's line, whose words, from 215, stay clear, as at 150% in the default window (216 against the heading at 213), and the rows below them, seen in the `polish.8` window check; between `polish.6` and `polish.8`, with the box's foot at 225, it ended 46 and 8 px above it, so the list's heading (then at 235) was wholly clear, seen in the `polish.6` window check; until `polish.6`, with the chips' row above the panel, the box's heading line with the pencil, the category and the top of the Original line, seen in the `ui.5` window check; until `ui.5`, the suggestions heading and first rows, seen in the `apply.26` window check, where Got it uncovered them; before `ui.3`, at 200% in a 900 by 600 window, the whole panel and two counts on the status bar's first row), and the find bar's last buttons where the centre column is too narrow for the bar and they spill into the side panel's column (1100 by 720 at 200% before `ui.3`). Until `polish.6` it also covered the chips at the right-hand end of their row when they ran that far (with five categories, at about 880 CSS px wide or less: a 1100 px window from 125%); from `polish.6` they were in the centre column beside it, and since `polish.10` they are in the toolbar's row, above it. With the side panel folded (900 by 600 from 125%, `ui.3`), until the author goes on: the top right of the prose (from `polish.6` to `polish.10` the right end of the chips' row as well) and of the find bar, at 200% the right part of the prose over its whole height and two counts on the status bar's first row, the side panel's drawer's top, the review selector included, as in place, when a change made in the open drawer brings the hint up over it, and at 200% the right end of an open chapter list's drawer, its + included; never the paragraph editor, as it waits while one is open. Got it is the way out, and the keys, Escape for the find bar among them, go on working meanwhile. The arrow points at Save's middle when it can reach it, else at the nearest point of the button it can, and only at a part of the button with no toolbar item under it, 12 px clear of the button's ends and of anything below (`SAVE_HINT_ARROW_CLEAR`); the hint hangs below the last row, so an arrow under Settings would point at Settings. When Save has wrapped onto a row above Settings and every part of it has one under it (before `polish.7`, with Copy result as well, about 720 CSS px wide or less: 900 by 600 at 125%, 1424 by 901 and 1280 by 800 at 200%; since, Save stayed on the first row in every window measured, C.99), the hint has no arrow (`data-arrow="none"`) and its words name the button. It sits under the notification cards (z-index 11 against 12), so a card wins should the two ever meet, above the page's unpositioned content, and under every dialog's backdrop, the menus and the hover card, and takes no focus, so the review keys go on working while it shows. When `apply.21` calls for a sentence about Obsidian, it goes in `SAVE_HINT_OBSIDIAN_NOTE`, and the hint adds it after its own three. The empty page ("Nothing open") and Accept all's question, a chip's Accept all included, end with "Nothing reaches the chapter until you press Save to chapter." (`NOTHING_UNTIL_SAVE`), the question on a line of its own.

**The Setup screen** (`setup.7` to `setup.9`; 5.6 items 4 to 7 give what it says and does). Claude's setup is a screen, not a dialog: "Set up Claude", with Close at its head and Done at its foot (`setup.19`), takes the place of the chapter list, the prose and the side panel, while the toolbar and the status bar stay, the notification cards sit at the top of its column, and the dialogs and the close question open over it with the page inert under them. Its status card says what the last check found, with Check again, Test the connection where a test can tell something, and Try the review anyway where the dialog would open anyway; under it the steps for the view on the system's own tab, each command with Copy, then Troubleshooting, Advanced and the privacy footer. The ways to it: the launch card's Open Setup, the status bar's Claude label (a button: Setup for Claude, its ChatGPT view for ChatGPT; Settings for OpenAI until `codex.6`), Setup beside Claude account in Settings, the welcome guide's Set up Claude, Claude in the toolbar's Review menu when Claude Code is missing or signed out, and a review that fails for a reason Setup can fix. The review keys, Ctrl+S and Ctrl+F do nothing behind it. Done, Close and Escape leave it for where it was opened from: Review with AI, opened again with the focus on its Start, when the dialog's Open Setup led there; the welcome guide, with the focus on the button that opened it, when the guide's did; otherwise the chapter. A way in pressed while Setup is open, the status bar's label or Settings' Setup over it, keeps that way back (5.6 item 5, `setup.19`). Until `setup.19` Escape did nothing on it, as it has no Cancel of its own, and Close always went back to the chapter, or to the guide under it. No button on Claude's view reads like a sign-in, and it starts none (5.6 item 7). Since `codex.2` the screen has a second view, ChatGPT's (5.7), opened by Setup on Settings' ChatGPT account row and, since `codex.3`, from wherever ChatGPT is chosen (5.7 item 6): "Set up ChatGPT" with Close, its status card with Sign in with ChatGPT or Sign out, the training warning with Open Data controls and the box "I have confirmed my data settings", and Done, which takes the focus once the sign-in has succeeded; it signs in, through OpenAI's own page in the browser, and the ways in above open Claude's view.

**The welcome guide** (`setup.11`). A fresh install has no settings file, so `onboardingDone` is false (11.3 d), and once the settings are in, the welcome guide takes the place of the chapter list, the prose and the side panel, in the Setup screen's layout (5.6 item 5): the toolbar and the status bar stay, the notification cards sit at the top of its column, it scrolls across the window's width with its page a centred column 720 CSS px wide at most (`.setup`, `.setup__page`), and the dialogs and the close question open over it, the page inert under them. Settings from before 1.0 that name a manuscript folder count as done, so an existing install never sees it unasked. The Setup screen comes first: the guide's Set up Claude opens Setup over it, and Setup's Done, Close or Escape goes back to it, with the focus on Set up Claude (`setup.19`). `welcomeShown`, `welcomeSteps` and `welcomeStart` in `src/shared/ui/welcome.ts` decide what it says, and `src/renderer/components/WelcomeScreen.tsx` draws it: "Welcome to Lapidary" with Skip at the head, a line saying that three steps get the app ready, that each says when it is done, that they can be done in any order and that Settings has Show the welcome guide again, then the three steps, each a card with its number, or a tick once it is done, at its side, its title, where it stands in a few words (read out as it changes, `aria-live`), what it means, and its buttons. The blue button is what the step still needs; a step that is done has none.

1. **Connect Claude.** Where it stands is the Setup screen's own title for the last check (`setupStatus`: "Checking Claude Code…", "Claude Code is not installed", "Claude Code is not signed in", "Claude is ready" and the rest), so it follows every check, the focus re-check included (5.6 item 6). It is done when Claude can review: ready, with an API key, or at a usage limit, which resets by itself, but not on a plan that cannot run Claude Code. Set up Claude opens Setup (5.6), and "Use ChatGPT instead" makes ChatGPT the provider (`settings:set`, `USE_CHATGPT`, `codex.6`; until then "Use OpenAI instead (experimental, pay per use)" stood there and made the OpenAI key the provider, and the step then asked for a key in Settings). With ChatGPT chosen, the step's status is the ChatGPT view's own title for where the sign-in stands, its text says that reviews go to ChatGPT on the author's plan with no API key (`CHATGPT_STEP_TEXT`), with Set up ChatGPT and Use Claude instead, and it is done once the author is signed in (5.8 item 8).
2. **Choose your manuscript folder.** Where it stands is the folder's path, or "No folder chosen yet"; it is done once one is chosen. A line says it is the folder that holds the chapters, the vault or a folder inside it, and four points say what that means: the app lists the .md and .txt files in it and its subfolders as chapters, leaving out a few, among them the guidelines file, Excalidraw drawings and anything whose name starts with a dot, such as Obsidian's .obsidian and .trash folders (`FOLDER_LISTS`; 6.1 leaves out more, so since `files.23` the line no longer says every file is listed); it changes a chapter file only when Save to chapter is pressed, after copying the version it replaces into a backup in its own data folder (6.3, 6.5); it adds one file of its own there, GUIDELINES.md, from a template the first time it needs it, and never changes it after that (section 10), or, when Settings names a guidelines file, it names that one instead; and reviews are kept in the app's own data folder, given by its path, not in the manuscript folder, or in the reviews folder chosen in Settings (`settings:effective`, 6.4). Choose folder, then Choose another folder, is the chapter list's folder picker, which reads the chapter list again.
3. **Fill in your style sheet.** It is done when the guidelines file is there and its style sheet is `filled` (`guidelines:status`, section 10). Otherwise it says "GUIDELINES.md is not there yet", "Still empty", with Review with AI's note (`STYLE_SHEET_EMPTY`, 5.5), "No Style sheet section", "Not checked yet" before the status is in, "Could not read GUIDELINES.md" with main's words, or "Choose a manuscript folder first", its buttons disabled. The buttons are Review with AI's and Settings' (`polish.3`; until then `setup.10b`'s Open in Obsidian, Open with default app and Show in folder): Open, the step's blue button until it is done, which reads "Create and open" while the file is missing, and Open folder, through `guidelines:open` and `shell:reveal`, each creating the file from the template first when it is missing, as the step's line says ("Both buttons below create it from a template first."). Their tooltips are Settings' (`openGuidelinesTitle`, `openFolderTitle`), which say so too while the file is missing, and a line under them says what Open did (`openedGuidelinesNote`), or why either did nothing. The status is read as the guide opens, whenever the manuscript folder, the guidelines file or the reviews folder changes in the settings, after each button, and whenever the window gets the focus back, as when the author returns from filling the style sheet in; only the newest answer counts.

Under the steps, **Start**, blue, is disabled until a manuscript folder is chosen, since the app has nothing to open without one, and beside it a line says what is left: "Choose a manuscript folder to start, or skip the guide for now.", or "Still to do: Connect Claude. You can start now and come back to it with Show the welcome guide again, in Settings.", or nothing once every step is done (`welcomeStart`). Start and Skip both put the guide away at once and write `onboardingDone: true`; a write that fails says so in a card, as the guide then shows again at the next start (`welcomeNotKept`). The guide stays away for the rest of the run whatever the settings say, by the store's `welcomeClosed` (`closeWelcome` in `src/renderer/state/welcome.ts`): after a write that failed, main still holds `false`, and the next settings reply from anywhere (Got it on the Save hint, the split, a change in Settings, the review dialog's model) brought the guide back over the chapter mid-session until the `setup.11` review. Settings' **Show the welcome guide again** writes `onboardingDone: false`, with `pro-model-preselected` added to `dismissedHints` in the same write so the guide shown again never changes the model (`welcomeAgainPatch`, `reopenWelcome`; C.67), and closes Settings and Setup, so the guide comes back, once that write is in, in place of whatever was open; a chapter open behind it stays open and is on screen again after Start or Skip. While the guide shows, the launch card (5.6 item 4) is not put up, and one that is up goes, since the first step says the same; the review keys, Ctrl+S, and Escape for the find bar and the suggestion editor do nothing behind it (`isModalOpen`), and Escape does nothing on the guide itself, as it did on Setup until `setup.19`. No button on it reads like a sign-in.

**Settings that could not be read** (`hardening.15`, 11.3 d, C.86). While settings.json is there but cannot be read, because another program holds it open as the app starts, or it is not JSON and no copy of it can be made, `settings:get` answers with no settings, only `readFailed` and which of the two it is, `reason` `refused` or `no-copy` (`SettingsReadFailure`, a fixed word and never the error), and the store keeps none (`readSettings` in `src/renderer/state/settingsRead.ts`, which keeps the newest reason). In place of everything else, the toolbar and the status bar too, the page shows one warning card in the Setup screen's column and in the look of its status card (`SettingsUnreadable`, words in `src/shared/ui/settingsRead.ts`): "Lapidary could not read its settings", then, for `refused`, "Another program may have settings.json open, such as a backup or sync tool, a virus scanner or an editor. Close it, then choose Try again." and "Until Lapidary can read the file it changes nothing in it, so your manuscript folder, your model and your other settings are kept as they are.", or, for `no-copy`, "settings.json is damaged: it is not valid JSON. Lapidary keeps a copy of such a file before it starts afresh, and no copy could be made, so it has left the file as it is." and "Mend the file, or move it out of its folder to start afresh, then choose Try again. Show diagnostics says why the copy could not be made.", with **Try again**, blue, **Show in folder** and **Show diagnostics** under them. Try again asks again; it is held, reading "Reading…", until the answer is in, and a read that fails again adds "settings.json still could not be read." under the lines, or, for `no-copy`, "settings.json is still not valid JSON, and no copy of it could be made.". Show in folder shows settings.json selected in its folder (`shell:reveal` with the fixed target `settings`), or the data folder once the author has moved the file away; Show diagnostics opens Diagnostics over the card, whose recent warnings hold `settings.read-failed code=…` or `settings.unreadable kept=none code=…`. Until the `hardening.15` review the card had only Try again and the first two lines for both reasons, so a damaged file whose copy failed was given advice that never ended the card, with no word of where the file is or why the copy failed. With no settings, the welcome guide does not show, the Pro preselection is not made, and a hint put away, the split and Show the welcome guide again write nothing (`reopenWelcome` writes nothing without settings), so nothing built from the defaults reaches the file once it can be read. A read that works puts the settings in the store, the page is drawn as usual with its chapter list, and main puts back the author's theme and zoom, which the window took from the defaults as it opened (`applyTheme`, `applyZoom`); a damaged file copied aside or moved away gives the defaults, and the welcome guide shows as on a first run. The notification cards stay over the card, for a Try again whose request fails, and the page's own error card or main's can come up there too: their Show diagnostics, like the card's, opens Diagnostics over it. The card's layout draws Diagnostics, the one dialog that needs no settings, and takes the page's `inert` only from it and the question; it first drew none and took `inert` from every dialog, so a card's Show diagnostics left the whole page inert with nothing over it, and the window could only be closed (the `hardening.15` review). No card with Open Setup can come up while the card stands: the launch card waits for settings (and the OpenAI key's cards, with Open Settings until `codex.6`, needed a chapter open).

Messages, progress and confirmation:

- **Notification cards.** Messages appear as floating cards anchored to the top-right corner of the manuscript pane, sized to their text and stacked when several are open; on the Setup screen, which has no manuscript pane, they sit at the top of its column, before it in the flow, so they never cover its Close or Check again and stay in view while it scrolls (5.6, `setup.7` and its review). A card closes only when its X is clicked: no click-away and no timeout, because a save error that vanished before it was read is worse than a stale card. The one card the app takes away itself is the launch card about Claude, under the key `claude-runtime` (5.6): once a check leaves Setup nothing to do, ChatGPT becomes the provider, or Setup is opened or the welcome guide shows, what it says is no longer true or no longer needed, so it is withdrawn by its key (`setup.7`, `runtimeCardAction`). Tones: info, warn, error. Cards about a recurring event (the watcher reloading the chapter, a save) pass a key, and a new one replaces the old, so a long typing session in Obsidian cannot bury the screen; the reload card then counts the run of reloads since it went up, so a later reload cannot hide what an earlier one took off the page (6.2). Save errors use this path like everything else: every card that says how a Save to chapter ended, failures included, shares the key `SAVE_CARD`, so a save refused again and again (a backup that cannot be made, 6.5) leaves one card, and a save that then works replaces it with "Saved to the chapter file.". The card Save to chapter shows when it finds the chapter changed on disk and rebases has no key and stays, because it counts the suggestions lost. A chapter that could not be opened, its file or the review it opens with unreadable (6.4, `apply.25`), says why under the key `open-chapter`: the next try replaces the card, and an open that works closes it. When the review is at fault the card names the chapter, "Could not open Chapter 12.md: ...", since main's words name only the review file or folder; a review whose latest decisions could not be written does not open either, from the chapter list, History or the review selector, and since `apply.25`'s review History and the selector use the same key for every open that fails, where each failure used to add a card of its own (6.4, `src/shared/ui/open.ts`).
