A chapter with merge markers gets a warning under the key `merge-markers` (`files.11`, 6.1): "Chapter 12.md has merge markers: lines that start with <<<<<<< or >>>>>>>. Git or a sync tool leaves them where two versions of the file disagreed, with both versions between them. Keep the words you want and remove the markers in Obsidian before you review or save this chapter. Lapidary has not changed the file." (`mergeMarkersText`). It shows when such a chapter opens, once however often it is opened, and when the chapter's text read again from disk has markers it did not have, at a reload (6.2), a review opened from History or Save to chapter finding the file changed (6.3 step 2), which then stops before writing anything and says so under `SAVE_CARD`; a chapter without them opening, or the text read again without them, closes it, and markers still there leave it as it is (`noteMergeMarkers` in `src/renderer/state/mergeMarkers.ts`, C.78). Cards sit under a dialog's backdrop (z-index 12 against 20), so a dialog that runs a save, Review with AI's "Save N changes, then review" and Submit manual review's "Save N changes, then build", shows inside itself what the save's cards said when it did not reach the file (5.5, 7.5); the cards were not raised above dialogs, because in the top-right corner they would cover the dialog itself, and at 200% there is no room beside it (`apply.20` review). An error the app did not expect leaves an error card with Show diagnostics, under the key `page-error` for the page's and `main-notice` for main's, each of which comes at most once a minute, whatever the errors (7.7, `hardening.4`). The update card (`release.9`) is one card under the key `update`, put up, changed in place or taken down as main's updater moves (`updateCardStep` in `src/shared/ui/update.ts`): a version on offer with Download, its download's percentage, the version ready with Restart now, and a download or install that failed. Its Download and Restart now leave it up, as the same card goes on to show what follows (`actionKeepsCard`), it keeps one width, 24em, with figures of one width (`note--update`), so neither it nor the cards under it move as the percentage grows a digit, it stays as it was while a check runs or Restart now is under way, and once the author has closed it it stays closed while the state it told lasts and comes back with the next. A press on its buttons that does nothing says why in a card of its own under `update-problem`. Control glyphs are inline SVG rather than characters (see C.18).
- **Progress.** While Claude works the label cycles "Thinking", "Thinking.", "Thinking..", "Thinking..." every 500 ms with the elapsed time beside it, then switches to "Writing suggestions (N tokens)" once output tokens arrive. Cancel stays next to it. `src/shared/ui/progress.ts` owns the wording.
- **Confirmation.** "Accept all", "Dismiss all", "Reset" and the per-chip bulk actions ("Accept 3 pending punctuation suggestions?", and for You "Accept your 2 pending edits?", whose lines say "Edits" where the others say "Suggestions", `polish.11`) open a small in-app modal, never `window.confirm`. It states the exact count and what is left alone: accept and dismiss only ever move pending suggestions, reset only clears decisions. Escape and Cancel back out; when nothing would change, a card says so instead of asking. `src/shared/ui/bulk.ts` computes both the affected ids and the wording. The same dialog asks the three-way questions before leaving a chapter or closing the window (11.3 i, `apply.6`): Cancel, the middle choice and the blue Save, left to right, in a dialog 460 px wide instead of 420, with the question's own default focused (Keep for later, or Cancel when only something would be lost). A question that cannot save hides Save, and an answer it does not show counts as Cancel. Labels never break inside a button; when the row does not fit, zoomed in, the last button moves to a second row on the right. `src/shared/ui/confirm.ts` decides the buttons and the focus. A question can be asked from inside another dialog or with the suggestion editor open, so the dialog sits above every other surface (`.modal-backdrop--confirm`, rendered last), takes Escape for itself, and shows the focus ring on its default however it was opened, since Enter answers that button. It holds the keyboard too: while a question is open everything else in the window is `inert`, the page (`.app-shell__page`) and the four other dialogs (`.app-shell__dialogs`, `ui.4`), both wrappers with `display: contents` and so laying out nothing, so Tab and Shift+Tab go round its buttons only, and when it closes the focus goes back to the element that had it when it opened, if that is still on the page (`apply.7` review). An Actions menu item puts the focus on Actions as the question opens, so Actions gets it back (`ui.4`, `polish.7`).
- **Find.** Ctrl+F opens a find bar as a strip across the top of the manuscript pane, above the scroller, so it is in view wherever the author is in the chapter (C.33); pressing Ctrl+F again returns to the box with the query selected. It shows a match count ("3 of 12"); Enter and Shift+Enter or the arrows step, Escape closes. Matches are painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API over the existing text nodes, so hunk spans, ghosts and offsets are untouched (C.15). Ghost text and the paragraph rail are excluded from the search. The pane scrolls to the active match only when the author asks to go there, by typing or stepping (`find.seek` in the store); a redraw, such as accepting a suggestion with the bar open, repaints the matches without moving the page.
- **Scrolling.** Every scroll the app makes for the author (keyboard focus, a list click, a find match, a comment, a paragraph opened for editing) is animated by `state/scroll.ts` with the timing in `shared/ui/scroll.ts`: quick for a short hop, proportionally faster for a long one, and never more than 320 ms. A new scroll cancels the one in flight, so rapid j/k or Enter always lands on the last thing asked for. Reduced motion makes it instant. Every element that scrolls has an opaque background in a colour token, so it keeps a composited layer of its own with LCD text while it moves (C.48).

Review pane rendering:

- **Paragraph rail** (Phase 5d). Every body paragraph has, in a rail to its left, its number (from 1, matching the prompt, 5.2) and a faded pen that opens it for editing in place (7.4). A paragraph with an open comment has its number in the comment colour, where a dot used to be. The rail sits in padding added to the measure, is never selected or copied with the prose, and the find bar skips it. A block that spans two paragraphs (a deletion straddling the blank line) is labelled "12-13". Frontmatter has no rail. The rail is 39 px wide and ends 11 px short of the text, where the margin marks sit (`small.8`): a bar, 3 px by 0.9em in the category colour, beside each line with a pending small change, and an ink arrowhead beside the line where the focused suggestion starts, whatever its size. A bar is a button 11 by 39 CSS px outside the prose: a click selects its change without scrolling and without taking the keyboard focus, so a, d, u and e then act, and hovering shows its card under the change, for reading. The arrowhead is the same button, which takes no pointer, so a bar that turns into it under the pointer keeps its element and its card closes as the pointer leaves it; a mark that goes away under the pointer, decided or made again by a save, closes the card it opened (`markHover` in `src/renderer/state/hover.ts`; the `small` review, C.68). The marks are children of the paragraph, placed by CSS anchor positioning on their change's live text (`marginMarks` and `markAnchorName` in `src/shared/ui/marks.ts`), so they follow reflow and zoom with no measuring; a paragraph join's bar sits beside the blank line it would remove. Decided small changes get no bar, so a worked chapter goes quiet. A merged number such as "12-13" stays on one line.
- Prose font (`--font-prose`: Literata where it is installed, else Georgia, then Times New Roman and any serif; none is bundled) at 17 px, `line-height: 2.3`, `white-space: pre-wrap`, a measure of 66 characters (`max-width: calc(66ch + 50px)`, the 50 px being the rail). Text is rendered character-for-character from `base.text` so offsets stay valid, and none of it is styled: Markdown and Obsidian syntax show as the characters typed, in the prose font, at one size, so `*...*` and `**...**` keep their asterisks and are neither italic nor bold, and a heading is its `#` and its words at the size of the prose. (This line said until `files.12` that emphasis markers were styled, italic, bold and headings larger; no commit in the repository's history styles them, and Appendix D's friend defaults settled that syntax is shown as plain text.) No Markdown-to-HTML conversion. Each paragraph is its own block, 1.1em below the one before, so the blank lines between paragraphs are not drawn as lines. The frontmatter is a block of its own above the first paragraph (`.frontmatter`): the UI font at 12 px in `--ink-faint` on `--panel-alt`, in a 1 px `--border` frame, with no rail, no suggestions and no pen.
- **The manuscript does not scroll sideways** (`ui.2`), wherever the centre column is wider than the pane's own side padding, which since `ui.3` is every window at every zoom (the narrowest centre column is 378 CSS px, a 900x600 window at 200%; Narrow windows, above). Every ghost stops inside the pane's side padding, or short of the margin column (below). A word longer than the line, such as a web address, breaks inside the word (`.prose { overflow-wrap: break-word }`; ghosts are `white-space: pre` and never wrap). `.pane` clips anything else at its own edge, the outside of its side padding (`overflow-x: clip`, which does not make it a scroller), and has `min-width: 0`, so in a narrow pane it gives the position strip its 14 px instead of staying as wide as its longest word and pushing the strip out, as it did in a 900x600 window at 150%. What the pane clips is hidden and cannot be clicked, so anything in it wider than a narrow column has to wrap: the paragraph editor's Cancel and Done share a row with its hint where there is room and otherwise wrap below it, on the right (7.4; at 900x600 and 150% the text column was 25 px before `ui.3`, and Done had been cut off, `ui.2` review). Before `ui.3` the side columns kept their widths whatever the zoom: in a 900x600 window from 175% the centre column (87 CSS px, then 25) was narrower than the pane's 80 px of side padding and the 14 px position strip, so it still scrolled sideways, and there, as in a 1100x700 window at 200%, the text column was 0 px, so the pane showed no text at all and the paragraph editor's buttons were out of reach; before `ui.2` those windows drew the chapter a letter to a line, past the pane, behind the scrollbar. Now the text column is at least 275 px (900x600 at 200%).
- Each hunk is an inline `<span class="hunk">` carrying its own `data-hunk-start` and `data-hunk-end`, with the live text in the line and a ghost row absolutely positioned above it (`top: -1.15em`, smaller font). The extra line height leaves room for the ghost. Ghost text is `user-select: none` so it can never join a selection.
  - **Colour means undecided.** Pending live text gets a 2 px underline in the category colour and a faint tint of it. Accepted gets a 2 px solid underline in the grey of the "was" ghost (`--ink-faint`) and no tint: the green underline it used to have read as "still active", which is the opposite of what it meant. Dismissed gets a 1 px dotted light-grey line. The hover tint follows the same rule, category-coloured only while pending, and so do a small change's capsule and an insertion's caret (`small.1`, `small.6`). The "?" legend and the suggestions-list status markers say the same thing, and the strip beside the scrollbar marks pending hunks only.
  - **The dismiss "x" is part of the ghost row**, immediately after the ghost text with a 0.4em gap, so it trails the ghost whatever the two widths are. Pinned to the span's corner it landed on top of the ghost's last letters whenever the ghost was wider than the live text. The row counts as part of the suggestion for the pointer and reaches down to the line of text, a strip joins the top of the word to it, and the x keeps its room while invisible, so moving from the word to the x never loses it; the hover grace period covers a diagonal path to an x that sits past the word (C.34). Clicking the ghost toggles the suggestion, as clicking the word does.
  - **Ghosts that would collide, or run out of the pane, are clipped.** Two suggestions close together on one line can have overlapping ghosts even when the words below them do not, and a long suggestion's ghost, one line of text, can run far past the right edge of the prose (a 40-word inserted sentence gave the pane a horizontal scrollbar, `ui.2`). No CSS rule can know either: both depend on where the line broke. `clipGhosts` in `src/renderer/state/ghosts.ts` measures the ghost rows after layout, and `ghostMaxWidths` in `src/shared/ui/ghosts.ts` gives any ghost that would run into the next one on the same line, or past the room its row has, a max width and an ellipsis, leaving room for the x that trails it; no ghost is cut below 22 px, nor short of the right edge of its key (`small.7`). That room (`ghostEdge`) is the pane's side padding, up to 6 px short of the pane's edge, where `.pane` clips (`GHOST_EDGE_MARGIN`), or, while the margin column shows, up to 10 px short of it (`GHOST_GAP`), so a row never covers a note. It is not the edge of the prose's text: a short ghost near the end of a line has always run a little past that, into the padding, with no scrollbar, and cutting it there made "-> watermill" read "-> water..." and an accepted insertion's lone "added" label read "ADD", sliced through a letter (`ui.2` review). The label is `inline-block` so that a replaced original's line-through does not strike it, which is also why a cut inside it ends without an ellipsis. Ghosts are clipped, not wrapped: a wrapped ghost would climb into the line above. The full text stays in the tooltip and in the suggestions list. Clipping changes no geometry the prose depends on, so it cannot loop. The pass runs after every change to the hunks, the scroller's size or the prose's, and as the margin column comes or goes.
  - The ghost is styled by **role, not position**, because the swap makes position meaningless: an original the author has replaced is always grey and struck through and is introduced by a small-caps "was"; a suggestion still on offer always carries the category colour and is introduced by an arrow. `ghostRole` in `src/shared/render.ts` decides which, and `ghostContent` what the row shows. The one exception: a small original (Small changes, below) is drawn bigger as an inline-block, which a line-through does not reach, so a replaced hyphen reads plainly as a hyphen; its "was" says it was replaced.
  - insertion (`original === ''`): live = a thin caret glyph; ghost = inserted text. Once accepted, the ghost reads "added", having no original to show (it used to read "was keep", which said the opposite), followed by what was added when that is small ("ADDED ,", `small.7`). The caret is inline at 0.8em, 2 by 15 CSS px, so it never leaves the word before it, as an inline-block one did at some window widths, and it follows the status: the category colour while pending, `--ink-faint` for an accepted deletion and `--border-strong` once dismissed (`small.1`).
  - deletion (`replacement === ''`): ghost shows a small "delete" tag, followed by the name of what it takes out when that cannot be seen ("-> DELETE SPACE").
  - **Small changes** (11.7, `small`). A change whose text is a comma, a space, a one-letter word or nothing is drawn bigger, never stored bigger: no hunk, offset or text in the line changes, so Save to chapter, Copy result, find and copy read exactly what they did (`isSmallText`, `isSmallLive` and `isSmallChange` in `src/shared/ui/small.ts`; Appendix C.68). In the line, a capsule sits under the live text, 0.75em wide or the text's own width, beneath its letters (every paragraph is isolated): the category colour at `--tint-small` with a 2 px category line at its foot while pending, a 2 px grey cup once accepted, a 1 px dotted line once dismissed, and focused, `--focus-bg`, with theme.8's hairline in the active comment's paragraph; the ghost above is not filled, as a word-sized change's is not (C.68). A transparent hit zone 0.9em wide lies over it, so the click target grows from about 5 by 22 to 16 by 23 CSS px. On a side where another change touches it, or text under two characters stands before the next, both pull back to the change's own edge (`flushBefore`, `flushAfter` in `segmentsIn`). A change whose live text holds a line break, such as a paragraph join, gets no capsule. Above the line, the ghost's small text is drawn bigger, the glyph at 1.25 times the ghost size and not struck through, and whitespace is named in small caps in a keycap, a 1 px box in the ghost's colour at 60% ("-> SPACE", "WAS PARAGRAPH BREAK"); punctuation keeps no box, as a box on every key piled the rows up on a busy line of dialogue (`small.7`). Everywhere a side is written out, the list, the hover card, the focused suggestion's box, Unanchored and the spoken name, a space, a break or small punctuation is named: "- (hyphen) -> (space)", with "(nothing)" only for the empty string (`sideText`).
  - A "?" popover in the status bar explains the three states in words, then the unsaved dot, the chips (since `polish.13` the comments chip too, and that the eye hides it with the rest), and, since `polish.12`, the suggestions list's tags, its green ✓ and red ✕ and the heading's count (and Show states, until `polish.17` took the box away), and ends with the keys and pens (`e` rewrites the focused suggestion; the pen beside a paragraph edits it) and that nothing reaches the chapter before Save to chapter or Ctrl+S (`apply.4`). It scrolls when the window is too short for it.
  - A thin strip down the right edge of the scroller marks where the pending suggestions are; clicking a mark jumps to one.
- **Hover is not focus.** Hovering a suggestion opens a custom tooltip within 100 ms (category, reason, "Original: ... / Suggested: ...", and a pencil) and adds a hover tint. It never moves focus and never scrolls, because focus scrolls the pane and a suggestion that slid out from under the pointer is unusable. The tooltip is positioned below the words so it cannot cover the ghost. Only keyboard navigation and clicks in the suggestions list scroll the pane. Because the card now carries a control, leaving the words schedules its removal after a short grace period instead of doing it at once, and entering the card cancels that (`src/renderer/state/hover.ts`).
- Interactions: click the ghost or hunk = toggle accepted; the "x" beside the ghost, right-click, or the `d` key = toggle dismissed; `j`/`k` and the arrows move focus, starting from the paragraphs on screen when nothing is focused or the focused change has been scrolled out of sight, and Shift+J and Shift+K go to the next and previous pending change, passing over decided ones and wrapping round (`stepFocus` in `src/shared/ui/navigate.ts`, `small.9`; letters are read in lower case and Shift from the event, so Caps Lock does not stop them); a click on a margin bar selects its change without scrolling (except that the arrows scroll the focused suggestion's box when Tab has put the focus there, `ui.5`, and move the split's handle when it has the focus, `ui.6`); `a` accept; `u` back to pending; `e` edit the focused suggestion's text; the pen in the rail edits a paragraph; `n` next paragraph with a comment, none while the comments' chip is hidden (`nextComment`, `polish.13`); Ctrl+S saves to the chapter, under the rules in 6.3. None of these keys, the arrows and Ctrl+F included, acts while a dialog, a question, Settings, the Setup screen or the welcome guide covers the page, or while the suggestion editor is open (`reviewKeysActive` and `isModalOpen` in the store): behind Review with AI, `a` had accepted a suggestion out of sight, which changed the dialog's count and its blue button, `e` had opened the suggestion editor over the dialog, and Ctrl+F had put the focus in the find bar behind it (`apply.20` review). Escape behind a dialog is the dialog's as well: Settings and Review with AI close on it, a question cancels, New chapter, Submit manual review and the welcome guide do nothing with it, and the Setup screen leaves on it as its Close does (`setup.19`, `useSetupEscape`), so it no longer closes the find bar or the suggestion editor out of sight behind them (`ui.1`). Nor does the suggestion editor act behind a dialog: one opened while it is open covers it, and it is inert until the dialog closes (7.4, `ui.1` review). Bulk actions on a category, in its chip's menu and in Actions for the chip the focus was last on (`polish.10`): accept all or dismiss all of it, behind a confirmation. Everything is reversible until Save to chapter, and after it too: a saved change turned back is one more change for the next Save to write, and each save first copies the version it replaces into the backups (6.5).
- **Suggestions list.** The right column lists every anchored hunk in document order, filtered by the category chips, under a heading that counts the decided ones as the comments' counts the resolved, "Suggestions (12 of 19 decided)", decided meaning accepted or dismissed, and "Suggestions (19)" while none is (`suggestionsHeading`, `polish.12`; it counts the rows listed, so a hidden chip's are out of both numbers). Each row has a tag at its left, "original -> suggested" clipped to one line, and edit, accept and dismiss icon buttons that act exactly as the pane does (a decided row also had a status word after its change until `polish.17`, below), each icon 16 CSS px in its 18 px button since `polish.14` (12 px with 3 px of padding before; the focused suggestion's pencil, drawn as one, too). The tag (`polish.12`, in place of a category dot) stands for the chip the suggestion is under, in the chip's colour: since `polish.14` three capitals centred in a box of one width, 34 CSS px, so every row's words start in one column (`TAG_ABBREVIATIONS` in `src/shared/ui/suggestions.ts`: SPE spelling, TYP typo, HOM homophone, GRM grammar, AGR agreement, TEN tense, PUN punctuation, WRD word-choice, RED redundancy, AWK awkward, CON consistency, FMT formatting, OTH other, and YOU for the author's own edits), where it was the chip's name in capitals, "GRAMMAR", "WORD-CHOICE", of as many widths; its tooltip is the name in full, "Grammar", "Word-choice", or "Your own words" on YOU (`rowTag`); it is read to a screen reader as the category, first in the row's name, which goes on with the change and its decision whatever the row shows ("grammar, began → begun, accepted", `rowLabel`). Click to put it back" (until `polish.12` it turned into a green undo arrow); a click on either puts the suggestion back to pending. The other two keep `--row-fade`, 35%, of the faint grey every row button has (`polish.14`; `polish.12` drew them a thinner stroke, which the author found "barely looks any different"), so the row plainly reads as done, and come back as any row button under the pointer, `--ink` on `--border`, and in `--ink` with the focus ring when the keyboard brings the focus to one; at rest they are under 3:1 by the author's choice (11.3 e). A pending row is as it was. A decided row says its decision by these buttons alone since `polish.17` (the author, 2026-10-23: "'Show States' button can go. The legend says what the tick and the ✕ do, and lists the fourteen tags with their names, each drawn as on its row (`polish.14`). In a narrow panel the row's two parts give way in turn (the `polish.12` review, C.108): the change first, down to a floor of 32 CSS px (`--row-text-floor`), then the tag, which is never wider than the room the floor leaves it; the row's button clips the rest, so nothing it holds reaches the pencil. Tab and Shift+Tab, finding nothing else in the window that can take the focus, go round the dialog's own controls, from the last to the first and from the first to the last; there is no Tab handler of the app's own. It takes the focus on its box as it shows and, when an install fails and it goes, hands it back as the dialogs do (`useDialogFocus`): to the Restart now that was pressed, the card's or About's, which stays through the install and then reads Restart now or Open the release page, or, should that have gone, to the first there of an open dialog's box, the update card's button and the toolbar's Settings (`UPDATE_OVERLAY_FOCUS_FALLBACK`, tried in that order by `firstFound`, not in the page's). In a development run StrictMode opens each dialog twice, with a pretend close between, and the second time the focus is already in it; that is not taken for where it was (`focusBeforeOpening`), and the cleanup keeps what it noted, so a development window hands the focus back as an installed build does rather than always to the fallback (found by the `release.9` review fix).

### 7.4 Editing inside the app

Accepting a suggestion used to be the only change the author could make without leaving for Obsidian. They can now write their own words, and **every edit goes through the hunk model**, so Save to chapter stays the only write path (CLAUDE.md rule 1) and an edit is as reversible and as re-anchorable as anything a model suggested. The rules are pure and tested in `src/shared/edit.ts`.

1. **Edit a suggestion.** A pencil in the tooltip, on the heading line of the focused suggestion's box ("Edit suggestion", `ui.5`), and on every row of the suggestions list (and the `e` key) opens a small floating editor prefilled with the suggestion's replacement: Save and Cancel, an "Accept now" checkbox, Ctrl+Enter and Escape. It floats over the page and its menus but under every dialog: Settings, Review with AI, New chapter or Submit manual review opened while it is open covers it (`.modal-backdrop` is drawn above `.editor`), and it is `inert` until the dialog closes, when it is back as it was, words and all (`ui.1` review). The Setup screen, which takes the main view's place (5.6), takes the editor off the page with it, so the words typed are kept in the store (`EditorRequest.text`, `setEditorText`) rather than in the panel: closing Setup brings the editor back with them, and while it is open the close question still counts them (`hasDialogText` reads them from the request; `setup.7` review, as the status bar's button reaches Setup with the editor open). The pencil again on the suggestion being edited moves the editor and keeps them; another suggestion starts afresh. Until then it was drawn over them and could still be typed in and saved with Ctrl+Enter, which rewrote and accepted the suggestion behind the dialog. Saving updates `replacement`, sets `edited: true`, keeps source, category and reason, and accepts it unless "Accept now" is unticked. The new words are always a change against what the chapter file says over the span (`editSuggestion(base, ...)`, `apply.22`, C.51). A suggestion already saved into the file (`baseSide: 'replacement'`) takes the saved words as its `original` and its base side, and the new words as its replacement: ticked, it is accepted and counts as one unsaved change, and Save to chapter writes the new words; unticked, it is pending, the page keeps the saved words, and Save writes nothing for it rather than putting the model's original back. A saved change the author had turned back shows the saved words again the same way. New words that read exactly as the file does leave nothing unsaved: both sides become the file's words, and a suggestion whose two sides are the same never counts as unsaved and always shows the file's words, whatever is decided on it afterwards (`changesBase`, `decidedText`), so rewriting a saved suggestion and then back to the saved words is a no-op, and turning it back or dismissing it later still is.
2. **Edit a paragraph in place** (Phase 5d, replacing editing a mouse selection, which caught stray spaces and fought with clicking a word). The faded pen in the rail swaps the paragraph for a text box in the same typeface, prefilled with the paragraph as the page reads it, every accepted change applied. The box grows with its text; Done or Ctrl+Enter applies, Cancel or Escape discards, after asking first when the box's text has changed ("Discard your changes to paragraph 12?", with Keep editing focused; `apply.16`). Below the box a hint, Cancel and Done share a row; where the column is too narrow for that, Cancel and Done wrap below the hint, still on the right, since the pane hides whatever reaches past its side padding (section 7, `ui.2` review). **Several paragraphs can be open at once**, each with its own Done. When a hunk straddles the blank line after a paragraph, the page already shows the two as one block, and the box takes the whole block. On Done, `planBlockEdit` word-diffs the page text against the box:
   - every changed run becomes its own accepted manual hunk (`source: 'manual'`, `category: 'other'`, `reason: 'Edited by author'`), so fixing two words far apart leaves two small hunks, not one that owns the paragraph; runs separated only by whitespace join, and each is trimmed to whole words, as the full-text diff does (4.4);
   - a run that touches a suggestion, overlapping it or merely adjacent to it, grows to take the suggestion whole: a model suggestion is superseded (dismissed, unanchored, `supersededBy`, reason kept behind "Superseded by your edit: "), and one of the author's own earlier edits is simply replaced, with anything it had superseded now pointing at its replacement;
   - typing exactly the fix a suggestion offered accepts that suggestion, keeping its category and reason;
   - typing the file's own words back needs no hunk: the suggestions in the way settle on the file's words (dismissed, or accepted when a save already wrote them in);
   - emptying the box deletes the paragraph with one blank line beside it, the one after if there is a next paragraph, as the full-text diff stores a deletion;
   - newlines at either end of the box are dropped; an unchanged box closes with nothing done. The box opens on the paragraph's words alone (4.1): never on the line break after the frontmatter's closing `---` where the body starts on the next line, which Done used to delete, so that Save put the first words on the `---` line, nor on a blank line that ends the text (`files.22`, C.76).

   A property test checks that, for generated chapters, suggestions, saved states and edits, the composed chapter always equals the text before the paragraph, then exactly what was typed, then the text after, with no overlapping hunks.

   While a paragraph is open, its suggestions are frozen (their list rows fade and their buttons are disabled) and the three bulk items in the toolbar's Actions menu are disabled (`polish.7`), because the box started from the page as it was and must commit against the same page. If the chapter file changes on disk while a box is open, the watcher still reloads the review and the box stays open; Done then refuses, says the paragraph changed, and keeps the author's text in the box. Opening another chapter asks first when a box's text has changed, in the same question as changes not saved to the chapter (7.7, `apply.7`): Save first applies the boxes as accepted suggestions and saves, Keep for later keeps them for when the author comes back, and a box left as it opened is kept without a question. Another review of the chapter, from History or the review selector, asks nothing (`apply.26`): the boxes are kept, and go back on that review where their paragraph reads the same, the others set aside (C.53). Save to chapter with boxes whose text changed asks to apply them first, as accepted suggestions, and saves nothing if any cannot be applied; boxes left as they opened are closed without a question when something is written (6.3). Review with AI and Submit manual review ask the author to finish or cancel them first.

   **Open boxes are kept on disk** (`apply.16`, 11.3 j). Every box open in a chapter is written to that chapter's drafts file 700 ms after the last keystroke, and the file goes when the last box closes, so closing the app, an update or a crash loses nothing typed in a box. Leaving the chapter keeps them too (Keep for later, 7.7, `apply.7`); until then leaving asked to discard open boxes, and Discard emptied the drafts file. Whenever a review of the chapter comes on screen, each box goes back where its block still reads exactly as when the box opened, with a card when typed text came back ("Paragraph 12 is open for editing again, as you left it."). The card goes when another chapter or review comes on screen, or once every box it names is applied or closed (`apply.7` review). A box holding typed text that cannot go back is set aside as a .txt in the app's data folder, and its card's Show the text opens it. A drafts file that cannot be read when the chapter comes on screen (another program holding it open, say) is never written over unread: each write for that chapter reads it first and writes nothing while it still cannot be read, and once it can, the boxes it held are kept after those on screen and come back the next time the chapter opens (C.53).
3. **From a comment.** "Edit text" on every comment card, in the margin and in the sidebar, opens the comment's paragraph as in case 2, with the comment's quote selected when it can be found. This replaces the "Insert as suggestion" idea from the original Phase 5 list.
4. **Edit the whole chapter** (Full edit, `rr.2`, C.112). The Mode select's Full edit (section 7) opens the chapter's body in one box, as the page reads it, every decision applied, from the first paragraph's first character to the last paragraph's last (`chapterForEdit`, `fullEditText`), the frontmatter above the box and not in it. On Done, `planChapterEdit` in `src/shared/edit.ts` plans the whole chapter in one pass by the rules of case 2, on the paragraphs the full-text diff aligns (4.4): the page and the box are read as paragraphs (`bodyPieces`, which split as `splitParagraphs` does with no frontmatter looked for), the paragraphs that read the same on both sides are matched in order (`diffArrays`, 4.4 step 1), and between two matched paragraphs, where both sides hold words, the word diff finds each changed run, as in a box over those paragraphs, a paragraph break added or taken out among them; paragraphs taken out are deleted with one blank line beside them, the one after where a paragraph follows and otherwise the one before, exactly as emptying their box deletes them (case 2): the suggestions inside them and in that blank line go with them, and none of the paragraph beside them, whose first or last words the change only meets; paragraphs put in go after the paragraph before them, behind a blank line, or at the top of the body before the first one, followed by one; and a change to the blank lines alone replaces them, taking nothing of the paragraphs on either side, as do the blank lines round paragraphs put in where neither of 4.4's places fits them. Of the two places 4.4 allows a paragraph put in, the one that touches no suggestion is taken when the other touches one, so a suggestion on the first or last words of the paragraph beside it is not taken with it; where both do, the paragraph put in takes it whole, as a box takes a suggestion at the end of its paragraph when a paragraph is typed after it (C.112: a paragraph taken out first took a suggestion beside it whenever neither place was free of one, which emptying its box never does). Each changed run then becomes the author's own accepted hunk, supersedes a model suggestion it takes, replaces an earlier edit of the author's, accepts a suggestion typed exactly, or settles one whose file words were typed back, all as in case 2 (`planRegions`, which `planBlockEdit` and `planChapterEdit` share). Newlines at either end of the box are dropped, a box of spaces is empty and deletes the body, and an unchanged box closes with nothing done. The frontmatter, and the line breaks between it and the body and after the body, are never in a change. The store applies a plan only when it composes to exactly the chapter typed (`fullEditResult`: the text before the body, then the box, then the text after) with no hunks overlapping, and otherwise keeps the box open, as it is, with "Full edit could not be applied exactly as typed, so nothing was changed. Your text is still in the box: copy it somewhere safe, then press Cancel." It refuses, keeping the box, when the chapter no longer reads as it did when Full edit opened, as after a change on disk the watcher reloaded: "The chapter changed on disk while Full edit was open, so nothing was applied. Your text is still in the box: copy it, press Cancel, then open Full edit again." A property test checks, for generated chapters with and without frontmatter, suggestions of every source and decision, insertions among them, saved states, and edits of words, breaks and whole paragraphs, that the plan composes to exactly that, with no overlapping hunks, every new hunk accepted and of the author's own, and nothing before the first paragraph. Nothing reaches the chapter file before Save to chapter (CLAUDE.md rule 1).

### 7.6 Read-only while a review runs (Phase 5d)

A review's result replaces the working set, so a decision made while it runs would vanish when it lands, and nothing used to stop the author making one. Now, while a review of the open chapter runs:

- the prose, the margin notes, the filter chips with their eye and the side panel are faded and `inert`, so no click, key or hover reaches them; the review-pane keys are ignored; the Review menu, Actions' three bulk items and Save to chapter are disabled (Copy result, Export HTML and Show backups, in Actions, are not; `polish.7`, `rr.1`); the store refuses every decision and edit for that chapter whatever the caller (`isLocked` in `state/store.ts`);
- a status card floats at the bottom of the manuscript pane, outside the scroller so it is always in view, with the progress label and Cancel review;
- other chapters stay open to read and edit. If the author has moved to another chapter when the result arrives, it is saved as that chapter's newest review and a card says so, instead of pulling the author back; opening the chapter shows it. If the chapter file changed on disk while the model worked, the result is rebased onto the text the chapter has now before it is shown.

The review dialog also warns when the page holds decisions the chapter file does not (`unsavedDecisionCount`): the model reads the file, and its result replaces the working set, so changes that were never saved would drop out of view (they stay in History) and be suggested again. Since `apply.20` its blue button is "Save N changes, then review", which saves and then starts, and starting without them takes "Review without them" and a question (5.5); until then the warning carried a Save to chapter button that left the dialog open.

### 7.5 New chapter, and manual reviews

Paste mode was one dialog doing two unrelated jobs. It is now two:

- **New chapter**, from a "+" beside the Chapters heading (the folder button next to it opens the manuscript-folder picker). File name, an extension radio (`.md` default, `.txt`), and a textarea for the text. The name is checked against the folder as it is typed and Create stays disabled while it is taken or unusable; the file is created through `files:create` (6.1), then the list refreshes and the new chapter opens.
- **Submit manual review**, from Manual in the toolbar's Review menu (`polish.7`). Paste a corrected version of the chapter that is open, or load it from a file, and the full-text diff (4.4) turns every difference into a suggestion. The review is saved to the reviews folder immediately, like a generated one, and carries `generator.kind: 'manual'`. When the page has changes the chapter file does not (`apply.20`, `buildManualReview` in `src/renderer/state/reviewStart.ts`), Build review asks "Replace the open review?" with three answers (`manualBuildPrompt`): Cancel, "Build without them", and the blue "Save N changes, then build", which is focused, so Enter never leaves them behind. Save then build runs Save to chapter (6.3) and builds only on `saved` or `nothing-to-save`, against the review on screen as it is then, so the text is compared with the saved chapter; a save that does not get there builds nothing and leaves the dialog open, with a red box between the pasted text and the buttons: "The review was not built, because the changes were not saved." and what the save's cards said, as in 5.5; where the pasted text was made from the chapter without those changes, the new review suggests putting their old words back, which the question says. Build without them compares with the file as it is and leaves them in the review from <date>, in History. When the open review has decisions but none the file lacks (all saved, or only dismissed), the older two-way confirmation still says that the working set is being replaced and that the old review stays in History (`replaceReviewPrompt`); with no decisions it builds at once. A dialog closed while the save runs builds nothing.

### 7.7 Leaving a chapter and closing the window

**Leaving** (`apply.7`, 11.3 i). A chapter clicked in the list, the chapter New chapter has just made, and another review of the open chapter, chosen in History or the review selector, each replace the review on screen, so each goes through `beforeLeaving` in `src/renderer/state/leave.ts` first. It lets a save under way end (`pendingSave()`, 6.3), then, for another chapter, asks `leavePrompt`'s question when the page holds changes the chapter file does not have, or paragraph boxes whose text changed:

- **The question.** "Leave <chapter>?". It says how many changes are not saved to the chapter and that they are kept in this review: the chapter opens with the review last on screen (6.4, `apply.26`), so they are where the author left them. Open paragraph boxes are kept as they were left and open again when the author comes back to the chapter (C.53).
- **Another review of the chapter asks nothing** (`apply.26`, the author's decision replacing the "Open the review from <date>?" question of `apply.7`'s review). Decisions live in each review and are written as they are made, the chapter opens with whichever review was on screen last, and open boxes are kept for the chapter and go back on the review that comes on screen where their paragraph reads the same, the others set aside as a .txt (C.53). Once it is on screen, the page tells main (`reviews:shown`), which records it as the review the chapter opens with. Changes not saved to the chapter in the review it replaces stay there, and the dot, Save and this question then follow the new one, so the selector's entry for the old one counts them ("2 not saved to chapter", section 7).
- **The answers.** Cancel, Keep for later (focused, so Enter keeps) and the blue "Save N changes first", or "Apply and save first" when a box changed. Save first runs `saveChapter` with the boxes applied without a second question and goes on only when the file then reads like the page (`saved` or `nothing-to-save`); a save that fails or is blocked stays, and its card says why. Keep for later goes on: the decisions are in the review and the boxes in the chapter's drafts file, both written before anything else is read, and the list's dot marks the chapter meanwhile (6.4). Cancel, Escape, or another question replacing this one stays.
- **No question** when nothing would be left unsaved, while a review of the chapter runs (the page is read-only and its decisions are written), or for what is already on screen: re-clicking the open chapter, whichever of its reviews is on screen (the chapter opens with that one, since it is the last on screen), or the review on screen in History, only writes what is waiting and reloads nothing, so the focus, the filters and the find bar stay as they were (`isOpenTarget`; it used to reload the review and reset them). It no longer reads the chapter file again either, so a change on disk that the watcher missed, on a synced or network folder say, shows once the author opens another chapter and comes back. Until `apply.26` the open chapter clicked from an older review opened the review last decided in and asked "Open the review from <date>?" (`openedBy`, now gone). Of several clicks made while a save runs or a question is open, only the last goes ahead.
- **The question holds the keyboard.** While it is open the rest of the window is inert, so Tab stays among its buttons and cannot reach Save to chapter, the chapter list or History behind it; when it closes, the focus goes back to where it was, a list row or a paragraph box, if that is still on the page (section 7, Confirmation).
- **New chapter** creates the file before asking, so Cancel leaves the new chapter in the list, unopened.

Before `apply.7`, leaving asked only about open boxes, as "Discard paragraph edits?", and Discard threw them away.

**Closing the window** (`apply.8`, main; `apply.9`, the page; 11.3 i). The page pushes what a close would put at risk whenever it changes (`CloseGuardState` over `app:guard-state`), and the close guard in main (`createCloseGuard` in `src/main/closeGuard.ts`; `src/main/ipc.ts` builds the app's one guard and `createWindow` attaches the window) decides at the window's `close` event from the last state it has, without asking the page then, since a page that has stopped responding could not answer (C.54):

- **At once, with no IPC:** a close Restart now has allowed (`allowNextClose('update')`, `release.8b`) or the page has agreed to; a close after the page's process has gone (`onRendererGone`, from the one `render-process-gone` handler); any close once Windows has said the session is ending; and a close with nothing at risk (`needsAttention`). A page that has pushed nothing since it loaded counts as nothing at risk; the page pushes as soon as it has loaded (`apply.9`), so this is only the moment before.
- **Otherwise the close is held.** The window is restored if minimised, shown and focused, and when it was not in front its taskbar button flashes too, until the close ends. A quiet test window (`dev.1`) is shown without the foreground, a minimised one is left minimised, and its button does not flash; the native box below is outside that switch and may raise the window and take the foreground (C.61). The page is sent `app:close-requested` once, with `quitting` when the whole app was asked to quit, and reports on `app:close-status`: `received` within 3 s, then `prompting` within 10 s of that, once its question (`closePrompt`, or its "Still writing your decisions") is on screen.
- **The native box.** When the page misses either time, or the author closes again before its question is up, main shows a box over the window (`unresponsiveDetail`, through `messageBoxOptions`): "<APP_NAME> is not responding" or "<APP_NAME> is still finishing", what the last state says is at risk, Wait and Close anyway. Wait is the default, and Escape answers Wait. Wait leaves the page its time and sets no new timer, so a page that is slow but working does not bring the box back every few seconds; another close opens it again at once. Close anyway destroys the window, which does not wait for the page, and quits the app when the close came from a quit. When the page answers after all (`received`, `prompting` or its decision), the box is taken away through its AbortSignal and whatever it was answered is ignored, since the page's own question is then on screen; `received` starts the 10 s. Once the question is up, a further close only brings the window forward. A box that fails to open counts as Wait.
- **The decision** (`app:close-decision`). True closes the window on the next tick, so the reply reaches the page first; when the close came from a quit it calls `app.quit()` again instead, since holding the close cancelled the quit, and that close goes through. False, or anything but a plain true, keeps the window and clears the quitting flag, so the next close asks afresh and a later plain close does not quit. A status or a decision with no close under way changes nothing, so the question Restart now asks of its own (`prepareToLeaveApp('update')`) cannot close the window, though false still clears the quitting flag.
- **A page that goes** during a close takes its box and timers with it, and the window closes, or the app quits, as the author asked, since nothing more can be saved; `onRendererGone` returns true then, so `hardening.4` offers no Reload or Quit for that window. A page that loads again, or pushes a state again, is asked again.
- **A reload is a new page.** A reload keeps the page's process, so no `render-process-gone` comes, but the document is new: the dev server's reload, Ctrl+R in development, `hardening.4`'s Reload window. When the main frame commits a new document (`did-navigate`), the guard forgets what the old page pushed, as it does for a new window, so a close before the new page pushes goes through at once. A close under way ends without closing: its box and timers go, the taskbar stops flashing, and the quit it came from is forgotten, as with the page's false. Its request went to the old document, which can no longer answer, and the reload came after the close, so the author is looking at the page they reloaded; the next close is asked of the new page. A late answer from the old page changes nothing, and an allowance stays, since it is the window's. Not `did-start-navigation`, which also fires for a navigation `will-navigate` then refuses, leaving the page where it was (C.54).
- **For Restart now** (`release.8b`, `runUpdateInstall` in `src/main/updateInstall.ts`): `allowNextClose('update')`, called before the installer quits the app (11.3 n), takes over a close under way; the function it returns takes the allowance back after an install that failed; and the allowance is used by one close, even one the page's own `beforeunload` then cancels. When electron-updater says the installer could not start after it has already queued the app's quit, main's `before-quit` cancels that one quit (`updateHoldsQuit`, C.94), so the window is neither closed nor asked about. In a `dev:clean` window with the fake update, a page that had pushed 3 decisions not saved closed by the install's quit with `close.allowed reason=update` and no `close.asked`; after an install that could not start, the quit was held (`update.install.quit-held`), and a WM_CLOSE was then asked about (`close.asked`) as before.
- **Shutdown is never blocked** (C.55). `query-session-end` and `session-end` only send `app:flush`, for the page to write its waiting review and drafts writes at once, and neither is prevented. After `session-end` every close goes through at once and any box goes; after `query-session-end` alone a close is still asked about, since the session may yet go on.
- **One quitting flag**, the guard's: `before-quit` sets it (`onBeforeQuit`), the page's false clears it, and `isQuitting` reads it for `hardening.4`.
- The log gets `close.asked`, `close.unresponsive`, `close.box-answer`, `close.decided` and the like, with the stage, the answer and `quitting` only, never the chapter (11.3 m).

**The page's half** (`apply.9`): `src/renderer/state/closeGuard.ts`, which App installs with the IPC calls, the two writers, `saveChapter` and the review's Cancel (History as last read until `apply.26`, which needed it only to date an older review), so it needs no DOM and is tested in node.

- **The push.** `closeGuardStateOf` reads the store: the open chapter, `unsavedDecisionCount`, boxes whose text changed, a review of the chapter running (`locked`) or of any (`reviewRunning`), typed dialog text (`hasDialogText`), and `writesPending`, which counts a review or drafts write waiting, under way, held over a drafts file that cannot be read, or failed and not made since, and a Save to chapter under way. A write that failed used to leave nothing pending, so a close after it went at once; the writers now keep the value until a write for it succeeds (`failures`, `retry` in `src/renderer/state/persist.ts`). The state is pushed once the page has loaded and then whenever it changes, in the same task as the change: a store subscription, and `call` sends before its first await. So a close that comes while the page is still busy with the decision that changed it is already held. In a `dev:clean` window, one evaluation accepted a suggestion and kept the page busy for 1.5 s, WM_CLOSE posted during it; the close was held, asked about once the page was free, and the decision kept. With the push put off to a timer, the same steps closed at once and the review on disk lost the decision.
- **The request.** `app:close-requested` runs `prepareToLeaveApp('close')`, which says `received` at once. A question already open (the leave prompt, or "Apply paragraph edits first?" from Ctrl+S) is answered Cancel, so a save waiting on it ends rather than running out the clock. The save under way and both writers' flushes, failed writes queued again first, then race 5 s (`WRITES_WAIT_MS`). The page stays live meanwhile, and a writer holds a value that arrives during its write for its own 700 ms and lets the flush end without it, so while the store still counts a write or a Save to chapter after a round and none has failed, the page goes round again within the same 5 s, each round in a task of its own so the clock still runs. A dismissal, a comment or a Save pressed while the writes run is therefore on disk before the window goes, even with nothing to ask (a review fix the same day). Past that, or when a write failed, the page asks "Still writing your decisions" (`stillWritingPrompt`): why, in the words of the writers' cards, which sit under the dialog, what else closing would lose, then Wait, in Cancel's place and focused, so Enter and Escape give it, and Close anyway. Wait tries the writes again for another 5 s. Then `closePrompt`'s question, with `prompting` sent first, in the confirm dialog that leaving uses, saying the decisions are kept in this review, the one the chapter opens with (`apply.26`; until then it dated an older review by History, `olderReviewFrom`). Every layout of the page has that dialog, with the rest of the page inert under it: the Setup screen can show over a review with changes not saved, and a close from there used to leave the question in the store with nothing on screen, while main, told `prompting`, showed no box either. With nothing to ask, only writes having been waiting, it answers true at once.
- **The answers.** Cancel stays. Save and close, or Apply, save and close, runs `saveChapter` with the boxes applied; that save is the one under way, so it is timed and asked about as the writes are, and the window goes only on `saved` or `nothing-to-save`, a save that did not get there leaving the window open with its card. Close, keep for later, or Close anyway, stops a running review. Every answer that closes writes what is waiting once more, against the same 5 s, before answering true. Each run ends with `app:close-decision`: false on Cancel, on a save that did not get there, or when something threw, with a card saying so.
- **Restart now** (`release.9`, `restartNow` in `src/renderer/state/updates.ts`) is refused while a review runs, of this chapter or another, with a card under `update-problem`, "Restart after the review finishes. Restarting now would stop the review that is running.", asking nothing; otherwise it calls `prepareToLeaveApp('update')`, which asks the same question and resolves true to go on. It reports no status, since no close is under way, and its decision changes nothing in main but the quitting flag. A call while a run is under way shares its answer, and a close request meanwhile is told `received`, and `prompting` when the question is up. A review started while the writes ran is refused in the same words once the answer is in. Then `UpdateOverlay` covers the window and `update:install` goes to main; an answer, or a pushed state, other than `installing` takes the overlay away, the update card says why, and the focus goes back to the Restart now that was pressed (section 7, Every dialog holds the keyboard). One Restart now runs at a time. In a `dev:clean` window with the fake update and a paragraph box changed, it asked "Close <APP_NAME>?" with Cancel, "Close, keep for later" and "Apply, save and close"; Cancel stayed, with no overlay and no install; "Close, keep for later" wrote the box to the chapter's drafts, showed the overlay and quit through `close.allowed reason=update` with no `close.asked`.
- **Shutdown.** `app:flush` queues failed writes again and flushes both writers, asking nothing (C.55).

**When the page fails** (`hardening.4`, C.81). Each way is logged (11.3 m), and nothing is written but through the page's own writers:

- **An error nothing caught**, in the page (a window `error` event) or in main (`uncaughtException`), leaves an error card with Show diagnostics: "Something went wrong in this window, and what you did last may not have finished. If it happens again, Show diagnostics has the details for a message or a GitHub issue." (`PAGE_ERROR_TEXT` under the key `page-error`), or the same about "Lapidary's background process" (`MAIN_ERROR_NOTICE` over `app:notice`, under `main-notice`), each at most once a minute whatever the errors, so a card closed is not brought back by another error that minute, which the log has (`PAGE_CARD_INTERVAL_MS`, `NOTICE_INTERVAL_MS`). A promise rejected with no handler is only logged, in either process. The same error again within a minute and Chromium's ResizeObserver notice are dropped (`createErrorFilter` in `src/shared/diagnostics/errorFilter.ts`), and each process writes at most 30 such lines a minute (`createRateCap`; the page's go to main as `log:renderer`, `createRendererLog` in `src/main/crash.ts`).
- **Drawing the page fails.** The `ErrorBoundary` round App shows `CrashFallback` in its place, laid out as the Setup screen: "Something went wrong", "This window ran into an error Lapidary did not expect, and cannot go on showing your chapter." It ends a close the failed page had under way and answers Cancel to a question that page had open, so the close is kept and that page's run asks nothing more, its close question with Save least of all; then it writes what the review and paragraph writers hold, failed writes queued again first (`writeAfterCrash`: `flushReviewWrites`, `flushDraftWrites`), and says "Your decisions and any open paragraph boxes are written. Reload window starts this window again, and they are there when you open the chapter.", or names a write that failed in the words of its card, with Try again. Reload window, blue and focused, is held until the writes end; it has the focus, with its ring, as the page opens, once the failed page's question has gone when one was open, and after Try again, whose link goes with the failure it sat in (`createCrashPage` in `src/renderer/state/crashPage.ts`); under it, Diagnostics, a line asking for the text with a message or an issue, and the report with Copy diagnostics (`DiagnosticsPanel`, Copy as a plain button). The page takes the close guard over (`installCrashedPageGuard`, `crashedPageState`): it names no chapter and counts nothing as unsaved, since decisions are kept in their review and boxes in their drafts once written and nothing can be saved to the chapter from here, so a close goes through at once unless a write is still waiting or a review is running, and then asks "Still writing your decisions" or the close question with Close anyway and no Save, in the question the page draws itself. An error in that page too, on its first render or a later one (the boundary catches once, C.81, so React hands it to the root's `onUncaughtError`), leaves a heading, a line and a focused Reload window over the empty window in plain DOM (`showBareFallback`), after the same writes, with the guard taken over but asking nothing: a close gives the writes their 5 s and goes.
- **The page's process goes** (`render-process-gone`). The one handler tells the close guard first, and a close under way then goes ahead (above). Otherwise, unless the app is quitting, Windows is ending the session (`isSessionEnding`), the process exited cleanly or the window has gone too, main shows a box over the window (`afterRendererGone`, `rendererGoneBox`): "Lapidary's window stopped working", the cause (it ran out of memory; it was ended from outside the app; it could not start; Windows stopped it because its code failed an integrity check; or it stopped unexpectedly), that decisions and open paragraph boxes are written as they are made, so Reload window starts the window again and they are there when the chapter is opened, apart from changes made in the second before it stopped, and "Quit closes Lapidary." Reload window is first, the default and what Escape gives; Quit calls `app.quit()`. A box that fails to open reloads. The box goes with its window, and an answer that comes after the window closed or the app began quitting does nothing.

## 9. Risks and things the implementer must verify

1. **Structured output and `maxTurns`.** The Agent SDK may satisfy `outputFormat` through an internal tool call and retries. If `maxTurns: 1` prevents a valid result, raise it to 3 and keep tools removed.
2. **Removing tools.** `Options` has `allowedTools` and `disallowedTools`; check `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts` for a top-level `tools` option and for the current built-in tool names before hardcoding the list. The call must never be able to read or write the vault.
3. **SDK inside Electron main.** _Superseded by C.42: there is no SDK; the app spawns the user's `claude` itself._ The SDK spawns the bundled native binary, so Node on PATH is not required. Verify in `npm run dev`. If it spawns through the JS runtime instead, set `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` in `options.env` or pass `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` pointing at a native `claude.exe`. Never point it at the npm `claude.cmd` shim.
4. **Packaging.** _Superseded by C.42: nothing of Anthropic's is packaged._ The native binary had to be unpacked from asar (`asarUnpack`).
5. **Model availability by plan.** Populate the model list from `q.supportedModels()`; do not assume `opus` exists on every plan.
6. **Refusal fallbacks.** Opus 5 can fall back to Opus 4.8 automatically when a safety classifier flags content, and some categories refuse with no fallback. Fiction with dark themes may trigger this occasionally. Show the explanation and record the actual model from `modelUsage`.
7. **Obsidian concurrent edits.** Detection is solid; prevention is not possible. Document the workflow.
8. **Policy.** The app is given away as open source and runs Claude Code. What keeps that within Anthropic's published terms as far as they can be read (sources and dates in Appendix A; Appendix D 8 and 21, C.42):
   - Each user installs, updates and signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, with Anthropic's installer and Anthropic's sign-in flow, on their own Claude plan or API key. Their usage is billed to them, and the app pays for, resells or intermediates none of it.
   - The app ships nothing of Anthropic's, neither binary nor library (`release.12` checks the package). It never reads, stores, displays or proxies Claude credentials. An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` already in the user's environment reaches Claude Code only through the inherited environment, unread and unchanged (`buildClaudeEnv`). It never starts a sign-in; Setup only shows commands for the user to run (CLAUDE.md rule 2 (a)).
   - It never sets or overrides Claude Code's client or entrypoint identity. The Usage Policy that takes effect on 2026-11-12 bars services that "misrepresent the product or client being used". `buildClaudeEnv` adds one variable, `CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS`, and `test/main/claudeOptions.test.ts` pins that (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
   - The author has not accepted the Commercial Terms (Appendix D 8). The legal page asks for them when Claude Code runs "in your products or services", and also says it does not prevent an end user signing in to the unmodified binary with their own subscription. No Anthropic page says which side of that line an app like this one falls on.
   - Anthropic may enforce its usage restrictions without prior notice, and acted against third-party tools in 2026 (Appendix A). If that happens to this app, Claude reviews may stop counting against the plan and be billed as extra usage, as third-party tools were in April 2026, or may fail. The OpenAI provider still works, and chapters and saved reviews are not affected.
   - The README carries `DISCLAIMER` (an independent project that runs Claude Code; can also review with ChatGPT, on each user's own ChatGPT plan, through OpenAI's Sign in with ChatGPT, where it said "It can also use OpenAI's API" until `codex.6`'s review; not made, endorsed or sponsored by Anthropic or OpenAI; no Anthropic software) and `AI_OUTPUT_NOTICE`, both from `src/shared/branding.ts` and checked by `test/branding.test.ts`.
   - No Claude, Anthropic or OpenAI marks in the app's name or logo (`test/branding.test.ts` checks the name; the Seam logo has no lettering). Claude Code is named only in plain text, as the tool the app runs.

## 10. Guidelines file

`resources/GUIDELINES.default.md` is the author-editable "CLAUDE.md for edits". It is copied to `<manuscript>/GUIDELINES.md` on first use and sent verbatim after the static instructions. The author fills in the style sheet section (spelling variant, Oxford comma, character names, invented terms).

`ensureGuidelinesFile` creates it with `COPYFILE_EXCL`, so an existing file is never touched, and only a .md or .txt path is accepted. Review with AI, Settings and the welcome guide offer it two buttons (`polish.3`, C.101). **Open** goes to the system's app for the file type, which is Obsidian when the author has made Obsidian the app for `.md` files, and when there is none shows the file in its folder and says so (`guidelines:open`, which the page sends nothing, is `openGuidelines` in `src/main/openGuidelines.ts`: `ensureGuidelinesFile`, then `openGuidelinesFile`). **Open folder** shows the file in its folder (`shell:reveal` with `guidelines`). Each creates the file from the template first when it is missing, and nothing is made or opened for a file that is not `.md` or `.txt`. Until `polish.3` the two were Open in Obsidian, which handed the system an `obsidian://open?path=` link, and Open (`setup.10b`, Appendix C "Open in Obsidian names no vault"). The read-only `guidelines:status` reports `{path, exists, styleSheet}`, where `styleSheetStatus` calls the section `blank` while it holds only the template's labels and placeholders, `filled` once any entry has a value, and `missing` when there is no "## Style sheet" heading (`setup.10`).

## 11. Release 1.0: Lapidary

Written 2026-10-14 for implementing agents who were not part of the release discussion. It turns the 21 ideas agreed that day, plus one from the same day's round 6 feedback (small changes, 11.7), into milestones M0 to M12. Two answers the same day changed it: the name is Lapidary, not Igneous (Appendix D 1), and the app ships no Claude Code binary and the author accepts no Anthropic terms, so each user installs Claude Code themselves (Appendix D 8). Sections 0 to 10 still describe the app; a task that changes one of them edits that section in the same commit. Task ids such as `brand.4` and `apply.9` are stable: cite them in commit messages and tick them here. A task that absorbed others names them, and the absorbed ids are never done separately.

Rules for every task in this section:

- **Order.** Milestones run in order unless marked "can overlap". Inside a milestone, follow the listed order.
- **Hot files, one task at a time.** `src/main/index.ts`, `src/main/ipc.ts`, `src/shared/ipc.ts`, `src/main/providers/claude.ts`, `src/renderer/App.tsx`, `src/renderer/state/store.ts`, `src/renderer/components/ReviewDialog.tsx`, `src/renderer/components/SettingsDialog.tsx`, `src/renderer/styles/app.css`, `electron-builder.config.cjs` and `package.json` each receive edits from four to six workstreams. Tasks touching them run one after another, never as parallel agents.
- **Rule 7 and numbering.** New Appendix C entries take the next free number at commit time (C.38 was next on 2026-10-14) and are cited by title, never by a pre-assigned number. Once `release.6a` lands, every user-visible change also adds a line under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Baseline.** On 2026-10-14 the working tree passed 364 tests in 26 files, typecheck, lint and format check. Counts only go up.
- **Safe verification.** Real-window runs use `npm run dev:clean` once `setup.15` exists, with `--quiet` since `dev.1` so the window stays out of the author's way (Appendix C "Quiet test windows"); before that, `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_USER_DATA=.dev-userdata REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=9222 npm run dev` (C.8, C.14). Saves go to a copy at `.dev-userdata/vault/`, never to the tracked `samples/`. Packaged runs use `dist/win-unpacked/Lapidary.exe --isolated-user-data=<scratch dir>` only. CDP key and wheel events skip Electron's input hooks (C.35); native close and file drags need real OS input.
- **Never, as an agent:** read `~/.claude/.credentials.json` or any `secrets.json`; run against the author's real settings; create Windows accounts, type credentials or sign in; click through SmartScreen; change OS or security settings; publish a release, change repo visibility or settings, force-push, or send a message. Those steps are marked **(author)**.
- **Commits.** Commit and push only as the author decided in `release.1`. Otherwise leave each milestone in the working tree with a proposed message.
- **Author sittings.** The author's hands-on steps are grouped: **A** (M0) decisions and the logo; **B** (M4) approvals to publish the repo; **C** (after M7) one UI session: theme contact sheet, scroll A/B, folder picker, the Obsidian save check, prompt wording; **D** (M11) the release session on a clean Windows account, then the 1.0.1 update proof.

### 11.0 Goal and scope

**Done** means a public, MIT-licensed repo `MichaelBradetLegris/lapidary` whose CI built and published `v1.0.0` as a GitHub Release, and on a clean Windows account: the friend downloads one installer, gets past the browser and SmartScreen warnings by following the README, installs Claude Code and signs in by following the Setup screen alone, reviews and saves a chapter, and receives `v1.0.1` through the in-app updater. The app is called Lapidary, has its own logo, dark mode, an unmistakable Save to chapter, a backup before every save, a close prompt, guards against encoding and Obsidian-syntax damage, a log file and Copy diagnostics.

**For** two people: the author (Windows 11, Claude Max) and a friend who writes novels in English in Obsidian, OS unknown. Windows first; macOS and Linux only if `files.17` says he needs them.
