**Out of scope for 1.0, and cuts** (with the reason, so nobody rebuilds them):

- Automatic save to chapter: Save stays the one explicit write (CLAUDE.md rule 1), and background writes would race Obsidian's autosave and sync.
- In-app restore or Compare of a backup: restore is by hand; Compare is a follow-up that must never become the chapter's current review.
- Portable exe: re-extracts about 600 MB into `%TEMP%` per launch and cannot update. Local tests use `dist/win-unpacked`.
- Code signing unless Smart App Control blocks the friend (`release.14`, costs money). macOS and Linux builds unless he needs them.
- Electron fuses (from `hardening.9`), build-provenance attestation, a custom title bar, Windows forced colours, the version viewer (section 8 Phase 6).
- An in-app sign-in launcher: the legal page bars offering Claude login. Setup shows a command to copy.
- Bundling Claude Code (author decision, Appendix D 8): the installer contains no `claude.exe` and the author accepts no Anthropic terms. Each user installs Claude Code with Anthropic's own installer and signs in with their own account. The SDK's JavaScript library goes too (11.6 question 21): the app runs the user's `claude` command directly (11.3 q, `cli.1`).
- Cut tasks: `setup.3`'s `claudeExecutable` setting and newest-wins choice (untested SDK/CLI pairs); `setup.16` expiry warning (the CLI may never emit it on the SDK channel); `theme.11` (covered by `hardening.3a`); `hardening.14` (superseded by `files.4`); `release.15` (folded into `setup.3`); `hardening.7`'s domain allowlist, link-scan test, IPC sender check and permission handlers (no remote content; `opensource.12` covers navigation); `hardening.4`'s rescue plan (writers already flush); a second About surface; the `theme.3`/`theme.4` zero-pixel gate (the CSS test and contact sheet stay); `files.7`'s pair and line combination rules and subset property (the touching rule stays; a joint case needs two model edits that combine, visible in the ghost text first); `brand.8` and the old `release.1` repo rename and history rewrite (moot under a fresh repo); portable-specific Setup wording and smoke tests; a custom NSIS uninstall macro for the updater cache (documented instead); `hardening.11b`, the OpenAI real-key check (Appendix D 16), moot since `codex.6` took out the key.
- `apply.18` (a tracked Claude Code spawner) becomes measure-first: `sdk.mjs` spawns without `detached`, so libuv's kill-on-close job object should end `claude.exe` with the app. Build the tracker only if the measurement finds a leftover process. Measured on 2026-10-17 against the user's own `claude.exe`, which replaced `sdk.mjs` in C.42: nothing was left, so there is no tracker (C.56).

### 11.1 Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why |
| -------- | ------ | --- |
| Name | Lapidary, written only as `APP_NAME` in `src/shared/branding.ts`; a case-insensitive guard test enforces it | Lapidary work cuts and polishes stone, obsidian included, and lapidary prose is polished and concise. Igneous was dropped because two Markdown apps for Obsidian users took it in October 2026 (Appendix D 1). Renames stay one edit (C.21) |
| Frozen identifiers | `APP_ID` `dev.bradetlegris.manuscript-review`; package name `manuscript-review`; `APP_DATA_DIR` `ai-grammar-checker`; `APP_REPOSITORY` `MichaelBradetLegris/lapidary`. Never change after 1.0 | The NSIS uninstall GUID and AUMID derive from appId; the install folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\manuscript-review` and updater cache `%LOCALAPPDATA%\manuscript-review-updater` from the package name (`app-builder-lib` `targetUtil.js`, `appInfo.js`); every installed `app-update.yml` holds the slug. A package name unlike `APP_DATA_DIR` keeps `--delete-app-data` away from the data folder |
| Logo | Seam, the original pebble with its rim, ghost line, line of type and dotted underline, in the turquoise palette of 11.3 (o) (Appendix D 2); the ember palette is the alternative | No letterform, not purple, clearly unlike Obsidian's tall faceted crystal, visible on a dark taskbar |
| Repository | A fresh public `lapidary` repo, created when the author asks (Appendix D 3), one root commit by the GitHub noreply address; the private `ai-grammar-checker` is archived; branch `main`, remote `origin` | Old commits carry the gmail and a profile path, and `wip` does not build |
| Licence | MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Michael Bradet-Legris" | Short, compatible with everything shipped |
| Anthropic terms | None accepted (author decision, Appendix D 8). The app ships no Claude Code binary; each user installs Claude Code and signs in with their own account or key | The author will not bind himself to Anthropic's Commercial Terms for a free tool a handful of people use. Appendix A has the research. The SDK library is replaced by direct calls to the user's `claude` (11.3 q) |
| Claude wording | Provider label "Claude"; plain text says it runs the Claude Code the user installed, signed in with their own account or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `DISCLAIMER` and `AI_OUTPUT_NOTICE` in the README; no control starts a login | The legal page's section on products that run Claude Code allows a plain-text statement that a product runs Claude Code, and no Claude Code or Anthropic name or logo in its own name or logo; it also bars offering Claude login (Appendix A). The SDK branding guidance is for SDK integrations, which the app no longer is |
| Claude binary | The user's own installed Claude Code, run directly as a command (11.3 q); no Anthropic package is a dependency or ships. The installed version must be at least `MIN_CLAUDE_CODE`, the version the flags were verified against, else Setup says to run `claude update` | Matches the author's decisions (Appendix D 8 and 21). Claude Code updates itself, so new models need no app release. The author's own copy had stalled at 2.1.266 on 2026-10-14, so the version check matters |
| Launch check | `claude auth status` plus the `initialize` handshake, which sends no prompt (an SDK handshake until `cli.1`); failures from real runs outrank "ready" | Today it says ready when signed out and spends two model requests per launch |
| Default model | `default` for new settings, passed as no `--model` flag; a Pro account gets Sonnet preselected; existing `opus` kept; Pro accounts see a limits note; `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` removed from the child env | `default` is Opus 5.5 on Pro since CLI 2.1.280 (model-config docs), so the note does the real work |
| Dev switches | Read only in `src/main/devSwitches.ts`; dev builds only; packaged builds accept `--isolated-user-data=<dir>` | A shell-profile variable must never redirect the stored ChatGPT sign-in (the stored OpenAI key until `codex.6`) |
| Theme | `nativeTheme.themeSource` from a `theme` setting; CSS tokens swap under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`; no IPC | Electron 44 drives the media query and the Windows title bar (DWM attribute measured) live; the CSP forbids a pre-paint script |
| Scroll bolding | Opaque token backgrounds on every scroller (C.48) | Measured: only an opaque scroller gets its own LCD-text layer |
| Unsaved signal | `unsavedDecisionCount` on the button ("Save 3 changes to chapter"), status bar and a dot before the chapter name; `store.dirty` removed | One exact measure; "Review saved" read as "chapter saved" |
| Leaving and closing | Save / Keep for later / Cancel, Keep for later focused (closing with nothing to keep offers Close anyway / Cancel, Cancel focused); a main-driven close handshake with 3 s and 10 s native fallbacks; shutdown never blocked | Nothing is discarded; a hung renderer cannot trap the window |
| Drafts | Open paragraph boxes persist under `<userData>/drafts` and come back, or are set aside as .txt | Updates, crashes and power loss skip every prompt |
| Backups | Before a Save that changes bytes, copy the old bytes to `<userData>/backups/`; keep newest 20 plus the first of each day for 30 days; no backup, no save | The friend may not use git; userData is never synced or indexed |
| Ctrl+S | Runs Save to chapter, except behind a modal, on repeat, in a paragraph box (card: press Done first), while the suggestion editor is open (card: press its Save first) or while locked | Reflex key; gating stops it cancelling prompts or saving without words still being typed |
| Encoding | Refuse non-UTF-8 files with advice per class; 4 MiB cap | Today bad bytes become U+FFFD, which Save would write |
| Obsidian syntax | App-owned prompt rule plus a pure guard that keeps out untouched model suggestions touching protected syntax (`keptOut`) | Deterministic and testable; compose unchanged |
| Reviews and files | A review belongs to its `sourcePath`; moved or renamed chapters adopt reviews by strict rules; `files:save` writes only chapters in the manuscript folder or opened this session | Today same-named chapters share reviews and Save can write the wrong file |
| Logging | Hand-rolled 1 MiB rotating log, scalar fields only, errors through one policy | No dependency; content cannot leak through structure |
| Installer | One-click per-user NSIS x64, `${productName}-Setup-${version}.exe`; `deleteAppDataOnUninstall` false | No UAC ever; it is exactly what the updater re-runs |
| Signing | Unsigned 1.0; Azure Artifact Signing only if Smart App Control blocks the friend (**about US$9.99/month, ongoing**) | SmartScreen warns at two-user scale even when signed; SignPath Foundation excludes proprietary components |
| Updates | electron-updater 6.8.10 and electron-builder 26.17.0 pinned (v26 line); GitHub provider, no token; check 15 s after launch and daily (toggle); download on consent; install only by Restart now with a visible installer; notify-only off Windows | Silent install-on-quit can half-install; 6.8.10 fixes a stale-blockmap bug |
| Versioning | SemVer from package.json; tags `vX.Y.Z`; 0.1.0 goes to 1.0.0; Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 | One number drives notes, About and the updater |
| CI | Check job on windows-latest and ubuntu-latest; Windows package job; draft release on `v*` tags with SHA-pinned actions and no cache | Free on a public repo |
| OpenAI | Sign in with ChatGPT alone, on the user's own ChatGPT plan (`codex.2`, `codex.3`); default never a -pro, -codex, -deep-research or -chat model; no API key since `codex.6` | Hobbyists will not pay per token, the author's word on 2026-10-24; the plan they already have pays |
| Telemetry | The app sends no analytics; Claude Code's own telemetry is documented with its opt-outs, not switched off | `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` also disables feature flags |
| Security | Single-instance lock, navigation and file-drop guard, CSP additions, IPC path guards (C.85); no fuses | Proportionate for a local app with no remote content |
| Electron | Latest 44.x before the cut: 44.9.3 pinned since 2026-10-21 (`release.21`; 44.7.2 was the latest on 2026-10-14), never a new major without a task of its own | Current Chromium fixes for the first install |
| macOS, Linux | Conditional. macOS arm64 ad-hoc signed, notify-only updates; Apple Developer Program (**US$99/year**) only if the author wants auto-updates there | Notarization costs money; no Anthropic binary ships either way |

- [x] `files.21` **Comments and labels follow their paragraphs through a save** (done 2026-10-15; C.44) (reported by the author 2026-10-14). Pure and store code; may land any time after M2.
  - **Cause.** `markSaved` in `src/renderer/state/store.ts` folds the decisions into a new base with `commitDecisions`, which moves each hunk's offsets. It leaves every comment's `paragraph` and every hunk's `paragraph` label unchanged.
  - **Effect.** A save that adds, joins or deletes a paragraph shifts every later comment by one; the usual case is a split made with the paragraph pen. The author split 42-43 after a paste from LibreOffice Writer into Obsidian had lost line breaks. His comments marked 63 and 77 then quoted text that sits in 64 and 78. Changes made in Obsidian are not affected: `rebaseReview` already remaps comments, by the paragraph's first 40 characters and then by the quote.
  - **Fix.** A pure `remapAfterCommit(review, committed)` in `src/shared/review.ts` maps each old paragraph's start offset through the committed hunks. A comment follows its paragraph, or, when that paragraph was split, the part that contains its `quote`. Hunk `paragraph` labels are recomputed from their new offsets with `paragraphIndexAt`. `markSaved` uses it.
  - **Repair.** A load-time `repairCommentAnchors`, run by `upgradeLoadedReview`, moves a comment whose `quote` is missing from its paragraph to the nearest paragraph that contains it. Reviews already shifted, such as the author's current chapters, then correct themselves.
  - **Records.** PLAN 3 and 6.3; Appendix C "Comments follow their paragraphs through a save".
  - **Verify.** `test/shared/review.test.ts`: split, join and delete a paragraph through accepted manual hunks and save; every comment and hunk label then points at the paragraph holding its quote. A fast-check property over random paragraph splits and joins. The repair moves a shifted comment and leaves a correct one untouched. Real window: split a paragraph with the pen and Save; the margin notes further down stay beside their quotes.

(2) `git tag -a pre-public <that commit> -m 'Tree published as the first public commit'`; run `npm run check:public` on a checkout of `pre-public` and, typed only in the terminal, `git grep -nI -i <username> pre-public` (no output); `git push ai-grammar-checker master pre-public`. (3) In a scratch clone: repo-local `git config user.name "Michael Bradet-Legris"` and `git config user.email "45394569+MichaelBradetLegris@users.noreply.github.com"` first; `git checkout --orphan main pre-public`; commit "Lapidary: first public commit (pre-1.0)", signed as decided in step 1; `git log -1 --format='%an <%ae> / %cn <%ce>'` shows the noreply address twice; `git diff pre-public main --stat` empty. (4) `gh repo create MichaelBradetLegris/lapidary --public --disable-wiki --description 'Review AI-suggested copyedits to your novel, one change at a time'`; set the clone's `origin` to `git@github.com:MichaelBradetLegris/lapidary.git`; `git push -u origin main`; topics obsidian, writing, copyediting, proofreading, electron. (5) `PUT repos/.../private-vulnerability-reporting`, `PUT .../vulnerability-alerts`, PATCH secret scanning and push protection on, a branch ruleset `main` (deletion, non_fast_forward) on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`, `PUT .../immutable-releases`; no tag ruleset, no automated security fixes. (6) Working folder: the same repo-local `user.name` and `user.email` as step 3 first, since agents keep committing and pushing here; `git remote add origin ...`, `git fetch origin`, `git switch -c main --track origin/main`; rebase any other branch with `git rebase --onto main pre-public <branch> --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author'`, so no rebased commit keeps the personal address; from now on, before every push, `git log origin/main..HEAD --format='%ae %ce'` shows only the noreply address; do not rename the folder. (7) `gh repo archive MichaelBradetLegris/ai-grammar-checker --yes`, then `git tag -d pre-public`, `git branch -D master`, `git remote remove ai-grammar-checker`. - [ ] `files.24` **Online-only files in a synced folder** (found by the `files.12` review, 2026-10-19). On Windows libuv may report every reparse point as a link in `readdir`'s file types, and `listChapters` follows only plain files and folders (6.1), so OneDrive's Files On-Demand placeholders, and other sync tools' online-only files, may be left out of the chapter list. No agent run may use the author's OneDrive, so: the author makes a scratch folder in his OneDrive with two short chapters, sets one to Free up space (online only) and the other to Always keep on this device, and gives an agent only that folder's path. The agent records, under Node 24 and in a `dev:clean` window pointed at that folder, what `fs.readdir(folder, { withFileTypes: true })` and `fs.lstat` say of each file and whether both chapters are listed. If the placeholder is left out, `listChapters` lists it while real links stay out as 6.1 says, for example by asking `fs.lstat` about an entry reported as a link (libuv's `lstat` should call a reparse point a link only when it is a symbolic link, a junction or an app alias, which the same check confirms on the placeholder), with a test on a stubbed directory entry; either way 6.1 and 6.6 record the result. Opening an online-only chapter makes OneDrive download it, which is OneDrive's doing.

Its rules start from the author's two converters in `../Markdown-Converter`, their folder beside this repository's (`markdown_to_royalroad.html`, `md_to_html.js`, `converter.html`), read before writing, and go further: (1) paragraphs from lines, a blank line a paragraph break, and a run of lines with no blank line between them a tight block, `<p style="margin-bottom: 0">` on all but its last (the author's status screens), a lone paragraph plain `<p>`; (2) `# ` to `<h1>`, `## ` and `### ` to their headings; (3) `***`, `**` and `*` to `<strong><em>`, `<strong>` and `<em>`, and `___`, `__` and `_` the same only when the markers pair on the line, since `_` is also a character in words; `~~` to `<s>`; `==` to `<mark>` only if Royal Road keeps it, else the words alone; (4) a line of `*`, `***`, `---` or `___` alone to `<hr />`; (5) `->` to →, `---` to —, `--` to –, and a backslash escape to the character it escapes; (6) curly quotes to straight ones as the author's converter does, as an option on by default until he says otherwise (`straightQuotes`); (7) the frontmatter, `%%` comments and HTML comments dropped, `[[target|alias]]` to its alias and `[[target]]` to its target, `[text](url)` to `<a>`, a tag and a block ID dropped, a footnote's words kept and its mark dropped, a callout's title and body as a `<blockquote>`, `> ` quotes as `<blockquote>`, `- ` and `1. ` lists as `<ul>` and `<ol>` unless the author's paste shows Royal Road spacing them badly, in which case tight paragraphs as his converter has them; `|` tables as `<table>`; (8) `<u>`, `<br>`, `<sub>` and `<sup>` typed in the chapter pass through, every other `<`, `>` and `&` is escaped, so a chapter can never carry markup it did not mean into the page (the author's converter escapes nothing). The `syntaxSpans` kinds (`files.6`) are the one list of what is Obsidian syntax; the converter reuses them rather than matching again. ### 11.3 Design notes

**(a) Startup order in `src/main/index.ts`.** Module scope: (1) `readDevSwitches({env: process.env, packaged: app.isPackaged, isolatedUserData: app.commandLine.getSwitchValue('isolated-user-data') or null})`; (2) `app.setPath('userData', switches.userDataDir ?? path.join(app.getPath('appData'), APP_DATA_DIR))`, then `chromiumSwitches(switches)` onto `app.commandLine` (only a quiet test window has one, `dev.1`); (3) `if (!app.requestSingleInstanceLock()) app.quit(); else start();` and everything below runs inside `start()`, so a losing instance writes nothing; (4) `initLog(<userData>/logs)`; (5) `installCrashHandlers`; (6) packaged win32 only: `app.setAppUserModelId(APP_ID)`. `whenReady` (async): `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)`; `registerCoreHandlers()` with every handler, including updates and the close guard (`handle()` only fills a Map and `installIpcBridge()` wires it once, so a later registration is silently dead); `installIpcBridge()`; `const settings = await loadSettings(); applyTheme(settings.theme); installTheme();`; `createWindow()` (themed `backgroundColor`, close guard, navigation guard, the one `render-process-gone` handler, window-open handler); `startUpdates()`. Events: `second-instance` restores and focuses (`bringForward`; a quiet test window is shown without the foreground, and left minimised when it is, `dev.1`); `before-quit` calls `closeGuard.onBeforeQuit()` and awaits nothing; `will-quit` calls `abortAll()` and `stopWatching()`; `window-all-closed` calls `app.quit()` off macOS.

**(b) Developer switches** (all read in `src/main/devSwitches.ts`; packaged builds ignore and log every one except the flag): `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_USER_DATA` (userData), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_OPENAI_BASE_URL` (was `STET_OPENAI_BASE_URL`; http or https only; ChatGPT's reviews too since `codex.3`, and theirs alone since `codex.6` took out the OpenAI API key, so a development run reviews against `test/helpers/mockOpenAi.ts`'s ChatGPT route, in the scenario the sign-in mock's token names, C.115), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_CHATGPT_AUTH_URL` (OpenAI's sign-in server, `https://auth.openai.com`, replaced for Sign in with ChatGPT: the issuer and the base of its authorization, token, revocation and key endpoints, http or https only, so a development run signs in against `test/helpers/mockChatGptAuth.ts`; `codex.2`, 5.7), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_NO_CLAUDE_CODE` (behave as if Claude Code were not installed; was `..._DEV_NO_BUNDLED_CLI` before C.42), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_FAKE_UPDATE` (the fake update: `createFakeUpdater` in electron-updater's place, with no request to GitHub, for a plan read by `parseFakeUpdate`: a version such as `1.0.1`, found and then downloaded and installed, the version and `download-fails` or `install-fails`, or `up-to-date`, `no-releases` or `offline` alone; anything else turns it off and logs `update.fake-ignored`; `dev:clean --fake-update <plan>`; named in Copy diagnostics; `release.8b`, Appendix C "What the updater settled where the plan left it open"), `MREV_VERBOSE` (echo Claude Code stderr), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_QUIET_WINDOW` (a quiet test window: shown without taking the foreground and kept rendering while covered; `dev:clean --quiet`; `dev.1`, Appendix C "Quiet test windows"), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_SHELL_STUB` (open nothing outside the app: every link, file and folder main would hand the system goes through `systemShell()`, which under the switch prints "[shell stub] ..." to the terminal instead, and main prints "[shell stub] on" as it starts; `dev:clean --shell-stub`; `setup.10b`, Appendix C "A shell that opens nothing"). `--isolated-user-data=<dir>` works in both builds and wins. The neutral prefix never changes with the name.

**(c) Claude child environment and options.** `buildClaudeEnv(base)` copies `base`, then removes `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` (the switch behind `--bare`) and the switches in (b), and adds `CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS = '1'`. It sets no SDK client variable, because the app is not the SDK (C.42). It never sets `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`: Claude Code is the user's own install and keeps itself current. Everything else passes unchanged, including `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING` and proxy variables. No sign-in method is removed. `claudeArgs` (in `src/main/providers/claudeOptions.ts`, built on `BASE_CLAUDE_ARGS`) keeps the same guarantees as flags: no built-in tools (`--tools ""`), no MCP servers (`--strict-mcp-config`), no setting sources (`--setting-sources ""`), no session persistence, `--permission-mode dontAsk`, and `cwd` = userData (rule 6). Never `--bare`: it disables subscription sign-in. Because `settingSources` is empty, `apiKeyHelper` and env blocks in `~/.claude/settings.json` are not read; the README says to set the variable instead.

**(d) Settings.** Keys added in 1.0, all normalised in `src/shared/settings.ts` with defaults: `theme` (`system`; anything else not in system/light/dark becomes `system`), `onboardingDone` (missing: true when `manuscriptFolder` is set, else false; while false the welcome guide shows, unless Start or Skip closed it earlier in the run, and Start, Skip and Settings' Show the welcome guide again write it, section 7, `setup.11`), `dismissedHints` (`[]`, unique strings; the ids in use are `pro-model-preselected`, `setup.1`, also written by Show the welcome guide again so the guide brought back never preselects (C.67), and `save-to-chapter`, the first-use Save hint of `apply.12`, section 7, and `chatgpt-plan-welcome`, Got it on OpenAI's welcome on the ChatGPT view, `codex.3`, 5.8 item 9), `checkForUpdates` (true), `updateDownloadConsent` (null or a version string), `sideSplit` (null, the usual split; else the side panel list's share of the height under the focused suggestion's box, a number strictly between 0 and 1, anything else becoming null; `ui.6`, section 7 The split), `columnWidths` (`{files: null, side: null}`, both columns at their usual widths; else `files`, the chapter list's, and `side`, the side panel's, each a share of the window's width strictly between 0 and 1, read on its own, anything else, or anything but an object, becoming null; `polish.5`, section 7 Column widths); `model` default becomes `default`, existing values kept. `chatgptModel` (`codex.3`, 5.8 item 2): the ChatGPT model, empty for the list's default, any string kept, as `openaiModel` was; `provider` takes `chatgpt` too. `openaiModel`, the OpenAI API key's model, went with the key in `codex.6`, and `provider` no longer takes `openai`: a settings.json written before then is read as any file with a key the app does not know, which `normalizeSettings` drops, and its `openai` provider as `claude`, the default, so the next save leaves out both (`settings.test.ts` and `settingsStore.test.ts`; checked in a window on such a file, C.115). `showRowStates`, which `polish.12` added for Show states, the box that wrote ACCEPTED or DISMISSED on the decided suggestion rows, went with the box in `polish.17` (section 7 Suggestions list, C.108): a settings.json written in between still holds it, and is read as any file with a key the app does not know, which `normalizeSettings` drops, so the next save, which writes the settings as normalised, leaves it out (`settings.test.ts` and `settingsStore.test.ts` hold both; checked in a window on such a file). The paths (`hardening.8`): `manuscriptFolder` and `reviewsFolder` are kept only when absolute (`isAbsolutePath` in `src/shared/paths.ts`, Windows' rule, which takes POSIX's absolute paths too and is the same on every system, so a test on Linux reads `C:\Novel` as Windows does) and holding no NUL, and `guidelinesPath` only when it is that and ends `.md` or `.txt` in any case, as `path.extname` reads the last segment (`extensionOf`; a path ending in a separator has none); anything else becomes null, the usual folder or file, so a hand-edited relative path is dropped, the next save writes null over it, and a dropped manuscript folder with no `onboardingDone` brings the welcome guide back. That drop is for a settings.json read from disk only. A save whose patch names one of the three as anything but null that the normaliser would drop (`droppedPathSetting` in `src/shared/settings.ts`; a key left out or sent as undefined is not looked at) is refused with `invalid-input` before anything is read or written, so the folder or file chosen before stays (`refuseDroppedPath` at the top of `save` in `settingsStore.ts`, the `hardening.8` review): a guidelines file named by its full path that is not .md or .txt in `assertGuidelinesFile`'s own words ("The guidelines file has to be a .md or .txt file, and rules.docx is not. Choose another one in Settings."), any other guidelines value as "The guidelines file has to be a .md or .txt file named by its full path. Nothing was changed; choose another one in Settings.", and a folder as "The reviews folder has to be named by its full path, from a drive or a network share. Nothing was changed; choose it again in Settings." (or "manuscript folder"), naming the setting, never the path. Settings shows a refusal where it shows any other failure and clears it with the next change, and its guidelines picker offers .md and .txt files; a name typed in the picker can still be anything, which is what the refusal is for. Read failures in `settingsStore.ts`: ENOENT gives cached defaults; a JSON parse failure first copies the file to `settings.json.corrupt-<yyyymmddhhmmss>` with `COPYFILE_EXCL`, logs `settings.unreadable`, then caches defaults, or, when no copy can be made, counts as a read that failed (`hardening.15`); any other read error retries once after 200 ms, then returns defaults without caching, and `save` re-tries the read and refuses to overwrite. While a read fails, `settings:get` answers `{ readFailed: true, settings: null }`, never the error, and the page holds no settings and shows the card section 7 gives (Settings that could not be read) in place of everything else (`hardening.15`). C.86 has the cases these rules leave open.

**(e) Theme.** Main sets `nativeTheme.themeSource` before the window exists; CSS overrides every colour token inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { color-scheme: dark; ... } }`. The window is hidden until first paint, load or 3 s (C.36), and its `backgroundColor` comes from `WINDOW_BACKGROUND`, which the test pins to `--bg`, so no light frame shows. Also: `a, a:visited { color: var(--accent) }`; zero-specificity `:where(select, input, textarea) { color: var(--ink) }` and `:where(input[type='password']) { background-color: var(--panel); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 4px; padding: 3px 6px }` (a background alone turns off the browser's drawing of the field, which falls back to a 2 px inset border, so it takes the other text fields' frame; no font, so `.modal__key-input` keeps its own); `accent-color: var(--accent-fill)`. Contrast tiers (WCAG 2.x, both themes): 4.5:1 for every text token and category on the three surfaces, categories on the active and flash paragraph backgrounds, `--ink` on every highlight, warn, danger and hover-tint background, `--ink-soft` and `--accent` on focus and selected rows, `--ink-soft`, `--accept` and `--danger` on `--warn-bg` (Test the connection's note and result in a Setup status card that warns, `setup.8`), `--on-accent` on the fills; 3:1 for `--ink-faint` and `--dismiss` on surfaces and highlights and for categories as marks, and since `polish.2` for the scrollbar's arrows and a field's resize handle on the gutter. The scrollbar's thumb is the one mark held under 3:1, by the author's choice (the bullet on scrollbars below). The author approved the light tweaks (Appendix D question 9), so since `theme.5` `--ink-faint` and `--dismiss` are `#8a8378` and `--warn` and `--cat-word-choice` `#84681c`, and every light pair passes with no per-token floor (the floors that would have applied otherwise were warn and word-choice 4.2, ink-faint 2.5, dismiss 2.4). Every new colour goes into both blocks with its pairs. `--unsaved` (`apply.4`) is the ember of changes not saved to the chapter: light `#ad4b0d`, dark `#ff8a3d` (the ember of the logo's original palette, (o)), on the dot before the chapter name (a mark, 3:1) and the status bar's count (text, 4.5:1), both on `--panel`. Light measures 5.46:1 on `--panel`, 5.09 on `--bg`, 4.79 on `--panel-alt` and 4.71 on `--selected-bg`, dark 6.77, 7.40, 6.09 and 5.53, so `apply.5`'s dot in the chapter list passes on a hovered or selected row too (`themeContrast.test.ts` checks both since `apply.5`). It replaces the `--accent` blue the dot had, so the dot no longer reads as a link or a comment. `--badge-conflict-bg`, `--badge-conflict-border` and `--badge-conflict-ink` (`files.11`) are the "conflict copy" badge in the chapter list, a rose pill under the copy's name, in the same row as the pending count's yellow: light `#fde8e6`, `#f0c4bf` and `#9c2a1f`, dark `#42221e`, `#6b3530` and `#ff9e94`; the ink on its background is text, 6.46:1 in light and 7.15 in dark (`themeContrast.test.ts`). `--selection-bg`, `--selection-prose-bg` and `--selection-ink` (`polish.1` and its review) are selected text, the band everywhere but the prose's lines, the prose's faint band and the ink on the first: light `rgb(0 190 200 / 45%)`, `rgb(70 255 255 / 20%)` and `var(--ink)`, dark `rgb(0 120 128 / 55%)`, `rgb(0 90 95 / 20%)` and `var(--ink)`, with their pairs and how plainly each must show in the bullet on text selection below. `--scrollbar-track`, `--scrollbar-thumb`, `--scrollbar-thumb-hover` and `--scrollbar-thumb-active` (`polish.2`) are the app's own scrollbar, the gutter and its thumb at rest, under the pointer and dragged: `var(--panel-alt)` in both blocks, light `#d0cabe`, `#c5beb0` and `#b7b0a2`, dark `#454139`, `#4e4940` and `#585248`, with the thumb's exception to the 3:1 of a mark in the bullet on scrollbars below. `test/renderer/themeCss.test.ts` pins every value in both blocks, so a changed value is edited there and here (dark) or on `theme.4`'s list of light differences (light) in the same commit. Surfaces for screenshots: Setup, nothing open, main view with a review covering every state, notification tones, find, paragraph editor, edit popover, lock card (by eye), every dialog, Bulk menu, legend and zoom.

Deliberate choices from `theme.8` (2026-10-16), after every surface was shot in both themes and the states screenshots miss were checked by hand:

- **Tints kept at 9%, 18% and 16% in dark.** Measured as the tinted box's WCAG contrast with what it sits on (the ratio counts screen flare, so dark differences are not overstated): a pending suggestion on the page is 1.14 to 1.18:1 in dark against 1.12 to 1.15 in light, hovered 1.35 to 1.45 against 1.26 to 1.34, and a decided one hovered 1.26 against 1.18. On the active paragraph dark is again the stronger, and on the focus yellow the two themes are within 0.04 of each other. The measure compares the range across the seven categories, lowest with lowest and highest with highest, and dark is at least light on every background. Category by category, spelling and homophone come out up to 0.03 lower in dark: spelling's pending tint is 1.145:1 on the dark page against 1.154 in light, and on `--focus-bg` 1.139 against 1.151 at rest and 1.302 against 1.334 hovered; homophone hovered on `--focus-bg` is 1.315 against 1.321. A gap that size is no reason to raise a share. At 100% and enlarged three times, every pending tint and hover in the main view is visible in dark. The tint is meant to be faint in both themes, as the 2 px category underline carries the state; raising it would make dark louder than light.
- **The small tints are the light shares in dark too** (`small.6`, 2026-10-19). By `theme.8`'s measure a capsule at rest is 1.300 to 1.380:1 on the dark page against 1.227 to 1.296 in light, hovered 1.590 to 1.755 against 1.406 to 1.540; on `--para-active-bg` 1.309 to 1.398 against 1.229 to 1.297, hovered 1.575 to 1.746 against 1.409 to 1.542; on `--focus-bg` 1.264 to 1.353 against 1.222 to 1.290, hovered 1.470 to 1.631 against 1.396 to 1.529. Dark is at least light, lowest with lowest and highest with highest, on all three. Category by category only spelling and homophone on `--focus-bg` come out lower in dark, spelling by 0.026 at rest and 0.059 hovered; that pair never shows, as a focused capsule is filled with `--focus-bg` itself rather than tinted over it. `--ink` on each category at `--tint-small-hover` over `--bg` is 9.67 to 10.59:1 in light and 7.95 to 8.78 in dark; `themeContrast.test.ts` checks that pair, and `themeCss.test.ts` pins both values in both blocks. Nothing is filled behind ghost text, which therefore meets only the page and the paragraph backgrounds its pairs check: until the `small` review a focused small change's ghost was filled with `--focus-bg`, where spelling, homophone, punctuation and other came to 4.14, 4.18, 4.28 and 4.03:1 in dark (light 4.70 and up), and `themeContrast.test.ts` now fails any rule that fills the ghost row.
- **The focus ring is the browser's own; there is no `--focus-ring`.** Chromium draws `outline: auto` as a double ring, rgb(229, 151, 0) with a white edge in light and rgb(238, 238, 238) with an rgb(16, 16, 16) edge in dark, so it shows on any background. The white ring that `theme.5` and `theme.7` noted on the find field, the edit popover's box and a focused select is that dark ring. Every Tab stop checked showed a ring in both themes, the filter chips and zoom buttons included, whose `overflow: hidden` would clip a ring drawn outside them (Chromium draws it inside there). A colour of the app's own would be held to 3:1, which the light orange (2.36:1 on `--panel`) does not reach, so light would change too. Three rules in `app.css` set the focus themselves, the first and the last added after this check: the side panel's split handle (`ui.6`, 2026-10-18) draws a 2 px `--accent` ring inside its 7 px band, where neither region covers it (section 7), and `--accent`, a text token, holds 4.5:1 on `--panel` in both themes; the paragraph box (`.para-editor__area:focus`) has no ring and shows its focus as a glow of `--accent-fill` (of `--accent` since `theme.12`, below) at 24% in place of the 12% it has at rest; and a dialog's box (`.modal:focus`, `ui.1`, 2026-10-18), which takes the focus as it opens, shows none, while its controls keep theirs.
- **Text selection has a band of the app's own since `polish.1` (2026-10-22); until then it was the browser's.** The author said yes in sitting C (`theme.10` a), "if it does not hurt usability". Before: white text on rgb(49, 101, 206) in light (5.4:1) and rgb(6, 57, 163) in dark (9.9:1). Ghost text is never selected (`user-select: none`), but it sits in the gap between lines that the band covers, so a ghost above a selected line is drawn on the band in its own colour: on the browser's light band the categories read at 1.02 to 1.27:1 and the struck-through "was" ghost at 1.44, on the dark one at 3.8 to 5.0 and 3.06, and in the window the red DELETE (drawn at 80%) measured about 1.35:1 in light and 2.9 in dark. C.105 has what the task left open; in short:
  - **Two bands, one turquoise** (since the `polish.1` review, 2026-10-22). The ghosts are only in the prose, so only the prose's lines (`.prose ::selection`) take the faint band, `--selection-prose-bg`, which the ghosts hold close to the page's luminance. Everything else takes `--selection-bg`, the same hue made plain to see: the side panel, the chapter list, the margin notes, the toolbar and status bar, the dialogs, every field, the paragraph box among them (`.prose input::selection, .prose textarea::selection`, which outweigh the prose's rule), and the Setup page's commands. Light's is `rgb(0 190 200 / 45%)`, #88dcdf over the page, dark's `rgb(0 120 128 / 55%)`, #0d4e51 over the page, both of the dots' hue (183° and 184°). Over anything it covers, `--selection-bg` is at least 28.1 apart from it in CIELAB and 1.39:1 by luminance in light (both on `--selected-bg`), at least 24.2 apart (`--selected-bg`) and 1.39:1 (`--focus-bg`) in dark; with protanopia simulated (Viénot), at least 9.9 and 17.0 apart. The prose's band, which polish.1 first laid everywhere, is 9.2 apart from the dark panel and 1.11:1, where a selected word in the find field, the edit popover or the Setup page's command block could hardly be seen, and in light 12.9 apart from the page but only 2.4 with protanopia simulated (6.1 in dark). The browser's own band was 72 apart from the dark panel and 83 from the light page.
  - **Translucent.** A band drawn opaque in the window hid every suggestion's underline and tint, the focus yellow and a small change's capsule inside the selection: Chromium paints the band with the selected text, over the inline box's own background and border, and the capsule lies under the paragraph's text. (The browser's own band is a little see-through, which is why its shots show the underlines darkened rather than gone.) So the prose's band, `--selection-prose-bg`, is a colour at 20%, and what marks a suggestion shows through it. `--selection-bg` is translucent too, at 45% and 55%, so a badge's or a focused row's colour still shows under selected text.
  - **The prose's band in light: `rgb(70 255 255 / 20%)`**, a turquoise at full brightness (hue 180°; the icon's dots are 183°), which over the page comes out #d4f7f4 (measured rgb(212, 247, 244)): 1.05:1 against the page by luminance, but 12.9 apart in CIELAB by hue. Its limits are the frontmatter's grey on a find match (3.01) and the underline under the band (consistency on the focus yellow, 3.18), and the ghosts keep the 4.5:1 of a category as text on it over the page and both paragraph yellows (lowest, consistency over `--para-flash-bg`, 4.58). A colour of the icon itself darkens the warm page faster than it tints it: the dots' `#4fd8e0` reaches the ghosts' limit at 13%, only 6.9 apart from the page, where the frontmatter's grey on a find match is already under 3:1 (2.94).
  - **The prose's band in dark: `rgb(0 90 95 / 20%)`**, a deep turquoise of the dots' hue, #162725 over the page (measured rgb(22, 39, 37)), 1.12:1 and 9.6 apart. Its limits are the ghosts (other over `--para-flash-bg`, 4.52) and the underline under the band (spelling on the focus yellow, 3.08 against the band over it); a brighter band, such as `rgb(0 185 175 / 16%)` at 15.9 apart, takes the ghosts down to 3.8 and the frontmatter's grey on a find match to 2.5.
  - **The selected text's ink.** `::selection` sets `--selection-ink` (`var(--ink)` in both blocks): on `--selection-bg` at least 9.75:1 over anything it covers in light (the conflict badge) and 6.04 in dark (a focused row). The prose keeps its own colours on its band (`.prose ::selection { color: currentColor }`: in a highlight `currentColor` is the colour beneath, as the window showed), which there are `--ink`, the frontmatter's `--ink-faint` and the active find match's `--find-active-ink`; `--selection-ink` would put light ink on the dark theme's orange under the band, 2.5:1. Own colours everywhere was weighed and not taken: light's categories, `--accept` and `--warn` on `--panel-alt` are 4.53 to 4.56:1 and fall to 4.37 under the prose's band and below 4.5 under any band that shows. `:not(.prose *)::selection` cannot keep the ink out of the prose, as a colour set on an ancestor's `::selection` is inherited by its descendants'.
  - **No band on a filled control.** `button.primary` and the active Setup tab draw their selection `transparent` in `currentColor`: white on `--selection-bg` over light's turquoise fill is 3.45:1, and 3.61 on the prose's band.
  - **Pairs** (`themeContrast.test.ts`, in both themes): `--selection-ink` on `--selection-bg` over the surfaces, the focused and selected rows, the paragraph box and the warning, error and badge backgrounds; on the prose's band, `--ink` over the prose's lines, the focus, a find match and every tinted suggestion, the active find match, and the categories as ghosts over the page and both paragraph yellows, at 4.5:1; and at 3:1 the "was" ghost, the frontmatter on `--panel-alt` and on a find match, and each category as a mark under the prose's band (a suggestion's underline, a small change's foot line) against the band over the page, both yellows and the focus. **How plainly each shows** (the review): `--selection-bg` over each background it covers is at least 20 apart from it in CIELAB (CIE76) and 1.3:1 by luminance, and the prose's band over the page, both paragraph yellows, the frontmatter's `--panel-alt`, the focus and a find match at least 8 apart, which stops it fading further; the prose's band laid where `--selection-bg` is fails the first floor in both themes, so the floor can fail. The test checks that both bands are translucent and the prose's under 50%.
  - **Measured in the window:** the DELETE tag 4.30:1 on the prose's light band and 4.38 on the dark one, the comma's keycap 4.92 and 6.12. The review's window painted `--selection-bg` as computed: over the Setup page's command block (`--panel-alt`) rgb(132, 217, 217) in light and rgb(20, 85, 87) in dark, 30.7 and 26.7 apart from the block, where the prose's band had been rgb(207, 241, 237) and rgb(36, 52, 49), 12.8 and 9.2 apart; over the paragraph box rgb(138, 223, 230) and rgb(14, 81, 89). An insertion's caret has no text, so the band leaves a gap around it as the browser's did, and the ghost of a suggestion on a paragraph's first line sits half in the paragraph's margin, which no band covers.
- **Scrollbars are the app's own since `polish.2` (2026-10-22); until then they were the browser's,** drawn from each block's `color-scheme`: 15 px wide, a rounded 9 px thumb, rgb(139, 139, 139) on rgb(252, 252, 252) in light (3.32:1) and rgb(159, 159, 159) on rgb(44, 44, 44) in dark (5.28:1), darker or lighter on hover, and an arrow at each end. In sitting C the author found them fine but asked for a few of the app's own to try, none thinner (`theme.10` c); from a sheet of three, and a fourth added after it, he picked D, the gutter with a square thumb a shade off the track, "a tiny bit darker though? Say 1.4 at rest rather than 1.2, and 1.6 hovered". C.106 has what the task left open; in short:
  - **The bar.** Every scroller (the prose, the chapter list, the side panel's regions, the dialogs and the legend, the Setup screen, the Copy diagnostics text, the text fields) has a 16 CSS px gutter in `--scrollbar-track` (`--panel-alt`) with a 1 px `--border` line on its inner edge, a square thumb 10 px wide between 3 px of clear track, and an arrow at each end, a triangle drawn with `conic-gradient()` in `--ink-faint`, `--ink-soft` under the pointer. It is drawn in CSS px, so it grows with the zoom (24 screen px at 150%), where the browser's kept to 15. The chips' row draws none (`scrollbar-width: none`, C.98).
  - **The thumb a shade off the track, a mark under 3:1** (the only one until `polish.14`'s faded row buttons, below). `--scrollbar-thumb`, `--scrollbar-thumb-hover` and `--scrollbar-thumb-active` are the gutter's warm grey a step further from the track each, darker in light and lighter in dark: on the track 1.41, 1.60 and 1.86:1 in light, 1.41, 1.60 and 1.85 in dark, measured the same from the window's pixels at 100% and 150%. D as the sheet drew it, `--border` at rest and `--border-strong` hovered, was 1.24 and 1.58 in light and 1.21 and 1.82 in dark. The author chose a quiet thumb over the 3:1 of a mark: `themeContrast.test.ts` names the exception, holds the three to 1.3 to 1.5, 1.5 to 1.7 and 1.7 to 2.0, each further from the track than the last, and keeps the floor for every other mark but `polish.14`'s faded row buttons, the arrows and a field's resize handle among them (3.24:1 on the light gutter, 4.42 on the dark).
  - **The rules.** Bare `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules, never scoped with `:root`, which in Chromium drops the thumb's hover and the arrows. A scroller given a `scrollbar-color`, or a `scrollbar-width` other than `auto`, gets the browser's bar instead, so `themeCss.test.ts` allows neither but the chips' `none`. In a box with rounded corners (the dialogs, the legend, the diagnostics text, the fields that can be made taller) the bar takes the box's corners, and a field's resize handle is the app's own, two short lines in `--ink-faint`, where the browser framed it in a light grey L beside a bar.
  - **Composited scrolling stays** (C.48): with the styled bar the prose, the suggestions list, the details region and the chapter list keep a scrolling layer of their own, contents opaque and their text LCD, in both themes and at 150%.
- **Disabled buttons** keep `opacity: 0.45` in both themes, and read as disabled, the filled blue ones too (Save to chapter, Create, Start review), and the filled turquoise ones of `theme.12` (Save to chapter with nothing open, seen in both themes). Since `polish.9` Save to chapter with nothing open is the ordinary button, faded the same way, and the faded turquoise one is "Saving…", from the save's start to its end, and a count while a review of the chapter runs (C.103, both themes in the `polish.9` window check and its review fix).
- **Margin notes** have no connector lines; a note is tied to its paragraph by its ¶ number, the paragraph's number in `--accent` and, while active, `--active-ring` around the note and `--para-active-bg` behind the paragraph. All read in both themes. The notification cards and the lock card over the scroller read in both themes, with greyscale text as C.48 accepts. The lock card was looked at during a real review against the OpenAI mock's `slow` scenario.
- **A focused suggestion in the active comment's paragraph gets a hairline.** `--focus-bg` on `--para-active-bg` is 1.05:1 in light (1.37 in dark), and such a suggestion was hard to find, so `.para--active .hunk--focused` draws `0 0 0 1px var(--focus-bg), 0 0 0 2px var(--active-ring)` in place of the 2 px `--focus-bg` spread: the same 2 px, so it covers no more of the neighbouring letters, with its outer pixel in the active comment's ring colour (1.27:1 on the paragraph in light, 3.14 in dark). Both are told apart by hue more than by lightness (the focus yellow is 1.03:1 on the light page), so there is no 3:1 tier; `themeContrast.test.ts` checks that the ring stands out from the paragraph more than the yellow does, in both themes.

Deliberate choices from `theme.12` (2026-10-21), the primary buttons in the icon's turquoise (the author: "make the primary button color the cyan from the icon, rather than the current blue"):

- **Light: the rim's dark end, deepened, under white.** `--accent-fill #147a86`, `--accent-hover #116670` and `--accent-active #0e555e` are the icon's rim at its darker end, `#178e9c`, at 86%, 72% and 60% of each channel, so the hue stays the rim's (about 186°) and each step darkens about as much as the blue's did (CIE L* 46.7, 39.2 and 32.7, the blue's 43.5, 35.6 and 29.3). White on them is 5.05, 6.65 and 8.47:1 (on the blue 5.67, 7.62 and 9.60); white on `#178e9c` itself is 3.90 and fails, and the lightest shade with some room, `#147d89`, gives 4.86. The fill is 4.97:1 on `--panel` and 4.64 on `--bg`, so the button stands off the page as the blue did (5.58 and 5.20). The other way the task offered, the page's ink on the dots' `#4fd8e0` (9.45:1), was not taken in light: that fill is 1.58:1 on `--bg` and 1.69 on `--panel`, so the button's edge would all but vanish, and a disabled one, at 45%, would be a pale wash.
- **Dark: the dots under near-black.** `--accent-fill #4fd8e0` is the dots' turquoise; `--accent-hover #4dc5ce` and `--accent-active #39b1bc` are the rim a fifth and half of the way down from `#5ad3db` to `#178e9c` (L* 79.7, 73.5 and 66.5); `--on-accent #16130f` is the dark block's darkest ink, `--find-active-ink`'s, at 10.78, 8.99 and 7.22:1. White would need a fill as deep as light's, which is 3.44:1 on the dark page and reads there as a dull petrol rather than the icon's turquoise, so dark draws the button as the icon draws its dots, bright on a dark ground. The fill is 10.11:1 on `--bg`: on a dark screen the primary button is the brightest thing, and it is still darker than `--ink`. So `--on-accent` is white in light and near-black in dark; `themeContrast.test.ts` holds it to 4.5:1 on all three fills in each theme.
- **The active Setup tab follows the button.** It is a filled control with `--on-accent` on it and shares the hover and press rules with `button.primary`; a blue tab under a turquoise Check again would put two fills on one card.
- **Ticked checkboxes and radio buttons follow too**, through `accent-color: var(--accent-fill)` on `body`. Chromium picks the tick's colour: white on the light fill, a dark grey, rgb(59, 59, 59), on the dark one (seen on About's Check for updates automatically).
- **The paragraph box's glow does not follow: it takes `--accent`, the blue of the box's own 1 px border.** Drawn in the window with the glow on `--accent-fill`, a turquoise glow round the blue line read as two colours in both themes, and in light 12% of the deep turquoise over the warm page came out a grey-green rather than a glow. On `--accent` the box has one colour round it. In light that is the same `#3b5bdb` as before, so the box does not change by a pixel; in dark the glow is 12% and 24% of the border's `#9db1ff`, where it was `#4263eb`, the old dark fill. `themeCss.test.ts` checks the border and both glows. The box's Done is a primary button and turns turquoise with the rest. CLAUDE.md, which an agent does not edit, still calls the box's focus a glow of `--accent-fill`: the author settles which is meant before the cut (11.4 step 1), so do not move the glow back to match it.
- **`--accent` stays blue** on text, links and the small marks, as the task asked unless the author says otherwise, and the selected row's `--selected-bg`, a pale blue, stays with it.
- Comments in the code and test names that call a primary button "the blue button" or "[blue]" were left as they are: none is a string the app shows. In this plan, "the blue button" and "blue" on a button mean the primary button (section 7).

Deliberate choices from `polish.12` (2026-10-23), the suggestions list's rows (the author: "the green arrow needs to pop a little more ... make the X and edit buttons a bit more faded"; section 7 Suggestions list):

- **`--accept-strong`, a stronger green for the accepted ✓ alone:** `#12873b` in light and `#4fd483` in dark, more saturated than `--accept` (HSL saturation 0.76 against 0.44 in light, 0.61 against 0.41 in dark; hue 141° and 144°, still green), drawn with a 2.6 stroke where the icons' own is 1.8. `--accept`, which already held 4.5:1 on the rows (5.17:1 on `--panel` in light) and is the green of the status bar's accepted count, the Suggested words in the focused suggestion's box and Setup's ready card, is unchanged: the ✓ was hard to see for its thin stroke and its muted green, not for its contrast. As a mark the new green holds 3:1 on the row at rest (`--panel`, 4.54 in light, 8.38 in dark), under the pointer (`--panel-alt`, 3.98 and 7.54), focused (`--focus-bg`, 4.13 and 5.51) and on the ✓'s own hover, which keeps its colour on `--border` (3.22 and 6.23); a brighter light green fails, #16a34a at 2.85 on `--panel-alt`. Pairs in `themeContrast.test.ts`, with a check that it stays more saturated than `--accept`.
- **The dismissed ✕ in `--danger`,** drawn bolder too, as the button of the row's decision, and kept in red on its own hover: 3:1 on the same four, the least 4.57 (on `--border` in light, `--focus-bg` in dark). The task named the stroke for the ✓ only; both are bold so the decided button reads alike in either state.
- **The other buttons fade by their stroke, not their colour** (until `polish.14`, below, which fades them by a share of the grey, under 3:1, at the author's word). The row buttons are `--ink-faint`, already near 3:1 where it is weakest (3.24 on `--panel-alt` in light, 3.22 on `--focus-bg` in dark), so the lightest grey that still holds 3:1 on all three of the row's backgrounds, #8e877c in light and #908a7e in dark, is too close to it to read as faded, and opacity would take them under 3:1. They keep `--ink-faint` and draw a 1.2 stroke, which reads plainly lighter beside the 1.8 of a pending row (seen in both themes at 100% and enlarged); under the pointer they are drawn as any row button, `--ink` on `--border` at 1.8. Their pairs are `--ink-faint` on the row's three backgrounds.
- **The tag has the panel's fill.** A tag is 9 px text and needs 4.5:1. The categories hold it on `--panel` and `--panel-alt`, but in dark four fall under it on the focused row's `--focus-bg` (spelling 4.14, homophone 4.18, punctuation 4.28, other 4.03), so the tag is filled with `--panel`, as a chip is, on every row, and its pairs are the categories and `--accent` on `--panel`. On the focused row it reads as a small pale label in light and a dark one in dark.

Deliberate choices from `polish.14` (2026-10-23), the suggestions list's rows again (the author: "make the not clicked ones fade more when the check / X is faded. It barely looks any different. It should clearly indicate 'we are done with this row'"; section 7 Suggestions list):

- **The fade is a share of the faint grey, under 3:1 at rest by the author's choice.** A decided row's two other buttons are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink-faint) var(--row-fade), transparent)`, `--row-fade` a share of 35% in both blocks, as the `--tint-*` shares are, so there is no new colour: on the row at rest, hovered and focused (`--panel`, `--panel-alt`, `--focus-bg`) 1.48, 1.43 and 1.45:1 in light and 1.74, 1.71 and 1.54 in dark, near the scrollbar thumb's 1.41 at rest, painted #d6d2cd on the light panel and #4c4841 on the dark one. It is the second mark under 3:1: `themeContrast.test.ts` names the exception beside the thumb's, this ink, this share and the row's three backgrounds and no other, and holds each ratio to 1.35 to 1.9, so the fade can neither vanish nor creep back towards `--ink-faint` itself (3.22:1 at its least). Under the pointer they are drawn as any row button, `--ink` on `--border`, a new pair at 3:1 (11.33:1 in light, 9.50 in dark), and with the keyboard's focus `--ink` on the row (a text pair already) beside the focus ring, which the fade leaves whole, as it is the ink's and not the button's opacity. A translucent ink keeps one fade over the three backgrounds, where an opaque lighter grey cannot: `--border-strong` is 1.80:1 on the light panel but 1.33 on the dark focused row. The thinner stroke went with it: faded, an icon keeps its own stroke, so its shape is a pending row's and only its ink pales. Each icon a row button draws is one path, since a translucent ink is painted once for each shape and builds up where two meet: the pencil was two until the review, its outline and the ferrule's line, and on every faded row the line's two ends showed as darker spots, 1.90:1 in light and 2.43 in dark, the second outside the band (C.110).
- **The icons are 16 px in the same buttons.** `.row__act svg` is 16 by 16 CSS px with 1 px of padding, where the icon was 12 with 3, so each button is still 18 by 18, and the row and the focused box's heading line (`--focus-head`, 18 px) are as tall as they were. The strokes are drawn in the icon's 16-unit box, so the plain 1.8 and the decision's 2.6 are now 1.8 and 2.6 CSS px, where they were 1.35 and 1.95. The focused suggestion's pencil is a row button and grows with them; the legend's tick is 16 px, as a row draws it.
- **The tag is 34 px wide.** HOM, the widest of the fourteen in Segoe UI at 9 px, measured 31.2 CSS px with a 1 px border and 3 px of padding, SPE the narrowest 24.3; the box is 34 px with 2 px of padding and its letters centred, which leaves room for a fallback font about a fifth wider before the ellipsis. Its letters, colours and fill are `polish.12`'s, so its text pairs are unchanged.

Deliberate choices from `polish.16` (2026-10-23), a colour for each category (the author: "can we choose colors that are more differentiated on purpose? For example, typo and spelling look almost identical. Grammar and Agreement also look very similar."):

- **One token per category, chosen as one set.** `--cat-<category>` for all thirteen in both blocks, in `CHANGE_CATEGORIES`'s order, and each `.cat-*` rule on its own token, where typo took spelling's colour, agreement and tense grammar's, redundancy and awkward word-choice's and formatting other's. Light, with each colour's CIELAB hue: spelling `#b3261e` (36°), typo `#576909` (113°), homophone `#016dba` (274°), grammar `#1f6f8b` (238°), agreement `#aa5106` (58°), tense `#9f3887` (336°), punctuation `#7a4fb5` (310°), word-choice `#84681c` (86°), redundancy `#2e756e` (187°), awkward `#c11e59` (8°), consistency `#2f7a4a` (151°), formatting `#905f4d` (46°, muted) and other `#484e70` (288°, muted). Dark, in the same order and on the same hues give or take 10°: `#ff7b72`, `#b6c973`, `#30a9ff`, `#5cc0e0`, `#ef8e3e`, `#fe9dee`, `#b994f5`, `#d9b44a`, `#34b7af`, `#ff78a8`, `#6cc28b`, `#f5b89c` and `#a2a0ba`. With You's `--accent` (295°, 286° in dark) the twelve that are colours stand round the wheel 15° to 51° apart in light and 20° to 41° in dark.
- **Why each hue is where it is.** Spelling's red, grammar's petrol blue, punctuation's violet, word-choice's ochre and consistency's green are the colours the author has read since the start, so they stay, value for value, and the eight others fill the wheel round them. The members of a family stand more than a fifth of the wheel apart (77° at the least): spelling's red, typo's olive and homophone's azure; grammar's blue, agreement's orange, opposite it, and tense's plum; word-choice's ochre, redundancy's teal and awkward's raspberry. Typo, the category the author named, has the one yellow-green, which nothing else is near; homophone has the azure between grammar's blue and You's, the most crowded part of the wheel in light, about as far from both as 4.5:1 on `--panel-alt` allows (31 and 36 apart in CIE76). Tense's plum and awkward's raspberry fill the stretch from the violet round to the red, redundancy the gap between consistency's green and grammar's blue, and agreement the orange between the red and the ochre. Formatting and other, which ask least attention, stay muted and are told apart by hue and by lightness: formatting a warm clay, the lighter (L* 45 in light, 80 in dark), other a cool slate, the darker (34 and 67), so each also stands clear of the comments' warm grey; light other was that grey itself (`#6d675e`) until now.
- **The floor** (`themeContrast.test.ts`, both themes): any two of the fifteen, the thirteen with You's `--accent` and the comments' `--ink-soft` as the chips' rules paint them, at least 15 apart in CIE76, and two of one family at least 35. Light comes to 21.3 at the least (formatting and the comments) and 41.9 within a family (formatting and other; spelling's family 74.6, grammar's 65.3, word-choice's 54.3), dark to 19.9 (homophone and You) and 40.2 (formatting and other). No floor was lowered: every category also keeps 4.5:1 as text and 3:1 as a mark, and the new colours come closest to those in light formatting, 4.61:1 on `--panel-alt`, dark homophone, 4.60:1 above a selected line in a flashing paragraph, and dark awkward's underline, 3.14:1 under the prose's band on the focus yellow.
- **In CIEDE2000 as well**, which is nearer than CIE76 to what the eye sees, above all between two strong colours: no two of the fifteen under 11 in light or 13 in dark. The closest are homophone with You and with grammar in light (11.2 and 11.3) and punctuation with You (12.9 in light, 13.0 in dark), two colours this task left as they were.
- **Where a comment takes it.** A margin card's edge and head word take its category's colour where a suggestion category has its name (C.109), so a comment of the category other now shows other's slate, where in light it showed the comments' grey; consistency's is as it was.
- **How the set was found.** A scratch search over CIELAB lightness, chroma and hue, each category in a window round its hue, every candidate rounded to 8 bits and held to every pair the contrast test sets a category, spreading the fifteen apart in CIEDE2000 with the CIE76 floors as hard limits and the five kept colours fixed; then candidate sets laid over the window's CSS and looked at in both themes, and four values of the chosen one moved a little by hand, three for headroom over 4.5:1 or 3:1 and light formatting a step further from agreement. A colour the author dislikes is one line in each block of `app.css`, with its pin in `themeCss.test.ts`, and the contrast test says whether the pairs and the floor still hold.

**(f) Claude status and the Setup screen.** Probes run in parallel and send no model request: `runClaudeCli(path, ['auth','status','--json'])` through `parseAuthStatus` (keeps only `loggedIn`, `authMethod`, `apiProvider`, `apiKeySource`, `subscriptionType`, `email`); the handshake, Claude Code's own `initialize` exchange over stream-json, which answers with the model list and the account and sends no prompt (`claudeHandshake.ts`, the process always ended; 60 s budget on the first check, 20 s later; C.46; until `cli.1` the SDK's `query()` with a prompt that never yields); `--version` of the one Claude Code found (until `cli.1`, of both the bundled and the installed binary). `auth status` is trusted only when it says signed out. `classifyClaude`, first match: `auth.loggedIn === false` gives not-signed-in; `account.tokenSource` `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` with no cloud provider gives ready, auth-token (`setup.17`, C.71: the token outranks an API key and the sign-in, a cloud provider outranks it, and `auth status` calls it `oauth_token`); `account.apiKeySource` set and not `none` gives ready, api-key; `account.apiProvider` not `firstParty` gives ready, cloud; `account.email` gives ready, subscription; `account.tokenSource === 'none'` gives not-signed-in (when `auth.loggedIn` was true: "Claude Code is signed in through its own settings (<authMethod>), which <APP_NAME> does not load. Sign in with the command below instead."); no account: `auth.loggedIn` true gives ready with credential from `authMethod` (`claude.ai`, `oauth_token` subscription; `api_key`, `api_key_helper` api-key; `third_party` cloud), otherwise error. A free plan adds a plan warning. `classifyClaudeFailure`, first match (the caller handles refusal before): startup reason (`cli_version_too_old` outdated; `org_verify_failed`, `gateway_signin_required` login-expired; `org_pin_api_key_conflict` billing with API-key wording; `shell_tool_missing` "could not find PowerShell or Git Bash"); usage limit by the SDK's prefixes, copied into `claudeStatus.ts` at `cli.1`; text `/login expired|session expired|token (has )?expired|token revoked/i` login-expired; a reply that ran out of room (`claudeReplyLimit`, `files.10`, C.77: text "Prompt is too long" the chapter too long to read, text "reached its context window limit" or stop reason `model_context_window_exceeded` a full context window, text "exceeded the N output token maximum" or an assistant `error` or result `api_error` of `max_output_tokens` the output limit, all failed in `replyLimitMessage`'s words with the chapter's words and the effort); the assistant-error table (every row of today's `mapAssistantError` but `max_output_tokens`, now the step before, plus `verification_required` billing, `cloud_credential_error` not-signed-in, `server_error` retry later); text rules (not logged in or please run /login; does not support this model or newer is required: outdated; invalid API key or disabled organization: billing with "An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is in use and was refused"; credit balance or spend limit; not available with the plan; high load; overloaded, 529, 429); a last reply that stopped at `max_tokens` (the result's `stop_reason`, else the last streamed `message_delta`'s) the output limit, so running out of turns or schema retries after a cut-off reply says why (`files.10`); today's subtype table; else failed. A successful result with no structured output that parses is the output limit too when its reply was cut off, else the wrong shape (`cutOffReply`, `files.10`). A rewritten message keeps the original in `detail`. Views (`setupView`, first match): missing-binary gives not-installed; not-signed-in gives expired if the last failure is login-expired, else signed-out; a last failure of login-expired or not-signed-in outranks a ready runtime; error gives "could not check"; last failure outdated; usage limit in force; credential api-key; ready. The last failure clears on a successful review or connection test, on a signed-out check followed by a ready one, and (outdated only) when the binary path or version changes; a plain re-check never clears a sign-in failure. Test the connection (`setup.8`, 5.6 item 5) is the one model request Setup sends, only when pressed: `ai:test`, Haiku, `--max-turns 1`, the system prompt "Reply with the single word OK.", the review's flags, environment and folder (rule 6), stopped after 60 s; offered in the status card where `canTestConnection` says, with the note "Sends one very small request to Claude, which counts against your plan like any other." on a Claude plan, and in the card's own terms for an API key, a cloud provider, the `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (C.71) or a check that failed (`connectionTestNote`, 5.6 item 5, `setup.8` review); held rather than disabled while it runs, as Check again is, so it keeps the keyboard focus (`heldButton`); its success sends `nextLastFailure` the `success` event that a review's sends (the task's `test-ok`). Review with AI opens Setup only for missing-binary or a definite not-signed-in; an error or timeout opens the dialog with a warning, and Setup offers "Try the review anyway" (`reviewGate`, `reviewDialogWarning`, `canTryReviewAnyway`, 5.6). Commands: `claude auth login`, with `& '<path>' auth login` on Windows and `'<path>' auth login` on POSIX under it whenever the path is known, for a terminal that does not find `claude` (single quotes with `'` doubled; `setup.7` shows both rather than choosing, since the terminal's PATH need not be the app's), on the tab of the system the app runs on only, since the path is that machine's (`pathForTab`, `setup.7` review); install-and-sign-in `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex; & "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin\claude.exe" auth login` or `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash && ~/.local/bin/claude auth login`; outdated gives `claude update`. Signed-out intro: "Claude Code is not signed in. If reviews worked before, your sign-in has ended; this happens from time to time and nothing in <APP_NAME> is lost." Footer: "<APP_NAME> never sees your Claude password or sign-in token. You sign in with Anthropic, in Claude Code and your browser." Missing-binary is the first-run state for most people: it leads with the install-and-sign-in command, says Claude Code is Anthropic's free command-line tool that needs a Claude plan or an API key, and that <APP_NAME> does not include it.

**(g) Reviews bound to chapter files.** Invariant: a review file lives in `folderFor(reviewsFolder, review.sourcePath)`. Belonging: `samePath(review.sourcePath, chapterPath, ci)`. Current review, the one the chapter opens with: the belonging review last on screen, recorded per chapter path in the folder's `.last-open.json` by `recordShown` (`reviews:shown`, when the page shows one from History or the selector) and by `saveReview` for every new entry, written only when it changes and never touching the review file; while nothing is recorded, or the file recorded is gone, the belonging review with the greatest `decidedAt ?? createdAt` (`apply.26`, 6.4, C.57); History stays in `createdAt` order. A review file in the chapter's folder that is there but cannot be read stops `reviews:load-latest` with the read words unless the record names a review that could be read, and the page stays on what was open, with a card that names the chapter (`apply.25` and its review, 6.4). A review whose latest decisions could not be written, even when tried again just before, does not open from the list, History or the selector (6.4). `saveReview` honours an explicit path only if it ends `.review.json` and lies in the right folder; otherwise it writes a new entry there and returns its path (never throws for a path reason, so a reviews-folder change cannot break saves). Adoption, only when nothing belongs and the candidate's source file no longer exists: (a) at least 2 matching trailing path segments in the same slug folder (moved vault), or (b) equal `base.hash` with at least 500 characters (renamed or moved in Obsidian); rank hash matches, then more segments; two old paths equal on both adopt nothing, since it cannot be told which one the chapter was. Adoption rewrites every history file of the old path into the new folder with the new `sourcePath` and removes each old file only after its copy is written, following a journal (`.adoption.json` in the reviews folder) that the next store call completes if a crash interrupts it; an info card names the old path.

**(h) Save path and backups.** `writeChapter` order: (1) read the raw bytes once, refuse non-UTF-8 (`files.3`), hash; (2) hash differs from `expectedHash`: `stale`; (3) new bytes equal disk bytes: `written`, `unchanged`, no backup; (4) `beforeReplace`: refuse a backups root inside the manuscript folder or the chapter's own folder (`assertOutside`), then write the backup unless identical to the newest; a failure aborts with "Could not back up the chapter before saving, so nothing was written: <reason>"; (5) re-read, and a changed hash returns `stale`; (6) `atomicWriteFile`: temp file in the same folder, rename, on EPERM, EACCES or EBUSY back off 50, 100, 200, 400, 800 ms, re-hashing the target before each retry (`changed` returns `stale`, `unreadable` skips a round), then `explainWriteError`; (7) remember the hash for the watcher; (8) `afterWrite` prunes backups, best effort. Layout: `<userData>/backups/<chapterSlug>-<first 8 hex of sha256(pathKey)>/` with a one-time `chapter.json` `{sourcePath}`, files named by local time, for example `2026-10-14 16.04.33 Chapter 12.md`, `-2` after the time on a collision. Retention keeps the newest 20 plus the oldest of each local day within 30 days and never deletes a name it cannot parse.

**(i) Leaving and closing.** `CloseGuardState = {chapter, unsavedDecisions, changedParagraphs, locked, reviewRunning, writesPending, dialogText}`, pushed once the page has loaded and then on change; since `rr.2` a Full edit whose text changed counts among `changedParagraphs`, with `fullEdit: true` (absent otherwise), so the questions and main's box name it rather than a paragraph. Main `createCloseGuard(deps)`: on window `close`, an allowed close, a gone renderer or nothing at risk closes at once with no IPC; otherwise preventDefault, reveal (restore, show, focus, flash), send `app:close-requested` once and arm a 3 s ack timer; no `received` opens a native "not responding" box (Wait / Close anyway); `received` arms a 10 s timer to a "still finishing" box; `prompting` clears both; a repeated close before `prompting` opens the box at once; every box has an AbortSignal so a late answer dismisses it; Close anyway destroys the window. `app:close-decision` true allows and closes on the next tick (and quits when quitting); false resets `quitting`. `query-session-end` and `session-end` only broadcast `app:flush`; shutdown is never blocked. `allowNextClose('update')` lets the update quit skip everything. What `apply.8` settled beyond this is in 7.7: after `session-end` every close goes through at once, Wait sets no new timer, the taskbar flashes only for a window that was not in front, a page that goes during a close ends it as asked, a reload is a new page whose arrival ends a close under way without closing (`did-navigate`), and a status or decision with no close under way changes nothing. Renderer `prepareToLeaveApp(reason)`: send `received`; race the in-flight save and both writer flushes against 5 s (on timeout or failure: "Still writing your decisions" with Close anyway and Wait); `closePrompt` (title "Close <APP_NAME>?"; buttons Cancel, "Close, keep for later" (focused) and "Save N change(s) and close", or "Apply, save and close" when a box changed, with no Save while a review of the open chapter runs; when nothing would be kept and only a running review or typed dialog text would be lost, Cancel (focused) and "Close anyway", with no Save; lines say how many changes are not saved to the chapter, that the decisions are kept in this review (always the one the chapter opens with, since `apply.26`: the review last on screen; the line for an older review, "The chapter opens with another review, so reopen this one from History.", went with it), and that the chapter file changes only on Save to chapter; that open paragraph boxes are kept and open for editing again when the author comes back to the chapter (the words `apply.7` gave them, C.53); that a running review stops and its result is lost; that text typed in an open dialog is lost); Save proceeds only on `saved` or `nothing-to-save`; Keep for later cancels a running review and flushes; a `finally` always answers. What `apply.9` settled beyond this is in 7.7: the push goes out in the same task as the change, a write that failed counts as pending until it is made and is tried again, Wait tries the writes again for another 5 s, the save that Save and close starts is timed like them, a write or a save that arrives while they run gets another round within the same 5 s, the Setup screen shows the question as the main layout does, and a question already open gives way. Leaving a chapter uses `leavePrompt` with the same three choices ("Save N change(s) first", or "Apply and save first" when a box changed, Keep for later, Cancel), titled "Leave <chapter>?", never prompts while locked, and re-clicking the open chapter, whichever of its reviews is on screen, or the review on screen in History or the selector, only flushes and reloads nothing (`isOpenTarget`, `apply.7`, 7.7). Another review of the open chapter, from History or the review selector, opens without a question (`apply.26`); the "Open the review from <date>?" title and `openedBy` are gone. While Full edit is open it does not open at all, and the card says "Finish or cancel Full edit first.", as for Review with AI (`beforeLeaving`, `rr.2` review): Full edit's box holds the body as the review on screen composes it, so over another review whose decisions differ anywhere it could not go back, and what was typed was set aside with a card saying the chapter no longer read as it did, which was untrue.

**(j) Drafts.** `<userData>/drafts/<first 16 hex of sha256(pathKey)>.json` holds `{version: 1, sourcePath, reviewId, savedAt, drafts: [{key, paragraphs, initial, text}]}` (at most 200 drafts, 1 MB text each), written by a keyed 700 ms writer, flushed on leave, close and session end; an empty set deletes the file (leaving keeps them: the leave prompt's Keep for later flushes them, `apply.7`). On open, a draft reopens only when its paragraph still reads exactly `initial`; a changed draft that cannot be placed is written to `drafts/set-aside/<chapter> <stamp>.txt` and a card offers Show the text. (`apply.16`, C.53.) Drafts belong to the chapter: they are placed whenever a review of it comes on screen, by the page's text at the draft's own index (`placeDrafts`), whichever review that is, and `reviewId` is a record. Show the text opens the .txt (`shell:reveal` `drafts` with the file's `name`). A draft that could not be set aside stays in the chapter's file until the next open; an unreadable file is moved aside as `<hash>.unreadable-<time>.json`; a file that cannot be read at all stays where it is and is never written over unread: each write for its chapter reads it first, is held while it still cannot be read and tried again at the next flush, and once it can be read its drafts are carried after those on screen until the next open. Escape or Cancel on a changed box asks (`discardDraftPrompt`, Keep editing focused). Full edit's box (`rr.2`, C.112) is kept in the same file, once something is typed in it, as `{key: -1, paragraphs: [], initial, text, whole: true}` (`WHOLE_DRAFT_KEY`; `isStoredDraft` accepts no other shape with the flag, and a box with no flag never has key -1): it goes back only where the chapter's body reads as `initial` (`fullEditText`) and no box is open, opening the chapter in Full edit with the card "Full edit is open again, as you left it.", and no box goes back beside it; one left as it opened is not kept, so the chapter opens in Main; one that cannot go back is set aside as a box is ("The chapter no longer reads as it did when you left Full edit open, so Full edit was not opened again. What you typed is kept in <name>."), its part of the .txt headed "Full edit, as you left it:" and "The chapter, as it read when you opened Full edit:". A write that fails says "What you typed in Full edit could not be kept: <reason>" in the card and the close question, where boxes have "The paragraphs you are editing could not be kept".
