**(k) Protected Obsidian syntax.** Hard spans: frontmatter; fenced code (3 or more backticks or tildes) and inline code; `%%...%%`, `<!-- -->`, `$$...$$` across lines (an unclosed one protects only its opening marker); embeds `![[...]]` whole; `[[target]]` whole, and `[[target|alias]]` as `[[target|` plus `]]` so the alias stays editable; links as `[` plus `](url)`; images whole; footnote refs `[^x]`, line-start `[^x]:`, inline footnotes `^[` and their `]`; block ids `^id` at line end; tags `#` at line start or after whitespace or `(` with at least one non-digit; callout `[!type]` with optional `+` or `-`; line-start `>` and heading `#` prefixes; thematic-break lines; bare http(s) URLs; HTML tags only for real element names (a, abbr, b, br, blockquote, center, code, del, details, div, em, font, hr, i, iframe, img, ins, kbd, li, mark, ol, p, pre, s, small, source, span, strong, sub, summary, sup, table, td, th, tr, u, ul, video, audio) or with attribute syntax. `files.6` settled the edges (C.72): an unclosed code fence also protects only its opening run; attribute syntax is a `name=value` attribute, and a real element counts only when all its attributes have values, so `<I know.>` is dialogue; the frontmatter span takes the line break after its closing `---`, and `bodyStart` is just past it; a character escaped with a backslash opens nothing. Not protected: emphasis, bold, strikethrough, highlight markers, indented code, inline `$math$`, tables, lists. Guarded hunks: `source 'claude'`, not authored, pending, `baseSide 'original'`, not stale, no `keptOut`. First failing rule wins: before `bodyStart` gives `frontmatter`; not inside one body paragraph gives `paragraph-break`; overlapping a hard span (a zero-length hunk strictly inside one) gives that kind; `original` or `replacement` containing `[ ] % $ ^ # < > | ~`, a backtick or a newline gives `markup`; applied alone, changing the paragraph's `syntaxSignature` (the paragraph read alone with `{ frontmatter: false }`, C.72) gives the kind of what changed, and changing its paragraph count gives `paragraph-break` (`files.7` settled both, C.73); where the chapter reads the paragraph in a wider context than it shows alone, because a span of the chapter crosses it (a code fence, comment or maths holding a blank line) or a code fence or `<!--` the chapter leaves unclosed comes before it and the suggestion's line would read as a fence line or hold `-->`, changing the chapter's `syntaxSignature`, read whole, gives the kind of what changed (the `files.7` review, C.73), as `.` after the closing fence of a code block holding a blank line would, since the fence would no longer close. In the overlap pass (`resolveOverlaps` with `touchingRule`), a guarded hunk that overlaps nothing on the page and starts exactly where the previous survivor on the line ends gives `combined`; the previous survivor is any hunk on the page, the author's own included, and one this rule keeps out is no longer on it, so it pushes no later hunk off as an overlap (the `files.7` review, C.73). A rebase runs the screen and the touching rule again on the hunks it places, in the same order, and places no hunk of any source before `bodyStart` (`files.20`, 4.5, C.74). A failing hunk becomes `anchor 'stale'`, `start = end = 0`, `keptOut: reason`, and keeps the model's own reason; the note reads "Kept out of the text: it would change Obsidian syntax (<label>). Make this change in Obsidian or with the paragraph pen if you want it.", where the label is the kind's `SYNTAX_LABELS` entry or "a paragraph break", "a markup character" or "together with the suggestion before it" (`KEPT_OUT_LABELS`, `keptOutNote` in `src/shared/diff/protect.ts`).

**(l) Encoding.** `classifyBytes` order: FF FE or FE FF prefix gives utf16; any NUL: utf16 when NULs fill at least 25% of the even or odd positions in the first 4096 bytes, else binary; valid UTF-8 (BOM allowed) passes; more valid multi-byte sequences than invalid bytes gives mixed (with the first bad line); else legacy. Messages: UTF-16 and legacy say how to re-save as UTF-8 (Notepad on Windows, VS Code elsewhere); mixed says to retype the N damaged characters in Obsidian and never re-save in Notepad; all end "The app has not changed the file." Decoding stays `toString('utf8')` so the BOM survives.

**(m) Logging policy.** Lines are `<ISO> <LEVEL> <event> k=v`, scalar fields only, strings scrubbed (OpenAI and Anthropic key shapes, Bearer tokens, signed tokens shaped as a JWT since `codex.2`, emails, the home directory in plain, forward-slash, percent-encoded and `file:///` forms) and cut at 300 characters; C.84 has how the file is written and what a line may name, and CLAUDE.md rule 9 the rule for new log calls. `loggableErrorFields`: `*-invalid-output` and `claude-refusal` log the code only; other app errors log code and message; `SyntaxError` logs its name and stack frames only (V8 quotes the input); errno errors log name, errno, syscall; others name, message, frames. Frames are read from the stack after the message, since V8's quote keeps the input's line breaks and a quoted line starting with "at" would pass for a frame (`hardening.3b`). Never logged: chapter text, prompts, guidelines, replies, `detail`, the account email, the key's last4, drafts, backups, and, since `codex.2`, a ChatGPT token, refresh token or authorization code, the client id, the state, the nonce, the PKCE verifier, the host id and the account's id; the sign-in's events are 5.7 item 9's. The events (`hardening.3b`): `ipc.failed` from `runHandler` (`src/main/ipcEnvelope.ts`), the envelope of every request, with the channel and the error's loggable fields, at warn, or error when the page is told `unknown`, never the payload, and not for `ai:review`, except a payload `checkPayload` refused before any handler ran (`src/main/ipcGuard.ts`, `hardening.8`: a channel that takes nothing sent something, another sent anything but a plain object, or a NUL in a path field, worded with the channel and the field, never the value), which is logged for every channel, a review's included, since `withLogging` never sees it; from `withLogging` (`src/main/providers/logged.ts`), the only place a runtime check, a model list or a review is logged, `ai.runtime` (provider, state, credential, cliVersion, minCliVersion, executable, authMethod, plan, planWarning, apiKeySource, durationMs: what Copy diagnostics shows, never the email or the status message; `keySource`, the OpenAI key's, went with it in `codex.6`), `ai.models` (provider, count, durationMs), `ai.review.start` (provider, model, effort, words, chars, paragraphs, guidelinesChars), `ai.review.done` (provider, model, changes, comments, inputTokens, outputTokens, costUsd, fallback, durationMs, and `costEstimated` until `codex.6`; inputTokens is the whole prompt, cached or not, for both providers: the Responses API's `input_tokens` holds its cached tokens, and Claude Code's `modelUsage` counts the cached part apart, as `cacheReadInputTokens` and `cacheCreationInputTokens`, which are added in) and `ai.review.failed` (provider, the error's loggable fields, durationMs; info when cancelled); `chatgpt.refresh` (`codex.3`, 5.8 item 10: outcome `done`, `ended` or `failed`, a fixed `reason` or the refresh error word OpenAI's page lists, the `status` OpenAI answered with, `kept=later` for a renewal held for its write, durationMs; never a token); a runtime check or model list that throws is logged once, as `ipc.failed`. `withLogging` keeps each provider's `lastRuntime` and `lastFailure`, moved as the renderer's are (`useAi.ts`, `nextLastFailure`) and from what the page is told: a review's failure as the envelope words it, read with the last usage notice, a test's included; a connection test by the answer `testConnection` gives, which the `ai:test` handler hands to `noteTest(id, result)` (`testSetupEvent`), because inside the provider a test that runs out of time ends as cancelled and one that throws something unforeseen as `unknown`, where the page is told `claude-failed` (or `openai-failed`, the OpenAI key's, until `codex.6`), and the page reads a test's usage limit with that test's own notice; a check that throws as the error status the page puts in its place (`state: 'error'`), which clears an outdated failure as the page's does. The renderer keeps Claude's last failure only; main keeps one for each provider. Both are read through `lastRuntime(id)` and `lastFailure(id)` in `providers/index.ts`. `file.save` (status `written`, `unchanged` or `stale`, chars, eol, bom, backup `created`, `reused` or `none`, durationMs; never the path), from the `files:save` handler; a save that throws is `ipc.failed`. `watcher.error` and `watcher.close-failed` take the error's loggable fields, so the code and syscall, never the message, which names the path. The crash events (`hardening.4`, 7.7): `main.uncaught` (origin and the error's loggable fields, at error) and `main.rejection` (at warn), `main.errors-capped`; the page's `log:renderer` lines as `renderer.error`, `renderer.rejection` (at warn), `renderer.render-failed` and `renderer.render-uncaught`, with only the fields in `RENDERER_LOG_FIELDS` (name, code, message, frames, error, errno, syscall and `components`, the app's own component names a render error happened in), and `renderer.log-capped`; `renderer.gone` (reason, exitCode and `outcome`, at info for a clean exit), `renderer.gone-answer` and `renderer.gone-box-failed`. The page's `ApiError` is an app error to the policy, as `AppFailure` is, so a reply its message quotes is never logged. Copy diagnostics (`hardening.5`) holds nothing the log may not, plus the folder paths, chapter count and settings Appendix D question 17 allows, with the home folder as `~`; it carries the log's last ten warnings and errors of the run, each as its time, level, event and the fields that say what failed (`REPORT_WARNING_FIELDS`: channel, code, name, errno, syscall and a few more), never a message, frames or a thrown value, since an app error's message names the chapter, its review file or its backup folder; it reads `lastRuntime` and `lastFailure` and runs no check, so it logs no `ai.runtime` (Appendix C "What Copy diagnostics holds").

**(n) Release and update workflow.** Builder: `publish: [{provider: 'github', owner, repo, releaseType: 'draft'}]`; `nsis: {oneClick: true, perMachine: false, runAfterFinish: true, createDesktopShortcut: true, shortcutName, artifactName: '${productName}-Setup-${version}.${ext}', differentialPackage: true, deleteAppDataOnUninstall: false}`; `win.target` nsis x64 only. `verify-package.ts`: asar listing has `/out/main/index.js` and `/package.json` and no `/samples`, `/test`, `/src`, `/dist`, `/.dev-userdata` (normalise backslashes); no `@anthropic-ai` package and no `claude.exe` or `claude` binary anywhere in the package; `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`, `LICENSE.txt`, `GUIDELINES.default.md` exist, and the notices name every package in the asar at its version; `--installer` adds `app-update.yml` (repo, no `publisherName` unless `EXPECT_SIGNED`, and then one), `latest.yml` (version, file name, size, sha512) and the installer's `.blockmap` (C.91). `release.yml` (`release.7`, C.93): on tags `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*`, two jobs on windows-latest in bash and no permission at the workflow level: `build` with `contents: read`, and `release` with `contents: write`, which runs nothing from the repository or npm, only `gh` on the files `build` hands over as an artifact kept one day, so the token that can write is never in a job that runs the build; actions pinned by commit SHA, checkout with `persist-credentials: false`, setup-node with `package-manager-cache: false` and no restored caches, the tag passed as `env: TAG` and never interpolated into scripts; `build`'s steps `node scripts/check-release.cjs "$TAG"` before `npm ci`, `branding:check` (as `prepackage` would otherwise bring package.json into line silently), lint, test, `npm run package`, verifier with `--installer`, `sha256sum` of the three files into `SHA256SUMS.txt` (the installer named by `installerName`, as the footer names it), notes from the CHANGELOG section plus footer (`node scripts/release-notes.cjs "$TAG" --out <file>`, not a shell redirect, which in Windows PowerShell writes UTF-16); `release`'s `gh release create "$TAG" --draft --verify-tag` with exactly 4 assets, refusing any other count (`--prerelease` when the version has `-`), titled with the app's name and the version. The author publishes with `gh release edit vX.Y.Z --draft=false --latest`, and a prerelease without `--latest`, as GitHub never makes a prerelease the latest release, which is the one the updater reads (`release.10`); drafts are invisible to the updater. Updater flags: `autoDownload false`, `autoInstallOnAppQuit false`, `autoRunAppAfterInstall true`, `allowPrerelease false`, `allowDowngrade false`, logger = the app log; since `release.8b` also `disableWebInstaller true` and the nil id in electron-updater's `x-user-staging-id` header (Appendix C "What the updater sends and keeps"). A consented version that reappears downloads from the cache without asking. Main's side is `src/main/updates.ts` (`release.8b`): the mode from `updateModeFor` (an installed build with no `resources/app-update.yml` is off, C.88), the first check 15 s after `startUpdates()` and then every 24 hours while `checkForUpdates` is on, the channels `update:get`, `update:check`, `update:download` and `update:install`, and the event `update:state` with the `UpdateStatus` of `src/shared/updates.ts`, whose `updateCardFor` and `updateStatusLine` give the card and About's line (Appendix C "What the updater settled where the plan left it open"). Restart now: the renderer refuses while a review runs ("Restart after the review finishes"), runs `prepareToLeaveApp('update')`, shows the overlay, invokes `update:install` (`restartNow` in `src/renderer/state/updates.ts` and `UpdateOverlay`, `release.9`; the overlay goes with any state but `installing`, 7.7); main `runUpdateInstall` (`src/main/updateInstall.ts`) calls `closeGuard.allowNextClose('update')`, `abortAll()`, `await writesSettled(2000)` (`src/main/writes.ts`: `files:save`, `files:create`, `reviews:save` and `settings:set` run inside `trackWrite`), `stopWatching()`, `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(false, true)` and awaits nothing after it (the NSIS installer stops every process under `$INSTDIR` about 1.3 s after it starts). An install error takes the allowance back (the function `allowNextClose` returns, `apply.8`), starts the watcher again and shows the error card; `update:install` answers `installing`, or `failed` at the install stage. One that electron-updater reports after `quitAndInstall` has returned, as 6.8.10 does for an installer it could not spawn, or no quit within 1 s, does the same, and main's `before-quit` cancels the quit electron-updater had queued; the card then points at the release page, as electron-updater starts one install a run (C.94).

**(o) Logo concepts.** Shared geometry: `pebble_points(cx, cy, a, b_top, b_bottom, n, rot)` is a superellipse, x = a·sgn(cos t)·abs(cos t)^(2/n), y = b·sgn(sin t)·abs(sin t)^(2/n) with b = b_bottom where sin t > 0 and b_top otherwise, rotated by rot about the centre; vertical gradients via `Image.linear_gradient('L')` and `ImageOps.colorize` through a polygon mask; values are fractions of the side, drawn at 8x and reduced with LANCZOS; the small spec applies at 40 px and below. **A "Seam"** (chosen 2026-10-14, in turquoise: rim #5ad3db to #178e9c, body #29393c to #121b1d, ghost #7d999b, line #f1efe6, dots #4fd8e0; the colours below are the ember original, kept as the alternative): pebble cx .5, cy .52, a .49, b_top .49, b_bottom .44, n 2.6, rotation -5 degrees; rim = whole pebble #f08a3c to #c2401c, inner pebble (each semi-axis minus max(.035, 1.25/size)) #4a3d36 to #211a17; large: ghost #9a8577 x .3189 to .6811, top .2873, height .0596, fully rounded; line #f4ecdc x .2337 to .7663, top .4185, height .1312, radius height/4; 5 dots #ff8a3d diameter .0789, gap .0425, centred, top .6473; small: no ghost, line top .355 height .18, 3 dots diameter .14 gap .07 top .605. These are `brand.7`'s numbers, which the author approved on 2026-10-21 from a second comparison sheet, after seeing `brand.6`'s ("a tiny bit bigger still"): the pebble taller only, as it already met the left and right edges, so the tilted outline spans about .026 to .964 of the side down; the large spec scaled again about y .49 with the new height; and a still taller line and larger dots at 40 px and below (C.92 has how). `brand.6`'s numbers, approved earlier the same day from a sheet comparing the icon before and after at 16 to 48 px on the taskbar's light and dark greys, made a pebble that fills the frame as the other icons on the taskbar do, with the large spec scaled with it about the pebble's middle so the 256 and 1024 px renders keep their proportions: the pebble at b_top .47, b_bottom .41, the large ghost at top .2982, height .0564, the line at top .4223, height .1241 and the dots of .0767 with gaps of .0452 at .6378, and the small line at top .37, height .16 with dots of .13 at .60. Seam as chosen on 2026-10-14 had the pebble at a .46, b_top .42, b_bottom .36, the large ghost at x .33 to .67, top .32, height .05, the line at x .25 to .75, top .43, height .11 and the dots of .07 with gaps of .045 at .62, and the small line at top .40, height .13 with dots of .10; C's "as A" below means those. **B "Ember tile"**: rounded square pad .03 radius .22, #ec7a3a to #a8361a; ghost #ffd2ad x .315 to .70 top .33 height .055; line #2a211d x .215 to .785 top .52 height .115 with serif uprights height .168 width .03; 6 dots #fff1e0 diameter .05 gap .04 top .688; small: line top .42 height .14, no serifs or ghost, 3 dots diameter .10 gap .07 top .64. **C "Cursor"**: pebble and rim as A with cy .53, b_top .41; line #f4ecdc x .20 to .54 centred at y .465 height .11 (small .14); ghost (large) #9a8577 x .26 to .50 top .30 height .05; ember #ff8a3d I-beam at x .66, stem width .075 (small .10) from y .27 to .69 (small .26 to .70), caps width .19 (small .22) height .065 (small .09), all rounded. None uses purple, facets or a radial spark. B sits closest to Claude's orange; C's I-beam reads as a letter. On macOS 26 any non-squircle icon sits on a grey tile, which `brand.10` handles.

**(p) Where data lives** (README and `opensource.11`). `%APPDATA%\ai-grammar-checker` (name predates the rename): `settings.json`, `settings.json.corrupt-*`, `secrets.json` (the ChatGPT sign-in since `codex.2`: its host id and registrations, and its tokens encrypted; the encrypted OpenAI key too until `codex.6`, a key from before then dropped at the next write), `secrets.json.corrupt-*` (codex.2 review), `reviews\` (default reviews folder, holds chapter text), `backups\` (full chapter copies), `drafts\` and `drafts\set-aside\` (typed prose), `logs\main.log` and `main.1.log`, and, once the updater has checked, `.updaterId`, a random id electron-updater keeps for staged roll-outs, which the app never sends (`release.8b`). `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\manuscript-review`: the app. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\manuscript-review-updater`: a cached copy of the installer, used for small updates. Uninstalling removes only the app folder; the README says how to delete the rest. The manuscript folder holds chapters and `GUIDELINES.md` (created once, never overwritten). The Claude sign-in belongs to Claude Code, never to the app. On macOS and Linux the data folder is `~/Library/Application Support/ai-grammar-checker` or `~/.config/ai-grammar-checker`.

**(q) Claude through the user's `claude` command** (11.6 question 21, `cli.1`). No Anthropic package is a dependency, so nothing of Anthropic's ships. `claudeCli.ts` runs the path from `setup.3` with no shell, `windowsHide`, `cwd` = userData, the env from `buildClaudeEnv`, and `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --tools "" --setting-sources= --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence --permission-mode dontAsk --effort <e> --max-turns 3 --include-partial-messages`, plus `--model <m>` unless the model is `default`. The system prompt and the JSON schema travel in the `initialize` control request (`systemPrompt: [text]`, `jsonSchema`), as the SDK sent them, so a long guidelines file never meets the Windows command-line limit; the chapter goes in as one user message on stdin. It reads NDJSON lines: `system` init, `assistant`, `rate_limit_event` (its `status`, `resetsAt`, `rateLimitType`, `utilization` and `isUsingOverage`: `readRateLimit`, `setup.9`, C.64), and `result` with `structured_output`, `usage`, `total_cost_usd`, `modelUsage`, `is_error` and `subtype`. The same classifiers as before map failures. Cancel ends the process tree (`taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` on Windows). The model list and account details come from the CLI's `initialize` control request over stream-json, which is what the SDK sent. Check it against the installed version first; if that exchange is unavailable, fall back to a static alias list (Default, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) without version labels. Every flag was present in Claude Code 2.1.266's `--help` on 2026-10-14: `--tools ""` disables all tools, and `--bare` must never be used because it turns off subscription sign-in. `MIN_CLAUDE_CODE` in `src/shared/ai/claudeStatus.ts` is the oldest version the argument test was verified against.

### 11.4 Release checklist

This is the checklist for 1.0.0. `docs/RELEASING.md` (`release.10`) gives the same steps for every release, with the checks that come round each time (Claude Code, electron-builder and electron-updater) and the smoke checklist for a release after 1.0.0. That checklist splits step 14 in two: the uninstall, the reinstall of the release being cut and the dark start first, and only then the previous release put back on for the update to find, so that a later release, too, has its own reinstall and dark start checked.

Before the cut (agent unless marked):

1. M0 to M10 ticked or recorded as cut in this section; sitting C held and its answers recorded (`theme.10`); the author has approved `theme.12`'s screenshots of the turquoise buttons (its tick names them), or the colours changed as he asked, and `opensource.13` has shot the README's screenshots again in them; the author has approved `polish.1`'s screenshots of the selection band (its tick names them), which he asked for "if it does not hurt usability", or the band changed as he asked; the paragraph box's glow settled with the author (the `theme.12` review): either he keeps it on `--accent`, the blue of the box's border, and changes the sentence of CLAUDE.md that calls it a glow of `--accent-fill`, or he picks the glow on `--accent-fill` or border and glow both on it (`editor-glow-choice.png` and `editor-glow-three-ways.png` among `theme.12`'s sheets), which a follow-up builds with `themeCss.test.ts` and 11.3 (e), and CLAUDE.md stays as it is; the author has pasted one chapter's Export HTML into a Royal Road draft beside his own converter's result, and the converter's rules follow what Royal Road kept, recorded in C.111 (`rr.1`); every M12 task marked build or cut in Appendix D.
2. `release.21` done; `npm view electron-builder dist-tags` and `npm view electron-updater dist-tags` checked for newer v26 patches.
3. The package verifier confirms that no Anthropic binary ships (Appendix D 8), and the pages in Appendix A were re-read for changes.
4. CHANGELOG `[1.0.0]` dated; README final; `npm run check:public` clean.
5. On a fresh clone of `main`: `npm ci`, `branding:check`, `check:public`, `lint`, `format:check`, `test`, `build`, `package` (verifier with `--installer`).

Cut:

6. `npm version 1.0.0 -m "Release %s"`; **(author)** approves `git push origin main` then `git push origin v1.0.0` (never `--tags` or `--all`).
7. The workflow creates a draft with exactly 4 assets; check `SHA256SUMS.txt` against the files.

Smoke test, sitting D **(author)**, on a new local standard account (Settings > Accounts > Other users > "Add a user without a Microsoft account") with no Claude Code, no `.claude` folder and no Node; record this PC's Smart App Control state:

8. Download the setup exe from the draft in Edge; screenshot every browser prompt; `Get-FileHash` matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The agent compares the screenshots of this step and the next with the steps in `.github/release-footer.md`, which `release.6b` wrote without seeing them, and corrects the footer, the draft's notes and the README's Installing section, which `opensource.11` took from the footer word for word (`test/scripts/docs.test.ts` fails when the two differ), before step 15.
9. Run it; screenshot SmartScreen; expect only a progress bar, no UAC, install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\manuscript-review`, shortcuts named Lapidary, a legible taskbar icon in light and dark.
10. About shows 1.0.0; Setup says Claude Code is not installed; the theme follows Windows; a second shortcut launch focuses the first window.
11. Install Claude Code and sign in using only the Setup screen (`setup.14`); the app turns Connected on refocus; record the CLI's printed lines; Test the connection works.
12. Copy `samples/manuscript` to Documents, complete the Welcome steps, run a review with the Default model, accept, dismiss, edit a paragraph, close with an open box (prompt), Save to chapter (backup created; Notepad shows the file with its line endings), Copy diagnostics (the agent checks the pasted text for versions and no secrets).
13. With the dev switch variables set in the environment, the app ignores them.
14. Uninstall: the app folder goes, the data folders stay; reinstall 1.0.0. Launch once with Appearance set to Dark: no light flash.
15. **(author)** Publish: `gh release edit v1.0.0 --draft=false --latest`. Check for updates now says "Up to date".

Updater proof: ship a small real fix as 1.0.1 through steps 4 to 7 and publish it. In the test account, 1.0.0 offers 1.0.1 within 15 s with a size; the download shows progress; Restart now with an open box raises the close prompt; after closing the box the overlay and the NSIS progress window appear and the app reopens as 1.0.1 with no UAC or SmartScreen; settings and reviews intact; Restart now during a review is refused; a downloaded but uninstalled update survives a restart without a second download. The agent reads "Full: X, To download: Y" from the pasted log and records sizes in PLAN; above about 20 MB for an app-only change, note `differentialPackage: 'store-asar'` (26.17.0) as a follow-up. Then the author runs `brand.9`'s carry-over checks on his own account, sends the friend the release link, and `files.13` begins.

Conditional on the friend's OS: **macOS** (`release.16`, `brand.10`): a `macos` job uploads dmg, zip, blockmaps and `latest-mac.yml`, a final job rewrites `SHA256SUMS.txt`; on his Mac: Safari download, Open Anyway, Setup ready, one review and Save, binary hash equals the manifest's, `codesign -dv` still shows Anthropic's team, the update card links to the release page. **Linux** (`release.17`): a `linux` job uploads .deb, .AppImage and `latest-linux.yml`; on Ubuntu 24.04 the deb installs, a review and Save work, and an AppImage updates itself.

### 11.5 Risks

- **Anthropic's terms move.** The author accepts no Anthropic terms and ships no Anthropic binary; each user runs their own Claude Code under their own agreement with Anthropic. The SDK documentation still discourages third-party products built on subscription sign-in, and Anthropic has pressed at least one free tool to drop it (Appendix A). If that happens here, Claude Code on an API key and ChatGPT remain. Mitigations: no login control, no credential handling, plain-text attribution, the pages re-read before each release.
- **Claude Code version skew.** Each user's Claude Code updates on its own schedule; the author's had stalled at 2.1.266 on 2026-10-14. Setup flags anything older than `MIN_CLAUDE_CODE`. A newer Claude Code could rename or drop a flag the app passes; the pinned argument test, the per-release check in `release.10` and a clear error (never a silent wrong answer) cover that.
- **Smart App Control or S mode** blocks an unsigned app outright. Ask early (`files.17`); signing costs money and does not remove SmartScreen at this scale.
- **The NSIS updater kills the app** about 1.3 s after it starts. Guard, flushes, overlay and `allowNextClose` happen before the installer is spawned; drafts and decisions are on disk within 700 ms.
- **A close-guard bug traps the window.** Clean states close with no IPC, the renderer always answers in `finally`, two native fallbacks end in `destroy()`, and a gone renderer is bypassed.
- **Content leaks** through new log calls, diagnostics, issues or screenshots. The scalar-only API, one error policy, content-scan tests, `check:public` and the issue-form checkbox guard against it; screenshots come from the mock.
- **Supply chain.** Whoever controls the GitHub account or the release job can update every install; unsigned updates are checked only by sha512. 2FA, SHA-pinned actions, no cache, draft-then-publish.
- **SDK and toolchain churn.** The Agent SDK ships almost daily and CI cannot run a live Claude call; v26 fixes hide under the `v26` dist-tag; electron-builder 27 and electron-updater 7 are alpha. Quarterly Dependabot, a manual bump routine, exact pins.
- **Update size.** Without Claude Code the installer is mostly Electron: 108.7 MiB, of which the app's own asar is 21.9 MiB before compression (measured in `release.4`'s review fix, C.88), and 109.4 MiB (114,717,919 bytes) with an asar of 23.9 MiB on Electron 44.9.3 (`opensource.11`'s scratch build of HEAD); deleting a published `.blockmap` turns every update into a full download. An app fix was thought to download most of the asar; `opensource.11` measured far less. Two `npm run package` builds of HEAD in a scratch worktree, the second at version 0.1.1 with one string changed in `src/shared/ui/about.ts`, gave blockmaps that electron-updater 6.8.10's own `computeOperations` (the plan behind its "Full: X, To download: Y" line) turned into a download of 1,168,479 bytes, 1.0% of the 114,717,952-byte new installer, plus the blockmaps it fetches, about 118 KiB each. Real updates, and one that moves Electron, may differ; 11.4's updater proof reads the real figure. electron-builder 26.17.0 also offers `differentialPackage: 'store-asar'`, which stores the asar uncompressed in the installer so that an app fix downloads about what changed, for an installer bigger by about what compressing the asar saves; 11.3 (n) keeps `true`.
- **Guard false positives** keep a few legitimate prose fixes out (a stray `#word`, "per cent" to `%`); they stay visible under Unanchored. Joint syntax creation by two model edits is possible after the trim and shows in the ghost text before acceptance.
- **Adoption** can attach a review from a disconnected drive to a same-named chapter; strict rules, a 500-character floor, no adoption on ties and an info card limit it.
- **Hot-file collisions** across workstreams: the one-task-at-a-time rule and the M2 seams.
- **The Linux CI leg** has never run; it stays non-required until it passes once.
- **The scroll fix may not be the whole story** (GPU, display); an "unchanged" A/B result is recorded as a known cosmetic issue.
- **Same-name products.** Igneous was dropped for this (Appendix D 1). On 2026-10-14 Lapidary had only small, unrelated software uses and no software trademark; the domain lapidary.app is someone else's.
- **Disk use**: the installed app, 342.1 MiB, plus the updater cache, which holds a copy of the installer, 108.7 MiB: about 450 MiB together (measured on the build in `release.4`'s review fix, which did not run the installer, C.88). On Electron 44.9.3, `release.21`'s build: `dist/win-unpacked` 361,843,466 bytes (345.1 MiB) and the installer 114,717,915 bytes (109.4 MiB), about 455 MiB, which the README rounds to 345, 110 and 460 MB (`opensource.11`). Uninstall leaves the cache behind (documented).

### 11.7 Small changes you can see (`small`)

A change that touches only punctuation, a space or a one-letter word gets trimmed to 0 or 1 characters (4.3, step 5). Its mark in the line is then only as wide as that one character: 4 to 7 px of underline, or a 2 px caret for an insertion. In the screenshot the author sent with the round 6 feedback (2026-10-14), paragraph 74's accepted hyphen-to-space in "double standard" is a 4 px grey line under a space, and the faint "WAS -" above it has a strike-through that merges into the hyphen. Paragraph 76's pending comma after "Mira" is a 2 px purple bar with a 3 px comma above it and an invisible x 23 px to its right. Both are hard to spot while scrolling and hard to hit: about 5 x 22 px on the line, against 68 x 21 px for the word "standard".

**Decisions.**

- **Drawn bigger, never stored bigger.** Nothing here changes a hunk field, an offset, a text node in the prose, or anything `compose.ts` reads, so Save to chapter and Copy result cannot change (CLAUDE.md rules 4 and 5). Widening the stored hunk instead would move offsets, demote neighbours in `resolveOverlaps`, and let `touches()` supersede it more often. It would also make the ghost repeat the whole word, against 4.3 step 5.
- **One definition of small.** `isSmallText(text)` lives in a new `src/shared/ui/small.ts`. After combining marks (`\p{M}`) are removed, the text is small when it has at most 1 code point, or at most 3 code points with no letter or digit (`\p{L}`, `\p{N}`). So "", ",", " ", "i", "--" and "..." are small; "an", "it" and "----" are not. `trim.ts` already widens every letter change to its whole word, so this catches exactly punctuation, whitespace and one-letter words, which are all under one em at 17 px. Each surface asks the question of the text it shows:
  - the line asks `isSmallLive`, which tests the live face and excludes text holding a line break, because that box is split across lines;
  - the keycap tests the ghost face;
  - margin marks and list rows ask `isSmallChange`, which tests both sides, so a row looks the same whatever its status.
- **The caret stays with its word and follows status.** `.hunk__caret` becomes `display: inline`. The inline-block caret broke away from "Mira" onto the next line at 3 of 651 window widths, the inline one at none, and no word joiner is needed. The caret turns `--ink-faint` when accepted and `--border-strong` when dismissed. Today it keeps the category colour, against "colour means undecided" (7).
- **A capsule under small live text.** An absolutely positioned `::after` on `.hunk__live`, 0.75em wide or the glyph's width if wider. It is painted beneath the glyphs (`.para { isolation: isolate }`, `z-index: -1`), so neighbouring letters stay pure ink.
  - Pending: the category colour at `--tint-small`, mixed over transparent so it also sits correctly on the active paragraph's yellow, with a 2 px category `border-bottom` across it.
  - Accepted: a 2 px `--ink-faint` border-bottom and no fill.
  - Dismissed: a 1 px dotted `--border-strong` line.
  - Hit zone: a transparent `::before`, 0.9em wide.
  - Touching hunks: both pseudo-elements pull back to the hunk's own edge on any side where the neighbouring plain text is shorter than 2 characters, so neither covers a touching hunk.
  - Why it moves nothing: absolute boxes add no advance, so line breaks, the span rect (scroll target, tooltip, popover), the inputs to `clipGhosts` and the heights of margin notes are unchanged.
  - Borders rather than box-shadow, because forced colours drop shadows.
  - The click target on the line grows from about 5 x 22 to 16 x 23 px.
  - When focused, the capsule (not the whole span) takes `--focus-bg`. The ghost above stays on the page, as a word-sized change's does, and the arrowhead marks the line. Until the `small` review `.hunk__ghost` took `--focus-bg` too, where spelling, homophone, punctuation and other came to 4.14, 4.18, 4.28 and 4.03:1 in dark, under the 4.5 that 11.3 (e) asks of a category as text; a ring with no fill read as a keycap round the whole ghost (C.68).
- **A keycap ghost.** A small ghost sits in a box: a 1 px rounded border in the ghost's colour at 60%, no fill, and the glyph at 1.25 times the ghost size. Since `small.7` only named whitespace keeps the box: with a box on every key the rows piled up on a dialogue line with six small changes, so punctuation and one-letter words are the bare glyph at 1.25 times, still unstruck.
  - Whitespace is named in small caps: SPACE, 2 SPACES, NO-BREAK SPACE, TAB, LINE BREAK, PARAGRAPH BREAK.
  - An accepted insertion reads "ADDED [,]" instead of a bare "ADDED".
  - Text decoration does not reach inside an inline-block, so a small original is not struck through. Its "was" label carries that meaning, and the rule in 7 that a replaced original is always struck through gets this exception.
  - Case 1 then reads "WAS [-]". An inserted space reads "-> [SPACE]" instead of an arrow pointing at nothing. On case 2 the hover-only x moves from +23 to +38 px, so a click aimed at the comma no longer dismisses it.
  - No fill, because light `--cat-word-choice` is exactly 4.5:1 on `--bg` and any tint behind it would fail the theme contrast test.
  - A pure `ghostContent(hunk)` in `src/shared/render.ts` chooses the role label, tag and key, replacing the inline choice in `HunkSpan.tsx`.
- **Words for invisible characters.** One table in `small.ts` (`whitespaceName`, `characterName`, `sideText`) feeds the list row, the tooltip, the details and stale pairs, and the aria-label.
  - Case 1's row reads "- (hyphen) -> (space)" instead of "- -> (nothing)", which described it as a deletion. "(nothing)" stays for the empty string only.
  - Words, not U+2423 or U+00B6: a new reader will not know those symbols, and Literata may lack them.
  - List rows for small changes also show a few words on either side, with the change in a chip styled like the keycap ("...up with Mira [-> ,] who had..."), built by a pure `changeInContext(base, hunk)`. Stale rows keep their pair.
- **Margin marks for pending small changes, and an arrowhead for focus.**
  - A 3 px x 0.9em bar in the category colour sits in the rail, level with each line that holds a pending small change. An ink arrowhead marks the line where the focused hunk starts, whatever its size.
  - The left edge is where the eye returns on every line, and it is where proofreaders and change bars put their marks.
  - Marks are buttons with no text, placed by CSS anchor positioning (`anchor-name` on `.hunk__live`, `top: calc(anchor(top) - 0.53em)`). That follows reflow, zoom and font loading with no measuring pass. Electron 44.3.0 ships Chromium 152, where a mock placed marks within 0.5 px, including next to a caret that had wrapped to the next line.
  - The 11 x 39 px target lies outside the prose. Hovering shows the tooltip under the change, for reading only; to edit, click the bar and press `e`. Clicking selects without scrolling, and then `a`, `d` and `u` act.
  - The bar and the arrowhead are one button under one key, so a bar that becomes the arrowhead under the pointer keeps its element and its leave still runs. A mark that unmounts while the pointer is on it closes its card itself (`markHover`), since React fires no leave for an element that has gone (the `small` review).
  - Decided small changes get no mark, so a worked chapter goes quiet.
  - Bars and arrowhead are drawn with borders. The rail narrows from 42 to 39 px.
- **Keys that start where the author is reading.**
  - Shift+J and Shift+K go to the next and previous pending change, skip decided ones, and wrap.
  - When nothing is focused, or the focused change is off screen, `j`/`k` (and their Shift forms) start from the paragraphs on screen; otherwise they step as today. Today the first `j` after scrolling jumps back to the old focus or to paragraph 1.
  - Today Caps Lock also disables `j`/`k`, because only lowercase is handled. Shift is now read from `event.shiftKey`.
  - Letters rather than `[` and `]`, which need AltGr on a Canadian French layout and never reach `keyboard.ts`.
  - The keys and the list sort with one comparator (start, end, id), which is the order `activeHunks` renders in. Today they break ties three different ways.

**What each shape looks like afterwards.** Capsule, cup (a grey line with no fill) and dotted line are all 0.75em wide; [x] is a keycap and "bar" is a margin mark. A focused hunk of any of these shapes has its capsule on `--focus-bg`, with the arrowhead in the rail; its ghost stays on the page. Word-sized hunks are unchanged apart from that arrowhead.

| Shape | Pending | Accepted | Dismissed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Comma inserted after "Mira" (case 2) | caret in a purple capsule; `-> [,]`; bar | comma over a cup; `ADDED [,]` | grey caret over a dotted line; faded `-> [,]` |
| Comma or doubled space deleted | the comma or gap in a capsule; `-> DELETE` (plus `[SPACE]` for whitespace); bar | grey caret over a cup; `WAS [,]` or `WAS [SPACE]` | glyph over a dotted line; faded `-> DELETE` |
| One-character swap, "." to "," | period in a capsule; `-> [,]`; bar | comma over a cup; `WAS [.]` | period over a dotted line; faded `-> [,]` |
| Hyphen to space, "double standard" (case 1) | hyphen in a capsule; `-> [SPACE]`; bar | a cup under the gap, reaching the edges of "e" and "s"; `WAS [-]`, not struck through; row "- (hyphen) -> (space)" | hyphen over a dotted line; faded `-> [SPACE]` |
| One-letter word, "i" to "I" | "i" in a capsule; `-> [I]`; bar | "I" over a cup; `WAS [i]` | "i" over a dotted line; faded `-> [I]` |

A change whose live text holds a line break, such as a paragraph join, gets no capsule. Its keycap names what replaces the break, and while it is pending its bar marks the line.

## Appendix B: development machine (2026-09-08, updated 2026-10-16)

Windows 11, Node 24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, git 2.45.2. Claude Code 2.1.266 is installed natively at `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe`. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not set. PowerShell 5.1 is the primary shell and Git Bash is available. Shell heredocs are unreliable on this machine: long ones fail, and escape handling has turned a backslash sequence into a control character. Files are therefore written with the editor tools, not shell redirection. The folder is a git repository. Since 2026-10-16 it is public at `github.com/MichaelBradetLegris/lapidary` (remote `origin`), default branch `main`, which began as one fresh commit of the tree (`opensource.9`); the earlier private repository keeps the old history. The folder has a repo-local identity, `Michael Bradet-Legris <45394569+MichaelBradetLegris@users.noreply.github.com>`, and `commit.gpgsign false`, so no public commit carries the personal address or a key tied to it. Under Appendix D 7 as changed on 2026-10-14, the agent may commit and push: it works on a branch per milestone, pushes it, and fast-forwards `main` once the milestone verifies. It never force-pushes, and the `main` ruleset refuses force-pushes and deletion anyway.

## Appendix C: deviations from this plan, recorded as they happened

### C.1 Vite 7 instead of Vite 8 (Phase 0)

electron-vite 5.0.0, the newest stable release, declares `vite: ^5 || ^6 || ^7` as a peer dependency. Vite 8 is only reachable through electron-vite 6.0.0-beta.1, and `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6 requires Vite 8 while version 5 covers Vite 4 to 7. The project therefore uses electron-vite 5.0.0 with Vite 7.3.6 and `@vitejs/plugin-react` 5.2.0, all stable releases. Nothing in the design depends on a Vite 8 feature. Revisit when electron-vite 6 ships stable.

### C.2 ESM main process, CJS preload (Phase 0)

`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` is ESM only (`"type": "module"`, `main: sdk.mjs`). Requiring it from a CommonJS Electron main bundle would depend on Electron's `require(esm)` support, which the plan never verified. The package is therefore `"type": "module"`, electron-vite emits `out/main/index.js` as ESM, and the preload is pinned to CommonJS (`out/preload/index.cjs`) so the window can keep `sandbox: true`. Paths in main use `import.meta.url` rather than `__dirname`.

### C.3 Typecheck runs through project references (Phase 0)

`tsc --noEmit -p ...` cannot be combined with `composite`, so `npm run typecheck` is `tsc --build --force` over `tsconfig.node.json` and `tsconfig.web.json`, both `emitDeclarationOnly` into `node_modules/.tmp`. Behaviour is the same: type errors fail the command, nothing lands in `out/`.

### C.4 Matches must respect word boundaries (Phase 1)

Sections 4.3 and 4.5 anchor on plain substring search. The property tests found this is not safe: "began" matches inside "beganning" and, in the generated cases, "w1" matches inside "w10", so a hunk could anchor to the wrong span and rewrite untouched prose. `cleanOccurrences` in `src/shared/diff/fuzzy.ts` now prefers matches whose neighbouring characters are not word characters, falling back to raw matches only when a word occurs solely mid-word. It also decides `exact` versus `ambiguous`.

Rebase gained a related change: instead of "look for the expected side, then the other side", it collects candidates for both sides and ranks them by word-boundary cleanliness first, then by distance from the old offset, with a one-character tie-break in favour of the side the hunk expected. Without this, an accepted hunk whose `original` still appears mid-word elsewhere re-anchored onto the wrong text.

### C.5 Rebase adopts what is on disk (Phase 1)

Section 4.5 says to update `baseSide` when the author applied a change by hand, but not what happens to the decision. Leaving a hunk `pending` while `baseSide` is `replacement` would make the next save silently revert the author's own edit. The rule implemented is: when the found side differs from the recorded one, the disk wins and the decision follows it. Text now showing the replacement becomes `accepted`; an `accepted` hunk whose text is back to the original returns to `pending`. When the found side matches the recorded side, which is the normal case, the decision is untouched, so the round-trip property in 4.5 still holds. Since `apply.23` the disk wins only where it plainly says so, and a hunk it seems to contradict, but not plainly, leaves the page instead (C.52).

### C.6 Rebase ranks candidates by surrounding context (Phase 3)

Ranking re-anchor candidates by distance from the old offset breaks on short common words. Driving the real app showed it: after a paragraph was inserted above them, an accepted `of` -> `have` hunk re-anchored onto an unrelated `of` and its decision was flipped back to pending. `rebase.ts` now scores every candidate by how many characters either side of it still agree with the old file (40 each way) and ranks word-boundary cleanliness first, then context agreement, then distance, then the expected side. There is a regression test for it in `test/shared/rebase.test.ts`. `apply.23` (C.52) adds zero-width places for a side that holds no text, counts the start and end of the file as agreeing where both texts begin or end there, and puts the expected side before distance.

### C.7 The guidelines file is not a chapter (Phase 3)

`GUIDELINES.md` lives in the manuscript folder and is Markdown, so it appeared in the chapter list and could be opened and reviewed. `files:list` now excludes the resolved guidelines path.

### C.8 How the running app is tested

electron-vite's dev command honours a `REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT` environment variable, so `REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=9222 npm run dev` exposes the renderer over the DevTools protocol without any code in the app. A short script can then evaluate expressions in the live window, including `await import('/state/store.ts')`, which returns the very store module the app is running. That is how the file list, save, watcher and rebase behaviour above were exercised against real files. No debugging hooks are compiled into the app.

### C.9 Tools are removed with `tools: []`, not a hardcoded deny list (Phase 4, risk 2)

`sdk.d.ts` has a top-level `tools` option documented as "`[]` (empty array) - Disable all built-in tools". That is used instead of enumerating `disallowedTools`, so the list can never drift as tool names change. The call also passes `mcpServers: {}`, `strictMcpConfig: true`, `settingSources: []`, `persistSession: false`, `permissionMode: 'dontAsk'` and `cwd: app.getPath('userData')`. `Options.env` REPLACES the subprocess environment rather than merging, so `process.env` is spread explicitly.

### C.10 `maxTurns` is 3, not 1 (Phase 4, risk 1)

The SDK delivers structured output through an internal end-turn tool call and retries on a schema mismatch, so one turn is not a safe budget. The value is 3 as the plan's risk note anticipated. The verified run used one turn of it.

### C.11 The zod JSON Schema target is `draft-07` (Phase 4)

Section 5.3 writes `z.toJSONSchema(..., { target: 'draft-7' })`. zod 4.5.4 accepts `'draft-04' | 'draft-07' | 'draft-2020-12' | 'openapi-3.0'`. The code uses `'draft-07'` and a test asserts the emitted `$schema`.

### C.12 The model dropdown keeps aliases the CLI does not list (Phase 4, risk 5)

`supportedModels()` on the author's Max plan returns `default`, `opus[1m]`, `claude-fable-5-1[1m]`, `sonnet`, `haiku`. Plain `opus`, which is the default setting and which the CLI resolves correctly to `claude-opus-5`, is not among them, so a plain `<select>` displayed the wrong row. `modelOptions` in `src/renderer/state/models.ts` prepends the stored value when the list does not contain it.

### C.13 Risk 3 is closed: the SDK runs its bundled binary from Electron main

_Superseded by C.42 (2026-10-14): the app no longer uses the SDK or bundles Claude Code._

No `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` and no `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` were needed. `checkRuntime()` found `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-win32-x64/claude.exe` and reported `state: 'ready'` with the account email and `Claude Max`. `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` is passed only when the bundled binary is absent and a native install is found instead.

### C.14 A dev-only userData override (Phase 5a)

The author's saved settings point at their real vault, so a test run must not read them. `src/main/index.ts` honours `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_USER_DATA` and calls `app.setPath('userData', ...)` at module scope, before anything can read the path. Since `hardening.1` only development builds honour the variable, read in `src/main/devSwitches.ts`; a packaged build takes `--isolated-user-data=<dir>` instead (C.39). Verification runs used `.dev-userdata` in the repo (gitignored) with settings pointing at `samples/`. Since `setup.15` they start through `npm run dev:clean` (C.43), on `.dev-userdata` or a scratch folder given with `--user-data`, whose settings point at a scratch copy of the manuscript, never at `samples/` itself, so a save cannot change a tracked file (section 11, Safe verification). Nothing in the app depends on the variable being set.

### C.15 Find uses the CSS Custom Highlight API, not `findInPage` or `<mark>` (Phase 5a, item 11)

Wrapping matches in elements would split the text nodes inside hunk spans, which is exactly the structure the offsets and the absolutely positioned ghosts depend on. `webContents.findInPage` avoids that but cannot be scoped, so it would count and highlight ghost text as if it were the chapter. `CSS.highlights` paints ranges over the existing nodes: no DOM change at all, and the tree walker skips `.hunk__ghost`, so the count only refers to real prose. `src/renderer/state/find.ts` degrades to counting and scrolling without painting if the API is ever missing.

### C.16 Bulk actions only move pending suggestions (Phase 5a, item 8)

The old `setAllStatuses` overwrote every hunk, so "Dismiss all" silently threw away work the author had already accepted. The confirmation wording the author asked for ("Suggestions you already accepted are not changed") is now the actual rule: accept and dismiss target only `pending` hunks, and reset targets only decided ones. `bulkPlan` returns the affected ids with the sentence, and the store applies exactly those ids, so the count in the modal cannot drift from what happens.

### C.17 The position strip approximates by character offset (Phase 5a, item 14)

The marks beside the scrollbar are placed at `hunk.start / base.text.length`. Prose sets at a constant line height, so character position tracks vertical position closely enough for a locator, and the alternative, measuring every hunk element on every reflow, is not worth the cost for a hint. Clicking a mark focuses and scrolls to the real element, so the approximation never decides anything.

### C.18 The "Ã—" glyph was in the source, not in the pipeline (Phase 5a, item 1)

`App.tsx` contained the characters `Ã` (U+00C3) and `—` (U+2014) where a multiplication sign was meant: someone's editor had read UTF-8 `C3 97` as Windows-1252 and saved the result. The file itself is valid UTF-8, which is why the chips' `×` rendered correctly and only this one did not. Rather than fix the character, every control glyph in the renderer is now an inline SVG path in `src/renderer/components/icons.tsx`, which no encoding round trip can corrupt.

### C.19 Dev shortcuts open DevTools detached (Phase 5a, item 10)

With the application menu removed, F12, Ctrl+Shift+I and Ctrl+R are handled in `before-input-event` and only when the app is not packaged. `toggleDevTools()` did not open a window on this machine; explicit `isDevToolsOpened()` plus `openDevTools({ mode: 'detach' })` does, and a detached window leaves the manuscript at full width. Note for future test rounds: CDP `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` does not reach `before-input-event`, and `SendKeys` does not deliver `{F12}`; real key presses through `keybd_event` do.

### C.20 The packaged app must be handed the unpacked binary (Phase 5b, item 1; risk 4)

_Superseded by C.42 (2026-10-14): nothing of Anthropic's is packaged any more._

`asarUnpack` alone was not enough. `bundledBinary()` looked in `app.getAppPath()` first, which once packaged is `resources/app.asar`, and Electron's fs shim answers `existsSync` for an unpacked file using its **archive** path. So the check passed, the asar path was handed to the SDK, and the spawn failed with a misleading "binary exists but failed to launch ... this usually means the binary does not match this system's libc". The packaged app reported `state: 'error'` with a message about musl on a Windows machine.

Two changes fixed it. `bundledBinary()` now rejects any candidate inside an asar outright and looks in `resources/app.asar.unpacked` first, and `resolvedExecutable()` passes the located path to the SDK explicitly whenever the app is packaged, rather than leaving the SDK to resolve its own sibling package with `require.resolve` (which would land inside the archive for the same reason). Development is unchanged: the SDK still finds its own binary, as C.13 recorded. The config unpacks both `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-win32-x64/**` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/**`.

### C.21 The app name is read out of the TypeScript source by two build scripts (Phase 5b, item 1)

`APP_NAME` lives in `src/shared/branding.ts`, which main and renderer import directly and `electron.vite.config.ts` substitutes into `index.html` through a `transformIndexHtml` plugin. The two consumers that cannot import TypeScript, `package.json` and the electron-builder config, read the constant out of that file with a regex in `scripts/branding.cjs`; `scripts/sync-branding.cjs` writes it into `package.json`'s `productName` and runs automatically as `prepackage`. It is not elegant, but it means renaming the app is a single edit, which is what the author asked for. Since `opensource.4` (2026-10-16) the same script also writes `repository`, `homepage` and `bugs` from `APP_REPOSITORY`. `npm run branding:check` runs it with `--check`, which writes nothing and exits 0 when package.json is in sync, or lists each field that differs and exits 1.

`APP_DATA_DIR` in the same file is deliberately **not** the display name. Electron derives `userData` from the application name, so tying the two together would move the author's settings and orphan every review in the default reviews folder the first time the app was renamed. `src/main/index.ts` pins `userData` to `%APPDATA%/ai-grammar-checker` unless `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_USER_DATA` overrides it.

### C.22 The icon is generated, not drawn by hand (Phase 5b, item 1)

`scripts/make-icons.py` holds one geometry spec in fractions of the icon's side and emits both `resources/icon/icon.svg` and every raster from it, so the vector and the bitmaps cannot drift. Rasters are drawn at 8x and reduced with LANCZOS, which is what keeps the 16 px version legible. Pillow writes the multi-size `.ico` directly. The art is name-neutral on purpose: a line of type, the coloured dotted underline this app puts under a pending suggestion, and the faint ghost line above it. An icon built from a letter would have to be redrawn with every rename. (The method stays; `brand.5` replaced the drawing with Seam in turquoise, C.92.)

### C.23 Superseded suggestions need a flag, not just a status (Phase 5b, item 3)

A suggestion swallowed by the author's own edit is dismissed and unanchored, but that is not enough on its own: its words usually still exist inside the edit that replaced them, so the next rebase re-anchors it happily, on top of the manual hunk, and `resolveOverlaps` then has to demote one of them on every reload. `Hunk.supersededBy` records which manual hunk took it, and `rebaseReview` leaves such a hunk stale as long as that hunk is still in the review. This is one field beyond what the feedback asked for, and it is the thing that makes "they leave the inline view and stay in the Unanchored section" true rather than usually true.

### C.24 Ghost collisions are solved by measuring, not by CSS (Phase 5b, item 2)

Whether two ghosts overlap depends on where the line broke, which is known only after layout. `clipGhosts` resets every ghost's max width, measures the rows, groups them by top, and clips any ghost that would run into the next one on the same line. Because ghosts are absolutely positioned, changing their width moves nothing the prose depends on, so the `ResizeObserver` that triggers the pass cannot be re-triggered by it.

`ui.2` (2026-10-18) gave the same pass a second limit and moved the arithmetic into the pure `ghostMaxWidths` (`src/shared/ui/ghosts.ts`), tested with fast-check. The limit was first the right edge of the prose's text (the prose's box less its right padding and border); its review moved it out to what a row can reach without being cut or covering a note, `ghostEdge`: 6 px inside the pane's padding box, where `.pane` clips (`GHOST_EDGE_MARGIN`, so the x never sits on that edge or against the position strip), or 10 px short of the margin column while it shows. At the text's edge, a one-word suggestion near the end of a line, which had always run a little into the pane's padding with no scrollbar, was cut ("-> water..." for "-> watermill"), and an accepted insertion's lone "added" label read "ADD". Rows are now grouped into lines before they are ordered left to right, so a row a pixel higher than its left-hand neighbour still counts as its neighbour; the old sort by top then left could take them in the wrong order. A lone row is measured too, where the old pass needed two, and every row is read before any is changed, in one layout. The pane's `overflow-x: clip` is a backstop for anything the pass does not cover, such as a ghost kept at the 22 px minimum whose row starts at the very end of a line, and it also keeps the reset at the start of each pass from laying out a horizontal scrollbar for that moment. What it clips is hidden and cannot be clicked, so whatever else the pane holds has to fit a narrow column or wrap; the paragraph editor's buttons wrap since the same review (section 7).

### C.25 OpenAI effort is passed through, not folded down (Phase 5c)

The brief expected `xhigh` and `max` to be mapped to the highest effort the API accepts. The installed SDK's `ReasoningEffort` type is `'none' | 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'`, so the highest accepted value is the value itself and `OPENAI_EFFORT_FOR` is the identity. It is still written as an explicit `Record<EffortLevel, OpenAiEffort>` so a new app effort level fails to compile until someone decides what it means to OpenAI. The dialog said all five levels are passed through and that not every model supports them, until `codex.5` took the note out (C.116); a 400 from a model that refuses one says so.

### C.26 `generator.provider` is filled by its own load step, not by `migrateReview` (Phase 5c)

`migrateReview` has a tested contract from Phase 5b: a review that needs no rename comes back as the same object. Filling `provider: 'claude'` inside it would have broken that contract for every pre-5c Claude review. The default lives in `withGeneratorProvider`, and `reviews.ts` runs `upgradeLoadedReview` (both steps, in order) on every file it reads. OpenAI reviews also get `kind: 'openai'`, so the history badge and anything else keyed on `kind` tell the two apart without reading `provider`. Hunks keep `source: 'claude'` for both providers: it is the "a model wrote this" marker the editing rules key on, and renaming it would invalidate every review on disk.

### C.27 The strict schema is derived, and its nulls are undone precisely (Phase 5c)

OpenAI's strict mode needs every property required and has no notion of an absent optional field, so the one optional property in the schema (a comment's `quote`) becomes required and nullable in the schema sent to OpenAI. A blanket "drop every null" on the way back would also drop a comment's `paragraph: null`, which is required and means "about the whole chapter", and zod would reject the reply. `stripOptionalNulls` walks the reply alongside the original schema and removes a null only where the original did not require the property. Constraint keywords strict mode has historically rejected (`minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum`, `maximum`, and so on) are dropped from the OpenAI copy only; zod still enforces them locally, and Claude's schema is untouched.

### C.28 A model setting per provider (Phase 5c)

One `model` setting shared by both providers would have sent `opus` to OpenAI the first time the author switched. `openaiModel` sits beside `model`, which keeps its name because that is what every settings.json on disk already says. An empty `openaiModel` means "the list's default", which main resolves with the same `defaultOpenAiModel` the dialog uses, so what the dialog shows is what is sent.

### C.29 The OpenAI model list is fetched lazily (Phase 5c)

Claude's list still arrives with the launch-time runtime check. OpenAI's needs a network call on the author's key, so it is fetched the first time the review dialog shows OpenAI, and again whenever the key changes. The OpenAI runtime check itself only reads the local secrets file.

### C.30 Timers in a hidden test window (verification note)

While driving the dev window over CDP, the page reported `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` part way through (the cause was not established; the window was not minimised), and Chromium's background timer throttling slowed `setTimeout`-based waits in the test script to a crawl. The driver's waits now spin on `MessageChannel`, which is not throttled. Nothing in the app changed; this is for future test rounds. Since `dev.1` the likely cause is known: Chromium marks a wholly covered window's page hidden, and `--quiet` turns that off for test runs (Appendix C "Quiet test windows").

### C.31 Blocks merge for a hunk that starts inside the blank line (Phase 5d)

`buildRenderBlocks` used to merge two paragraphs into one block only when a hunk crossed the end of the first paragraph's text. A deletion of the last paragraph from its editor starts in the blank line before it, so it crossed no paragraph's text and belonged to neither block: composed correctly, drawn nowhere. The rule is now "a hunk starts before the next paragraph and ends after this block", which includes the old case. Deletions from the editor otherwise take the blank line after the paragraph, exactly as the full-text diff does.

### C.32 The status card lives outside the scroller (Phase 5d)

It was first a sticky card at the top of the pane. The pane is a stretched flex item, one screen tall, with its content overflowing it, so the sticky card scrolled away after the first screen. It now floats at the bottom of the pane's non-scrolling wrapper, like the notification cards at its top-right.

### C.33 The find bar lives outside the scroller (Phase 5e)

The same trap as C.32. The bar was sticky inside the pane, which is one screen tall with its content overflowing, so more than a screen down it opened out of sight and Ctrl+F seemed to do nothing. While it was open out of sight, every redraw also scrolled back to the active match, because the scroll ran on every repaint rather than only on a request. It is now a strip above the scroller, and scrolling is tied to `find.seek`, which only typing and stepping advance and which never goes back to zero.

### C.34 The x is invisible, not absent, until the suggestion is hovered (Phase 5e)

With `display: none`, an x that sat past the end of its word took no space, so a pointer arriving where it would appear found nothing to hover and the x never came back. It now keeps its room at zero opacity and is out of the tab order (the keyboard dismisses with `d`). Ghost clipping reserves that room when it shortens a ghost.

### C.35 Keys and wheel sent over DevTools skip Electron's input hooks (verification note, Phase 5f)

Key presses and wheel events injected with `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` / `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` reach the page but never pass through `before-input-event` or produce `zoom-changed`, so the zoom shortcuts cannot be tested that way. They were tested with real input sent through Windows (`keybd_event`, `mouse_event`) to the app's own window, after checking it was in the foreground. Real key presses arrive as `keyDown`.

### C.36 The window shows on first paint, page load or a timer, whichever comes first (packaging fix, 2026-10-14)

The window is created hidden and shown on `ready-to-show`, so it never flashes blank. In the packaged build on the author's machine, on Electron 44.3.0, that event never arrived: the process ran, the page loaded and rendered (checked over DevTools), and the window stayed hidden, so the installed app seemed not to open. Forcing `ShowWindow` on it brought up a working app. `did-finish-load` and a 3-second timer are now fallbacks in `createWindow`, and whichever fires first shows the window, once. The rebuilt package showed its window 0.6 s after launch. Development was never affected.

2026-10-21 (`release.21`, review fix): Electron 44.4.4's release notes list a fix for `ready-to-show` never firing for some hidden windows on Windows and Linux, and the app now runs on 44.9.3. Two scratch packaged builds of the same commit, not committed, logged each of the three triggers with its time from the window's creation and never showed the window, so no launch took the foreground; each was started three times through `dev:clean --exe` on a fresh scratch userData. On 44.3.0 `did-finish-load` came at 74 to 93 ms, the timer at 3 s, and `ready-to-show` not at all in the 10 s each run lasted. On 44.9.3 `did-finish-load` came at 75 to 158 ms, `ready-to-show` at 270 to 443 ms and the timer at 3 s. That fits the fix 44.4.4 lists being the one for this bug, though no version between the two was tried, and on both the page finishing its load is what shows the packaged window. The fallbacks stay: they cost nothing, the window is still shown only once, and a window that stays hidden looks like an app that does not open.

Verification note: `npm run package` fails with `EBUSY ... unlink dist\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar` while VS Code holds that file open (the Restart Manager API named VS Code as the holder). Restarting VS Code releases it.

### C.37 A copy from the page is the chapter's plain text (2026-10-14)

The author copied a paragraph and the paste contained the word "insertion". It was a visually hidden label inside every insertion, and the find bar matched it too. A real copy also showed more: the plain text had a blank line in front of every suggestion, because each ghost row is a box of its own, and the HTML carried the app's markup. The hidden word is gone; "insertion" is now part of the suggestion's `aria-label`. The `.prose` element handles `copy` itself and writes only `text/plain`: the chapter text the selection covers, as the page currently reads (pending suggestions show the original, accepted ones the replacement), with a blank line between paragraphs. `NOT_PROSE` in `renderer/state/prose.ts` is the one list of decoration that find and copy both skip, and the join is `joinProsePieces` in `shared/ui/copy.ts`. A copy inside an open paragraph editor is left to the textarea.

### C.38 Renamed to Lapidary: what moved and what did not (`brand.1`, 2026-10-14)

**What moved.** `APP_NAME` is now `Lapidary`, and with it:

- the window and HTML titles;
- package.json's `productName` (through `sync-branding.cjs`);
- the installer and shortcut names;
- the README title.

The package name went from `ai-grammar-checker` to `manuscript-review`, the frozen name the installer folder and the updater cache will use (11.1). `APP_ID` (the unchanged `dev.bradetlegris.manuscript-review`) and `APP_REPOSITORY` (`MichaelBradetLegris/lapidary`) joined `APP_NAME` in `src/shared/branding.ts`. `scripts/branding.cjs` now reads any constant there by name, so the builder config takes `appId` from it instead of repeating the string. The Claude client tag is `<app name in lower case>/<version>`. The OpenAI dev variable is `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, a prefix that never changes with the name.

**What did not move.** `APP_DATA_DIR` stays `ai-grammar-checker`, so settings, the encrypted OpenAI key and reviews in the default folder stay where they are (C.21). The review files' `SCHEMA_NAME` is unchanged, so existing reviews load as before. `APP_ID` did not move either, so an installed "Stet" from an earlier build has the same NSIS GUID (`NsisTarget.js` derives it from appId when `nsis.guid` is unset) and the same install and uninstall registry keys (`multiUser.nsh`). The Lapidary installer therefore treats Stet as an older version of itself: it starts from Stet's install folder, runs Stet's uninstaller silently with `/KEEP_APP_DATA --updated` (`installSection.nsh`, `uninstallOldVersion` in `installUtil.nsh`), and Installed apps afterwards shows a single entry, Lapidary. The data folder they share is untouched. Today's assisted installer adds a `Lapidary` subfolder to the folder it starts from (`instFilesPre` in `assistedInstaller.nsh`), so it lands in `Programs\Stet\Lapidary`; the one-click installer of 11.3 (n) would use Stet's folder as it is. This is read from the electron-builder 26.15.3 templates; no install of a Stet build followed by a Lapidary build has been run yet. (Corrected on 2026-10-16: this section first said Stet was a different app to Windows and had to be uninstalled by hand.)

### C.39 Dev switches are ignored by packaged builds (`hardening.1`, 2026-10-14)

Every development switch is read in `src/main/devSwitches.ts`, and nowhere else reads one from `process.env`. The switches are `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_USER_DATA`, `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_NO_CLAUDE_CODE` (renamed by C.43), `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_FAKE_UPDATE` and `MREV_VERBOSE`. A packaged build ignores them all and keeps their names for the log. A variable left in a shell profile could otherwise have sent the stored OpenAI key to another server, or moved an installed app's settings. The one switch a packaged build honours is the `--isolated-user-data=<dir>` command-line flag: it has to be typed for each launch, so it cannot linger, and it is how packaged builds are tested without touching real settings. It also wins over the variable in development.

The OpenAI SDK fills its base URL, organization, project and admin key from `OPENAI_*` variables whenever an option is left out. `clientOptions` therefore sets all of them, and a test builds a real client with hostile values in every one of those variables. A packaged build also sets the SDK's `logLevel` to `off`. `OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS` is still read by the SDK, but a header cannot change where the request goes.

### C.40 One running copy per user data folder (`release.18`, 2026-10-14)

Two copies of the app on the same data folder would race on `settings.json` and the review files. `src/main/index.ts` takes `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` right after setting userData, and Chromium keys the lock on that folder. The copy that loses quits before it writes anything. The one already running restores, shows and focuses its window on `second-instance`.

A test run with its own scratch folder still starts beside the author's copy. Checked with real launches: a second launch on the same folder exited in 0.4 s with code 0 and brought the minimised first window back, and a launch on another folder ran alongside.

`src/main/providers/controllers.ts` tracks every AbortController that work in flight holds: reviews, and for now the Claude runtime check and the model list. `will-quit` aborts them all synchronously and stops the watcher. That replaces the old `before-quit` and `window-all-closed` calls to `stopWatching()`. A packaged Windows build sets its AUMID to `APP_ID`, so a pinned shortcut and the running window share a taskbar button.

### C.41 The window refuses navigation and file drops (`opensource.12`, 2026-10-14)

The page is the whole app, and anything that replaced it would run with the preload bridge. Before this change, `location.href = 'https://example.com'` over CDP replaced the app outright (the negative control). Now `will-navigate` asks `navigationAction` in `src/main/navigation.ts` what to do:

- **allow** a reload of the page itself, fragment ignored;
- **external** for any other http or https address, which opens in the system browser instead;
- **block** everything else, including `file:`, `data:` and `javascript:`.

The handler reads `details.url`, because the url argument is deprecated in Electron 44. `will-attach-webview` is refused. `webSecurity` and `allowRunningInsecureContent` are stated at their safe defaults. The CSP gains `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-src 'none'`.

In the renderer, `dragover` and `drop` are stopped only when the drag carries files, so a file dropped on the window cannot replace the app and lose open paragraph boxes, while dragging text inside the page still works.

Checked in the rebuilt app:

- it renders under the new CSP;
- a synthetic file drop is stopped and a text drop is not;
- `location.href = 'file:///C:/Windows/win.ini'` leaves the app in place.

The web-address branch is unit-tested only, because triggering it opens a browser tab. A real drag from Explorer onto an open paragraph box is left to the author.

### C.42 Claude is the user's own `claude` command, not the SDK (`cli.1`, `setup.1a`, 2026-10-14)

Under Appendix D 8 and 21 the app ships nothing of Anthropic's. `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` and its two peers, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, are gone from the dependencies. The builder config no longer unpacks anything, and the app runs the Claude Code each user installs, found at `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe` or on PATH.

`src/main/providers/claudeCli.ts` speaks the same newline-delimited JSON over stdin and stdout that the SDK spoke:

- an `initialize` control request, which carries `systemPrompt: [text]` and `jsonSchema` and is answered with the model list and the account;
- the chapter as one user message;
- then `system`, `stream_event`, `assistant`, `rate_limit_event` and `result` messages, read exactly as before.

Everything was checked on 2026-10-14 against the author's installed Claude Code 2.1.266, with a cleaned environment:

- `initialize` returned the models and the account and sent no prompt;
- a Haiku probe and a review of samples Chapter 02 through the rebuilt app returned structured output (the review found the seeded "would of"), with cost and model usage;
- no `claude.exe` was left behind after the app quit.

Deviations from 11.3 (c) and (q):

- **System prompt and schema.** They go in `initialize` rather than in `--system-prompt` and `--json-schema`, so a long guidelines file cannot meet the Windows command-line limit.
- **Client variable.** `buildClaudeEnv` sets no `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP`, because the app is not the SDK.
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`.** It is removed from the child environment: it is the switch behind `--bare`, which turns off subscription sign-in. A dev run started from inside a Claude Code session has it set, which is one reason verification runs need the cleaned environment of `setup.15`.

The runtime check now costs no usage. It runs `--version` and `auth status --json`, keeping only `loggedIn`, `authMethod`, `apiProvider` and `subscriptionType`, then the `initialize` exchange; the old check sent a real prompt. The model list reuses that answer for ten minutes.

`MIN_CLAUDE_CODE` in `src/shared/ai/claudeStatus.ts` is 2.1.266, the version the flags were verified against; an older copy is reported with `claude update` as the fix. The SDK's usage-limit prefixes were copied into the same file. `test/helpers/fakeClaude.ts` replays the protocol for `test/main/claudeCli.test.ts`, covering:

- success, malformed lines, a failure reported as a success with `is_error`, a usage limit, a refusal, an assistant error, the wrong output shape, a rejected flag, an early end, Cancel and quitting;
- the argument list, pinned.

The cost of this route: the model list depends on the user's copy of Claude Code. The author's 2.1.266 still lists Opus 5 as the default; `claude update` brings Opus 5.5. A future Claude Code could also change the protocol, which `release.10`'s per-release check covers.

### C.43 Verification runs use a cleaned environment (`setup.15`, 2026-10-14)

`npm run dev:clean` (`scripts/dev-clean.cjs`) starts the app with every variable named `CLAUDE*`, `ANTHROPIC*` or `DISABLE_*` removed, and prints their names but never their values. A shell inside a Claude Code session carries about thirty of them. Some change what the app's own Claude Code child does: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` routes it through the session's proxy, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` turns off subscription sign-in.

The launcher always uses a scratch userData (`.dev-userdata`, `--user-data <dir>`, or `--user-data-fresh` for a first run) and DevTools on port 9222. Its other flags:

- `--claude-config-empty` or `--claude-config <dir>`: point `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at an empty or given folder;
- `--api-key-dummy`: set a dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`;
- `--no-claude-code`: behave as if Claude Code were not installed;
- `--quiet`: a quiet test window (`dev.1`, Appendix C "Quiet test windows");
- `--exe <path>`: run a packaged build with `--isolated-user-data`.

The last switch, `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_DEV_NO_CLAUDE_CODE`, replaces `..._DEV_NO_BUNDLED_CLI`: since C.42 there is no bundled copy to skip, and "not installed" is the state the Setup screen must be tested in. In a development build, `claude.ts` warns once, in the terminal and the log, when `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL` or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set.
