After Open, the guide's note and Settings' say "Opened <path>." or "Created <path> from the template and opened it."; the second said "Created <path> from the template." before. Open folder leaves Settings' note empty, as Show in folder did, and Review with AI reads the status again after either button, so the note about an empty style sheet follows a file that Open folder has just made.
- **What main is sent.** `guidelines:open` took `via`, `obsidian` or `default`; it now takes nothing (`TAKES_NOTHING` in `src/main/ipcGuard.ts`), so a payload is refused before the handler runs, and the file is always the one the settings name. `openGuidelines` is `ensureGuidelinesFile`, then `openGuidelinesFile`. The check that `setup.10b`'s review put before `ensureGuidelinesFile` went: the one refusal it made that `ensureGuidelinesFile` does not, a `.txt` file for Obsidian, went with Obsidian, and `ensureGuidelinesFile` refuses a file that is not `.md` or `.txt` before it makes a folder, which the test of a `.docx` guidelines file pins (nothing made, nothing opened). `shell:reveal` keeps its target name, and neither channel is ever sent a path. Its `guidelines` target is `revealGuidelines`, Electron-free beside `openGuidelines` and tested the same way: `ensureGuidelinesFile`, then `showItemInFolder` (the review fix; before, the branch sat in `ipc.ts`, where no test reached it).
- **What went.** `src/shared/obsidian.ts` (`obsidianOpenUrl`, `isObsidianOpenUrl`, `obsidianLinkPath`, `obsidianOpensFile`, `isFullPath`, `encodeLinkValue`) and the 12 tests of it at the head of `test/shared/obsidian.test.ts`, whose tests of the syntax a review leaves alone stay; `assertCanOpen` and `openInObsidian` in `src/main/openGuidelines.ts`, and their tests; `OpenGuidelinesVia`; `OPEN_IN_OBSIDIAN` and `canOpenInObsidian`; the guide's `OPEN_WITH_DEFAULT_APP`, `CREATE_AND_OPEN_IN_OBSIDIAN` and `SHOW_IN_FOLDER`, and its action ids `open-obsidian`, `open-default` and `show-in-folder`, now `open-guidelines` and `open-guidelines-folder`. The window still refuses to navigate to an `obsidian://` link (C.41).
- **Settings' row.** Change, Open and Open folder are on the file's own row, where Change and Show in folder were, and the row under it that held Open in Obsidian and Open guidelines file went, so the dialog is 657 CSS px tall at 100%, where it was 692. "Open guidelines file", which `setup.10b` kept because the README and section 7 named it, is Open, and both now say so. Three buttons leave the path less room than the reviews folder's two, measured in a quiet window with the page's size set over DevTools: in the default window (1424 by 900 inside), 200 CSS px against 243 at 100%, 189 against 233 at 125% and 192 against 235 at 150%, the buttons on one line; in the smallest (884 by 561), 185 against 228 at 100%, 114 against 157 at 150%, 32 against 75 at 175%, and at 200% none against 10, with Open folder on a second line inside the dialog and nothing scrolling sideways. The path keeps its tooltip and is the buttons' description while there is no file. Review with AI's path has 269 px at 100% in the default window.

### C.102 The category on the focused box's heading line (`polish.8`, 2026-10-22)

The author found the focused section "a bit big in general" and asked whether its heading and the line under it could be one (2026-10-22). They are: the heading line reads "Focused suggestion · punctuation" and ends in the pencil, and the box is 119 CSS px where it was 139 (section 7, The focused suggestion). This records what the task left open.

- **The line's parts.** `.side__focus-head h3` is a flex row of two parts: the heading's words (`.side__focus-title`, in `--ink-faint`) and the category's box (`.side__focus-cat`, in `--cat`), which starts with the separator (`.side__focus-sep`, " · " in `--ink-faint`) and ends with the anchor when it is not exact, in `--warn` (`.detail__anchor`), as the category's own line had it. The words are the ones that line used: the category's name, "your edit" for words the author wrote, in the colour of the category they came from, and "change" when there is none. No token is new: the `--cat-*` colours on `--panel` are already held to 4.5:1 in both themes (`themeContrast.test.ts`), and the line is the 11 px uppercase the category's line was. `.detail__cat` and `--focus-cat` went with that line.
- **A narrow panel.** `ui.5` kept the category on a line of its own because on the heading line one or the other would be cut short. Here the heading's words give way: they shrink to an ellipsis and then to nothing (`flex: 0 1 auto`, `min-width: 0`), and the category's box never shrinks (`flex: none`), so it is whole unless it is wider than the whole line by itself (`max-width: 100%`, ending in an ellipsis). A first version let the category shrink as well, with a thousandth of the heading's share: in the default window "word-choice ambiguous" then lost 0.04 px and showed an ellipsis in place of its last letters, so the category takes no share at all. Measured in the window: in the default window at 100% (the line 277 px wide) the whole heading fits beside every category, and only the longest line, "word-choice ambiguous", cuts it, to "FOCUSED SUG…"; in the smallest window at 100% (a 236 px panel, the line 193 px) "typo" fits beside it, "your edit" cuts it short and "word-choice ambiguous" leaves "F…"; in a 1100 by 700 window at 150% (a 211 px panel, the line 158 px) the heading's words go entirely for "word-choice ambiguous", and the category ends in an ellipsis.
- **The separator's spaces.** The separator starts the category's box, a flex item and so a block of its own, where a leading space would be dropped, so it keeps its spaces with `white-space: pre`, on screen and in the accessibility tree.
- **What a screen reader is given.** The heading's node in the accessibility tree (DevTools' `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree` in the window) is a level 3 heading named "FOCUSED SUGGESTION · TYPO", "FOCUSED SUGGESTION · YOUR EDIT" and "FOCUSED SUGGESTION · WORD-CHOICE AMBIGUOUS", the last whole while its words were cut on screen, and "FOCUSED SUGGESTION" with nothing focused. The capitals are `text-transform`'s, which Chromium applies to the name of every heading in the panel, as it did to "FOCUSED SUGGESTION" before. The pencil is still "Edit suggestion", and Tab still goes from the selector to the pencil, then to a box with more text than it shows, then to the list.
- **The body.** Original starts 4 px under the heading line, as the category did (the pair's top margin is now 0, where it made the 4 px under the category), and the body holds 80 px: two lines of explanation, as before, and the text shown with nothing focused, two lines in the default window and three in panels 211 to 240 px wide, with nothing to scroll.
- **What the panel gained**, measured in quiet `dev:clean --no-claude-code` windows sized with `SetWindowPos`, on a scratch copy of the samples with the sample review of Chapter 01 (6 suggestions, 3 comments), on the commit before and on this one, the same in both themes. In the default window (1440 by 940, 1424 by 901 inside) at 100%, the box is at 86 to 205 CSS px (86 to 225 before), the list starts at 205 (225), its heading at 215 (235) and its first row at 236 (256), the region below at 381 (401) with 488 px (468), and the Comments heading at 391 (411); the list itself, its six rows, keeps its 169 px. Under the box: 664 px (644) in the default window at 100% and 367 (347) at 150%; in the smallest window at 100%, 305 (285) with the status bar on two rows, and 324 with one; 321 (301) in a 1000 by 900 window at 150%, in the drawer; 287 (267) in a 1000 by 985 window at 175%.
- **The hint and the split.** Section 7 has their new figures. The first-use hint hangs where it did, so in the smallest window at 100% it now covers the whole box and the top 2 px of the list heading's line, whose words stay clear, as at 150% in the default window; checked by eye in both themes. The split's handle moves 109 or 128 px in the smallest window at 100%, where it moved 49 or 68 after `polish.6`: the footer `polish.7` took away gave 40 px of that and the category's line 20.
- **Not built.** A box with one line of explanation, the next step should the author find the panel still short.

### C.103 Save to chapter is plain until something is waiting (`polish.9`, 2026-10-22)

The author asked for Save to chapter to be an ordinary button while there is nothing to save, so that its turquoise says changes are waiting (2026-10-22). `SaveButtonState.primary` decides it: it is true when a chapter is open and `unsavedDecisionCount` is above 0, as the dot is, and throughout a save, and the toolbar gives the button the class `primary` only then. Nothing in app.css changed. This records what the task left open.

- **Disabled and saving keep their looks.** Read as: the fade (`opacity: 0.45`) and "Saving…" are as they were, rather than a turquoise kept whatever the count. Disabled is the fade over whichever button the count gives. A save starts only once it has found changes to write (`runSave`), so "Saving…" is the faded turquoise, as before, from the save's start to its end. It is not taken from the count, which falls to 0 before the save ends: `runSave` folds the decisions into the new base as soon as the chapter file is written (`markSaved`), then writes the review (`writeReviewNow`, a round trip to main) before its `finally` clears the flag; so too when main found the bytes already there (`unchanged`), and on a second try after a rebase that left no change to count. As first built, `primary` went with the dot in every state, and "Saving…" turned plain for that last stretch of every save, after the turquoise one (the `polish.9` review; about 10 ms in the window). Since the review fix `saveButtonState` gives `primary` whenever `saving`, and the dot still goes with the count. While a review of the chapter runs, a chapter with changes waiting keeps its faded turquoise and its count. A chapter with nothing to save, the page with no chapter open and pasted text show the faded plain button, where they showed a faded turquoise: kept turquoise there, the button would say something is waiting when nothing is, and would turn turquoise as a review starts on a chapter with nothing to save.
- **A paragraph box.** Text typed in an open paragraph box is not a change yet: it counts towards neither the label nor the dot, and Save asks about it first (7.4). The button stays plain with it, as the label and the dot do, and turns turquoise when Done makes the text a change. Counting the box too would give a turquoise "Save to chapter" with no count and no dot.
- **The first-use hint and the legend.** The hint shows only while a change is waiting, and never while a save is under way or the chapter is locked (`saveHintVisible`), so its arrow and its "Press Save to chapter" are always on the turquoise button, enabled; a property test in `test/shared/saveHint.test.ts` holds the two together. The button keeps its width with either class (the same 1 px border and padding), so the arrow keeps its place. The legend says "For the open chapter, Save to chapter and the status bar count them.", which still holds, so no word changed; it does not name the colour.
- **Hover and press.** The plain button takes the ordinary hover (`--panel-alt`) and, like Settings, has no pressed look of its own; the turquoise one darkens on hover and press as `theme.12` made it.
- **Nothing else moves.** The toolbar has no other primary button, and the dialogs keep theirs (Start review, Create, Done and the rest), each the action its dialog is there for. The README's screenshots (`opensource.13`) show "Save 2 changes to chapter", which stays turquoise.

### C.104 The side columns' widths are shares of the window, and fold where they did (`polish.5`, 2026-10-22)

The author asked for the chapter list and the side panel to be resizable by handles between them and the prose, built like the split, with the widths kept as fractions of the window's width, the prose keeping `ui.3`'s minimum and `ui.3`'s folding still happening when the window is too narrow for the widths kept (2026-10-22). That is section 7's Column widths. What the task left open, and why it went this way:

- **To the nearest pixel.** A share is written to six places, as the split's is, and `keptWidth` draws it to the nearest pixel, not down as the usual widths are: rounded down, 0.438202 of the default window's 1424 px drew 623 px for a handle let go at 624. To the nearest pixel, a width written in a window comes back exactly in it (a property in `test/shared/columnHandle.test.ts`).
- **No most but the prose's.** The usual widths stop at 230 and 320 px; a width set stops only where the prose would have less than 480 px beside the other column as drawn, so the panel can take half the default window for long comments (714 px beside the list's 230). A fixed most was weighed and left: any figure would be wrong for some window, and as a share a width set grows with the window past it anyway (the panel's 714 px in the default window is 1284 in a 2560 px one). The least is the floor `ui.3` shrinks to, 150 and 200 px, where the columns' contents had already been looked at, not the usual least of 170 and 240.
- **The folds stay where they were.** `columnLayout` keeps its four steps and puts the widths set in place of the usual ones. Whether a column folds depends on the floors alone (below 830 px for the list, 712 for the panel), so a width set never folds a column sooner or keeps it in place longer; between, widths too wide for the window shrink toward the floors in proportion, as the usual ones do (step 2). A property test holds the folds to those of the usual widths for any shares.
- **A drag where the columns have given way.** In step 2 the prose has its 480 px and both columns are narrower than set, so a handle there can only narrow its column. Moving one writes that column's share alone: the other column gets back what it gave before the prose gets more, and where the two still do not fit, step 2 shrinks the moved column too, so its edge lands a little short of the pointer. Writing what is on screen for both, the other way, would turn a usual width into a share whenever the author touched the other handle in a small window, and that column would then grow past its usual most in a wide one. Measured in the smallest window at 100% with the usual widths: the panel's handle dragged 30 px right left the panel 206 px, and the list took back its 2 px (170) and the prose the rest (508).
- **A drawer leaves the other column as drawn.** A drawer used to leave both strips and 48 px of the prose, which with usual widths always left the side panel in place uncovered too; a list set wide could have covered it, so a drawer now leaves its strip, the other column as drawn and the 48 px.
- **The band lies beside the scrollbars, not on them.** The split's band is centred on its line. Centred, the band on the side panel's edge would cover 3 px of the prose's scrollbar, and the band on the list's edge 3 px of the list's; each band instead reaches from the line into the column with no scrollbar at that edge. The grip is drawn centred on the line, a pixel over each side. Laid over the edge, the band takes no width: a grid column of its own would have taken 6 px from the prose for each handle and changed every figure in Narrow windows.
- **The chip row's scrollbar** (the review, 2026-10-22). The prose's left edge had one scrollbar after all: the chip row's, under the chips, which scrolls sideways (`polish.6`). In the default window with the list at 242 px the band covered its first 6 px, the left part of its left arrow: with the row scrolled to 300 a click at 245 px left it there, and a drag from there moved the list. The row now has a left border 6 px wide in its own colour; a scrollbar starts inside its box's border, so the arrow begins where the band ends (a click at 288, the band's end, scrolled the row; one at 287 did not), and with 6 px of padding inside the border the chips stay where they were. Of the review's other two ways, starting the band below the row would need the row's height, which changes with the chips, their scrollbar and the zoom, and laying the row over the band would cover the band's focus ring over the row. The line under the row is now the top border of the wrapper below it: the row's own bottom border met the 6 px one at the corner, and the join, drawn on the diagonal from the outer corner to the inner one, tapered the line off along those 6 px (looked at in 8x crops). A chip that Shift+Tab brings in on the left now sits 12 px inside the border, 18 from the row's edge, where it sat 12; the first chip still sits at 12. A source check ties the border to the band's reach, and a scan of every scrollbar on the page in the window found none under either band. (Gone with `polish.10`, which put the chips in the toolbar's row and gave the row no scrollbar, C.98.)
- **The browser's focus ring.** The split draws a 2 px `--accent` ring inside its band, because the opaque regions on either side would paint over a ring outside it. A column's handle lies above both columns, so the browser's own ring shows round its band (`auto`, rgb(229, 151, 0) with its white edge in light), as CLAUDE.md asks for everywhere but its three exceptions.
- **Home and End by the column, not the edge.** As in WAI-ARIA's window splitter, whose value is the size of the pane it controls: Home gives the column its least width and End its most, so on the side panel's handle Home moves the edge right. The arrows move the edge the way they point. The up and down arrows are left to the suggestions, as j and k are.
- **One handle at a time, cut short by a fold.** Each handle is its own hook (`useColumnHandle`), and while a drag lasts it hands the page the width it has reached in place of the setting. A zoom key that folds the column under a drag takes the handle away with the pointer capture, which tells it nothing; the release then reaches the window, which ends the drag there and keeps nothing.
- **The writer the split's.** The split's writer became `createSettingWrites` in `state/settingWrites.ts`, over the key it writes; `state/split.ts` keeps its names on it, and `state/columnWidths.ts` writes `columnWidths` with the other column's share as it is.
- **A verification note: the first frame.** The first frame the page draws after a load comes before the settings, with the usual widths, as it already had "No manuscript folder chosen yet." in the list; the next has the widths set. Measured on a reload of a window with the list set to 300 px: 230 px for one frame, at 61 ms, then 300.

### C.105 Two translucent selection bands, the prose's faint for its ghosts, and the prose in its own colours (`polish.1` and its review, 2026-10-22)

The author asked for a selection colour of the app's own in sitting C, "if it does not hurt usability" (`theme.10` a), and `polish.1` asked for a band from the icon's turquoise family in the prose, the side panel and the dialogs, with the selected text's ink at 4.5:1 on it and a ghost, its underline and a small change's capsule still readable on it. 11.3 (e)'s bullet on text selection has the values and figures. What the task left open, and why it went as it did:

- **Translucent, not a colour of its own.** The first band tried in the window was opaque, a pale turquoise, and inside the selection the underlines, the tints, the focus yellow and the capsule were gone: Chromium paints the band with the selected text, after the inline box's background and border, and a capsule is drawn under the paragraph's text (11.7). The browser's own band is slightly see-through, which is why its shots showed them darkened. The prose's band, `--selection-prose-bg` since the review, is a colour at 20% in both blocks, and the contrast test fails it at 50% or more; `--selection-bg` is translucent too (below).
- **The ghosts at 4.5:1, the marks at 3:1.** A ghost is text in its category's colour, so on the prose's band over the page and both paragraph yellows it keeps the 4.5:1 a category has as text; the "was" ghost and the frontmatter keep the 3:1 of faint text. An underline or a small change's foot line lies under the band, so it is checked as painted, the band over the category against the band over what it sits on, at the 3:1 of a mark. A capsule's fill and a suggestion's tint are faint on purpose, as on the page, and have no tier; the dismissed ghost at 32% and the tag at 80% have none either.
- **Everywhere, not in three places; two strengths since the review.** Ctrl+A selects the toolbar, the chapter list and the status bar as well, so the band covers the page. `polish.1` made that one band, the faint one, since two bands on one page might read as two kinds of selection; the review (below) gave everything but the prose's lines a stronger band of the same hue, and the paragraph box too.
- **One ink outside the prose, its own colours in it.** Outside the prose `--selection-ink` (`var(--ink)` in both blocks) holds at least 9.75:1 on `--selection-bg` in light and 6.04 in dark, where own colours would not: in light, categories, `--accept` and `--warn` on `--panel-alt` are 4.53 to 4.56:1 and any band that shows takes them under 4.5. In the prose the text is `--ink` already, and own colours keep the active find match's dark ink on the dark theme's bright orange (`--find-active-ink`, 6.0:1 under the prose's band, where `--selection-ink` gave 2.5). `.prose ::selection` sets `color: currentColor`, which in a highlight is the colour beneath it, the find match's included; checked in the window. `:not(.prose *)::selection` was tried first and does not work: with highlight inheritance a `::selection` colour set on an ancestor reaches its descendants'.
- **No band on a filled button.** White on `--selection-bg` over light's `--accent-fill` is 3.45:1 (3.61 on the prose's band), so `button.primary` and the active Setup tab, and anything inside them, draw their selection `transparent` in `currentColor`; their labels are not something anyone copies.
- **The prose's light band is a turquoise at full brightness, not one of the icon's.** Over the warm page the band must stay within about 0.07 of its luminance for the ghosts' 4.5:1, and an icon colour darkens it faster than it tints it: the dots' `#4fd8e0` reaches the limit at 13%, 6.9 apart from the page in CIELAB. `rgb(70 255 255)`, hue 180° against the dots' 183°, is 12.9 apart at 20%. Its dark band is a deep turquoise of the dots' hue, `rgb(0 90 95)`, 9.6 apart. A search over hues 176 to 192° and shares of 4 to 80%, against every pair above, found nothing much stronger in either theme.
- **The review: a band to see outside the prose** (2026-10-22). Checked in a quiet window, the one band was close to invisible wherever selecting is itself the action, above all in dark: Ctrl+F selects the query already in the find field so that typing replaces it, the edit popover selects its text as it opens, one click selects a Setup command (`user-select: all`), and select-all in the paragraph box or a dialog. Over the eleven backgrounds it lies on outside the prose (below) it was 1.03 to 1.06:1 by luminance in light and 1.02 to 1.12 in dark, 12.1 to 15.8 apart in CIELAB in light and 7.3 to 13.7 in dark (9.2 on the dark panel, at 1.11:1), and in light 2.4 apart from the page with protanopia simulated (Viénot), about the least anyone sees; the browser's own band was 72 apart from the dark panel. The author asked for the band "if it does not hurt usability", and a selection nobody can see hurts it. Only the ghosts held the band that faint, and they are only in the prose, so the prose keeps it (`.prose ::selection`, `--selection-prose-bg`, the values above) and everything else takes `--selection-bg`, the same hue made plain: light `rgb(0 190 200 / 45%)` and dark `rgb(0 120 128 / 55%)`, both of the dots' hue (183° and 184°), #88dcdf and #0d4e51 over the page. The paragraph box is in the prose but has no ghost over it, so `.prose input::selection, .prose textarea::selection`, one element more specific than `.prose ::selection`, give it the strong band. Over the eleven backgrounds it can lie on (the surfaces, the focused and selected rows, the paragraph box, the warning and error cards, the badges) it is 1.39 to 1.48:1 and 28.1 to 36.7 apart in light, 1.39 to 1.83:1 and 24.2 to 37.5 apart in dark, at least 9.9 and 17.0 apart with protanopia simulated, with `--ink` on it at 9.75:1 or more in light and 6.04 in dark. The test now holds `--selection-bg` to 20 apart and 1.3:1 over each of them, and the prose's band to 8 apart over its lines, the frontmatter, the focus and a find match, so neither fades unseen. Weighed and not taken: an opaque strong band, which would hide a badge's or a focused row's colour under selected text, and one faint band with these figures put to the author. What is left for the author's approval, with the screenshots the `polish.1` tick names: in light the two bands differ plainly in strength when a selection runs from the prose into the side panel, a pale band in the prose and a clear turquoise around it, the same hue; and the prose's light band is still 2.4 apart from the page with protanopia simulated (6.1 in dark), which the ghosts leave no room to raise.
- **A verification note.** `getComputedStyle(element, '::selection')` gives the band and ink a selection there resolves to, and `getSelection().selectAllChildren()` over CDP shows it with no input; with the `::selection` rules deleted from the page's style sheets (a reload brings them back) the same page shows the browser's own, for a before and after in one window.

### C.106 The scrollbars are the app's own: D, its thumb a shade darker (`polish.2`, 2026-10-22)

From the second sheet the author picked D, C's gutter with a square thumb a shade off the track, and asked for the thumb a little darker: "Say 1.4 at rest rather than 1.2, and 1.6 hovered?" 11.3 (e)'s bullet on scrollbars has the result. What step two settled where the task left it open:

- **The thumb's colours.** Each is the hex nearest its ratio on the line D's own two lay on, `--border` to `--border-strong` and on past it, kept to the gutter's hue (about 40°): light `#d0cabe`, `#c5beb0` and `#b7b0a2`, 1.409, 1.596 and 1.861:1 on `#f1eee8`; dark `#454139`, `#4e4940` and `#585248`, 1.408, 1.600 and 1.848 on `#2d2a25`. The task asked for the dragged thumb one step darker again; it is a step about as large as the one from rest to hover (the ratio times 1.14, then 1.16), where D's dragged `--ink-faint` (3.24 and 4.42:1) jumped far past the hover. They are written out in both blocks rather than mixed from other tokens: no token has these shades, and the contrast test reads a token as a colour.
- **Four tokens, not seven.** The sheets' variants also named `--scrollbar-line`, `--scrollbar-arrow` and `--scrollbar-arrow-hover`, each another token's value in both themes, so the rules name `--border`, `--ink-faint` and `--ink-soft` directly, and the tokens are the task's four: the track, `var(--panel-alt)` in both blocks so that it follows the panels, and the thumb's three states.
- **What Chromium takes** (Electron 44.9.3). Step one found that `:root` in a scrollbar rule's selector drops the part's state, the thumb's `:hover` and the buttons' `:single-button` (`polish.2`'s note), so the rules are bare and the few scoped ones begin with a class. In the window `scrollbar-color: auto` and `scrollbar-width: auto` on the prose kept the styled bar (16 px), while a colour pair gave back the browser's 15 px bar and `thin` a 10 px one: the standard properties win over `::-webkit-scrollbar` unless they are `auto`. `themeCss.test.ts` therefore allows no `scrollbar-color` and no `scrollbar-width` but the chips' `none`.
- **Rounded boxes.** Drawn square, the gutter showed past a dialog's 8 px corner, a pale square on the backdrop at the top and bottom right of Settings at 150%. `border-radius: inherit` on the parts changed nothing (a scrollbar part takes no value from its scroller), so each rounded scroller's bar is given its box's radius less the 1 px border: 7 px for `.modal` and `.legend` and 3 px for `.diagnostics__text`, on the bar and its two end buttons; 4 px for the two fields that can be made taller, `.paste-field textarea` and `.editor__area`, on the top of the bar and its up arrow, and on the corner and the resize handle below it. `themeCss.test.ts` finds the rounded scrollers and the resizable fields in app.css and checks each, so a new one fails until it has its corners.
- **The resize handle.** Beside a bar, Chromium frames a field's resize handle with a 1 px light grey line along its top and left, as it did with the browser's bar; on the dark gutter it was a white L. `::-webkit-resizer` draws the handle instead, two short lines in `--ink-faint` (a `linear-gradient()` at 135° in a 9 px square 3 px from the corner), and no frame; `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` carries the gutter's line down beside it. With no bar the field shows the same two lines on its own background, where the browser drew its grey ones.
- **The Setup screen** keeps `scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges`, which holds its page centred under the cards whether or not it scrolls (the `setup.7` review): its left gutter is empty, in the page's `--bg`, and the right one draws the bar.
- **Measured in the window** (2026-10-22): a quiet `dev:clean --no-claude-code` window at the bottom of the stack, 1440 by 940 (the page 1424 by 901 at 100%, 96 DPI), focus emulated, Chapter 01 with 37 suggestions in thirteen categories and 12 comments, the prose scrolled 30% and the suggestions list 40%, nothing injected. On the prose's bar and the suggestions list's, at rest, with the pointer on the thumb and with the thumb held, the thumb on the bare track beside it read 1.41, 1.60 and 1.86:1 in light and 1.41, 1.60 and 1.85 in dark, at 100% and at 150%; the thumb 10 screen px across at 100% and 15 or 16 at 150% (an edge column blended), its corners square, the line `--border` and the track `--panel-alt` as computed; pressing on the thumb did not scroll. A wheel notch moved the prose 120 px, each arrow 40 px, a 100 px drag of the thumb 187 px (188 by its length), and a click on the track under the thumb paged to the end (667 px, all the prose had left, under a page of 723). The chapter list (with 30 filler chapters) at 100% and 150%, Settings and the legend at 150%, the Setup screen at 100% and 150% and the Copy diagnostics text at 150% (opened to show, the page's clipboard stubbed) drew the same 16 px bar, its thumb at 1.41:1 in both themes and its arrows at 3.27 and 4.42:1 (light, dark; `--ink-faint` anti-aliased), and the dialogs', the legend's, the diagnostics text's and both fields' corners rounded with their boxes (Submit manual review's paste field and the edit popover's box, each with a long text and a short one, closed with Cancel and Escape); the chips' row, overflowing at 150%, drew none. C.48 has the composited scrolling.

### C.107 Chips as menus, an eye for all, the old size, and a You chip (`polish.11`, 2026-10-23)

After using `polish.10` the author found the chip's ▾ "a bit clunky and too small", and asked for the chip itself to open its menu on a click anywhere, with Show or Hide, Show only, Accept all and Dismiss all; for an eye open and an eye closed at the left of the toolbar to show or hide every category, since Show only hides the rest; for the chips and their type back at the size they had, shrinking only when needed; and for a You chip, "Unsure if Other = You though. If they are, I think they should be the same color, and likely the same name." Section 7 (Layout, Toolbar order, the suggestions list, Confirmation) has the result; what the task left open, or the window showed, is here.

- **Other and You.** `other` counted three things (`hunk.category ?? 'other'`): the model's `other`, the author's own edits, which the paragraph box makes with `category: 'other'` (`manualHunk` in `src/shared/edit.ts`), and a manual review's suggestions, which carry no category. So Other was partly You, as the author suspected, and the task gave the author's edits a chip of their own. `chipKeyOf` puts a suggestion whose source is the author's (`source: 'manual'`) under You, and every other under its category, `other` for none. The task's "`other` keeps only the model's `other`" is read as "keeps none of the author's edits": a manual review's suggestions are not the author's own edits (their rows have no you marker, and a manual review may be another tool's corrections pasted in), and left out of `other` they would have had no chip at all, so they stay under it. Every suggestion in the text is under exactly one chip, and hiding a chip hides exactly what it counts (a property test in `test/shared/chips.test.ts`). A model's suggestion the author reworded (`edited`) keeps its category's chip: its source and category are the model's, though its row keeps the you marker (`isAuthored`), so for it the marker and the chip differ; `polish.12` gives every row a tag of its chip's category. You is last in the row whatever its count, in `--accent`, the colour of `.row__you` (`.cat-you`), which `themeContrast.test.ts` already holds to 4.5:1 on `--panel` in both themes as text. Its questions say "your edits": "Accept your 2 pending edits?", "Edits you already dismissed are not changed.", "You have no pending edits to accept.", and Actions' items for it "Accept all your edits" and "Dismiss all your edits". Hiding You hides the author's edits as hiding a category hides its suggestions: they leave the list, the margin, the position strip and the keys' steps, and the line shows the text without them, as it does for a hidden category's accepted suggestions; Save still writes them.
- **An edit made while its chip is hidden** (the `polish.11` review). Show only and the eye's Hide all both hide You, so it is easy to edit a paragraph with You hidden. The box then added the edit, the card said "Paragraph 2: 1 change added, already accepted." and the status bar counted it, but the line read as before, the list had no row for it and the focused suggestion's box showed "(nothing) -> Later." for an edit nowhere on the page: the author would think it lost (seen in the window on Chapter 01). The same happened, before `polish.11` too, to a suggestion of a hidden category that the box accepted because the author typed exactly its fix: the word typed went from the line. `commitDraft` now shows the chip of what it applied, You for the edits it adds and the category of a suggestion it accepts, in the same update that focuses the first of them, and leaves every other chip hidden; a box that adds nothing, or only turns a suggestion down because the author typed the file's words back, changes no chip. Showing You as the box opens was the other choice; it would show the author's edits again for a box then cancelled. Tests: `test/renderer/store.test.ts` (both cases, and the chips left alone), and `test/renderer/marks.render.test.ts`, which renders the review pane with an accepted and a pending edit of the author's and a model's `other` suggestion and holds the prose, the margin marks and the position strip to `chipHidden`: with You hidden the edits are gone and the line reads the base text, with other hidden they stay and the model's goes. Before it, a review found that both the prose's filter and the strip's could go back to the category alone with every test passing.
- **The menu.** Hide (Show on a hidden chip), Show only, and under a line "Accept all 3" and "Dismiss all 3" (`chipMenuLabels`). N is how many of the chip's suggestions are still pending, `bulkPlan`'s count, which is what either would move and what its question then says; at 0 both are greyed out with the note the question would have given as their tooltip ("There are no pending grammar suggestions to accept."), which the arrows skip. Show only hides every other chip in the row (`showOnlyHidden`), not every category there is, so a chip that comes later, as You does with the author's first edit, is shown. The chip is a menu button: `aria-pressed`, which the toggle had, makes Chromium call a button a toggle button (checked: the tree gives the chip `button` with `hasPopup: menu` and `expanded`, and no `pressed`), so its state, shown or hidden, is the first word of its description, its tooltip, "Shown. Click for Hide, Show only, Accept all and Dismiss all." It opens as the toolbar's menu buttons do, the down arrow on its first item and the up arrow on its last (`menuButtonKey`), which the task did not list: the arrows on a focused chip used to move between suggestions (keyboard.ts), and a menu button takes them. A second click on a chip with its menu open closes it, as on Review and Actions. The menu's name is "grammar suggestions" or "Your edits".
- **The eye.** An open eye (an almond and a pupil) while every chip in the row is shown, and a closed one (a lid and three lashes) otherwise (`IconEye`, `IconEyeClosed`, 16 px in `--ink-soft`, in a toolbar button 30 by 26 CSS px at 100%). Its name says what it does, "Hide all categories" or "Show all categories", and so does its tooltip. It reads only the chips in the row (`allChipsShown`): a hidden category with no chip left, as when its suggestions have lost their place, leaves it open. Hide all hides the chips in the row; Show all clears the filter. It is in the chips' bar (`.chips__eye`), so it fades and goes inert with them while a review of the chapter runs, and there is none where there are no chips. Actions lists the same two under a line after the focused chip's items, each greyed out when it would change nothing (`allChipsHidden`).
- **The steps.** `CHIP_STEPS` holds four sizes, the polish.6 size (13 px on a normal line, 2 by 8 px of padding, 6 px apart), 12.5 px (2 by 7, 5 apart), 12 px on a 16 px line (1 by 6, 5 apart) and polish.10's compact size (11.5 px on 16, 1 by 5, 4 apart); app.css draws each under `[data-chip-step]` and `chipsRow.test.ts` holds the two to each other. Each step takes 5 to 6% off the chips' width, so between the old size and the compact one the row fits about one more chip a step. `chipsStep` picks the first step at which the chips' widths and the gaps between them fit the row less its 6 px of padding. The widths come from a copy of the chips drawn at every step out of sight (`.chips__measure`: absolute, 0 by 0, `overflow: hidden`, `visibility: hidden`, `aria-hidden`, spans rather than buttons), not from the widths at one step scaled: Chromium's text does not scale exactly with its size, and a choice from what is drawn could swing between two steps as each redraw measured the other. The row's width does not depend on its chips (the bar's `flex: 1 1 8em`, the row filling what the eye leaves), so the choice changes only with the window, the zoom, the fonts or the chips themselves. The row's padding is 2 by 3 px, where it was 3 px with 8 at the end for the ▾: at the old size a chip is 23.3 CSS px tall (17.3 px of line, 4 of padding, 2 of border), and the row with 4 px of padding is a toolbar button's 27.3, so the toolbar is 42 CSS px at 100% at every step, as it was. The browser's focus ring fits inside the row at the old size and the compact one (looked at four times enlarged).
- **What went.** The ▾ (`.chip__more`) and the raise that showed it (`.chip:hover` and `.chip:has(:focus-visible)` at layer 1 with a negative margin and a ring); the open chip keeps the menus' layer and is lit in `--panel-alt`. `.chip__toggle` is `.chip__button`; `chipCategories` is `chipCounts`; `categoryOf` in `suggestions.ts`, which nothing used once the filter and the questions read `chipKeyOf`, is gone. The store's `hiddenCategories` holds chips, `ChipKey`, and has `setHiddenCategories` beside `toggleCategory` and `clearCategoryFilter`.
- **Measured**, in a quiet `dev:clean --no-claude-code` window sized with `SetWindowPos`, on a scratch copy of the samples whose Chapter 01 has 37 suggestions in thirteen categories and three of the author's edits, accepted, and with copies of it whose reviews hold a set of categories chosen from the measured widths to land on each step: in the default window (1440 by 940, the page 1424 by 901) at 100%, beside "Save to chapter", 11 categories at the old size (986 CSS px of chips in 1002.6), 12 at the first step (977) and another 12 at the second (965), and 13 at the compact size (947); Chapter 01's thirteen and You beside "Save 3 changes to chapter" overflow at the compact size (991 in 941), with › and the line, and fit at the old size at 80% and at the second step at 90%. Thirteen beside "Save 12 changes to chapter" overflow by 13 px (953 in 940), where `polish.10` had 16 px to spare: the eye's 34 px. In the smallest window (900 by 600, the page 884 by 561) at 100%, 5 categories at the old size (422 in 462.6), 6 at the first step (448) and another 6 at the second (449), 7 at the compact size (445), and Chapter 01 overflows. The toolbar was 42 CSS px, one row, at every step, and at 110 to 200% its rows were as `polish.10` measured them (C.98): one in the default window at every step, one in the smallest up to 150% and at 175% beside "Save to chapter", and two at 175% with a count on Save and at 200%. Screenshots of each of these in both themes, looked at. Over DevTools with the focus emulated, in both themes, 27 checks each (`p11/menu.mjs`): Tab from the eye to the first chip with the ring; Enter, Space, the menu key and Shift+F10 opened the menu on Hide and the up arrow on Dismiss all 3; the arrows moved, Escape gave the focus back to the chip and Tab went on to the next; the accessibility tree as above; Show only from the keyboard hid the other 13 chips, left 3 rows and closed the eye ("Show all categories"); the eye then showed all and opened, hid all (no rows, no suggestion in the text) and showed all again; a click on a chip left of its middle opened its menu, Hide hid it, its menu then offered Show, a second click closed a menu, and a right-click opened one; "Accept all 3" asked "Accept 3 pending spelling suggestions?" and Escape gave the focus back to the chip; You was last in the you marker's colour, its Accept all 0 and Dismiss all 0 greyed out with "You have no pending edits to accept." and "... to dismiss.", and hiding it took the 3 rows with the you marker out of the list and left the 37 others; Actions, after a chip, held Accept all grammar, Dismiss all grammar, Show all categories and Hide all categories, and Show all categories there showed You again. Tab and Shift+Tab through the overflowing row in both windows stopped once on each chip, 27 stops, each wholly in view, clear of the arrows, with the ring. Shots and measures in the session's scratch folder `p11/out`.

### C.108 The suggestion rows: a tag per chip, clearer states and the decided count (`polish.12`, 2026-10-23)

The author, with `polish.11`'s request: "The personal Edits have [YOU] on them at the left. Can we add similar tag, with the same color as the pills, for all the other categories?"; the accepted arrow "needs to pop a little more", the X and edit buttons "a bit more faded", the X "red instead of turning it into a green undo"; a checkbox for ACCEPTED and DISMISSED "so I can see which one I like best"; and "(X of Y resolved) beside Suggestions, similar to comments". Section 7 (Suggestions list) and 11.3 (d, e) have the result; what the task left open, or the window showed, is here. Show states, its words and its setting went in `polish.17`, once the author had seen the new buttons (the last item).

- **The tag is the chip's.** `rowTag` names the chip the suggestion is counted under (`chipKeyOf`), so the list and the chips agree: the category, `other` for a manual review's suggestions, which carry none, and "you" for the author's own edits. A model's suggestion the author reworded was tagged "you" until now (`isAuthored`) and is tagged with its category, as C.107 foresaw; that its words are the author's is in the tag's tooltip, "Reworded by you", and in the row's spoken name, as "Your own words" is the YOU tag's tooltip. The focused suggestion's box still says "your edit" for both. The tags differ in width, PUNCTUATION more than twice TYPO, so the rows' words start where their tag ends; a column as wide as the widest tag would take about a quarter of the usual 320 CSS px panel from every row.
- **Read as the category.** Chromium puts text in the accessibility tree as `text-transform` draws it (the list's heading is "SUGGESTIONS (5 OF 22 DECIDED)" there, read over DevTools), so a tag's capitals would reach a screen reader as capitals. Every row's main button now has a name of its own, `rowLabel`: the tag's words as the chip names them, "reworded by you" where it applies, the change as `summaryLine` writes it, and the decision, "grammar, began → begun, accepted"; until now only a small change's row had one, and a word-sized row was named by its text. The decision is in the name whether or not Show states writes it on the row; since `polish.17`, when no row writes it, the name is the one place it is said in words.
- **The states.** `rowButtonLook`: a pending row's three buttons are as before; on a decided row the button of its decision is on and the other two fade. The task named a thicker stroke for the ✓ only; the dismissed ✕ has it too, so the decided button reads alike in either state. Each keeps its colour under the pointer, on `--border` (pairs in `themeContrast.test.ts`), while a faded button under the pointer is drawn as any row button, `--ink` at the usual stroke, so it shows it can still be pressed. Why the fade is a thinner stroke rather than a lighter grey, and why the ✓ has a token of its own, is in 11.3 (e). The names stay "Undo accept" and "Undismiss suggestion"; the ✕'s tooltip is the task's "Dismissed. Click to put it back", which Chromium gives a screen reader as its description. The ✓ keeps "Undo accept" as its tooltip: the task gave a new one only to the ✕, whose icon no longer says what a click does. The same ✕ in the prose's ghost row (HunkSpan) is unchanged.
- **Show states** (gone in `polish.17`, the last item). `showRowStates` (11.3 d), on by default, is a checkbox labelled "Show states" with the tooltip "Write ACCEPTED or DISMISSED on the rows you have decided", at the right of the heading's line. It is written through `createSettingWrites`, as the split and the columns' widths are (`state/rowStates.ts`), so the list follows at once and a close waits for the write (`PAGE_WRITES`). Off, the words are not drawn and nothing else changes. Where the panel is too narrow for both, as the side panel's 236 CSS px in the smallest window, the box goes under the heading and the line is 31 CSS px tall against 15; `measureSplit` measures that line (`.side__list-head`) where it measured the `h3`, so the split's least height for the list follows it.
- **The count.** `suggestionsHeading` counts the rows listed, `groupSuggestions`' inline group, as "Suggestions (22)" did before: with a chip hidden, its suggestions are out of both numbers ("Suggestions (3 of 20 decided)" with You hidden on a review whose 22 rows had 5 decided, 2 of them the author's), and the status bar counts the whole review. "Suggestions (19)" while none is decided is the task's; the comments' heading reads "Comments (0 of 3 resolved)" in that case, and "Comments (0)" only with no comments.
- **The tag's fill and colour.** The tag is filled with `--panel`, as a chip is, so its 9 px words hold 4.5:1 on every row (11.3 e), and it keeps its colour once its suggestion is decided, as its chip does; only `.row__cat` draws it (a test holds that).
- **The box and the review keys** (review fix). Show states is the first checkbox in the main view that stays on screen once clicked (the comments' Resolve unmounts), and a click leaves the focus on it. The key handler counted every `INPUT` as typing, as it counts a select (C.57, "The selector and the review keys"), so the review keys did nothing after a click on it. A checkbox is no longer typing (`isTypingField`): no review key is Space, which the handler leaves to the box (its switch returns before `preventDefault` on a key it does not know), and the boxes that sit behind a dialog or in the suggestion editor are covered by `reviewKeysActive` already. The box keeps the focus rather than being blurred after a change, as the review selector is, so it can still be ticked again from the keyboard. A radio button stays typing: its group takes the arrows, and none is in the main view. The box went in `polish.17`; the rule stays, so a checkbox the keyboard reaches, as a comment's Resolve with Tab, does not hold the review keys either.
- **A narrow row** (review fix). The tag and the status word were `flex: 0 0 auto`, so in a narrow panel the change, the only part that gave way, went to nothing, and the button, which did not clip, drew the status word over the pencil. Now the change has `flex: 1 1 0` and a floor, `--row-text-floor`, 32 CSS px, four of Literata's figures, so it takes what the others leave and never shrinks beside them; the status word is the only part that shrinks (`flex: 0 1 auto`, with "…"); the tag is never wider than the button's width less the floor and the gap, so it ends in "…" only once the change is at its floor; and the button clips. A floor of 40 px cut the status word in the 1150 px window, where `polish.12`'s rows kept it whole with 33 px of change; 32 px leaves every row there as it was. Where the word would show fewer than two letters it is not written at all, on any row, rather than as "A…" or a sliver of a letter: a container query hides it below a panel 246 CSS px wide inside its border, where the widest tag (WORD-CHOICE, 77 px), the floor and two gaps leave it 23 px. The query reads the panel (`.side`, `container: side / inline-size`), whose width the column or the drawer sets, not the row's button, whose width moves by the list's 16 px scrollbar and so from chapter to chapter, as the panel's height did in C.49; the threshold assumes the scrollbar. The colour guard's test that there is no `@container` (C.49) now allows this one and fails a container on a height. Hiding the word by wrapping it onto a hidden second line would decide row by row, but left its room empty beside a change cut to the floor. `polish.17` took the word, the query and the container away (the last item): the change and the tag give way as above, and the guard fails any container again.
- **Show states gone** (`polish.17`, 2026-10-23). The author, once he had used `polish.14`'s rows: "'Show States' button can go. With the new styles, it is unneeded." The box, the ACCEPTED and DISMISSED it wrote (which a decided row had shown from the first builds, as lower-case words drawn in capitals, before `polish.12` put them behind the box) and `showRowStates` went together: `state/rowStates.ts` and its place in `PAGE_WRITES`, `SHOW_STATES_LABEL` and `SHOW_STATES_TITLE`, `.side__list-head`, `.side__states`, `.row__status`, the container query and `.side`'s `container`; the legend's suggestions-list item no longer names the box. The heading is the list's first child again, the `h3` that `measureSplit` measures, as before `polish.12`, and its line no taller in a narrow panel than in a wide one: 15 CSS px in the default window (the panel 319 inside) and in the smallest (235), in both themes, where under `polish.12` the box went under the heading there and made the line 31; at 200% in the default window (199) the heading's own words, "SUGGESTIONS (11 OF 22 DECIDED)", take two of its lines with nothing beside them, as `polish.12`'s longer count does not fit there. Kept: the heading's count, `rowLabel`'s decision in each row's name, and `isTypingField`'s rule for checkboxes (The box and the review keys, above). Every row now has one width of change, a decided one's as a pending one's (section 7). The CHANGELOG's Unreleased line that had added Show states says instead that the rows no longer write the words, since the box never shipped and the words did. A settings.json that holds `showRowStates` is read as one with any unknown key (11.3 d). README's step 5 no longer names the box; its screenshots showed it until `polish.18` shot them again.

### C.109 A chip for the comments (`polish.13`, 2026-10-23)

The author, after `polish.12`: "there should be a comments pill so they can be turned invisible, and the eye button also turns them invisible". Section 7 (Layout, Toolbar order, Comments as margin notes, One comments list, Interactions and the legend's line) has the result; what the task left open is here.

- **Its colour.** The task gave "the comments' own colour (the margin card's)". A margin card has no hue of its own: its edge is its category's colour where the category has one (consistency and other, whose names the suggestions' categories share) and `--border` otherwise, and the word at its head is `var(--cat, var(--ink-soft))`. So the chip's words are `--ink-soft` (`.cat-comments`), the head's colour for every other comment category, which `themeContrast.test.ts` already holds to 4.5:1 as text on `--panel` and on `--panel-alt`, the open chip's light. The app's other comment colour, `--accent`, which a commented paragraph's number takes, is You's, the chip beside it, and two blue chips side by side would read as one pair. No token was added. Until `polish.16` light `--ink-soft` had `--cat-other`'s value (#6d675e), so a review with suggestions under other had two grey chips, their words different and the comments chip always the one just before You, and in dark the two differed (#bdb5a8 and #a8a092); `polish.16` gave other a cool slate of its own, #484e70 in light and #a2a0ba in dark, so they now differ in both themes (11.3 e).
- **When it is drawn, and what it counts.** It counts the open comments, as the task said, unanchored ones and those about the whole chapter included, as the side panel lists them. It is drawn while the review has any comment at all, so a review whose comments are all resolved reads "comments 0", as their greyed cards are still there to hide. A review with comments and no suggestion in the text now has a chips' row, the eye and the comments chip, where it had none.
- **What hiding hides.** The margin's cards and the side panel's list, as the task said. Also the margin's column, which with no card goes as it does for a review with no comments, the prose taking its room back; the comment colour of the commented paragraphs' numbers, with their tooltip "This paragraph has a comment"; and the light on the active comment's paragraph, which comes back with the comments: left, each pointed at a comment that was not shown. The side panel writes "Hidden. The comments chip at the top shows them again." under the heading, where "No comments." goes for a review with none (`commentsNote`), so the space under a heading that counts comments does not read as comments lost. The task's "comment keys" are read as the cards' own keys, Enter and Space on a card, which go with the cards, and `n`, which does nothing while the comments are hidden, as j and k pass over a hidden chip's suggestions; its choice moved out of keyboard.ts into `nextComment` in `src/shared/ui/comments.ts`, where it is tested.
- **The chip in the code.** `ChipKey` stays the chips of suggestions, which `bulkPlan`, `chipKeyOf`, `chipBulkLabel` and the rows' tags take; `RowChip` adds `comments`, and the filter (`hiddenCategories`, `toggleCategory`, `setHiddenCategories`), Show only, the eye and `useChipFocus` hold `RowChip`. `suggestionChip` gives null for the comments chip, so FilterChips gives it no Accept all or Dismiss all, `chipMenuLabels` giving only its first two words, and Actions lists none after it. Its menu behaves as every chip's does (`useMenu`), and its tooltip is its description, as theirs are.
- **Tests.** `test/shared/chips.test.ts`: its place, count and names, and a property test over random suggestions and comments that the suggestions' chips are as without comments, that it sits after every category and before You, that hiding it hides no suggestion, that Show only on any other chip hides it and on it hides every suggestion, and that the eye's Hide all hides it; Show only's and the eye's tests over random rows hold it among the chips. `test/shared/comments.test.ts`: `commentsNote`, `nextComment`, and that `n` goes nowhere while hidden for any comments and any focus. `test/renderer/commentsChip.render.test.ts`: the toolbar, the review pane and the side panel rendered with the comments shown, hidden from the chip, after Show only and after the eye. `test/renderer/chipsRow.test.ts`: the source, the margin handed no card, `n`, the legend and the colour.

### C.110 Bigger row icons, a plainer fade and three-letter tags (`polish.14`, 2026-10-23)

The author, after `polish.12`: "For the edit, check, and x icons, can you make them a bit bigger inside of their buttons? Also, make the not clicked ones fade more ... It should clearly indicate 'we are done with this row'"; and of the tags, "I am not so much a fan of the pills all being different lengths. It would look cleaner if the word corrections all started on the same column ... make the pills 3 letters". Section 7 (Suggestions list) and 11.3 (e) have the result; what the task left open, or the window showed, is here.

- **The table is one record over every chip.** `TAG_ABBREVIATIONS` in `src/shared/ui/suggestions.ts` is typed `Record<ChipKey, string>`, so a category added to `CHANGE_CATEGORIES` fails the build until it has three letters, and the test holds that each is three capitals and no two are the same. GRM, the task's choice for grammar, over GRA. The tag's text is the three letters themselves; app.css still writes the tag in capitals, which changes nothing now.
- **The tooltip is the name in full, as a tooltip writes it.** "Grammar", "Word-choice": the chip's word with a capital, as the side panel's other tooltips start with one. A reworded suggestion's reads "Grammar, reworded by you", where it read "Reworded by you", so the name stays first; the author's own keep "Your own words", which says more than "You" would. What a screen reader hears is as `polish.12` had it ("grammar, began → begun, accepted"), as the row's name never held the tag's capitals.
- **The legend's list.** A Tags item after the suggestions list's, each tag drawn by `.row__cat` itself in its colour beside its name, in the chips' order (`TAG_KEYS`, `tagName`: the category as its chip writes it, and "your own edits" for YOU). Two columns: three overflowed the legend's 380 px by 22 px and gave it a sideways scrollbar. `Legend` is exported from StatusBar.tsx so a render test can hold the list.
- **What fades.** The ink alone, `--ink-faint` at `--row-fade` (11.3 e), not the button's opacity, which would have faded the focus ring and the hover's `--border` with it. Under the pointer or with the keyboard's focus a faded button is shown in full: the task asked for the hover; the focus is added because a keyboard user who tabs onto a 1.5:1 button would not see what has the focus. The stroke is the icon's own, where `polish.12` thinned it: thin and faint together left a line that was hard to see at all at 100%. One share in both themes: dark comes out a little plainer (1.54 to 1.74:1 against 1.43 to 1.48), and both read as done beside a pending row in the window. Show states and the status word are as they were.
- **Which icons grew.** Every `.row__act`: a row's pencil, ✓ and ✕, and the focused suggestion's pencil, which is drawn as a row button and would otherwise have been the one small pencil in the panel. The margin cards' and the prose's ✕ are other buttons and are as they were. The legend's tick follows the rows.
- **The narrow rows.** `polish.12`'s order holds (the change down to its floor, then the status word, then the tag), and so does its rule that no row writes the word where it would show fewer than two letters; but the container query that applies it was computed from the widest tag, WORD-CHOICE's 77 px, and with every tag 34 px the same sum gives 203 CSS px, not 246. At 200% in the default window (199) the word is still left out, every change keeps 57 px and no tag is cut, where 10 tags ended in "…". In the smallest window (235) every decided row now writes ACCEPTED (51 px) or DISMISSED (55 px) whole, its change at the floor or just above (32 to 36 px), as the 1030 to 1150 px windows did under `polish.12`; a pending row there keeps 93 px of its change. Were the author to prefer the change to the word in that window, the query going back to 246 px is the whole of it. (`polish.17` took the word and the query away, C.108: every row there now keeps 93 px of its change.)
- **Left for the author.** CLAUDE.md says the scrollbar's thumb "is the one mark under 3:1"; since this task the faded row buttons are a second, which `themeContrast.test.ts` names. An agent does not edit CLAUDE.md, so its line is the author's to bring up to date. The README's screenshots (`opensource.13`) showed `polish.12`'s long tags and thin fade, while its text said three-letter tags, until `polish.18` shot them again.
- **One path per icon** (review fix). The fade is a translucent ink, and the browser paints each `<path>` of an icon on its own, so where two overlap the ink is laid twice, about 58% where it should be 35%. `IconPencil` was two paths, its outline and the ferrule's line, whose ends sit on the outline: every faded pencil, on each accepted and dismissed row, had two darker spots there, measured in the window at 1.90:1 on the light panel and 2.43 on the dark one (1.97 and 2.57 shot at 3x), where its ✕ and ✓ are 1.47 and 1.74; 2.43 is outside the 1.35 to 1.9 that `themeContrast.test.ts` holds the fade to. `polish.12`'s opaque grey hid it. The pencil is now one path with two subpaths, whose stroke is painted once, as the ✕'s crossing already was: faded, it is 1.47 and 1.74 as the others are. Everywhere else it is drawn in an opaque ink or faded as a whole by the button's `opacity` (a pending row, the focused suggestion, the comment cards, the paragraph's pencil, the hover card), and there it looks the same: on a pending row 7 pixels at the joints differ at 1x, by at most 18 of 255, and nothing else in the row's buttons does. Fading the svg with `opacity` in place of the ink would also have painted each icon as one, but the fade's ratios are modelled and tested as `--row-fade` of `--ink-faint` (11.3 e), and that model and its tests would have had to change. `suggestionRows.render.test.ts` holds every row button's icon to one `<path>` and no other shape.

### C.111 What the Royal Road converter settled where the plan left it open (`rr.1`, 2026-10-23)

`src/shared/text/royalroad.ts` (`toRoyalRoadHtml(text, { straightQuotes })`) turns the text Copy result copies into the HTML Royal Road's chapter editor takes when it is pasted there, and Export HTML, under Copy result in the Actions menu, copies it (section 7). These are the choices that were its own, each pinned by `test/shared/royalroad.test.ts`.

- **What the author's pages did.** Read on 2026-10-23, never run. `markdown_to_royalroad.html`, the newest (last changed 2026-10-17): `# ` to `<h1>`; `**...**`, then `*...*`, to `<strong>` and `<em>` by a regular expression on each line; “ and ” to `"` and ’ to `'`; every backslash removed; `->` to →, `---` to —, `–-` (an en dash and a hyphen) to — and `--` to –; each line trimmed, blank lines dropped, a line of one `*` `<hr />`, a line with a line of text after it `<p style="margin-bottom: 0">`, any other `<p>`, and an `<h1>` line as it was; the lines joined with line breaks, and nothing escaped. `converter.html` and `md_to_html.js` (2025) paired `***`, `**` and `*` by counting them on each line (`md_to_html.js` also `___`, `__` and `_`, which `converter.html` had commented out) and wrote `<p style="margin-top: 0">` before a blank line and `<p style="margin-bottom: 0; margin-top: 0">` elsewhere. The newest page's shape is the one kept: `TIGHT_P`, `<p style="margin-bottom: 0">`, on every line of a run but its last.
- **Lines.** A line that reads as nothing once its syntax is left out (tags, a comment, a block ID, an embed, an image in the vault, a footnote's mark) is left out, not read as a blank line, so the lines round it stay one tight block, as they are one paragraph in Obsidian; the lines inside the frontmatter or a comment are left out the same way, blank ones included. A heading, a rule, a list, a table, a quote or a code block ends a run, and the line before it is a plain `<p>`. Runs of spaces and tabs become one space and each line is trimmed, as the author's converter trimmed. The HTML puts each paragraph, heading, rule, table row and list item on a line of its own, a nested list on the lines after its item's words.
- **Emphasis** by CommonMark's delimiter rules, within one line: left- and right-flanking runs, `_` inside a word a letter of it (`snake_case`, `un_frigging_believable`) and `*` inside one a marker (`un*frigging*believable`), the rule of three, and markers that pair with nothing as typed. Markers pair on one line only, so no tag runs from one `<p>` into the next. `***x***` is written `<strong><em>x</em></strong>`, as `rr.1` has it, where CommonMark writes `<em><strong>x</strong></em>`; a reader sees the same. `~~` pairs as `*` does, but only as a run of two: `~` and `~~~` stay as typed. Pairing keeps CommonMark's `openers_bottom`, so a line of 20,000 markers that pair with nothing takes 23 ms where it took 800.
- **Highlight.** `==x==` gives the words alone: no one has seen Royal Road keep `<mark>`, and a sanitiser that drops a tag it does not know may drop the tag's words with it. If the author's paste shows `<mark>` kept, `pairing` gives `mark` for `=`.
- **Headings.** `####` to `######` give `<h4>` to `<h6>`, as the first three give theirs; closing `#`s after a space are left out, and a heading with no words is left out.
- **Rules.** Every thematic break `syntaxSpans` finds (`***`, `---`, `___`, `* * *`, longer runs) and a line of one `*`, the author's scene break; `**` alone is text. A `---` under a line of text is a rule, as the detector reads it (C.72), where CommonMark would make that line a heading.
- **Arrows and dashes.** A run of hyphens before `>` is →, so `-->` is →, not `-→`. Neither these nor the quotes touch code, maths or a web address.
- **Escapes.** A backslash before one of CommonMark's ASCII punctuation marks is left out and the mark stays as typed, opening nothing: no emphasis, tag, link or dash. Before anything else the backslash stays (`C:\Novel`), and at the end of a line, a line break in Markdown, it is left out, each line being a paragraph already. The author's converter removed every backslash.
- **Quotes.** ‘ becomes `'` too, which the author's converter left curly.
- **Links.** A link is `<a href>` only to an `http`, `https` or `mailto` address; any other (a note in the vault, `javascript:`) gives its words alone, as does a link in a link's words, and a link whose words run onto the next line. A bare web address, and one in angle brackets, is a link with the address for its words, the brackets left out. A link's title is left out.
- **Internal links** give their alias, or their target as written: `[[Note#Heading]]` is "Note#Heading", where Obsidian shows "Note > Heading". Embeds are left out.
- **Images.** `![alt](https://...)` is `<img src alt />`; an image in the vault is left out, as Royal Road could not show it.
- **Footnotes.** A reference's mark is left out. A definition, `[^1]: words`, keeps its words where it stands, a paragraph like any other. An inline footnote's words go to the end of the HTML, a paragraph each, in the order they come, where Obsidian shows them, rather than standing in the sentence with nothing round them.
- **Callouts and quotes.** A callout's title is the first line of its quote, in `<strong>`, in one run with its body's lines; a callout with no title gets its type's name in title case, `[!note]` and `[!NOTE]` both "Note", as Obsidian titles it; `+` and `-` are passed over, so a folded callout is shown open. Quotes nest by their `>`s; a line under a quoted paragraph with fewer `>`s runs on in the quote, and `>` alone is a break inside it, as in CommonMark.
- **Lists.** `-`, `*` and `+` give `<ul>`, `1.` and `1)` give `<ol>`, with `start` when the first number is not 1. An item indented two columns or more past the list's first nests (a tab is four); blank lines between items keep one list; a line under an item with no blank line runs on in it after `<br />`. As in CommonMark, a list breaks into a paragraph only with an item that holds something and, numbered, starts at 1, so "1984. A year" under a line stays prose. `- [ ]` and `- [x]` keep their brackets as typed.
- **Tables** as GitHub reads them: a line with a `|` that is neither escaped nor inside a span, over a delimiter row of as many cells; rows to the first line without such a `|`, each cut or filled to the header's cells; `\|` is a `|` in a cell, and a `|` inside `[[...|...]]` or code divides nothing; `:---:`, `---:` and `:---` give `style="text-align: ..."` on the cells.
- **Code and maths** are their text as typed, without their markers: a fenced block's lines a tight block, the fences left out and no Markdown read inside, inline code and maths in the line. There is no `<code>` or `<pre>`, as nothing says Royal Road keeps them. A fenced block in a quote or a callout (a status screen in `> [!info]`) is a block all the same: `syntaxSpans` reads it as inline code from the opening backticks to the closing ones, the `>`s of the lines between inside it, and when only the quote's markers come before the opening fence and nothing after the closing one, its lines are read at the quote's depth, each without as many `>`s as the quote has (and the one space after each), the fences left out. Any other line of inline code or maths begun on an earlier line of a quote loses its `>`s the same way, so `> $$` ... `> $$` gives the maths alone. A `~~~` fence in a quote stays as typed, as the detector does not read it as code. An unclosed fence or `$$` stays as typed (C.72), so the rest of the chapter is not code, and so does an unclosed `%%` or `<!--`, which the detector gives as its marker alone: it shows as typed even alone on its line, where a closed comment's lines are left out (Lines, above). Before the `rr.1` review it was left out, so "Sales %% rose" read "Sales rose" and the `<` of `<!--` was the one `<` neither escaped nor a tag.
- **HTML.** `<u>`, `<sub>` and `<sup>` pass, in lower case, only with no attributes and their closing tag on the same line, so a stray one cannot underline the rest of the page; `<br>`, `<br/>` and `<br />` pass as `<br />`. Every other tag typed is escaped and shows as typed, `<i>` and `<span>` among them, and every `&` is `&amp;`, so a typed entity such as `&nbsp;` shows as typed too.
- **What the HTML can hold**: `p` (with `style="margin-bottom: 0"`), `h1` to `h6`, `strong`, `em`, `s`, `u`, `sub`, `sup`, `a` (`href`), `blockquote`, `ul`, `ol` (`start`), `li`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th` and `td` (`style="text-align: ..."`), `hr`, `br` and `img` (`src`, `alt`), each closed in order, no `<`, `>` or `&` outside them but as `&lt;`, `&gt;` and `&amp;`, and no `"` in an attribute but as `&quot;`. The second property test holds every output to that, which `rr.2`'s Preview can rely on; its `<a>` and `<img>` carry the chapter's own web addresses.
- **Tests.** One group for each of `rr.1`'s eight rules; the Obsidian sample chapter whole, against the HTML written out; Chapter 01 and 02, ten and three plain paragraphs; and the composed text, a pending suggestion read as its original and an accepted one as its replacement. Two properties (fast-check): chapters built of pieces of every kind of syntax, each piece knowing the words a reader sees of it, give those words in order, the inline footnotes' last, after the tags are stripped (500 runs each time); and strings of up to 60 pieces of markup give only the tags above, closed in order, with no bare `<`, `>` or `&` and no letter or digit the text did not hold (1,000 runs). Twenty runs of the file, about 30,000 chapters, found one counterexample, in the generator: a chapter that opens with a `---` rule and has another `---` line later opens with frontmatter, as Obsidian and `frontmatterRange` read it, so the generator no longer opens a chapter with that rule. The `rr.1` review added fixed cases for what the properties cannot see: a `"` in a link's address and in an image's address and words, written `&quot;` (the second property's pieces build such a link or image only by chance, so they now hold one of each); a code block and maths in a quote and a callout, whose `>`s are not letters (the first property's chapters now hold a code block in a quote too); an untitled callout typed `[!NOTE]`; and an unclosed `%%` and `<!--`.
- **Speed.** About 2.5 ms for a 57,000-character chapter (Chapter 01 42 times) and 4.3 ms for 59,000 characters of every kind of syntax (Chapter 03 22 times), of which `syntaxSpans` takes 0.8 and 1.2 ms. The detector's own worst case is the worst here too: a line of 20,000 unmatched `[` takes about 1.3 s, all of it in `syntaxSpans` (its look to the paragraph's end, C.72).
- **Waiting for the author: Royal Road itself.** No agent may use the author's account. He pastes one chapter's Export HTML into a draft chapter in Royal Road's editor, as he pastes his converter's output, beside that output, and says what came out wrong; the rules follow, and this entry records what Royal Road kept: the tight blocks' spacing, the headings, `<hr />`, `<s>`, `<u>`, `<sub>` and `<sup>`, the quotes, the lists (rule 7: tight paragraphs instead if Royal Road spaces them badly), the tables and their alignment, the links and images, and whether it would keep `<mark>` (Highlight, above). 11.4 step 1 waits for it.

### C.112 What the three modes settled where the plan left it open (`rr.2`, 2026-10-24)

`rr.2` gave the Mode select, Full edit's box and Preview's page their shape (section 7, The Mode select; 7.4 item 4). This is what the build decided where the task left a choice, and why.

- **Where the mode lives.** Main and Preview are the store's `viewMode`; Full edit is open exactly while its box is, `drafts[WHOLE_DRAFT_KEY]` (`currentMode`). Every way the box closes, Done, Cancel, a save that applies it, another chapter or another review on screen (which the review selector and History no longer open while Full edit is, below), so leaves Full edit without a second flag to keep in step, and opening Full edit sets `viewMode` to Main, so its Done and Cancel go back to Main, where the author sees the changes as hunks, whichever mode it was opened from. `setReview` sets Main for another chapter and keeps Main or Preview for another review of the same chapter. No setting holds the mode.
- **Full edit's box is a box.** It is a `ParagraphDraft` with `whole: true`, key -1 and no paragraphs, so the machinery boxes already have does for it what it does for them: it freezes every suggestion (`inDraft` is true for every paragraph while it is open), Save to chapter, the leave question and the close question count it as a changed box and apply it with "Apply and save first" or "Apply, save and close" (`commitAllDrafts`, which plans it with `planChapterEdit`), the bulk actions and the review dialogs are refused while it is open, and it is kept on disk and put back by the drafts writer (11.3 j). The words follow it: `CloseGuardState.fullEdit`, `SaveButtonInput.fullEdit` and `SaveShortcutContext.inFullEdit` swap a paragraph's words for Full edit's. A Full edit left as it opened is not written, since it holds nothing to lose, so a chapter left in an untouched Full edit opens in Main; one with typed text comes back in Full edit with its card, which is the one place a chapter does not open in Main, as a paragraph box with typed text comes back open.
- **The switch questions.** "Asks as leaving the page does" gave three cases. Leaving a changed Full edit offers Apply first, focused, Discard and Cancel, with no Keep for later: a Full edit kept while Main or Preview is on screen would freeze every suggestion in a view the author went to in order to decide them, or, left unfrozen, be set aside by the first decision. Opening Full edit over changed paragraph boxes offers Apply first, focused, or Cancel: the box would hold their paragraphs a second time, and a box kept beside it could not be applied once Full edit's Done changed its paragraph. Leaving Main for Preview over changed boxes offers Keep for later, focused, as the leave question does, since Preview changes nothing under them, besides Apply first and Cancel. Boxes left as they opened just close on the way into Full edit.
- **The diff.** The paragraph box's word diff over the whole chapter would let a common word in one paragraph match one in another, and its cost grows with the chapter, so the paragraphs are aligned first, as the full-text diff aligns them (4.4 step 1), and the word diff runs over each stretch between matched paragraphs, which also keeps the box's own rules for each change. 4.4 step 2's pairing by position is kept for a stretch whose word diff passes 1,000 edits (`GAP_EDIT_LIMIT`, jsdiff's `maxEditLength`). Measured in Node on the sample's Chapter 01 repeated to 55,974 characters in 411 paragraphs: with every word changed the plan took 32.8 s without the limit and 250 ms with it; every "the" changed, 23 ms; a word changed in every paragraph, 36 ms; three words, 1 to 3 ms; each plan composed to exactly the chapter typed. A paragraph taken out is planned as emptying its box plans it (review fix): 4.4's place, the blank line after it where a paragraph follows and otherwise the one before, and only the suggestions inside it and in that blank line. The first version let it take a suggestion of the paragraph beside it whose first or last words the change only met, always for the first and the last paragraph, which have one place each, and for a middle one with a suggestion on both sides; emptying the box takes none of them, and nor does Full edit now: the change's edges say so (`Edge` in `src/shared/edit.ts`: `own` at the paragraph's own edge, which takes an insertion right at it, as the box does, and `free` at the outer edge of the blank line, which takes nothing), `toBase` stops at a suggestion left out at an edge (an accepted deletion reads as nothing, so the plain text on either side of it meets at one page offset), and such a change is never trimmed to a bare insertion at its edge, where the next paragraph's own insertion may sit. One blank line too many between two paragraphs took both their edge suggestions, for a change Markdown does not even show; a change to blank lines alone, and the blank lines round paragraphs put in where neither of 4.4's places fits them, now take nothing of the paragraphs beside them. Tests hold each case to the emptied box's plan, and a property checks, over generated chapters, that paragraphs taken out leave every suggestion outside them as it was (500 runs each time, 20,000 once with the composing property). A paragraph put in alone between matched paragraphs takes 4.4's place, the blank line after it or before it, but the other place when the first touches a suggestion and the second does not, so that adding a paragraph after one ending in a pending suggestion does not supersede it; where both do, it takes one whole, as a box does when a paragraph is typed at its end.
