A change of words touching a suggestion takes it whole, as a box's does: on the sample chapter a paragraph break typed between "when." and a pending "Its → It's" takes that suggestion with it, to Unanchored, as typing the same break in a paragraph box does, and one typed after "the door.", with no suggestion beside it, is a hunk of its own.
- **Exactly as typed.** The store applies a plan only when `composeText` of the new hunks equals `fullEditResult`, the text before the body, the box, and the text after, and no hunks overlap; a plan that does not is refused with the box kept (`FULL_EDIT_NOT_EXACT`). The property test, 500 runs each time the tests run and 30,000 once for `rr.2`, has never produced one; the check is there so that a fault in the planner could never change the chapter into something the author did not type.
- **The box.** The prose's typeface at 17 px, the paragraph box's 1.75 line height and `--accent` border, the browser's own focus ring rather than the paragraph box's glow, so CLAUDE.md's three exceptions to the ring stand, and no resize handle. It takes the column's height less the frontmatter above it and the foot below, and at least 12em, below which the column scrolls: in the smallest window at 200% the column is 154 CSS px tall, 121 of them under the select's strip, the box starts under the frontmatter, and Done is a scroll of 228 px away. The caret starts at the top. The frontmatter is shown in Main's frontmatter block, its tooltip "Frontmatter, which Full edit leaves as it is".
- **Preview's page** is the converter's HTML read back through a list of what the converter writes (`previewTree`), not set as `innerHTML`: a tight paragraph's `style` becomes `rr-tight`, a cell's `text-align` `rr-align-*`, a list's `start` stays, a link keeps its words and its address as a tooltip with no `href`, so a click in the preview opens nothing, and a web image becomes its words in a frame ("Image: the mill at dawn"), as the page fetches nothing from the web; any other element gives its words to the one round it. Royal Road's own stylesheet was not fetched, at runtime or for the build: the paragraph spacing, 1.2em, and the headings' 1.6em and 0.6em are those of the author's converter's preview (`markdown_to_royalroad.html`), which he used beside Royal Road; the line height is 1.6 rather than its 1.5, in the prose's serif, and a quote's last line has no margin under it. An empty chapter says "Nothing to preview yet: the chapter has no words." The author judges it against a published chapter (11.4 step 1, with `rr.1`'s paste).
- **Main's own.** The find bar, the hover card, the margin notes, the position strip and the rail are drawn in Main only; leaving Main closes the find bar and the hover card, and Ctrl+F does nothing elsewhere. Edit text on a comment in Preview goes back to Main, where its box opens; in Full edit it is refused, as a pen would be. The review keys are Main's too (review fix): in Preview, j moved the focus to a suggestion the page did not mark, a accepted it, e opened the suggestion editor over the page, and the down arrow, taken to step through the suggestions, left the page where it was. `reviewKeysActive` is false outside Main, so none acts there and the handler returns before `preventDefault`: the arrows, Home, End and the page keys are the browser's, which scrolls Preview's page once it has been clicked or reached with Tab, as End and Page Down already did. In Full edit, where the keys could act only with the focus outside the box, they do nothing either, and the pencils still say why they cannot open.
- **The cards** (review fix). At 1424 by 900 the notification cards, pinned to the column's top right, ran from 668 to 1088 CSS px; Main's prose stops at about 730, short of its margin notes, but Full edit's box ran to 1024 and Preview's page to 1038, so the cards covered the box's first lines, where the caret starts, and Preview's first paragraph. In a scroller 820 CSS px wide or more, Main's `GUTTER_MIN_WIDTH`, both now keep Main's margin, 344 px (`.pane--gutter`'s 22 px of padding, 22 px gap and 300 px column), free on the right: the box runs from 270 to 760 and the page from 270 to 744, about where Main's prose runs. It is a `clamp()` on the scroller's width in `.fulledit`'s and `.preview`'s right padding, since the app's CSS keeps no container query (`themeCss.test.ts` fails one, C.49). A long card still reaches about 90 px over their right edge, as over Main's prose. Below that width, as at 200% in the same window (a scroller of 464 CSS px), the cards stand over the text in every mode, as they do in Main, where there is no room to keep.
- **Another review** (review fix). Choosing another review of the chapter from the review selector, which stays enabled in Full edit, or from History, while Full edit held typed text, asked nothing (`apply.26`'s rule): the other review came on screen, Full edit's box went with the old review's drafts, and the drafts writer, finding that the other review composes the body differently wherever the two reviews' decisions differ, set the text aside with "The chapter no longer reads as it did when you left Full edit open", which was untrue. It is refused now while Full edit is open, typed in or not, with "Finish or cancel Full edit first.", as Review with AI is (`beforeLeaving` in `src/renderer/state/leave.ts`); the selector goes back to the review on screen. Asking Apply first, Discard or Cancel, as leaving Full edit for another mode does, was the other way; a refusal says plainly what to do and costs one click, and the author's workflow has no reason to change reviews in the middle of Full edit.
- **The strip** of the Mode select is 33 CSS px at 100%, which the column gives up in every mode; the select is 16 px from the column's right edge, clear of the side panel's handle, and the strip's empty left is all the chapter list's handle covers. The notification cards keep the top right of the wrapper under it. A select floating over the pane's top padding would have kept the 33 px, but it would cover the prose in a narrow column and once the page scrolls.
- **The focus after a choice.** A choice that lands in Main or Preview blurs the select, as the review selector's choice does (`apply.26`), so the review keys act at once: with the focus left on it, j, k and a did nothing after Preview to Main until the author clicked the page. Full edit's box takes the focus as it opens; after Cancel in a question the focus goes back to the select, as the question gives it back to where it was. The price is a keyboard user's place: the next Tab starts from the top of the window, as after a choice in the review selector.
- **Each mode's place.** The three modes draw in one scroller, so a switch left the new view wherever the old one was: Main came back at whatever offset Preview had been scrolled to, clamped to Main's height. Main and Preview now each keep their own offset for the open chapter (`modePlace`, pure, in `src/shared/ui/modes.ts`; `useModePlaces` writes it as the scroller scrolls and puts it back in a layout effect, before the frame is painted, and not animated, as it is a view coming back rather than a move the author asked for). A mode not shown yet in the chapter starts at its top, and Full edit always does: its box opens afresh each time, the caret and the box's own scroll at the top, and Done and Cancel close it, so it has no place to come back to (review fix: this bullet, the CHANGELOG and the README first said every mode kept its place). Another chapter forgets them all, so a chapter opened from Preview shows Main from its top; a chapter opened in Main keeps the scroller as it was before `rr.2`. Back in Main, the page's first render is shorter than it becomes once ReviewPane has measured the scroller and laid out its margin column, so the browser cut a place deeper than that first height down to it, and nothing put it back: left at 300, 500 or 664 px on Chapter 01 at 1424 by 900, Main came back at 254 each time (review fix). The place is now held (`holdPlace`, `PLACE_HOLD_MS`): put back after each layout in which the scroller's content changed size, from a ResizeObserver, whose callbacks run before the frame is painted, so the page is not drawn at the cut place; until it is reached, the author scrolls or moves on (a wheel, a key, a press or a touch, anywhere), or 1.5 s pass, after which a page that never grew so tall, as a chapter made shorter meanwhile, stays where it got to. The scroller's own moves while a place is held are not taken as the author's place.
- **Verified in the window** (`rr.2`'s tick has the figures, and those of the review fixes): quiet `dev:clean --no-claude-code --shell-stub` windows on scratch copies of the samples, focus emulated, the foreground read after every step of the last two runs.

### C.113 What Sign in with ChatGPT settled where the plan left it open (`codex.2`, 2026-10-24)

- **One sign-in, kept registrations.** The plan speaks of one sign-in, kept for an account; OpenAI's pages speak of registrations, a client id issued for one account in one workspace. The app keeps every registration it was issued and one sign-in at a time. A plain Sign in with ChatGPT reuses the registration used last; **Use another account**, offered while signed out once a registration is kept, registers anew through `dynamic_agent_client`, as OpenAI's page on accounts says to add one. Signing in while signed in is refused (the view never offers it). The app sends no `id_token_hint` or `login_hint`: after Sign out it keeps neither the ID token nor the email, so OpenAI's page shows its account selector, and an answer for another account on a kept registration is refused and revoked ("To use that account, choose Use another account").
- **The way in.** ChatGPT is no provider until `codex.3`, so "on Setup whenever ChatGPT is chosen" is, for now, the view chosen from Settings' new ChatGPT account row, between the Claude account and the OpenAI key; `codex.3` opens it from where ChatGPT becomes the provider. The Setup screen keeps its one `setupOpen`, and `setupFor` (`claude` or `chatgpt`) names the view; Claude's launch card, its re-check as the window comes back and the status bar's usage notice follow Claude's view only (`claudeSetupOpen` in App). The ChatGPT view leaves Claude's launch card where it is, as it says nothing the card says.
- **The button's words and look.** "Sign in with ChatGPT", the plan's words, is one of the two labels OpenAI's button page approves; its UX guidelines would call the action "Continue with ChatGPT". The button is the app's ordinary primary button, with no ChatGPT logo: nothing of OpenAI's ships, and its brand page bars suggesting an endorsement. A question for the author: "Continue with ChatGPT", or a logo, would follow OpenAI's guidelines more closely.
- **A sign-in that does not grant the plan.** OpenAI's page would keep it with plan use off; the app has no use for the identity alone, so it revokes the refresh token, keeps nothing, and marks the registration so that the next sign-in sends `prompt=consent`, which OpenAI's page names for asking again (`force_reconsent` waits for OpenAI's confirmation for an integration).
- **The port and the listener.** A port the system picks for each attempt rather than 1455, Codex's, so the app and a Codex sign-in never meet; OpenAI allows the port to change. The listener answers only a GET of `/auth/callback` whose Host is its own address (a page that rebinds a name to 127.0.0.1 gets an empty 400), tells an answer with another state "Not this sign-in" and waits on, and gives the tab its page within 90 s of the answer.
- **The client id is kept at the callback**, before the exchange, so a code refused with `invalid_grant` is tried again on the same registration, as OpenAI's page says, rather than registering the app a second time. Its account's `sub` follows once a sign-in with it is checked.
- **What the page is told** (`ChatGptStatus`): beside signed in or not and the plan, the box, whether a sign-in is waiting (so a reloaded page still shows the wait), whether a registration is kept (for Use another account), whether safeStorage can encrypt, and a development run's sign-in server. Never a token, the client id, the account's id or its email.
- **`shell:open-external`, by name.** The app had no such channel: its links reach the browser through the window's open handler. The Data controls button is a button, so the page asks main for the page by its name (`ExternalPage`), main holds the address (`EXTERNAL_PAGE_URLS`), and the shell stub prints it in a test run; the page can still never hand the shell an address. Main reads it through `externalPageUrl`, which takes only the table's own names, so an inherited one such as `constructor` or `__proto__` opens nothing, tested with them, an address and values that are not strings (codex.2 review).
- **The Data controls address** is `https://chatgpt.com/#settings/DataControls`, ChatGPT's own address for that tab, found on none of OpenAI's pages read (Appendix A); the warning also gives the way by hand, so it holds should the address stop opening the tab.
- **The warning's words.** "On personal ChatGPT plans (Free, Go, Plus and Pro)": OpenAI does not train on Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces' content by default, so the warning names the plans it is about; and "may use", as OpenAI's terms put it. It says that a review sends the chapter and the guidelines file, that the app cannot see the setting, and, in the author's words, that leaving it on is allowed but not recommended. The view always shows it.
- **The box** belongs to a registration, an account in a workspace, so another workspace asks again; it is disabled while signed out, with a note saying why, and never disabled while main writes it, which would take the focus of a box ticked from the keyboard. The gate it makes, "which the first review needs", is `codex.3`'s, which brings the first review.
- **Sign out's revocation** is tried three times at most, after 0.5 s and 1.5 s, for a dead connection or a 5xx; any other answer stops it; the tokens go either way, and the view says whether OpenAI confirmed it.
- **The wait** ends after 10 minutes; a new sign-in replaces the one waiting, whose answer then fails as cancelled; Sign out and quitting end it; a sign-in replaced before its browser opened opens none.
- **secrets.json.** The key's functions and the sign-in's share `updateSecrets`, which reads the file, changes one part and writes it back, one write at a time per folder: until `codex.2` saving or removing the key wrote the whole file, which would have dropped the sign-in. The tokens, scopes and expiry are one ciphertext; the host id, the registrations' client ids, the account's `sub` (an opaque id) and the plan are plain, and the privacy footer says so (codex.2 review: it said the app kept only the tokens). Off Windows the file is written 0600 (`atomicWriteFile`'s new `mode`), as OpenAI's page asks; Windows keeps the profile folder to its user. **A read that failed is never an empty file** (codex.2 review). Until the review `readSecrets` read every failure as an empty file and `updateSecrets` built its write on it, so a read refused for a moment, by a tool holding the file, and a write that then went through dropped the other credential, the registrations and the host id, which in the window took one tick of the box with the file held for 0.4 s. A write now reads strictly, as settings.json's save does (`hardening.15`, C.86): no file is empty, a refused read refuses the write, and a damaged file is copied aside first, or nothing is written. The read is not tried again, unlike settings.json's, which waits 200 ms: the request fails with the read's words and the author tries again. The sign-in's decisions read strictly too (`readChatGptChecked`), since a lenient read there would register the app again or take another account's sign-in on a kept registration, and Sign out would say OpenAI ended a sign-in it never read. The status stays lenient, as the review asked, but remembers what it last read or wrote in the run and gives that while the file cannot be read: without it the refresh after a refused tick told the page "not signed in", disabled the box and left the view there after the file came back.
- **The plan's name** comes from `chatgpt_plan_type` in the ID token's `https://api.openai.com/auth` claim, which Codex reads and OpenAI's pages for this sign-in do not mention; an unknown word is capitalised, anything else dropped, and none leaves "Signed in to ChatGPT" without a plan.
- **A failed request to OpenAI says how** (codex.2 review). Until the review the key endpoint's error status read "could not finish the sign-in with OpenAI (no answer). Check your connection and try again.", a 200 token answer without its tokens "(no tokens in the answer). Check your connection ...", and the log had no status for the keys. `exchange` is now three reasons: `no-answer` (the request threw: the only one that names the connection), `server` (an error status, with it) and `malformed` (an answer not in the form OpenAI documents); `getJson` reads the status and the body as `postForm` does, and the log has the `endpoint`. A key set that is JSON but holds no usable key is still the ID token's `key` problem. The mock's `notokens`, `jwksfails` and `jwksjunk` play them.
- **The log** has the five events of 5.7 item 9 and never a secret; `scrub` now also takes out anything shaped like a JWT, the shape of the access and ID tokens, as a backstop.
- **Tested without an account.** `test/helpers/mockChatGptAuth.ts` answers as OpenAI's pages describe, signs its ID tokens with a key it makes at start, and changes one answer by scenario; the switch `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_CHATGPT_AUTH_URL` points a development run at it, and a packaged build ignores it. There is no packaged smoke in `codex.2`: a packaged build ignores the switch, so its Sign in would open OpenAI's real page in the author's browser; `codex.3`'s packaged smoke covers the view.
- **Left to `codex.3`** (done there but for the author's own review and the packaged smoke, C.114): the reviews, the refresh of an ended access token (the mock has no refresh grant yet), the model list, the limits and errors, the provider in the review dialog, the Review menu and the status bar, the warning and the box's gate before the first review, OpenAI's "Using ChatGPT plan", "Manage usage" and first-sign-in welcome, and the README's section on reviewing with ChatGPT.

### C.114 What ChatGPT's reviews settled where the plan left it open (`codex.3`, 2026-10-24)

- **Structured output, tried first.** A ChatGPT review sends the API key's `json_schema` format unchanged. The mock's ChatGPT route takes it, so the question 5.7 left is settled for the mock only; the author's own review on his Plus plan settles it for OpenAI's route. A refusal of it (`subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability` naming `text.format`, the code OpenAI's page gives for an input the route does not take) says so in words of its own and points at Claude or an API key; nothing falls back by itself, as reading a review from prose is not what the app does, and the Codex CLI fallback `codex.2` named would be a task of its own. The author's review is `codex.4`, which the `codex.3` review added, so that it is not left under a ticked box.
- **The limits come from headers OpenAI does not document for this route.** OpenAI's pages on models and inference, preview limitations, errors and recovery and its UI guidelines say nothing of the plan's hourly or weekly usage in an answer: usage-limit errors only, and ChatGPT's usage settings as the way to see more. The app reads the headers Codex reads from ChatGPT's own back end (`x-codex-primary-used-percent` and the rest, the names compiled into the Codex CLI 0.149.1 on this machine, read from its binary on 2026-10-24), so if the route sends them the status bar words them as setup.9 words Claude's; if it does not, a notice comes only with a usage-limit refusal, as "Usage limit reached". Codex 0.149.1 also has a rate-limit event in its stream, which is not read. The author's review records which arrives.
- **"Hourly and weekly".** The plan's words; Codex's two windows are 5 hours and a week. The app names a window by its length (`windowKind`), so 300 minutes is the "5-hour limit" Claude's notices name, 10,080 the weekly one, and an hourly window would read "hourly limit".
- **A limit not named.** OpenAI's page warns against reading a reset time, or the whole plan as used up, from the usage-limit code alone, so a refusal without limit headers gives no reset, and the card says the limit may be the plan's or the one OpenAI sets for the app. Buy app credits, OpenAI's second action for it, is not offered, as the app sells none.
- **`input` as a list**, the chapter as the one user message, as the preview limitations page asks; the API key's request keeps its string, which OpenAI's API takes as the same message.
- **No retries.** OpenAI's example for this route sets `max_retries=0`; an API key's review keeps its one retry.
- **The renewal's margin**: 60 s before the access token's end (`RENEW_BEFORE_MS`), for a clock a little off, and after a 401, once. The token reference's `earliest_refresh_at` is named without what to do with it, so the app does not read it.
- **One renewal, which a review's Cancel does not end.** The waiting request stops; the renewal goes on, since one cut short after OpenAI had rotated the refresh token would leave the app holding a spent one. Quitting still ends it.
- **A renewal held for its write.** A renewal secrets.json will not take, as while a sync tool holds it (the codex.2 review's case), is held in memory for the run and written with the next request, logged `kept=later`; until then the plan shown is the one before. The `codex.3` review found the next renewal compared with the sign-in before the held one was written, so a held token that had ended by the next review, or that OpenAI refused, lost the sign-in: once written, the held renewal is the sign-in a renewal is compared with, a renewal reads the kept sign-in again as it starts, Sign out ends the held refresh token, which is the live one, and the spent one too, and a held renewal goes with the sign-in it renewed (5.8 item 3).
- **A sign-in replaced during a renewal**: the renewal is ended at OpenAI, and the request takes the new sign-in's fresh token (a mutation run found this path untested; until then it failed as not signed in). A sign-out during a renewal fails the request as not signed in.
- **`invalid_client`** ends the sign-in, as the refresh token's own errors do, and keeps a plain Sign in from reusing that registration, so the next one registers anew: for the app, OpenAI's "fix the client configuration" can only mean a new registration. Use another account is then not offered either, as no registration is the one a plain Sign in reuses. Tested since the `codex.3` review with the mock's `refreshinvalidclient`.
- **The renewed ID token** is read but not checked again: it comes straight from the token endpoint, over HTTPS, in answer to the app's own request, and carries no nonce of an attempt. Its account must be the kept one's, or the renewal is ended at OpenAI and nothing of it kept, and the plan it names replaces the kept plan.
- **Not signed in, never a failed review.** The ChatGPT view opens with the reason under its buttons in the warning colour, and no card goes up: a card with Open Setup, as Claude's failures have, would be a failed review's card in all but name.
- **The Review menu** names the providers as the dialog's Provider list does, "Claude", "ChatGPT" and "OpenAI (API key, experimental)", rather than "With Claude" and the rest: the menu's button says Review, and codex.1 and codex.2 listed them so. Each has a tooltip (`REVIEW_WITH_TITLES`), and Manual is under a line. An item writes its provider as a setting the page takes at once (`chooseProvider`, the columns' writer's rule), so the dialog opens on it and a close waits for the write. Setup's ready line, which said "With AI, in the Review menu, can use Claude.", now says "Claude, in the Review menu, starts a review.", and the page with nothing open names all three.
- **OpenAI's welcome** is a box on the ChatGPT view under the status card, not a modal: the view is where the sign-in was made, and a modal there would cover the warning the author reads next. It shows once per computer (the hint `chatgpt-plan-welcome`), not once per account; Got it hands the focus to the account button, which the window check found left on nothing.
- **The dialog's warning** shows while the box is not ticked and, once it is ticked in that opening, until the dialog closes, since hiding it at once would take the box out from under the keyboard's focus. Main's gate is the same box (`chatgpt-data-settings`).
- **The default model** is the first OpenAI lists that is not a -pro, -codex, -deep-research or -chat one: the route gives no dates to sort by, and the list's order is OpenAI's. An answer in an API key's shape (`data` of `id`s) is read too, should the route answer so.
- **No connection test** for ChatGPT: its view has no Test the connection, as a review is its test, and `ai:test` answers "has no connection test", as for any provider without one.
- **No cost.** A plan's review shows none in the status bar or History; its token counts are kept.
- **A model list that fails is said, and asked for again** (`codex.3` review). It was kept as an empty list for the rest of the run, so the dialog said "no models" with Start disabled and no reason, and 5.8 item 2's failure for an empty list could not be reached without a model stored. Now main's words are kept apart (`modelsError`) and shown under the Model row with Try again, for any provider, since OpenAI's list had the same gap; the dialog asks once more as an opening first shows the provider, not on every draw, which would ask again in a loop; and a ChatGPT sign-in that has gone still empties the list, as its runtime check then says not signed in. Main's words for a sign-in OpenAI refused after its renewal no longer say "for this review", since the list shows them too.
- **The packaged smoke** is not done here: a packaged build ignores both switches and `--quiet`, so its window would take the foreground, and its Sign in would open OpenAI's real page. It is the author's, with his review, as `codex.2` left its own; `codex.4` carries both, and docs/RELEASING.md's smoke checklist has ChatGPT in its step 5.
- **Tested without an account**: the two mocks, `mockOpenAi.ts`'s ChatGPT route keyed by the token's `mock_scenario` claim, which `mockChatGptAuth.ts` puts in the tokens it makes (`--api-scenario` or `POST /mock/api-scenario`), or set over it with `POST /mock/scenario`, so a window run can change it without a new sign-in.

### C.115 What taking out the OpenAI API key settled where the plan left it open (`codex.6`, 2026-10-24)

- **When the key leaves secrets.json.** At the file's next write, not at the next save of settings, which the task's check named: settings.json never held the key. `readOnce` keeps only the parts this version knows (`knownParts`: `version` and `chatgpt`), so a key from before is dropped as the file is read, never used and never written back, and every write of secrets.json (a sign-in, a sign-out, the data settings box, a renewal) leaves it out. Nothing writes the file at start-up for its sake: that would be a write the author did not ask for, and a failed one would need words of its own. What settings.json held of the key, `provider: "openai"` and `openaiModel`, goes at its next save: the provider reads as Claude, the default, and the model is dropped as any key the app does not know is (11.3 d).
- **The welcome guide's other provider.** "Use ChatGPT instead" (`USE_CHATGPT`) stands on Claude's step where "Use OpenAI instead (experimental, pay per use)" stood: without it the guide would offer Claude alone, and ChatGPT could be chosen only from the Review menu once the guide was closed. The task named only the OpenAI path's going; the ChatGPT step it leads to is `codex.3`'s, with Set up ChatGPT and Use Claude instead.
- **A review saved on a key.** `GeneratorKind` keeps `openai`, and `GeneratorProvider`, the kinds a model wrote (`Exclude<GeneratorKind, 'manual' | 'file'>`), types a saved review's provider, so `Provider`, what can review now, is `claude` and `chatgpt` alone. History, the review selector and the status bar name such a review "OpenAI (API key)" (`PROVIDER_NAMES`), where they said "OpenAI". History's badge keeps its words on one line, the time giving way first (`.history__item .badge`), since "OpenAI (API key)" wrapped onto two lines in the window check. `costEstimated` stays on the saved generator, so such a review's cost still says "estimate", and went from `ProviderResult`, `ai:review`'s answer and the log, as no provider sets it now.
- **The status bar's button** opens the Setup screen for either provider, so its tooltip is one constant, `RUNTIME_BUTTON_TITLE`, "Open Setup", where `runtimeButtonTitle(provider)` gave "Open Settings" for the key.
- **The scenarios only a key reached.** `mockOpenAi.ts`'s key route went, with `scenarioForKey`, and its ChatGPT route gained the five scenarios only a key had: `unauthorized` a 401 for every request, the model list too; `ratelimit` a 429 and `servererror` a 500 for a review, the model list still answering; `unverified` the 400 OpenAI gives a streamed request from an organisation that has not verified its identity; `skippedonly` a list of only models the default passes over (`CHATGPT_SKIPPED_ONLY_MODELS`). They read in the ChatGPT provider's words, not the key's: `unauthorized` renews the sign-in once, then says OpenAI did not accept it (`signInNotAccepted`), the sign-in kept; `ratelimit` that OpenAI is limiting requests from the sign-in; `unverified` a request the route refused (status 400), as the verification words were about an OpenAI organisation, which a ChatGPT plan has none of; and `skippedonly`'s default is the first model listed, gpt-5.5-pro, as `defaultChatGptModel` takes the first when it would pass over them all. A bearer that is not a sign-in's token, as a key is, gets the 401 OpenAI gives a key it does not know.
- **How a window run picks a scenario.** From the sign-in: `node test/helpers/mockChatGptAuth.ts --port 4600 --api-scenario <name>`, or `POST /mock/api-scenario` to it, puts the name in the tokens it makes from then on, a renewal's included, and the API mock answers by the token's `mock_scenario` claim; `POST /mock/scenario` to the API mock sets one over every token's until an empty body clears it, so a run changes scenario without signing in again. CLAUDE.md's mock paragraph and CONTRIBUTING.md's Testing without an account say so. A sign-in kept from an earlier mock is a registration a restarted mock does not know ("unknown client"), so a new run signs in with Use another account, which registers anew, or on a new data folder.
- **What stays.** `buildClaudeEnv` still removes `OPENAI_API_KEY` from Claude Code's environment (11.3 c), though the app no longer reads it: `clientOptions` states the bearer and the address outright, so neither the package's `OPENAI_API_KEY` nor `OPENAI_BASE_URL` can move them (`responsesRequest.test.ts`, whose hostile environment sets both, and checks the client's `apiKey` as well as its `baseURL` since `codex.6`'s review: the package takes `OPENAI_API_KEY` when `apiKey` is left out). The log still scrubs OpenAI key shapes (11.3 m), and the bug report template still asks for API keys to be left out, as Claude Code can sign in with one.
- **The CHANGELOG.** Unreleased's lines about the key were edited out or reworded, and Removed has a line for it (`codex.6`'s review; the task said to add none, since no release carried it). The 0.1.0 section, the author's private builds under the name Stet, lists OpenAI on an API key, and Removed already names two other things only those builds had, the copy of Claude Code inside the app and the portable exe, so a feature of 0.1.0 that goes is a removal in this file. The line says what replaces the key, Review with ChatGPT through Sign in with ChatGPT, and what becomes of a 0.1.0 install's key, provider and reviews (the first bullet above, and "A review saved on a key"). About's line under Added says what Lapidary is and is not in `DISCLAIMER`'s new words, which no longer say "OpenAI's API".
- **The README's screenshots** still show the key: `polish.18` shot `review.png` and `review-dark.png` on a made-up one, so their status bar reads "OpenAI ready (key ends 7Qa2)" and "$0.0201 estimate". `polish.21` shoots them again through ChatGPT, after `polish.20`, which changes the rows they show.
- **Settings' box** is 588 CSS px tall at 100% without the key's row, against 689 measured the same way in the #14 build with no key saved.

### C.116 What the plain Review with ChatGPT dialog settled where the plan left it open (`codex.5`, 2026-10-24)

- **The rows.** Claude's four, Provider, Model, Effort and Guidelines, with ChatGPT's Account between Provider and Model as before, then the last-review line, Start review and the footer, as for Claude. The training warning with its box stays under the account before the first review, and the line beside a disabled Start says what it waits for, as 5.8 item 5 has it. `chatgptReview.render.test.ts` holds the two dialogs to the same markup, the Account row and the lists' options apart.
- **Open Setup while there is no sign-in.** "Not read yet", before main has answered, and "waiting for the browser" count as no sign-in: Start waits in both, and the view is where the sign-in is made or followed. Without the button the row was 17 CSS px tall against the 27 of the rows around it, so it would have moved everything under it as a sign-in came or went; `modal__row--account` gives it a button's height, `calc(1lh + 10px)` (its line, 4 px of padding and 1 px of border above and below), measured 27 px with the button and without in both themes.
- **The focus.** A sign-in that ends its wait while the dialog is open takes Open Setup away; a focus left on it goes to the dialog's box, as the model list's Try again hands its own on (a source check in `chatgptWiring.test.ts`). The window run could not reach it: without Claude Code the dialog opens on ChatGPT only once signed in, and with Claude Code installed the author reaches it by choosing ChatGPT in a dialog opened for Claude.
- **The development endpoint line.** In a development run on `MANUSCRIPT_REVIEW_OPENAI_BASE_URL` the dialog showed the runtime's message, "Using a development endpoint: <address>", under the Model row. Claude's dialog has no such line, so it went too. Main still gives the message in `ai:runtime`'s answer, where a drive can read it; the log still leaves it out (`loggedProvider.test.ts`), and Copy diagnostics names the switch ("OpenAI base URL"). `apply.14`'s check read that line to tell a packaged build from a development one; a check like it now reads `ai:runtime`, or the `devswitch.ignored` line a packaged build logs.
- **OpenAI's guidelines.** OpenAI's UI and UX page for Sign in with ChatGPT (Appendix A) describes "Using ChatGPT plan" with Manage usage by the model choice; the dialog leaves both out at the author's word. Manage usage stays where that page also puts it: the first sign-in's welcome on the ChatGPT view, until Got it, and the usage limit's card. The task said the note "stays on the Set up ChatGPT page", and as built it did not: the page had OpenAI's welcome until Got it and no Manage usage after it, and "Using ChatGPT plan" stood nowhere in the app. The review (2026-10-24) found the gap, which the author would only have met here, and its fix put the note on the view: while signed in, once the welcome has gone, the status card ends with "**Using ChatGPT plan.** Reviews count against your ChatGPT plan's usage limits, and nothing is billed per token." and Manage usage as a link, the dialog's note as it was, its words trimmed of "with no API key" now that the key has gone (`codex.6`). While the welcome is up the card leaves the label to it, which says the same with its own Manage usage, so the view never shows two (5.7 item 6, 5.8 item 9). Information for the author, not legal advice: this is a guidelines page, not the terms, which answered 403 on 2026-10-24.
- **The effort.** The levels map to OpenAI's reasoning effort as before (`toOpenAiEffort`, 5.0), and a model that refuses one still says so: a 400 reads "... The model or the effort level may not be available on it: choose another under Model or Effort in Review with AI." (`chatgpt-failed`), and `subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability` names the parameter (5.8 item 7).
- **Gone from the code.** The dialog's `onManageUsage`. `USING_CHATGPT_PLAN` and `CHATGPT_PLAN_NOTE` in `src/shared/ui/chatgpt.ts` went too and came back with the review's fix, for the view's status card; `MANAGE_USAGE_BUTTON` stays for the welcome, the status card and the usage limit's card. The README's step on reviewing with ChatGPT no longer names the two; its step on signing in does.
- **The effort's words elsewhere** (the review). PLAN 5.0's Effort bullet and the comment on `OPENAI_EFFORT_FOR` still said the dialog warns that not every model accepts every level; both now say the error does (`chatgpt-failed`, 5.8 item 7), and C.25 says the dialog did until `codex.5`.

## Appendix D: release 1.0 answers

The author's answers to 11.6, dated, numbered as there. A question not listed here is still open.

- **1. Name** (2026-10-14): **Lapidary.** The author had become unsure about Igneous once it turned out to be in use elsewhere, and chose Lapidary from this research:
  - **Trademarks.** Rubrik's software mark IGNEOUS (US Reg. 5926931) was cancelled on 2026-06-19. Every live IGNEOUS mark in the US and Canada covers unrelated goods.
  - **Same niche.** Two free Markdown apps named Igneous, both aimed at Obsidian users, launched in the ten days before: a notes app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that opens Obsidian folders (getigneous.com, 2026-10-07), and a GNOME desktop editor described as an alternative frontend to Obsidian (github.com/H4RL33/igneous, 2026-10-05).
  - **Recommendation.** Rename for confusion and discoverability, not legal risk. **Lapidary** is first: the craft of cutting and polishing stone, obsidian included, and "lapidary" prose is polished and concise. It has no software trademark, no Obsidian plugin or theme, no notable app, and lapidary.app is taken. **Ventifact**, a stone polished by wind-blown sand over years, is the cleanest name but obscure. **Stet** looked clean on narrow checks only.
  - **Ruled out.** Whetstone, which is crowded with 2026 AI writing tools. Basalt, Pumice, Granite and Onyx, which are already Obsidian plugin or theme names.
- **2. Logo** (2026-10-14): concept A "Seam" is the direction, but with a more rock-like body, like obsidian, in place of the flat basalt fill. The squarish-round pebble shape stays. Three variants with the same rim and foreground are in `dist/logo-concepts/rock/`, with `compare.png` and each folder's `render.py`:
  - **conchoidal:** black glass with curved fracture ripples, ranked first as the most rock-like;

The ember original is the alternative he may return to. The sectioned-rock prototypes in `dist/logo-concepts/sections/` were not taken.

## Appendix A: billing and policy sources (checked 2026-09-08, re-checked 2026-10-16, Claude Code setup pages re-read 2026-10-19, Sign in with ChatGPT pages read 2026-10-24 and four of them re-read that day for `codex.3`)

The list below is the 2026-09-08 check. Every page in it still loaded on 2026-10-16; what has changed since, and what the release depends on, is in the subsection after it. Five Claude Code pages that the Setup screen and the README rest on were re-read on 2026-10-19 for `setup.13`, in the subsection after that. OpenAI's pages on Sign in with ChatGPT for open-source apps, which `codex.2` follows, were read on 2026-10-24, in the subsection after that, and four of them were re-read the same day for `codex.3`, in the last.

- **OpenAI, Codex CLI and Sign in with ChatGPT** (read 2026-10-22 for `codex.1`; the URLs and quotes are in the agents' report `codex-research.md`): the Codex CLI repository (github.com/openai/codex) is Apache-2.0 and documents `codex exec` for non-interactive use with `--json` JSONL output and `--output-schema`, a read-only sandbox, and `-c` settings that turn off the shell, apps, image and web-search tools; `codex login status` answers in text with an exit code; credentials sit in the user's `~/.codex/auth.json` or the system store. OpenAI's Terms of Use (effective 2026-01-01) bar automatically or programmatically extracting data or Output, with no published exception for Codex CLI; OpenAI's own Claude Code plugin runs the local Codex CLI under the user's own sign-in. The Usage Policies (effective 2026-11-20) have no clause on misrepresenting a client; the Sign in with ChatGPT terms (2026-09-29) say not to impersonate OpenAI, another application or another open-source project, and bind apps that integrate that sign-in. Sign in with ChatGPT is documented for "ChatGPT plan usage in your open-source app"; whether it allows `json_schema` output is not documented. Plan pages: Plus and above include the CLI with estimated five-hour message limits and possible weekly limits, Pro without the five-hour limit; the Free plan's access is stated differently on two of OpenAI's pages. Consumer plans train on content unless the user turns it off under Data controls. The app-server (JSON-RPC over stdio) is labelled experimental and not for production. Several pages name models and plans the agent did not see elsewhere; they are reported as read.
- Help Center, "Use the Claude Agent SDK with your Claude plan": update dated June 15 says the planned change is paused; Agent SDK, `claude -p`, and third-party app usage still draw from the subscription's usage limits. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15036540-use-the-claude-agent-sdk-with-your-claude-plan
- Claude Code docs, Legal and compliance: OAuth is for subscription holders' ordinary use of Claude Code and native apps; developers may not offer claude.ai login in their own products or intermediate credentials; an end user signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription is allowed. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance
- Agent SDK overview and quickstart: bundled native binary, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the documented developer path. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart
- Authentication: credential precedence, Windows storage location. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication
- Structured outputs, streaming, cost tracking, TypeScript reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/structured-outputs , https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-output , https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking , https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript

### Anthropic terms for a free open-source release (research dated 2026-10-14, re-read 2026-10-16; 11.6 question 8)

Quotes were checked by a second, independent pass on 2026-10-14, and again on 2026-10-16 against copies of the pages saved that day. This is information for the author, not legal advice.

- **Re-read on 2026-10-16.** Every page below loaded, and none has changed in a way that matters here since the 2026-10-14 research. Each was compared with its newest Wayback capture, dated 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-14; the Consumer Terms and Commercial Terms only by their unchanged effective dates. The legal page's only change since 2026-08-30 is its Healthcare compliance (BAA) section, rewritten between 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-08. The bullets below also record text that was already on these pages on 2026-10-14 but was left out then.
- **Legal and compliance page.** Running Claude Code "in your products or services" requires agreeing to the Commercial Terms "unless we've mutually agreed otherwise". The conditions are: the binary is unmodified, no built-in sign-in method is restricted, and no paying for, reselling or intermediating users' usage. The page's only example of such a product is hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure. The same page says Anthropic does not permit "third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications", but does not prevent an end user "signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription". That section first appears in Wayback between 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-30. A 2026-02-18 capture instead said subscription OAuth tokens in any other tool, "including the Agent SDK", were not permitted; that sentence was gone by 2026-04-13. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance
  - **Using the Claude Code name and logo.** A product may say accurately, in plain text, that it has Claude Code preinstalled or that it "runs Claude Code". It may not use the Claude Code or Anthropic names or logos in its own product, feature or company name, in its logo, or in a way that suggests Anthropic built, endorses or partners with it. Any other use of Anthropic's names or logos falls under the Trademark Guidelines and needs written permission. The paragraph is in every capture from 2026-08-30 on. It sits in the section on products that run Claude Code under the Commercial Terms, and it is the only Anthropic text found on plain-text mentions; the plan follows it as guidance. Its rule is the plan's: no Claude or Anthropic marks in the product name or logo, and Claude Code named only in plain text. `DISCLAIMER` uses the page's own wording, that the app runs Claude Code.
  - **Also on the page since at least 2026-08-30, not recorded before.** Developers may not route requests through Free, Pro or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users. They may not collect, store or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens, and sign-in to a Claude account "must complete through Anthropic's own flow". Anthropic may enforce these restrictions "without prior notice". The advertised Pro and Max limits "assume ordinary, individual usage" of Claude Code and the Agent SDK. Under License, Free, Pro and Max users are under the Consumer Terms, and Team, Enterprise and API users under the Commercial Terms.
- **Anthropic Trademark Guidelines** (effective 2024-08-01; identical to the 2026-10-04 capture). They cover Anthropic's names, logos, brand elements and anything it uses to identify its products. Anthropic's marks may be used only as it specifically permits, in materials it approves beforehand, and never in a way that implies sponsorship, endorsement, or a relationship or affiliation with Anthropic. Marks may not be altered or carry a trademark symbol. The guidelines say nothing about plain-text mentions of a product; the legal page's paragraph above is the only text found on that case. https://www.anthropic.com/legal/trademark-guidelines
- **Consumer Terms** (effective 2025-10-08), which govern Free, Pro and Max users of Claude Code. Section 3 bars accessing the Services "through automated or non-human means", except with an Anthropic API key or "where we otherwise explicitly permit it". The app runs `claude -p` as a child process, which is scripted access. The texts treated as that explicit permission are the legal page's clause that an end user may sign in to the unmodified binary with their own subscription, and the Help Center's 2026-10-07 statement that `claude -p` and third-party apps can still use subscription limits. Section 12, "Use of our brand", bars using Anthropic's name, logos or trademarks in connection with other products, or in a way that implies affiliation, endorsement or sponsorship, without prior written permission. The legal page's name-and-logo paragraph is the only Anthropic text that addresses a plain-text statement that a product runs Claude Code; whether its section applies to this app is the open question in section 9 risk 8, bullet 4. https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms
- **Agent SDK overview and quickstart** (actively maintained; reworded between April and August 2026 and kept after the August rewrite of the legal page; on 2026-10-16 the overview matched its 2026-10-10 capture, and the quickstart differed from its 2026-10-04 capture by one word). Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third-party developers "to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products", agents built on the SDK included, and points them to API keys instead. The SDK "is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service", including in products offered to others. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview
  - **Branding guidelines** on the overview page, written for partners integrating the Agent SDK. Claude branding is optional. Allowed: "Claude Agent", "Claude" inside a menu already labelled "Agents", and "{YourAgentName} Powered by Claude". Not permitted: "Claude Code" or "Claude Code Agent", or visuals that mimic Claude Code. The product keeps its own branding and must not appear to be Claude Code or any Anthropic product. These rules address SDK integrations, which the app no longer is (C.42, Appendix D 21). It meets the last one anyway: its name, logo and window are its own, and its provider label is the plain "Claude". A GitHub issue asking for the same guidance for projects that run the Claude Code CLI, anthropics/claude-code#24600, was closed as not planned on 2026-03-11 with no answer from Anthropic.
- **Commercial Terms** (effective 2025-06-17; no newer version posted on 2026-10-16). Nothing in them depends on charging money, and no page exempts free or open-source projects. The author would be the Customer and the people he gives the app to his Users. Acceptance is free: signing in to the Console says "By continuing, you agree". D.3: the Customer must notify Users that factual assertions in outputs should be checked before they are relied on; the README's `AI_OUTPUT_NOTICE` says so anyway, as plain good practice. K.2: the Customer defends Anthropic against third-party claims about the Customer's or Users' inputs, or about use that breaches the Usage Policy, and pays resulting judgments or approved settlements. This duty is uncapped (L.3 excludes it), while other liability is capped both ways at fees paid. Section F grants no rights by implication; the legal page's clause is the only text that permits shipping `claude.exe`. https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms
- **Usage Policy** effective 2026-11-12, published on anthropic.com on 2026-10-08 and so not yet in force on 2026-10-16. The version it replaces, effective 2025-09-15, has no such clause. Under "Do Not Abuse Our Platform" it bars reselling, proxying or otherwise providing access to Claude through unauthorised means, including services that "route requests through consumer subscriptions or misrepresent the product or client being used". The app runs the real `claude` binary and never sets or overrides its client or entrypoint identity (CLAUDE.md rule 6). Anthropic's announcement of the new version, "2026 Usage Policy update" (2026-10-08), lists its changes without mentioning this clause. The same version names Claude Code users and the end users of products that integrate Claude among the people it binds, and its bypass bullet now includes circumventing "the account sign-up or log-in process"; the app never starts or handles a sign-in. https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup and https://www.anthropic.com/news/2026-usage-policy-update
- **Help Center, Agent SDK with your plan.** Update of 2026-10-07: Max and Team plans now include monthly API credits that cover the Agent SDK, `claude -p`, the Claude API and Claude Managed Agents, and the SDK, `claude -p` and third-party apps can still be used "with your subscription limits". The June 15 notice that the planned change is paused is still there. The page's earlier text, including the promise of notice before changes, is gone. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15036540-use-the-claude-agent-sdk-with-your-claude-plan
- **Help Center, Monthly API credits for Max and Team plans** (new on 2026-10-07). The credits cover `claude -p` and the Agent SDK when they run with an API key from the linked Console organisation. Signed in with a Claude plan instead, `claude -p` and Agent SDK usage "still draw from your plan's usage limits". That is how the app's reviews run: a review counts against the user's plan limits, or is billed to their key when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17154008-monthly-api-credits-for-max-and-team-plans
- **API credits for subscribers** (platform docs, first archived 2026-10-07). Max 5x $100 and Max 20x $200 a month; Team $20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat, pooled and capped at $500; Free, Pro and Enterprise are not eligible. Its coverage table lists the Claude API, Claude Managed Agents, the Agent SDK and the Playground as covered, and Claude Code, extra usage in the Claude apps and other platforms as not covered. This page does not mention `claude -p`, while the Help Center says the credits cover it when run with a key from the linked organisation; that was not tested. The README and Setup must not say the credits pay for the app's reviews. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/api-credits-for-subscribers
- **Enforcement in 2026.** In January, Anthropic said third-party harnesses using subscriptions are prohibited (https://venturebeat.com/technology/anthropic-cracks-down-on-unauthorized-claude-usage-by-third-party-harnesses). In March, OpenCode, a free open-source tool, removed its Pro/Max login after "anthropic legal requests", along with an Anthropic prompt file and other Anthropic references (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18186). In April, third-party tools such as OpenClaw were moved off plan limits onto separately billed extra usage (https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/04/anthropic-says-claude-code-subscribers-will-need-to-pay-extra-for-openclaw-support/). In May and June, a separate billing plan for Agent SDK usage was announced and then paused. Searched through 2026-10-16: no report of action against an app that runs the unmodified binary with each user's own sign-in.
- **Asking Anthropic.** "Contact sales" leads to an Enterprise checkout with no form for individuals. A support request is a courtesy; silence is not approval.

The OAuth bullet now links the Help Center's article on logging in. The app: as before (section 9 risk 8); Setup shows commands and starts no sign-in (Appendix C "No in-app sign-in launcher").
- **Authentication** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication). Which credential wins, highest first: a cloud provider chosen by `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`; `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which a terminal session asks about once but `-p` always uses when it is there; an `apiKeyHelper`; `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; Anthropic profile and federation credentials; the subscription sign-in from `/login`. On Windows the login is kept in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`, or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when that is set. A login within three days of its end warns at start-up in a terminal session; once it has ended and cannot be renewed, every request fails with "Login expired · Please run /login". A Console sign-in without an API key (2.1.242 and later) keeps an Anthropic profile outside the configuration folder (`%APPDATA%\Anthropic` on Windows, auth mode `user_oauth`), ranked below a working `/login`, and signs Claude Code out of any claude.ai login stored on the machine (that last point read again for the `setup.13` review, 2026-10-19). The app: the README's API key route, and Setup's line that the key is used in place of the plan, hold, since reviews run with `-p`; `apiKeyHelper` lives in a settings file, which the app does not load, as Setup's troubleshooting says (11.3 c); "Login expired" is read as `claude-login-expired` by `classifyClaudeFailure`'s expiry rule, so Setup shows the sign-in-ended view. An `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` was tried with a dummy token on 2026-10-19 (`setup.17`, Appendix C "An ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is the token, not a Claude plan"): 2.1.302's `auth status --json` says `loggedIn` true, `authMethod` `oauth_token` and no key, and its `initialize` reply names `tokenSource` `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` with no email, plan or key, with an empty configuration folder and over this machine's Max sign-in alike, which the token displaces (Claude Code then warns that the claude.ai connectors are off); beside an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` both answers name the key's source too and `auth status` still says `oauth_token`. The check read the token as a Claude plan, through `oauth_token`, until `setup.17`, and now names it. Not tried: how they describe a profile sign-in; one with an email and no API key would probably read as a Claude plan, and Test the connection's note would then say it counts against the plan. `release.13` tries a keyless Console sign-in just before `setup.14`'s sign-in, which brings back the claude.ai login the Console sign-in removes; until then the README does not offer `claude auth login --console`.
- **CLI reference, `auth status`** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference). `claude auth status` prints JSON, or prose with `--text`, and exits with 0 when logged in and 1 when not. The JSON's `authMethod` is one of `none`, `claude.ai`, `oauth_token`, `api_key`, `api_key_helper` and `third_party`, and from 2.1.268 the JSON also names the configuration folder in `configDirectory`. `claude auth login` takes `--email`, `--sso` and `--console`. The app: `credentialFromAuthMethod` maps exactly those five methods beside `none`; `runClaudeCli` keeps the answer of an exit code 1, since signed out is an answer; `parseAuthStatus` keeps only its six fields, so the folder's path is never kept or logged. The page also lists every flag of 11.3 (q) with the meaning the app relies on, `--max-turns` among them (print mode only, no limit by default), and warns that `claude --help` does not list every flag: 2.1.302's `--help` leaves out `--max-turns`, which 2.1.266's listed, and which `setup.8`'s real test ran with on 2.1.302 (C.63). `release.10`'s per-release check of the flags reads this page for a flag `--help` leaves out.
- **Troubleshoot installation and login** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install). On Windows the PowerShell installer puts `claude.exe` in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`, and when that folder is not on PATH it says so, with the fix, in its "Setup notes", without changing PATH itself; CMD has an installer line of its own. WinGet (`winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode`) and Homebrew (`brew install --cask claude-code`, the stable channel, about a week behind; `claude-code@latest` for the newest) do not update themselves. An npm install on Windows meets PowerShell's execution policy at `claude.ps1`, and `claude.cmd` is the way round it. An older Claude Desktop can register a `Claude.exe` in the `WindowsApps` folder that comes first on PATH. A self-update that failed can leave no `claude.exe`, only a `claude.exe.old.*` backup to rename back (before 2.1.281 the backup could be deleted too). For sign-in: when no browser opens, `claude auth login` prints the link and reads a pasted code from the terminal, which is also the fallback on Windows when pasting into the interactive prompt fails; an expired token is cured by signing in again; an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` left from an old employer or project overrides a subscription and can fail with "This organization has been disabled". The app: the install line signs in through the full path and the full-path forms are right; Troubleshooting's "open a new terminal" helped only when the folder was already on PATH, so since `setup.17` its answer leads with the full-path form where Setup shows one and names the installer's folder where it does not (5.6 item 5); the npm answer stands; a `WindowsApps` alias is never taken by the lookup, which leaves that folder out and whose `canRun` refuses an alias anyway, but a terminal runs it when it comes first on PATH, which Troubleshooting now answers on the Windows tab (5.6 items 1 and 5, `setup.17`); the disabled organisation is `API_KEY_REFUSED_MESSAGE`'s case; a `claude.exe` lost in an update reads as not installed, and the not-installed install line puts it back.
- **Model configuration** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config). Default is Opus 5.5 on Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise and the API since 2.1.280, and was Sonnet 5 on Pro and Team Standard before (Appendix C "Default is Opus 5.5 on Pro since CLI 2.1.280", with the order of the choices that decide it). On the Anthropic API `opus` became Opus 5.5 at 2.1.280, `sonnet` Sonnet 5.5 at 2.1.284 and `haiku` Haiku 5.5 at 2.1.293; `fable` is Fable 5.1 from 2.1.257. A `/model` choice made in `-p` mode lasts for that session only. The app: `RECOMMENDED_CLAUDE_CODE`, 2.1.283, was set for Opus 5.5 and predates Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, so a copy between 2.1.283 and 2.1.292 gets no update note while it lacks one of the newest models; `release.10` moves the yardstick each release.

### OpenAI (research dated 2026-09-11, Phase 5c)

- OpenAI's documented route for a third-party app is an API key from a Platform account, billed per token to that account. That is what the OpenAI provider used, from Phase 5c until `codex.6` took it out. The SDK reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` by default and the app passes a stored key explicitly. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs and https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses
- (Superseded: OpenAI has since documented Sign in with ChatGPT for open-source apps, read for `codex.1` on 2026-10-22 and for `codex.2` on 2026-10-24, below; the app signs in that way since `codex.2`, and the API key stayed as it was until `codex.6` took it out.) Signing in with a ChatGPT subscription (Plus, Pro, Team) inside a third-party app has no stated permission. The only subscription sign-in OpenAI documents is for its own Codex tools; public requests for a "Sign in with ChatGPT" for other apps are still open feature requests, and routing a Codex login through another app is described in the community as unsupported. So the app offers no ChatGPT sign-in and says in the dialog that OpenAI reviews are billed per token, not to a ChatGPT subscription. Sources seen: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/10974 (404 when re-checked on 2026-10-16) , https://community.openai.com/t/login-with-chatgpt-allow-users-to-use-their-own-plus-subscription-in-3rd-party-apps/1378506 , https://community.openai.com/t/api-chatgpt-subscription-cannot-use-api-with-chatgpt-subscription/875542
- Prices for the cost estimate, standard tier: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (copied into `src/shared/ai/pricing.ts` on 2026-09-11, which went with the key in `codex.6`).

### Sign in with ChatGPT for open-source apps (read 2026-10-24, `codex.2`)

Read live on 2026-10-24, before the build, as `codex.2` asks; no page carries a date of its own. Each bullet says what the page says that bears on the app, in this plan's words; how the app stands against it is in 5.7 and Appendix C "What Sign in with ChatGPT settled where the plan left it open". Information for the author, not legal advice. No agent has a ChatGPT account, and nothing was signed in: the author's own first sign-in is the real check.

- **Overview** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source). ChatGPT plan usage is offered to open-source and locally hosted apps, which may ask for permission to use the user's plan for eligible Responses API requests; it gives no access to the user's conversations. Paid or remotely hosted apps are sent to an interest form. A client is the OAuth registration the user authorises, and its issued client id is bound to that user and the workspace chosen at registration; a host is where an instance of the app runs, and one client may have several hosts. The host id (`ext_agent_host_id`) is made and kept before a host's first sign-in, is opaque, never an email or a user id, and is no credential; its forms are a JWK thumbprint URN (recommended), `urn:uuid:` with a version 4 UUID made once, or `did:key`; restarting the app or signing in again is not a new host. The steps: choose the account, keep the host id, start a listener and make fresh state, nonce and PKCE values; open the authorization with a new registration or the saved client id, the browser coming back to the loopback port with the code, the state and, for a new registration, the issued client id; check the state, exchange the code with the client id and the verifier, check the ID token and the scopes granted, and keep the credentials; then send Responses requests with the bearer token, `store: false` and `stream: true`, read to `response.completed`. Later sign-ins reuse the saved client id.
- **Registration and sign-in** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/sign-in). A first sign-in sends `client_id=dynamic_agent_client`, only the registration's entrypoint, never saved or exchanged, with `ext_agent_host_id` and `agent_name_hint`, the app's own name, used consistently; the callback brings the issued client id (shaped like `oaiapp_...`), kept and reused for that account; no client secret and no partner key. The authorization endpoint is `https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/authorize`, with `client_id`, `agent_name_hint` (first sign-in only), `ext_agent_host_id`, optional `id_token_hint` and `login_hint` on a later sign-in, `response_type=code`, a `redirect_uri` on 127.0.0.1, never `localhost` (its example is port 1455 and path `/auth/callback`; the port may change between sign-ins, the scheme, host and path may not), `scope` `openid profile email offline_access resource.invoke chatgpt.tokens.use.direct`, `resource` `https://api.openai.com/v1`, and a fresh `state`, `nonce` and S256 `code_challenge` each attempt, every value URL-encoded, the listener started before the browser opens. A later sign-in with no `id_token_hint` shows the account selector, with no workspace choice or consent screen, and the client stays bound to its workspace. The callback: `error=access_denied` is checked for its state and stops the sign-in; otherwise `code`, `state`, `scope` and, for a new registration, `client_id`; the state is checked first; a later sign-in's callback may leave the client id out and is refused if it names another; a new registration's callback without one is an unfinished registration. The exchange is a form POST to `https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token` with `grant_type=authorization_code`, the issued client id, the code, the verifier and the same `redirect_uri` and `resource`; on `invalid_grant` the code is dropped and the sign-in started again with the issued client id. The answer holds `id_token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `token_type` Bearer, `expires_in` and the scopes. The ID token's signature is checked against OpenAI's published keys, and its issuer (`https://auth.openai.com`), its audience (the issued client id), its expiry and the nonce; its `sub` is the account, and neither the email nor `sub` names a workspace; a returning account's identity is checked before its credentials are replaced. The plan may be used only when the scopes granted include `chatgpt.tokens.use.direct`; a valid ID token alone does not allow it. Credentials are kept apart for each client id and identity, written atomically with owner-only permissions (0600 on Unix), never committed or logged.
- **Accounts and sessions** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/profiles-and-sessions). Each account's registration, client id and credentials are kept apart and never mixed; signing in to the same account on the same host reuses its client id and the host id, without `agent_name_hint`; another account is added through `dynamic_agent_client`. A refresh is a form POST to the token endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`, the issued client id, the refresh token and the resource, without `scope`; refresh tokens rotate, and refreshes of one session are made one at a time. Signing out revokes the refresh token first, at the discovery document's `revocation_endpoint`, with `token`, `token_type_hint=refresh_token` and the issued client id; an empty 200 is success, an already invalid token included; a failed connection or a 5xx is tried again with a delay while the token is there; then the tokens are cleared, keeping the account's mapping to its client and the host id. When the app clears them without a confirmed revocation, it tells the user, who can disconnect the app in ChatGPT's settings. Revoking does not delete the registration. Tokens stay out of browser storage, source control, logs, analytics and support transcripts, and out of URLs.
- **Token reference** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/token-reference). The answer's fields are `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token`, `token_type`, `expires_in`, `scope` and `earliest_refresh_at`. An access token lasts an hour (`expires_in` 3600), a refresh token 30 days, each refresh giving a new one with 30 days more. The access token's claims are listed (`sub`, `aud` `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `client_id`, `scope`, an opaque `https://api.openai.com/auth`, `iss`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`, `nbf`); the ID token's are not, so nothing documents the plan's name in it.
- **Errors and recovery** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/errors-and-recovery). A sign-in whose scopes lack `chatgpt.tokens.use.direct` keeps the sign-in with plan use off, and the user who chooses to turn it on is sent through OAuth again with the saved client id and `prompt=consent` (`force_reconsent` only once OpenAI has confirmed it for the integration), never on every sign-in. Plan usage errors stop the request and never move it to another way of paying; the status, the body's shape, the code and the request id are kept. It lists the codes for a review's failures (`subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible`, `subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded` with ChatGPT's usage settings, https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage, as the way out, and others), for `codex.3`. A disconnection is learnt only from a request or a refresh that fails; an unusable refresh token (`invalid_grant`, `refresh_token_expired`, `refresh_token_reused` and others) means signing in again.
- **UI and UX guidelines** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/ui-ux-guidelines) and **the website button** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/website). The guidelines call the action "Continue with ChatGPT", with the ChatGPT logo, and the product and section "Sign in with ChatGPT"; the button page approves both labels, each with a white or a black logo, and asks for OpenAI's approved branding. For plan use they describe a first-sign-in welcome, "You're using your ChatGPT plan" with Got it, "Using ChatGPT plan" by the model choice with Manage usage, and "Usage limit reached" with Manage usage first, which belong with the reviews (`codex.3`).
- **Models and inference** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) and **preview limitations** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/preview-limitations), for `codex.3`: the model list is `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` with the bearer token, a `models` array of `slug`, `display_name` and `visibility` (those with `list` are shown); a review is `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` with the bearer token, `store: false` and `stream: true`, read to `response.completed`, never ChatGPT's own back end; system messages are refused (instructions or developer messages instead), and `max_output_tokens`, `metadata`, `prompt`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `truncation`, `user` and others are left out. Neither page mentions structured output (`text.format` with `json_schema`), which stays the open question `codex.3` settles.
- **The discovery document** (https://auth.openai.com/.well-known/openid-configuration): issuer `https://auth.openai.com`; authorization, token, revocation (`https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/revoke`), keys (`https://auth.openai.com/.well-known/jwks.json`) and userinfo endpoints; `code` only, `S256` only, RS256 ID tokens; a public client (`none`) is accepted at the token and revocation endpoints. The app writes these addresses in rather than reading the document at each sign-in.
- **Quickstart** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart): ChatGPT plan usage is open to all open-source partners; eligible Plus and Pro users can use their plan without an API key; the open-source flow registers the client with no client secret or partner key.
- **Not read on 2026-10-24.** The Sign in with ChatGPT terms (https://openai.com/policies/sign-in-with-chatgpt-terms/) and OpenAI's Help Center answered 403 to the agent's fetch, so the terms stand as `codex.1` read them on 2026-10-22 (above, and `codex-research.md`): the app uses its own name during sign-in and does not impersonate OpenAI, another application or another open-source project; requests come from the user's own machine; the plan serves only the app the user connected; the app charges nothing for it; the tokens stay local and under the user's control. The Data controls page's address, https://chatgpt.com/#settings/DataControls, is the ChatGPT web app's long-used address for that tab of its settings and appears on none of the pages read; OpenAI's help pages, as search results quoted them on 2026-10-24, give the way by hand, Settings, then Data controls, then Improve the model for everyone, which the warning names too. The author's first sign-in checks the address.

### Sign in with ChatGPT pages re-read for `codex.3` (2026-10-24)

Re-read before the build, for the reviews, with the Codex CLI on this machine for what OpenAI's pages leave out. How the app stands against them is in 5.8 and Appendix C "What ChatGPT's reviews settled where the plan left it open". Information for the author, not legal advice.

- **Models and inference** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference): the model list is `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` with the bearer, a `models` array whose entries with `visibility` `list` are shown by `display_name` and sent by `slug`, chosen again when the account changes; a review is `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` with the bearer, `store: false` and `stream: true`, a success only at `response.completed`; usage-limit errors arrive as `response.failed` events with `subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded` or `subscription_sharing_usage_unavailable`, possibly after the stream has begun. It names no structured output, no rate-limit header and no usage figures.
- **Preview limitations** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/preview-limitations): `input` as a list holding what each request needs; `instructions` or developer messages for system guidance, a system message refused; no `previous_response_id` over HTTP; refused parameters `background`, `conversation`, `max_output_tokens`, `max_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `moderation`, `multi_agent`, `prompt`, `prompt_cache_retention`, `safety_identifier`, `temperature`, `top_logprobs`, `top_p`, `truncation` and `user`; function and custom tools only. Nothing on structured output or `reasoning`.
- **Errors and recovery** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/errors-and-recovery): admission failures before any stream (401, 403, 503, a `{"detail": ...}` body to read as diagnostic text); the Responses codes and what to do: `subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible` (403: explain, and do not repeat the request or loop through OAuth), `subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded` (429: pause plan requests, link to ChatGPT's usage settings, read neither a reset time nor an empty plan from the code alone), `subscription_sharing_usage_unavailable` and `subscription_sharing_user_unavailable` (503: keep the credentials, retry later with a bounded backoff), `subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability` (400: `error.param` names what to take out; do not send the same body again), `subscription_sharing_route_not_supported` (403), `subscription_sharing_invalid_user` (401: sign in again only after a confirmed revocation or a refresh error that ends the sign-in), `chatpass_v2_scope_not_authorized` and `chatpass_v2_invalid_authorization_context` (403: check the client and the grant). Refresh errors that end the sign-in: `invalid_grant`, `invalid_refresh_token`, `token_expired`, `refresh_token_expired`, `refresh_token_invalidated` and `refresh_token_reused`; `invalid_client` means fixing the client. Credentials are kept through failures of the network or of OpenAI's servers.
- **UI and UX guidelines** (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/ui-ux-guidelines): the welcome after the first sign-in with plan use only ("You’re using your ChatGPT plan", "Eligible usage in this app uses your ChatGPT plan. Manage usage in your ChatGPT settings.", Got it); "Using ChatGPT plan" with Manage usage by the model choice, Manage usage opening `https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage`; "Usage limit reached" with "Review your plan or this app's limit in ChatGPT settings.", Manage usage first and Buy app credits second for an app that sells credits; a new sign-in told as sign out and sign in again. Nothing on a limit approaching, its windows or its reset.
- **Codex CLI 0.149.1** (on this machine; `codex --version` run, and its binary's strings read on 2026-10-24): the limit headers `x-codex-primary-used-percent`, `x-codex-primary-window-minutes`, `x-codex-primary-reset-at` and the `secondary` set, with `x-codex-active-limit`, `x-codex-rate-limit-reached-type` and the credits headers, which Codex reads from ChatGPT's own back end, not this route, and a rate-limit event in its stream. Whether `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` sends any of them to a Sign in with ChatGPT token is undocumented; the author's review records it.
